standard: Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute benchmark of 3% blood culture contamination; project aim to reduce contamination from 2.0% to 1.0% by March 2020
finding: 39 contaminants (2.0%); monthly rates varied 0.0-5.7%; compliance with standard bottle inoculation and skin preparation steps 50% each (observational audits, n = 20).
change: Four PDSA cycles: standardised bottle inoculation with a transfer device; standardised skin preparation for cannulation; aseptic technique education package; minimum 1 mL blood volume with a blood culture sticker and record book.
setting: Level 6 neonatal unit (14 NICU and 34 special care beds), Women's and Children's Hospital, North Adelaide
cycle1_result: 39 contaminants (2.0%); monthly rates varied 0.0-5.7%; compliance with standard bottle inoculation and skin preparation steps 50% each (observational audits, n = 20).
intervention: Four PDSA cycles: standardised bottle inoculation with a transfer device; standardised skin preparation for cannulation; aseptic technique education package; minimum 1 mL blood volume with a blood culture sticker and record book.
cycle2_result: 10 contaminants (0.90%); compliance with inoculation process 100% and skin preparation 95%; at least 1 mL collected in 94% of 450 collections.
other_findings: Aseptic technique test scores rose from 39% to 92% (n = 10, P < 0.001); no skin burns or unsuccessful sampling events occurred.
authors: Allen E; Cavallaro A; Keir AK
citation: Allen E, Cavallaro A, Keir AK. A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Blood Culture Contamination in the Neonatal Unit. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2021;6(3):e413. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000413. PMID: 34046542.

topic: Antibiotic prescribing for respiratory tract infection
title: Operationalising outpatient antimicrobial stewardship to reduce system-wide antibiotics for acute bronchitis.
standard: Guidelines recommending no antibiotics for acute uncomplicated bronchitis; aim to reduce antibiotic prescribing from 65% to <32% by April 2020
finding: Antibiotics prescribed in 314 of 486 (64.6%) acute bronchitis/URI encounters; 667 of 1054 (63%) over January to December 2018.
change: Seven PDSA cycles: provider needs-assessment interviews; CDC patient education materials and supportive care prescription pads; individual comparative feedback emails; individualised focused case reviews with high prescribers; primary care grand rounds.
setting: 18 community-based outpatient clinics, VA Tennessee Valley Healthcare System
cycle1_period: July to December 2018 (6 months before intervention)
cycle1_result: Antibiotics prescribed in 314 of 486 (64.6%) acute bronchitis/URI encounters; 667 of 1054 (63%) over January to December 2018.
intervention: Seven PDSA cycles: provider needs-assessment interviews; CDC patient education materials and supportive care prescription pads; individual comparative feedback emails; individualised focused case reviews with high prescribers; primary care grand rounds.
cycle2_result: Antibiotics prescribed in 154 of 418 (36.8%) encounters (p=0.002 across periods).
other_findings: The target of <32% was not reached; feedback emails were high effort with low read rates, while case reviews of 14 high prescribers gave the largest reduction. No change in return visits or calls; VA clinics improved more than contract clinics.
authors: Johnson MC; Hulgan T; Cooke RG; Kleinpell R; Roumie C; Callaway-Lane C; Mitchell LD; Hathaway J; Dittus R; Staub M
citation: Johnson MC, Hulgan T, Cooke RG, Kleinpell R, Roumie C, Callaway-Lane C, et al.. Operationalising outpatient antimicrobial stewardship to reduce system-wide antibiotics for acute bronchitis. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(3):e001275. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001275. PMID: 34210668.

title: Checklist to aid young physicians managing obstetric emergencies in rural India: a quality improvement initiative.
standard: Completeness of 31 agreed data points on first information sheets (items based on hospital policy and Ministry of Health guidelines); aim >90% completeness
finding: Mean first information sheet completeness 73.95%; 1 of 12 (8.33%) fully complete.
change: PDSA cycles: education session for interns; wall notes of required data points; a printed antenatal care (ANC) admission checklist, then implemented with shift-wise training and nursing officers printing it each shift.
setting: Obstetric emergency, Sub-District Hospital Ballabgarh (secondary care, AIIMS New Delhi rural health project)
cycle1_result: Mean first information sheet completeness 73.95%; 1 of 12 (8.33%) fully complete.
intervention: PDSA cycles: education session for interns; wall notes of required data points; a printed antenatal care (ANC) admission checklist, then implemented with shift-wise training and nursing officers printing it each shift.
cycle2_result: Mean completeness 86.34% (p<0.001); 16 of 65 (24.62%) fully complete (p=0.2); ANC checklist used in 69.72% of sheets.
other_findings: Physical examination items improved most; high-risk pregnancy documentation rose from 0% to 56.66% (17/30). Sheets with the checklist were more complete than those without (87.74% vs 74.42%).
authors: Puntambekar V; Sharma AK; Yadav K; Kumar R
citation: Puntambekar V, Sharma AK, Yadav K, Kumar R. Checklist to aid young physicians managing obstetric emergencies in rural India: a quality improvement initiative. BMJ Open Qual. 2021;10(Suppl 1):e001435. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001435. PMID: 34344735.

title: Improving Clinical Handover on an Electronic Communication Platform: A Quality Improvement Project.
standard: National handover guidance (RCP Acute Care Toolkit) SBAR components on a local proforma: admission date, estimated discharge date, presenting complaint, past medical and social history, escalation status, issues, updates and plans
finding: Admission date 51%; estimated discharge date 60%; presenting complaint 100%; social history 82%; escalation status 20%; issues 12%; important updates 71%; plans 100%
change: Teaching for foundation doctors, posters of the proforma, ward 'Careflow champions' and re-education at mandatory teaching
setting: St Peter's Hospital, Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (weekend handover lists and three random wards on an electronic SBAR platform)
cycle1_result: Admission date 51%; estimated discharge date 60%; presenting complaint 100%; social history 82%; escalation status 20%; issues 12%; important updates 71%; plans 100%
intervention: Teaching for foundation doctors, posters of the proforma, ward 'Careflow champions' and re-education at mandatory teaching
cycle2_result: Admission date 58% (+13.7%); estimated discharge date 80% (+33.3%); social history 92%; escalation status 67% (+335%); issues 29% (+242%); important updates 96%; plans 100%
other_findings: 710 handovers were assessed over four PDSA cycles. Admission date completion fell from 94% to 58% in the last cycle with junior doctor rotation and the COVID surge rota.
authors: Tan XL; Park H; Patel J; Murden M
citation: Tan XL, Park H, Patel J, Murden M. Improving Clinical Handover on an Electronic Communication Platform: A Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2021;13(10):e19156. doi:10.7759/cureus.19156. PMID: 34873500.

topic: Time to senior review in paediatrics
title: Improving paediatric flow in an UK Paediatric Assessment Unit.
standard: RCPCH Facing the Future: tier two doctor review within 4 hours and consultant review within 14 hours of admission
finding: 92% (24/26) seen by a registrar or above within 4 hours; mean wait 104.2 min; consultant review not measured
change: Extended weekend consultant on-site cover, flagging patients awaiting consultant review on the handover sheet, and a tier two roster with at least two doctors on at all times
setting: Paediatric Assessment Unit, Birmingham Heartlands Hospital, teaching hospital
cycle1_result: 92% (24/26) seen by a registrar or above within 4 hours; mean wait 104.2 min; consultant review not measured
intervention: Extended weekend consultant on-site cover, flagging patients awaiting consultant review on the handover sheet, and a tier two roster with at least two doctors on at all times
cycle2_result: 96.2% seen by a tier two doctor within 4 hours (from 82.9% in cycle 3, p=0.028)
other_findings: Consultant review within 14 hours rose from 53.3% (cycle 2) to 95% (cycle 3, p=0.005). Length of stay rose from 229 to 329 min despite earlier review; 177 of 288 data sets were complete.
authors: Li D; Abeywickrema M; Vadeyar S; Ward A; Abberton T; Rweyemamu J
citation: Li D, Abeywickrema M, Vadeyar S, Ward A, Abberton T, Rweyemamu J. Improving paediatric flow in an UK Paediatric Assessment Unit. BMJ Open Qual. 2022;11(1):e001561. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001561. PMID: 35086860.

title: A quality improvement project: Reducing the number of unnecessary plain abdominal radiographs performed in the emergency department of a London district general hospital.
standard: Royal College of Radiologists iRefer guidelines (2017) for plain abdominal radiography
finding: 79% of requests had at least one indication meeting iRefer guidance; 27% of radiographs diagnostic; 50% aided clinical management
change: Teaching session for ED clinicians on iRefer guidance and radiation dose, plus posters in the department and on the shared drive
setting: Emergency department, London district general hospital
cycle1_result: 79% of requests had at least one indication meeting iRefer guidance; 27% of radiographs diagnostic; 50% aided clinical management
intervention: Teaching session for ED clinicians on iRefer guidance and radiation dose, plus posters in the department and on the shared drive
cycle2_result: 87% met iRefer guidance; 47% diagnostic; 70% aided clinical management; 15% fewer radiographs
other_findings: Over half of studies needed more than one image. Constipation was a common indication even though a radiograph does not diagnose constipation.
authors: Kyriakides J; Khamar R; Khani A; Khatkar H
journal: Journal of family medicine and primary care
citation: Kyriakides J, Khamar R, Khani A, Khatkar H. A quality improvement project: Reducing the number of unnecessary plain abdominal radiographs performed in the emergency department of a London district general hospital. J Family Med Prim Care. 2022;11(1):190-193. doi:10.4103/jfmpc.jfmpc_1193_21. PMID: 35309616.

title: Quality improvement initiative to improve infant safe sleep practices in the newborn nursery.
standard: AAP Infant Safe Sleep guidelines; composite 'perfect sleep' measure; aim 70% within 1 year
finding: 41.9% of sleeping infants met 'perfect sleep'; 38.0% of sleep areas had extra items; 15.3% inappropriately bundled; 87.0% in a safe location; 90.3% on their back; 3.8% raised bassinette head.
change: Seven PDSA cycles: nursing education module; parent education with door hangers then crib cards; temporary then permanent supply of wearable blankets (sleep sacks) with laundering; reminder to labour ward nurses to give empty bassinettes; gifting sleep sacks to take home.
setting: Mother-baby unit, suburban community hospital in North Carolina (Duke University Health System)
cycle1_result: 41.9% of sleeping infants met 'perfect sleep'; 38.0% of sleep areas had extra items; 15.3% inappropriately bundled; 87.0% in a safe location; 90.3% on their back; 3.8% raised bassinette head.
intervention: Seven PDSA cycles: nursing education module; parent education with door hangers then crib cards; temporary then permanent supply of wearable blankets (sleep sacks) with laundering; reminder to labour ward nurses to give empty bassinettes; gifting sleep sacks to take home.
cycle2_result: 'Perfect sleep' rose to 67.3% (goal of 70% not met); extra items 20.2%; inappropriate bundling 3.8%; safe location 92.0%; back sleeping 98.1%.
other_findings: Improvements were sustained over 12 months after the last PDSA cycle; over 3100 observations were recorded in total. Extra items in the bassinette, often due to storage, remained the main cause of failure.
authors: Shaikh SK; Chamberlain L; Nazareth-Pidgeon KM; Boggan JC
citation: Shaikh SK, Chamberlain L, Nazareth-Pidgeon KM, Boggan JC. Quality improvement initiative to improve infant safe sleep practices in the newborn nursery. BMJ Open Qual. 2022;11(3):e001834. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-001834. PMID: 35922090.

title: Improving the Acceptance Rate of Centchroman As a Postpartum Contraceptive Through a Quality Improvement Initiative.
standard: SMART aim to increase centchroman acceptance as a postpartum contraceptive to at least 50%
finding: Baseline centchroman acceptance rate 2.9%.
change: Staff seminar, then three PDSA cycles: information charts in postnatal clinics; awareness sessions by nursing staff; counselling by resident doctors.
setting: Postnatal clinics, ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Faridabad (tertiary care hospital)
cycle1_result: Baseline centchroman acceptance rate 2.9%.
intervention: Staff seminar, then three PDSA cycles: information charts in postnatal clinics; awareness sessions by nursing staff; counselling by resident doctors.
cycle2_result: Acceptance rose to 15.3%, 56.3% and 78.2% after PDSA cycles 1-3; overall acceptance 81.7% during 12-week follow-up.
other_findings: Continuation rates were 96.7%, 89.5% and 78.6% at 1, 3 and 6 months; discontinuation was mainly due to preference for IUDs or medroxyprogesterone injections.
authors: Sarkar A; Wadhawan I; Raj A; Nagabhushana P; Singh P
citation: Sarkar A, Wadhawan I, Raj A, Nagabhushana P, Singh P. Improving the Acceptance Rate of Centchroman As a Postpartum Contraceptive Through a Quality Improvement Initiative. Cureus. 2022;14(9):e29277. doi:10.7759/cureus.29277. PMID: 36277560.

title: A Prospective Quality Improvement Initiative to Address the Barriers to Postpartum Tubal Ligation Among Multiparous Women.
standard: Aim to increase postpartum tubal ligation among multiparous women by 50% from baseline
finding: Baseline prevalence of postpartum tubal ligation 30.2%.
change: Three PDSA cycles: modified consent form with a PPTL column and red sticker on antenatal cards plus provider counselling; group antenatal education for women; counselling of partners and birth attendants.
setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital (ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Faridabad)
cycle1_result: Baseline prevalence of postpartum tubal ligation 30.2%.
intervention: Three PDSA cycles: modified consent form with a PPTL column and red sticker on antenatal cards plus provider counselling; group antenatal education for women; counselling of partners and birth attendants.
cycle2_result: PPTL rose to 49.5% after cycle 1, 68.8% after cycle 2 and 74.4% after cycle 3; continuation rate 72% at the end of follow-up.
other_findings: Six-monthly audits were proposed; women not wanting PPTL all opted for postpartum intrauterine devices.
authors: Sarkar A; Panneer S; Vanya V; Wadhawan I
citation: Sarkar A, Panneer S, Vanya V, Wadhawan I. A Prospective Quality Improvement Initiative to Address the Barriers to Postpartum Tubal Ligation Among Multiparous Women. Cureus. 2022;14(9):e29641. doi:10.7759/cureus.29641. PMID: 36321020.

title: Incidental lymphadenopathy in renal transplantation.
standard: No published standard; unit guideline introduced after cycle 1 that all incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes are biopsied
finding: 11 (14.47%) had incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes biopsied at the surgeon's discretion; all showed reactive changes only
change: Unit guideline that all incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes at transplantation undergo histological assessment regardless of size
setting: Renal transplant unit, The Newcastle upon Tyne Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: 11 (14.47%) had incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes biopsied at the surgeon's discretion; all showed reactive changes only
intervention: Unit guideline that all incidentally enlarged iliac lymph nodes at transplantation undergo histological assessment regardless of size
cycle2_result: 8 (4.85%) had enlarged nodes, all biopsied: 5 reactive, 2 with no nodal tissue, 1 chronic lymphocytic leukaemia
other_findings: The CLL diagnosis led to reduced immunosuppression. The authors recommend histology for incidental nodes with suspicious features or over 10 mm (positive yield 1 in 19, 5.26%).
authors: Ho NX; Malik AK; Moulding S; Farrow F; Talbot D; White S; Rix D; Sen G; Manas D; Amer A; Figuereido R; Wilson CH
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
citation: Ho NX, Malik AK, Moulding S, Farrow F, Talbot D, White S, et al.. Incidental lymphadenopathy in renal transplantation. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2024;106(3):245-248. doi:10.1308/rcsann.2023.0043. PMID: 37489513.

title: Improving the Quality of Operative Notes in Vascular Surgery: A Retrospective Analysis.
standard: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland Code of Practice for Surgeons (2018) operative note content
finding: Time of procedure 0%; elective/emergency 9.4%; anaesthetist 59%; complications 25%; additional procedures 12.5%; blood loss 0%; antibiotic prophylaxis 0%; closure technique 59.4%; uploaded to EVOLVE 28.1%
change: Theatre checklist poster, scanner in theatre with instruction poster and video for uploading notes, individual scanner accounts and staff education at M&M meetings
setting: Department of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery, University Hospital Galway, tertiary centre
cycle1_result: Time of procedure 0%; elective/emergency 9.4%; anaesthetist 59%; complications 25%; additional procedures 12.5%; blood loss 0%; antibiotic prophylaxis 0%; closure technique 59.4%; uploaded to EVOLVE 28.1%
intervention: Theatre checklist poster, scanner in theatre with instruction poster and video for uploading notes, individual scanner accounts and staff education at M&M meetings
cycle2_period: Third cycle, about six months after baseline
cycle2_result: Time 6.25%; elective/emergency 50%; anaesthetist 90.6%; complications 90.6%; additional procedures 75%; blood loss 9.3%; antibiotics 28.1%; closure technique 100%; uploaded to EVOLVE 90.6%
other_findings: Time, blood loss and antibiotic prophylaxis improved in the second cycle (28.1%, 34.3%, 43.7%) but fell again in the third. All notes were handwritten.
authors: Akasha M; Alfatih A; Mohamed M; Acharya Y; Alawy M
citation: Akasha M, Alfatih A, Mohamed M, Acharya Y, Alawy M. Improving the Quality of Operative Notes in Vascular Surgery: A Retrospective Analysis. Cureus. 2024;16(2):e54791. doi:10.7759/cureus.54791. PMID: 38529458.

topic: Chest trauma and rib fracture management
title: Improving the Diagnosis of Rib Fractures in the Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project in a District General Hospital in the United Kingdom.
standard: Project SMART aim: 90% of chest wall injuries diagnosed at the initial ED assessment (informed by London Major Trauma System 2018 guidance on elderly trauma)
finding: 61% of chest wall injuries diagnosed at the initial ED encounter (30 of 77 missed; text also reports 61% missed); mean time from attendance to first CT 477 minutes
change: Thoracic trauma proforma with a modified PIC score and CT criteria, updated trust chest trauma pathway allowing contrast CT, a resus drawer for the proforma, and teaching, posters and email reminders
setting: Emergency department, William Harvey Hospital, district general hospital and trauma unit, East Kent Hospitals University NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: 61% of chest wall injuries diagnosed at the initial ED encounter (30 of 77 missed; text also reports 61% missed); mean time from attendance to first CT 477 minutes
intervention: Thoracic trauma proforma with a modified PIC score and CT criteria, updated trust chest trauma pathway allowing contrast CT, a resus drawer for the proforma, and teaching, posters and email reminders
cycle2_result: 91% diagnosed at initial ED assessment (3 missed); time to first CT 169 minutes; proforma completed in 9 cases
other_findings: Modified PIC score use reached 26% of chest wall injury cases. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted teaching and the electronic record change prevented a digital proforma.
authors: Naeem S; Aziz S; Carballido F; Leung J
citation: Naeem S, Aziz S, Carballido F, Leung J. Improving the Diagnosis of Rib Fractures in the Emergency Department: A Quality Improvement Project in a District General Hospital in the United Kingdom. Cureus. 2024;16(3):e56873. doi:10.7759/cureus.56873. PMID: 38659561.

title: Adherence to Preoperative Fasting Guidelines in Elective Surgical Patients.
standard: International (ASA/European Society of Anaesthesiology) and Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh fasting guidance: clear fluids until 2 hours and solids until 6 hours before surgery (morning list: solids to midnight, clear fluids to 06:30; afternoon list: breakfast before 07:00, clear fluids to 11:00)
finding: 86 (95.6%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids and 90 (100%) >6 hours from solid food; 18 (20.0%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids; 48 (53.3%) received both verbal and written instructions.
change: Institutional action plan: explicit morning and afternoon fasting rules, fasting information at pre-hospitalisation and preoperative clinic visits, and explanatory leaflets for patients.
setting: Cardiac, thoracic and vascular surgery departments, RUDN University-affiliated teaching hospital, Moscow
cycle1_period: September (baseline audit; year given as 2022 in methods and 2023 in abstract)
cycle1_result: 86 (95.6%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids and 90 (100%) >6 hours from solid food; 18 (20.0%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids; 48 (53.3%) received both verbal and written instructions.
intervention: Institutional action plan: explicit morning and afternoon fasting rules, fasting information at pre-hospitalisation and preoperative clinic visits, and explanatory leaflets for patients.
cycle2_period: December (final monthly re-audit after October and November)
cycle2_result: 33 of 57 (57.9%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids (p=0.021); 27 (47.4%) fasted >6-12 hours from solid food (p=0.005); 3 (5.3%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids.
other_findings: Across all 306 patients median fasting was 4.5 hours for clear fluids and 14.5 hours for solids; afternoon-list patients fasted longer (clear fluids 6.2 vs 3.4 hours, p<0.001). Both instruction types were received by 70.3% after the action plan.
authors: Sidik AI; Lishchuk A; Faybushevich AN; Moomin A; Akambase J; Dontsov V; Sobolev D; Ilyas Mohammad Shafii A; Najneen F; Ak G; Ahlam D; Adam MK; Baatiema L; Benneh C; Adu-Gyamfi PKT; Agyapong F; Mensah KB
citation: Sidik AI, Lishchuk A, Faybushevich AN, Moomin A, Akambase J, Dontsov V, et al.. Adherence to Preoperative Fasting Guidelines in Elective Surgical Patients. Cureus. 2024;16(10):e71554. doi:10.7759/cureus.71554. PMID: 39544576.

title: Striving for excellence in ventilator bundle compliance through continuous quality improvement initiative in the intensive care unit of a tertiary care hospital in India.
standard: Ventilator bundle compliance (all five components documented); aim >90% within 6 months
finding: Ventilator bundle compliance 40.7%, lowest for daily sedation vacation with SBT and thromboprophylaxis; VAP 62.4 per 1,000 ventilator days.
change: PDSA cycles: multidisciplinary educational boot camp with WhatsApp group; bundle checklist in ICU progress chart signed by nurses and residents and countersigned by consultants, random inspections and a placard; simulation and micro-scenarios to standardise technique, with coloured bed marks for head elevation.
setting: 15-bed closed adult ICU, tertiary care hospital (Dr. S.N. Medical College, Jodhpur)
cycle1_result: Ventilator bundle compliance 40.7%, lowest for daily sedation vacation with SBT and thromboprophylaxis; VAP 62.4 per 1,000 ventilator days.
intervention: PDSA cycles: multidisciplinary educational boot camp with WhatsApp group; bundle checklist in ICU progress chart signed by nurses and residents and countersigned by consultants, random inspections and a placard; simulation and micro-scenarios to standardise technique, with coloured bed marks for head elevation.
cycle2_period: September 2022 to August 2023 (6 months after compliance >90%)
cycle2_result: Compliance >70% after cycle 1 and >90% after cycle 2; VAP fell to 25.7 per 1,000 ventilator days (P=0.004; incidence rate ratio 2.34).
other_findings: Total ventilation days and ICU length of stay also fell significantly (P=0.007 and P=0.002).
authors: Paliwal N; Bihani P; Jaju R; Mohammed S; Prakash P; Tharu V
citation: Paliwal N, Bihani P, Jaju R, Mohammed S, Prakash P, Tharu V. Striving for excellence in ventilator bundle compliance through continuous quality improvement initiative in the intensive care unit of a tertiary care hospital in India. Acute Crit Care. 2024;39(4):535-544. doi:10.4266/acc.2024.00101. PMID: 39558598.

title: Prevention and Control of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection (CAUTI): A Patient Safety and Quality Improvement Project.
standard: CDC CAUTI prevention guidance, HOUDINI nurse-driven catheter removal protocol and CAUTI care bundle
finding: Mean CAUTI rate 1.28 per 1000 catheter days.
change: Three PDSA cycles: staff education, HOUDINI nurse-driven removal protocol with posters and a campaign; monitored HOUDINI and care bundle compliance; closed urinary drainage system introduced; external catheters as alternatives; internal audits with feedback; patient and family education and a urinary catheter passport.
setting: Sultan Bin Abdulaziz Humanitarian City, 511-bed rehabilitation facility, Riyadh
cycle1_result: Mean CAUTI rate 1.28 per 1000 catheter days.
intervention: Three PDSA cycles: staff education, HOUDINI nurse-driven removal protocol with posters and a campaign; monitored HOUDINI and care bundle compliance; closed urinary drainage system introduced; external catheters as alternatives; internal audits with feedback; patient and family education and a urinary catheter passport.
cycle2_result: Mean CAUTI rate 0.42 per 1000 catheter days (p=0.04); eight consecutive points below the centre line from July 2023 to May 2024.
other_findings: Bundle and HOUDINI compliance were monitored but compliance figures were not reported; a sustainability plan included automating the HOUDINI tool.
authors: Plando R; Obaid L; Al Baker AS; Khan O; Solatorio M; De Leon BJ; Tabasin VM; Obsioma RA
citation: Plando R, Obaid L, Al Baker AS, Khan O, Solatorio M, De Leon BJ, et al.. Prevention and Control of Catheter-Associated Urinary Tract Infection (CAUTI): A Patient Safety and Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2024;16(10):e72105. doi:10.7759/cureus.72105. PMID: 39575052.

title: Standardized CT KUB Protocols for Nephrolithiasis: A Retrospective Analysis of Radiation Exposure and Cranial Extent Guidelines.
standard: IR(ME)R principle of minimising radiation; local protocol to start CT KUB at the T10-T12 vertebral level (no formal national guideline)
finding: 48% (n=49) of scans started above T10, 51% (n=52) from T10-T12 and 1% below T12; mean effective dose 6.37 mSv above T10 vs 4.56 mSv from T10-T12.
change: Findings presented to urology and radiology departments and a new protocol to commence CT KUB from T10-T12 devised.
setting: District general hospital, Doncaster Royal Infirmary
cycle1_result: 48% (n=49) of scans started above T10, 51% (n=52) from T10-T12 and 1% below T12; mean effective dose 6.37 mSv above T10 vs 4.56 mSv from T10-T12.
intervention: Findings presented to urology and radiology departments and a new protocol to commence CT KUB from T10-T12 devised.
cycle2_result: 21.9% (n=23) started above T10, 75.2% (n=79) from T10-T12 and 2.9% below T12; mean dose 6.76 mSv above T10 vs 4.12 mSv from T10-T12.
other_findings: Kidneys were fully visualised from T10 in 98.6% of all scans, but from T12 in only 79.2%, supporting T10 as the cranial limit.
authors: Jarral F; Hamdy A; Mohamed G; Mobayen R; Dave N; Eltawil M; Mohan A; Abusand O; Tokidis E; Akbar J
citation: Jarral F, Hamdy A, Mohamed G, Mobayen R, Dave N, Eltawil M, et al.. Standardized CT KUB Protocols for Nephrolithiasis: A Retrospective Analysis of Radiation Exposure and Cranial Extent Guidelines. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e75743. doi:10.7759/cureus.75743. PMID: 39687674.

topic: Second-trimester fetal anomaly scan image quality
title: Feasibility of a Standardised Mid-Trimester Ultrasound Protocol: A National Multicenter Study.
standard: CNEOF 2022 national mid-trimester ultrasound protocol (21 recommended and 3 additional standardised views) with a 73-criterion consensus quality assessment score
finding: 9028 of 9240 (97.8%) recommended images recorded; feasibility of recommended views 88.5-100% (>95% for 20 of 21); 319 of 440 (72.5%) scans had no recommended view missing; 64 of 73 (88%) conformity criteria met in over 90% of cases.
setting: 88 operators of the French college of fetal ultrasound (CFEF) in public and private hospitals and private practice across France
cycle1_result: 9028 of 9240 (97.8%) recommended images recorded; feasibility of recommended views 88.5-100% (>95% for 20 of 21); 319 of 440 (72.5%) scans had no recommended view missing; 64 of 73 (88%) conformity criteria met in over 90% of cases.
other_findings: Weakest criteria included adrenal gland visibility (63.7%), cavum septi pellucidi (85.4%) and cervix views (about 87%); self- and peer-assessment agreed well (AC1 >0.80 for 70 of 73 criteria). Shorter scans and BMI >30 were associated with more missing images.
authors: Bultez T; Salomon LJ; Mahallati H; Fries N; CNEOFT2 Study Group
journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
citation: Bultez T, Salomon LJ, Mahallati H, Fries N, CNEOFT2 Study Group. Feasibility of a Standardised Mid-Trimester Ultrasound Protocol: A National Multicenter Study. BJOG. 2025;132(8):1065-1073. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.18102. PMID: 39949187.

title: Improving drug charting practices and documentation among nurses in emergency department at a regional hospital, Bhutan: a quality improvement initiative.
standard: Hospital transcription protocol; complete drug chart documentation to be maintained above 90%
finding: 44.9% (45%) of drug charts complete; adherence to standard charting practice 51%; transcriber signature/name recorded in 45%.
change: Four 2-week PDSA cycles: sensitisation teaching on medication errors and the transcription protocol; standardisation to a single drug chart; red pens at the nursing station for antibiotic charting; daily drug chart monitoring and feedback by pharmacy.
setting: Emergency department, Eastern Regional Referral Hospital, Mongar
cycle1_result: 44.9% (45%) of drug charts complete; adherence to standard charting practice 51%; transcriber signature/name recorded in 45%.
intervention: Four 2-week PDSA cycles: sensitisation teaching on medication errors and the transcription protocol; standardisation to a single drug chart; red pens at the nursing station for antibiotic charting; daily drug chart monitoring and feedback by pharmacy.
cycle2_result: 98% of drug charts complete; adherence to standard charting practice 98%; transcriber signature 95%.
other_findings: Completeness was 81% after cycle 1 and 88% after cycle 2, passing 90% after cycle 3; only 48% of staff were initially aware of the transcription protocol.
authors: Wangmo P; Wangdi S; Lhamo G; Dorji J; Wangmo J; Wangchuk N; Nepal HK
citation: Wangmo P, Wangdi S, Lhamo G, Dorji J, Wangmo J, Wangchuk N, et al.. Improving drug charting practices and documentation among nurses in emergency department at a regional hospital, Bhutan: a quality improvement initiative. BMJ Open Qual. 2025;13(Suppl 1):e003188. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2024-003188. PMID: 40054992.

title: Improving capacity and flow in a children and young people's Community Eating Disorder Service (CEDS): how a quality improvement initiative led to a reduction in waiting times in the service.
standard: Commissioned target of routine assessment within 2 weeks (urgent within 5 days); national standards 1 week urgent and 4 weeks routine. Aim: reduce routine referral wait from 17 weeks to 2 weeks in 12 months.
finding: Average wait from routine referral to assessment 17 weeks; 73 patients on psychiatry wait list; 50 families on therapy wait list; 65 inactive cases.
change: QI with PDSA cycles: weekly referral meeting with referral tracker and 2-week deadline for referrers; single-clinician triage and assessment; revised co-designed referral form; psychiatry wait list review, clinics three mornings a week, joint reviews and medication/prescription clinics; therapy wait list review and capacity planning; monthly caseload audit; shorter 2-page discharge letter; staff recruitment campaign.
setting: Children and young people's Community Eating Disorders Service (CEDS), East London NHS Foundation Trust (Tower Hamlets, Newham, City & Hackney)
cycle1_result: Average wait from routine referral to assessment 17 weeks; 73 patients on psychiatry wait list; 50 families on therapy wait list; 65 inactive cases.
intervention: QI with PDSA cycles: weekly referral meeting with referral tracker and 2-week deadline for referrers; single-clinician triage and assessment; revised co-designed referral form; psychiatry wait list review, clinics three mornings a week, joint reviews and medication/prescription clinics; therapy wait list review and capacity planning; monthly caseload audit; shorter 2-page discharge letter; staff recruitment campaign.
cycle2_result: Average routine wait fell to 2 weeks (88% reduction), sustained; psychiatry wait list 73 to 0 by December 2022; therapy wait list 50 to 0 by April 2023; inactive cases 65 to 0.
other_findings: Agency staff spend fell from about £130,000 a year to 0 by February 2024; staffing rose from 64% (July 2022) to 77% (April 2023) with no current vacancies.
authors: Ulhaq S; Cheradi K; Ahmed A; Thanki K; Dalby M
citation: Ulhaq S, Cheradi K, Ahmed A, Thanki K, Dalby M. Improving capacity and flow in a children and young people's Community Eating Disorder Service (CEDS): how a quality improvement initiative led to a reduction in waiting times in the service. BMJ Open Qual. 2025;14(1):e002959. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2024-002959. PMID: 40122574.

title: Developing an online educational platform to expedite ADHD medication initiation in child and adolescent mental health services: a quality improvement project.
standard: Project aims: reduce time-to-treatment initiation (TTI) for ADHD medication by 10% and increase proportion initiated on medication by 5% by February 2024; NICE NG87 recommends medication as part of a treatment plan.
finding: Mean TTI 86 days; 64% (n=76) of young people started on ADHD medication; satisfaction 4.13/5 (n=13).
change: Online post-diagnostic psychoeducation platform (videos, Q&A, e-form medication decision portal with physical health e-form, useful links), emailed to families; QR code posters; text message prompts (PDSA 2); patient experience video (PDSA 3).
setting: Neurodevelopmental Team, outpatient CAMHS, Brent, Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: Mean TTI 86 days; 64% (n=76) of young people started on ADHD medication; satisfaction 4.13/5 (n=13).
intervention: Online post-diagnostic psychoeducation platform (videos, Q&A, e-form medication decision portal with physical health e-form, useful links), emailed to families; QR code posters; text message prompts (PDSA 2); patient experience video (PDSA 3).
cycle2_result: Mean TTI fell to 43 days (n=82) after PDSA 3 (reported elsewhere as 51 days, 41% reduction); 70% (n=52) started on medication; satisfaction 4.37/5 (n=21).
other_findings: TTI fell stepwise from 86 to 60 (PDSA 1), 54 (PDSA 2) and 43 days (PDSA 3); about 8 hours of clinician time saved over 2 months.
authors: Stanton N; Aziz A; Jakhra S; Morganstein L; Bailey S; Kramer T; Obeng I
citation: Stanton N, Aziz A, Jakhra S, Morganstein L, Bailey S, Kramer T, et al.. Developing an online educational platform to expedite ADHD medication initiation in child and adolescent mental health services: a quality improvement project. BMJ Open Qual. 2025;14(1):e003148. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2024-003148. PMID: 40154989.

title: Identifying frail patients at the front door: a quality improvement project on improving identifying frailty and accuracy of Clinical Frailty Scale in the emergency department in an acute general hospital.
standard: NHS England CQUIN 05 (2023/24): identify frailty in ED patients aged 65+ using the Clinical Frailty Scale, CGA if CFS 6 or above. SMART target 70% correct identification of CFS 6+ by November 2024; ED nurse scores compared with frailty intervention team scores.
finding: Correct identification of moderate frailty (CFS 6+) 45–51%; exact CFS accuracy 17%.
change: Two PDSA cycles of ED nurse training: CFS lanyard card to standardise scoring, 1:1 brief teaching (135 sessions), group/virtual sessions, posters, newsletter and emails (cycle 1, November 2023); plus quizzes, scenarios and individual feedback (cycle 2, September to October 2024).
setting: Emergency department, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (acute general hospital)
cycle1_result: Correct identification of moderate frailty (CFS 6+) 45–51%; exact CFS accuracy 17%.
intervention: Two PDSA cycles of ED nurse training: CFS lanyard card to standardise scoring, 1:1 brief teaching (135 sessions), group/virtual sessions, posters, newsletter and emails (cycle 1, November 2023); plus quizzes, scenarios and individual feedback (cycle 2, September to October 2024).
cycle2_result: Correct identification of CFS 6+ rose to 74–78% (78% at 9–13 October 2024); exact CFS accuracy up to 42%.
other_findings: After cycle 1 correct identification rose to 70% then ranged 58–68%; exact accuracy rose to 30% but fell back to 17%, so sustainability of accuracy is uncertain.
authors: Zhang Y; Cosimetti A; Montagu A
citation: Zhang Y, Cosimetti A, Montagu A. Identifying frail patients at the front door: a quality improvement project on improving identifying frailty and accuracy of Clinical Frailty Scale in the emergency department in an acute general hospital. title: Implementation of the bedside paediatric early warning system, its sustainability in clinical practice and patient outcomes: a quality improvement initiative.

finding: Compliance 84% in the pilot unit; in the first year compliance was below target for reassessment, escalation and physician review.
change: Electronic PEWS integrated into the EMR with an action plan; training of about 600 staff and at orientation; modified action plan with observation frequency; staged roll-out to wards, ER and PICU; unit-specific action plans; quarterly compliance audits with feedback.
setting: King Abdullah Specialist Children's Hospital, academic tertiary paediatric hospital (about 220 beds), Riyadh
cycle1_result: Compliance 84% in the pilot unit; in the first year compliance was below target for reassessment, escalation and physician review.
intervention: Electronic PEWS integrated into the EMR with an action plan; training of about 600 staff and at orientation; modified action plan with observation frequency; staged roll-out to wards, ER and PICU; unit-specific action plans; quarterly compliance audits with feedback.
cycle2_result: Reassessment and rescoring 95-100%, escalation 100% and physician review 100% over the past 6 years; pilot compliance rose to 96% after the action plan change.

change: 'Straight to CT' pathway with registrar-requested scans, mandatory STONE score prompts in ICE/iRefer requests, three staff training sessions with prompt cards and intranet guides, dedicated porter slots and fast-track radiology queue with hot reporting, early SAU/CDU transfers.
setting: Emergency department, Lister Hospital, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust (district general hospital)
cycle1_result: Median urine dip turnaround 144 min, CT-KUB request 166 min, CT report 124 min; RCEM four-hour compliance 16.7% (19/114); calcium tested 50.9% (58/114); urate 0% (0/114); STONE score 5.3% (6/114); repeat CT within 3 months 19.3%; median ED stay 7.5 h.
intervention: 'Straight to CT' pathway with registrar-requested scans, mandatory STONE score prompts in ICE/iRefer requests, three staff training sessions with prompt cards and intranet guides, dedicated porter slots and fast-track radiology queue with hot reporting, early SAU/CDU transfers.

finding: No staff member placed all waste items correctly; commonest score 5/9 (32%); most common error was putting all items in the yellow clinical bin. Of 39 general anaesthetics, sevoflurane used in 30 and desflurane in 7.

cycle1_period: December 2022 for anaesthetic gas review; question sheet date not stated
cycle1_result: No staff member placed all waste items correctly; commonest score 5/9 (32%); most common error was putting all items in the yellow clinical bin. Of 39 general anaesthetics, sevoflurane used in 30 and desflurane in 7.

cycle1_result: 30-day readmission rate 14.2% (4/28), above GIRFT benchmarks; median length of stay 6 days. Causes: blocked catheter/urinary retention, port-site hernia, collection near anastomosis, gastrointestinal symptoms.

title: Quality improvement: enhancing antibiotic stewardship for suspected early onset neonatal infection by refining use of the Kaiser Permanente screening tool and using a CRP threshold of 20 mg/L.
standard: NICE NG195 neonatal infection guideline and Kaiser Permanente Neonatal Infection Calculator (KPNIC); aim to reduce antibiotic initiation and duration in low-risk infants.

setting: Neonatal unit and transitional care unit, University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust (tertiary neonatal service)
cycle1_result: 13% of live births started on antibiotics for suspected EONI in 2018; 12.4% of live births >35 weeks in 2019; 1089 transitional care cefotaxime care days in 2019.
intervention: Five PDSA cycles: CRP threshold raised to 20 mg/L to stop antibiotics at 36 hours in well culture-negative infants ('20 is the new 10'); GBS-positive mothers added to KPNIC; use of KPNIC risk after clinical exam rather than risk at birth; background EONI rate changed to 1/1000; KPNIC extended to 34 weeks. cycle2_result: 6.8% of live births >34 weeks on antibiotics in 2024 and 6.6% in 2025 (to 30 June); transitional care cefotaxime days fell to 270 in 2024 (75% reduction).

standard: Comparison with published outcome/complication rate data from other home parenteral nutrition (HPN) centres and designated intestinal failure units
finding: 121 patient-years (median duration 217.8 days); line sepsis 0.35 episodes/patient-year, line occlusion 0.25, subacute bacterial endocarditis 0.02, cholestasis 0.17, central venous thrombosis 0.03; all within the range of published data.
setting: John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford
cycle1_result: 121 patient-years (median duration 217.8 days); line sepsis 0.35 episodes/patient-year, line occlusion 0.25, subacute bacterial endocarditis 0.02, cholestasis 0.17, central venous thrombosis 0.03; all within the range of published data.
other_findings: Principal indications: Crohn's disease 35.2%, mesenteric infarction 11.4%, surgical complications 17.0%, intestinal motility disorder 10.7%.
authors: Green CJ; Mountford V; Hamilton H; Kettlewell MG; Travis SP
journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
citation: Green CJ, Mountford V, Hamilton H, Kettlewell MG, Travis SP. A 15-year audit of home parenteral nutrition provision at the John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford. QJM. 2008;101(5):365-369. doi:10.1093/qjmed/hcn011. PMID: 18292099.

topic: Familial hypercholesterolaemia management in lipid clinics
title: Are patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia well managed in lipid clinics? An audit of eleven clinics from the Department of Health Familial Hypercholesterolaemia Cascade Testing project.
standard: UK 'Simon Broome' register diagnostic criteria for familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH), and appropriate advice/treatment and family tracing
finding: 79% met Simon Broome criteria for definite/possible FH; 89% on a statin; family pedigree recorded in notes ranged 1-71% (mean 35%) between sites; GP advised to test first-degree relatives in 4-52% (mean 27%); relatives contacted and tested in 6-50% (mean 32%).
setting: 11 NHS Trust lipid clinics, England (Department of Health FH Cascade Testing project)
cycle1_result: 79% met Simon Broome criteria for definite/possible FH; 89% on a statin; family pedigree recorded in notes ranged 1-71% (mean 35%) between sites; GP advised to test first-degree relatives in 4-52% (mean 27%); relatives contacted and tested in 6-50% (mean 32%).
other_findings: FH patients are generally well cared for in lipid clinics in England, but family tracing practice varies widely between clinics.
authors: Hadfield SG; Horara S; Starr BJ; Yazdgerdi S; Bhatnagar D; Cramb R; Egan S; Everdell R; Ferns G; Jones A; Marenah CB; Marples J; Prinsloo P; Sneyd A; Stewart MF; Sandle L; Wang T; Watson MS; Humphries SE
citation: Hadfield SG, Horara S, Starr BJ, Yazdgerdi S, Bhatnagar D, Cramb R, et al.. Are patients with familial hypercholesterolaemia well managed in lipid clinics? An audit of eleven clinics from the Department of Health Familial Hypercholesterolaemia Cascade Testing project. Ann Clin Biochem. 2008;45(Pt 2):199-205. doi:10.1258/acb.2007.007078. PMID: 18325186.

topic: Community services provision for severe arthritis
title: Provision of medical and community services to people with severe arthritis; an audit.
standard: not reported
finding: Patients with RA were referred to hospital far more often than those with OA (only half of OA patients referred); provision of social services/community OT was greater for those seen in hospital; a substantial minority with severe OA had not been considered for joint replacement or had suboptimal provision of aids and adaptations.
setting: Community (identified via social service records), Newcastle upon Tyne
cycle1_result: Patients with RA were referred to hospital far more often than those with OA (only half of OA patients referred); provision of social services/community OT was greater for those seen in hospital; a substantial minority with severe OA had not been considered for joint replacement or had suboptimal provision of aids and adaptations.
other_findings: Joint surgery recipients gained temporary benefit, though disease progression compromised this after several years.
authors: Foster HE; Pyle C; Walker DJ
citation: Foster HE, Pyle C, Walker DJ. Provision of medical and community services to people with severe arthritis; an audit. Br J Rheumatol. 1991;30(5):356-360. doi:10.1093/rheumatology/30.5.356. PMID: 1833021.

title: Quality audit programme for (99m)Tc and (131)I radioactivity measurements with radionuclide calibrators.
standard: Activity measurement accuracy within +/-10% window
finding: 94% of centres were within +/-10% for 131I activity measurement; for 99mTc, 1 of 10 centres deviated by more than +/-10%
setting: Nuclear medicine centres, India
cycle1_result: 94% of centres were within +/-10% for 131I activity measurement; for 99mTc, 1 of 10 centres deviated by more than +/-10%
other_findings: 12th cycle of an ongoing national 131I audit programme; first audit conducted for 99mTc.
authors: Joseph L; Anuradha R; Kulkarni DB
journal: Applied radiation and isotopes : including data, instrumentation and methods for use in agriculture, industry and medicine
citation: Joseph L, Anuradha R, Kulkarni DB. Quality audit programme for (99m)Tc and (131)I radioactivity measurements with radionuclide calibrators. Appl Radiat Isot. 2008;66(6-7):994-997. doi:10.1016/j.apradiso.2008.02.047. PMID: 18346900.

title: National comparative audit of the use of platelet transfusions in the UK.
standard: Audit standards developed from national guidelines for platelet transfusion (documented reason for transfusion, platelet count checked pre-transfusion, appropriate thresholds)
finding: 3726/4421 (84%) transfusions evaluable; 1601/3726 (43%) non-compliant with audit standards; reason documented in 93%; platelet count not measured pre-transfusion in 29%; threshold >10x10^9/L used for 60% of prophylactic haematology transfusions without risk factors; threshold >30x10^9/L used for 59% of prophylactic critical care transfusions; platelet transfusion given without bleeding in 11% of cardiac surgery patients.
change: Recommended written local guidelines for platelet transfusion and clinician training about appropriate use; audit to be repeated in about three years.
setting: 187 UK hospitals (168/263, 64%, in England)
cycle1_result: 3726/4421 (84%) transfusions evaluable; 1601/3726 (43%) non-compliant with audit standards; reason documented in 93%; platelet count not measured pre-transfusion in 29%; threshold >10x10^9/L used for 60% of prophylactic haematology transfusions without risk factors; threshold >30x10^9/L used for 59% of prophylactic critical care transfusions; platelet transfusion given without bleeding in 11% of cardiac surgery patients.
intervention: Recommended written local guidelines for platelet transfusion and clinician training about appropriate use; audit to be repeated in about three years.
other_findings: Reasons for high non-compliance were not explored; more research and more detailed critical care/cardiac surgery guidelines recommended.
authors: Qureshi H; Lowe D; Dobson P; Grant-Casey J; Parris E; Dalton D; Hickling K; Waller F; Howell C; Murphy MF; National Blood Service/Royal College of Physicians National Comparative Audit of Blood Transfusion programme
journal: Transfusion clinique et biologique : journal de la Societe francaise de transfusion sanguine
citation: Qureshi H, Lowe D, Dobson P, Grant-Casey J, Parris E, Dalton D, et al.. National comparative audit of the use of platelet transfusions in the UK. Transfus Clin Biol. 2007;14(6):509-513. doi:10.1016/j.tracli.2008.01.002. PMID: 18359658.

topic: Regional perinatal audit design and evaluation
title: Design and evaluation of a regional perinatal audit.
standard: not reported
finding: Substandard care factors present in 25% of all perinatal death cases; 35% after 23 completed weeks; 52% of intrapartum deaths
setting: Amsterdam hospitals, GPs and independent midwives
cycle1_result: Substandard care factors present in 25% of all perinatal death cases; 35% after 23 completed weeks; 52% of intrapartum deaths
other_findings: External audit panel review was comparable to the regional audit committee's review; audit members felt able to discuss substandard care openly.
authors: Alderliesten ME; Stronks K; Bonsel GJ; Smit BJ; van Campen MM; van Lith JM; Bleker OP
journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
citation: Alderliesten ME, Stronks K, Bonsel GJ, Smit BJ, van Campen MM, van Lith JM, et al.. Design and evaluation of a regional perinatal audit. Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol. 2008;137(2):141-145. doi:10.1016/j.ejogrb.2007.06.002. PMID: 18375264.

topic: Prehospital severe head injury management audit
title: [Audit of the prehospital management of severe head injured patients in the "Pays-de-la-Loire" region].
standard: not reported
finding: Field medical care 54+/-28 min; transport 32+/-29 min; total time to hospital 1h55+/-48min; direct admission to a centre with on-site neurosurgery 68%; mortality before 24th hour 23%
setting: SAMU prehospital emergency services, Pays-de-la-Loire region
cycle1_result: Field medical care 54+/-28 min; transport 32+/-29 min; total time to hospital 1h55+/-48min; direct admission to a centre with on-site neurosurgery 68%; mortality before 24th hour 23%
other_findings: Identified delayed referral to tertiary hospital, limited CT image transmission, absence of mannitol administration, and organisational problems in 21% of cases as targets for improvement.
authors: Bouhours G; Lehousse T; Mylonas J; Lacroix G; Gondret C; Savio C; Couillard C; Beydon L
journal: Annales francaises d'anesthesie et de reanimation
citation: Bouhours G, Lehousse T, Mylonas J, Lacroix G, Gondret C, Savio C, et al.. [Audit of the prehospital management of severe head injured patients in the "Pays-de-la-Loire" region]. Ann Fr Anesth Reanim. 2008;27(5):397-404. doi:10.1016/j.annfar.2008.02.015. PMID: 18423956.

title: UK audit of glomerular filtration rate measurement in 2001.
standard: not reported
finding: Overall root median square (RMedS) variability was 5.8 ml/min/1.73m2 for normalised data, decreasing to 0.6 ml/min/1.73m2 when centres were grouped by analysis method; variability was mainly due to different methods of analysis.
setting: UK centres (national)
cycle1_result: Overall root median square (RMedS) variability was 5.8 ml/min/1.73m2 for normalised data, decreasing to 0.6 ml/min/1.73m2 when centres were grouped by analysis method; variability was mainly due to different methods of analysis.
other_findings: Radionuclide GFR techniques confirmed as method of choice; standardising methodology could dramatically reduce intercentre variability.
authors: Cosgriff PS; Fleming JS; Jarritt PH; Skrypniuk J; Bailey D; Whalley D; Houston A; Burniston M; Blake GM
citation: Cosgriff PS, Fleming JS, Jarritt PH, Skrypniuk J, Bailey D, Whalley D, et al.. UK audit of glomerular filtration rate measurement in 2001. Nucl Med Commun. 2008;29(6):511-520. doi:10.1097/mnm.0b013e3282f813cb. PMID: 18458597.

topic: Blood-borne virus testing and treatment access in prison
title: Audit into blood-borne virus services in Her Majesty's Prison Service.
standard: not reported
finding: Almost a quarter of arrivals had contact with blood-borne virus (BBV) services; 75.4% reported IV drug use history; 20% of these declined testing; average time from imprisonment to testing was 86 days (halved since October 2006); 50% positive for hepatitis C antibody, 83.3% of these had active virus; average 38 days from testing to referral; all tested for HIV were negative.
setting: Women's prison, north of England (179 prisoners)
cycle1_result: Almost a quarter of arrivals had contact with blood-borne virus (BBV) services; 75.4% reported IV drug use history; 20% of these declined testing; average time from imprisonment to testing was 86 days (halved since October 2006); 50% positive for hepatitis C antibody, 83.3% of these had active virus; average 38 days from testing to referral; all tested for HIV were negative.
other_findings: Efficiency improvements are needed if prisoners are to access BBV services promptly while incarcerated.
authors: Murray E; Jones D
citation: Murray E, Jones D. Audit into blood-borne virus services in Her Majesty's Prison Service. Int J STD AIDS. 2008;19(5):347-348. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2007.007205. PMID: 18482968.

title: Basics in advanced life support: a role for download audit and metronomes.
standard: 2005 Resuscitation Guidelines emphasis on chest compressions, monitored via electronic ECG/CPR download analysis
finding: Deficiencies in the standard of basic life support were identified, though not unique to this service.
change: Introduction of metronomes and provision of feedback to ambulance crews based on download audit.
setting: One UK ambulance service (South East Coast Ambulance Trust)
cycle1_result: Deficiencies in the standard of basic life support were identified, though not unique to this service.
intervention: Introduction of metronomes and provision of feedback to ambulance crews based on download audit.
cycle2_result: Major improvements in basic life support performance following introduction of metronomes and crew feedback (no numeric data reported).
other_findings: A planned multicentre UK trial of compressions before/after defibrillation could not proceed due to informed consent concerns, so the new protocol was introduced in a single service instead.
authors: Fletcher D; Galloway R; Chamberlain D; Pateman J; Bryant G; Newcombe RG
citation: Fletcher D, Galloway R, Chamberlain D, Pateman J, Bryant G, Newcombe RG. Basics in advanced life support: a role for download audit and metronomes. Resuscitation. 2008;78(2):127-134. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2008.03.003. PMID: 18486301.

topic: Radiology reporting turnaround time and productivity
title: Picture archiving and communication systems lead to sustained improvements in reporting times and productivity: results of a 5-year audit.
standard: Internal baseline reporting time and productivity metrics compared before and after PACS installation
finding: Baseline reporting time: plain radiographs 6.8 days, specialist modalities (CT/MRI/ultrasound/nuclear medicine) 4.1 days; patient episodes 11,531/month; 32 whole-time-equivalent (WTE) reporting radiologists.
change: Introduction of picture archiving and communication system (PACS) and digital dictation.
setting: Large teaching hospital, St George's Hospital NHS Trust, London
cycle1_result: Baseline reporting time: plain radiographs 6.8 days, specialist modalities (CT/MRI/ultrasound/nuclear medicine) 4.1 days; patient episodes 11,531/month; 32 whole-time-equivalent (WTE) reporting radiologists.
intervention: Introduction of picture archiving and communication system (PACS) and digital dictation.
cycle2_result: Plain radiograph reporting time decreased 26% (6.8 to 5 days, p=0.002); specialty modality reporting time decreased 24% (4.1 to 3.1 days); productivity improved 18%; patient episodes increased 30% to 15,057/month with WTE radiologists up 15% to 37.
other_findings: Sustained improvements reflect the efficiencies and cultural change accompanying PACS introduction.
authors: Mackinnon AD; Billington RA; Adam EJ; Dundas DD; Patel U
citation: Mackinnon AD, Billington RA, Adam EJ, Dundas DD, Patel U. Picture archiving and communication systems lead to sustained improvements in reporting times and productivity: results of a 5-year audit. Clin Radiol. 2008;63(7):796-804. doi:10.1016/j.crad.2007.12.015. PMID: 18555038.

title: Two year audit of perinatal mortality at Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital.
standard: not reported
finding: Perinatal mortality rate 30.7/1000; extended perinatal mortality rate 47.9/1000
change: Improvements in care of mothers and newborns; standard perinatal death audit forms used
setting: Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital
cycle1_result: Perinatal mortality rate 30.7/1000; extended perinatal mortality rate 47.9/1000
intervention: Improvements in care of mothers and newborns; standard perinatal death audit forms used
cycle2_n: 1517 total births (22 stillbirths, 10 early neonatal deaths)
cycle2_result: Significant reduction in perinatal mortality rate compared with the earlier one-year study, despite increased births
other_findings: Deaths classified using Wigglesworth's classification; emphasises antenatal care and neonatal intensive care.
authors: Shrestha M; Manandhar DS; Dhakal S; Nepal N
citation: Shrestha M, Manandhar DS, Dhakal S, Nepal N. Two year audit of perinatal mortality at Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital. Kathmandu Univ Med J (KUMJ). 2006;4(2):176-181. PMID: 18603894.

topic: Physical intervention use and injury rates in brain injury unit
title: Physical interventions to manage patients with brain injury: an audit on its use and staff and patient injuries from the techniques.
standard: not reported
finding: Physical interventions (PI) used on 1427 occasions; 90.1% lasted less than 10 minutes; patient injury rate 0.98%; staff injury rate 6.5%, both considerably lower than rates reported for other clinical populations.
setting: Neurobehavioural unit, St Andrews Healthcare, Northampton
cycle1_result: Physical interventions (PI) used on 1427 occasions; 90.1% lasted less than 10 minutes; patient injury rate 0.98%; staff injury rate 6.5%, both considerably lower than rates reported for other clinical populations.
other_findings: A multidisciplinary approach, including physiotherapist input, is credited with the comparatively low injury rates.
authors: Stubbs B; Alderman N
citation: Stubbs B, Alderman N. Physical interventions to manage patients with brain injury: an audit on its use and staff and patient injuries from the techniques. Brain Inj. 2008;22(9):691-696. doi:10.1080/02699050802270022. PMID: 18698519.

title: Departmental audit of malaria control programme 2001-2005 north west frontier province (NWFP).
standard: Roll Back Malaria (RBM) initiative strategy targets
finding: Budget fell from Rs 5.043 million (2002) to Rs 3.3 million (2005); slides examined increased 62% from 2001 to 2005; annual parasite incidence peaked at 3.01-3.57/1000 in 2002-2003 then fell to 2.01/1000 in 2005 (double the 2001 rate of 1.09/1000)
setting: Malaria Control Programme, North West Frontier Province
cycle1_result: Budget fell from Rs 5.043 million (2002) to Rs 3.3 million (2005); slides examined increased 62% from 2001 to 2005; annual parasite incidence peaked at 3.01-3.57/1000 in 2002-2003 then fell to 2.01/1000 in 2005 (double the 2001 rate of 1.09/1000)
other_findings: Provincial commitment to RBM strategy was not matched by resources; no evidence of feedback or dissemination of data to districts.
authors: Asif SA
journal: Journal of Ayub Medical College, Abbottabad : JAMC
citation: Asif SA. Departmental audit of malaria control programme 2001-2005 north west frontier province (NWFP). J Ayub Med Coll Abbottabad. 2008;20(1):98-102. PMID: 19024199.

topic: Acute poisoning patient assessment and management quality
title: Improvement in the management of acutely poisoned patients using an electronic database, prospective audit and targeted educational intervention.
standard: Predefined criteria for clinical assessment and management of acutely poisoned patients, derived from identified shortfalls
finding: 77.6% of poisoned-patient presentations had clinical management graded as 'good'.
change: Bimonthly audit meetings; targeted educational lectures and case-based clinical scenarios; weekly case-based anonymised electronic feedback reports sent to ED staff caring for poisoned patients.
setting: Emergency department, tertiary-level inner-city London teaching hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' Poisons Unit)
cycle1_result: 77.6% of poisoned-patient presentations had clinical management graded as 'good'.
intervention: Bimonthly audit meetings; targeted educational lectures and case-based clinical scenarios; weekly case-based anonymised electronic feedback reports sent to ED staff caring for poisoned patients.
cycle2_result: Proportion of presentations graded as 'good' management significantly increased to 89.4%.
other_findings: An electronic clinical toxicology database enabled systematic collection and review of information to design and implement the educational interventions.
authors: Greene SL; Wood DM; Gawarammana IB; Warren-Gash C; Drake N; Jones AL; Dargan PI
citation: Greene SL, Wood DM, Gawarammana IB, Warren-Gash C, Drake N, Jones AL, et al.. Improvement in the management of acutely poisoned patients using an electronic database, prospective audit and targeted educational intervention. Postgrad Med J. 2008;84(997):603-608. doi:10.1136/pgmj.2007.066043. PMID: 19103819.

title: An audit of vaccination coverage among vaccination service workers in Puglia, Italy.
standard: Recommended vaccinations for healthcare workers (hepatitis B, influenza, varicella, MMR)
finding: 54.5% had received hepatitis B vaccine and 32.7% influenza vaccine (2007-08 season); 4.6% susceptible to varicella (2.6% vaccinated); 9.3% susceptible to measles/mumps/rubella (5.9% vaccinated)
setting: Apulian Vaccination Services, Puglia Region
cycle1_result: 54.5% had received hepatitis B vaccine and 32.7% influenza vaccine (2007-08 season); 4.6% susceptible to varicella (2.6% vaccinated); 9.3% susceptible to measles/mumps/rubella (5.9% vaccinated)
other_findings: Identifies need for ongoing education about vaccine requirements among healthcare workers.
authors: Tafuri S; Martinelli D; Caputi G; Arbore A; Lopalco PL; Germinario C; Prato R
citation: Tafuri S, Martinelli D, Caputi G, Arbore A, Lopalco PL, Germinario C, et al.. An audit of vaccination coverage among vaccination service workers in Puglia, Italy. Am J Infect Control. 2009;37(5):414-416. doi:10.1016/j.ajic.2008.10.030. PMID: 19216005.

title: Maternal mortality: an autopsy audit.
standard: not reported
finding: Maternal mortality rate 1133/100,000 live births; acute fulminant viral hepatitis was the commonest indirect cause of death (41.5%); pregnancy-induced hypertension 13.4%; puerperal sepsis 11.2%
setting: Tertiary care hospital, T N Medical College, Mumbai
cycle1_result: Maternal mortality rate 1133/100,000 live births; acute fulminant viral hepatitis was the commonest indirect cause of death (41.5%); pregnancy-induced hypertension 13.4%; puerperal sepsis 11.2%
other_findings: Fallacies identified in the autopsy process; recommends emphasis on clinicopathologic correlation and microbiological studies.
authors: Jashnani KD; Rupani AB; Wani RJ
citation: Jashnani KD, Rupani AB, Wani RJ. Maternal mortality: an autopsy audit. J Postgrad Med. 2009;55(1):12-16. doi:10.4103/0022-3859.48435. PMID: 19242072.

title: Audit from preschool developmental surveillance of vision, hearing, and language referrals.
standard: not reported
finding: Median waiting time for appointment: ophthalmology 46 days, audiology 175 days, speech therapy 83 days; poorest attendance rate in speech therapy (75%); approximately 60% of ophthalmology referrals were justified and 20% had a clear defect; 55% of audiology referrals had altered impedance or hearing impairment (only half of those under review improved spontaneously); 80% of speech therapy assessments found a language problem.
setting: Inner city area, preschool medical examinations
cycle1_result: Median waiting time for appointment: ophthalmology 46 days, audiology 175 days, speech therapy 83 days; poorest attendance rate in speech therapy (75%); approximately 60% of ophthalmology referrals were justified and 20% had a clear defect; 55% of audiology referrals had altered impedance or hearing impairment (only half of those under review improved spontaneously); 80% of speech therapy assessments found a language problem.
other_findings: Many health problems were detected that parents were unaware of or did not use services for; organisational changes suggested to improve service effectiveness.
authors: Rona RJ; Reynolds A; Allsop M; Morris RW; Morgan M; Mandalia S
citation: Rona RJ, Reynolds A, Allsop M, Morris RW, Morgan M, Mandalia S. Audit from preschool developmental surveillance of vision, hearing, and language referrals. Arch Dis Child. 1991;66(8):921-926. doi:10.1136/adc.66.8.921. PMID: 1929488.

topic: Forensic competency assessment audit for rape survivors with intellectual disability
title: An audit of competency assessments on court-referred rape survivors in South Africa.
standard: not reported
finding: 91.5% female, 21.7% under 16 years old; ~80% classified with moderate or severe mental retardation; over 90% were judged able to testify; almost two-thirds unable to make an informed decision to consent to sexual intercourse
setting: Court-referred forensic mental health service
cycle1_result: 91.5% female, 21.7% under 16 years old; ~80% classified with moderate or severe mental retardation; over 90% were judged able to testify; almost two-thirds unable to make an informed decision to consent to sexual intercourse
other_findings: Intended to inform quality improvement in forensic mental health assessment of vulnerable rape survivors.
authors: Pillay AL
citation: Pillay AL. An audit of competency assessments on court-referred rape survivors in South Africa. Psychol Rep. 2008;103(3):764-770. doi:10.2466/pr0.103.3.764-770. PMID: 19320210.

title: Interhospital transport audit criteria for helicopter emergency medical services.
standard: Nationally established criteria for medically appropriate helicopter interhospital transport
finding: 97% (1792/1839) of interhospital transfers judged justified for helicopter transport per national criteria
setting: Connecticut LIFE STAR helicopter emergency medical service
cycle1_result: 97% (1792/1839) of interhospital transfers judged justified for helicopter transport per national criteria
other_findings: Additional acceptable transport criteria developed following panel review of 401 flights not meeting existing criteria.
authors: Gabram SG; Stohler S; Sargent RK; Schwartz RJ; Jacobs LM
citation: Gabram SG, Stohler S, Sargent RK, Schwartz RJ, Jacobs LM. Interhospital transport audit criteria for helicopter emergency medical services. Conn Med. 1991;55(7):387-392. PMID: 1935060.

title: UK National Audit of Sexual History-taking: case-notes audit.
standard: National guidelines for sexual history-taking in genitourinary medicine clinics
finding: A high proportion of case-notes were completely legible; considerable inter-regional variation in adherence to national guidelines, particularly for documentation of discussing condom use, HIV risk assessment, offer of a chaperone, assessment for hepatitis B vaccination and hepatitis C testing, and sexual contact issues (percentages not given in this abstract).
setting: Genitourinary medicine clinics, UK (national)
cycle1_result: A high proportion of case-notes were completely legible; considerable inter-regional variation in adherence to national guidelines, particularly for documentation of discussing condom use, HIV risk assessment, offer of a chaperone, assessment for hepatitis B vaccination and hepatitis C testing, and sexual contact issues (percentages not given in this abstract).
other_findings: Data were aggregated by region and clinic to allow comparison to national averages and guidelines.
authors: Carne C; McClean H; Bhaduri S; Gokhale R; Sethi G; Daniels D; National Audit Group of the British Association for Sexual Health and HIV
citation: Carne C, McClean H, Bhaduri S, Gokhale R, Sethi G, Daniels D, et al.. UK National Audit of Sexual History-taking: case-notes audit. Int J STD AIDS. 2009;20(5):351-354. doi:10.1258/ijsa.2009.009057. PMID: 19386974.

title: Perinatal audit using the 3-delays model in western Tanzania.
standard: 3-delays model methodology
finding: Perinatal mortality rate 38/1000; first delay occurred in 19.0% of cases, second delay in 21.5%, third delay in 72.5%; leading causes birth asphyxia (19.0%) and prolonged/obstructed labour (18.5%)
setting: Regional hospital, Kigoma, western Tanzania
cycle1_result: Perinatal mortality rate 38/1000; first delay occurred in 19.0% of cases, second delay in 21.5%, third delay in 72.5%; leading causes birth asphyxia (19.0%) and prolonged/obstructed labour (18.5%)
other_findings: Most substandard care occurred after admission to the health facility (third delay), suggesting institutional care improvements could reduce mortality.
authors: Mbaruku G; van Roosmalen J; Kimondo I; Bilango F; Bergström S
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
citation: Mbaruku G, van Roosmalen J, Kimondo I, Bilango F, Bergström S. Perinatal audit using the 3-delays model in western Tanzania. Int J Gynaecol Obstet. 2009;106(1):85-88. doi:10.1016/j.ijgo.2009.04.008. PMID: 19439297.

title: Decreasing trends in malnutrition prevalence rates explained by regular audits and feedback.
standard: Dutch National Prevalence Measurement of Care Problems (LPZ) malnutrition indicators
finding: Malnutrition prevalence rates in 2004 formed the baseline of a decreasing trend to 2007 in hospitals and home care; rates remained stable in nursing homes
change: Annual multicentre audit and feedback from the national LPZ measurement; participation in national improvement programmes
setting: Dutch hospitals, nursing homes and home care organisations (national LPZ prevalence measurement)
cycle1_n: 80 hospitals, 141 nursing homes, 48 home care organisations
cycle1_result: Malnutrition prevalence rates in 2004 formed the baseline of a decreasing trend to 2007 in hospitals and home care; rates remained stable in nursing homes
intervention: Annual multicentre audit and feedback from the national LPZ measurement; participation in national improvement programmes
cycle2_result: More frequent LPZ audit participation was associated with lower malnutrition prevalence (P<0.001); participation in national improvement programmes also reduced prevalence (P=0.027)
other_findings: Prevalence rates remained stable in nursing homes despite decreases seen in hospitals and home care organisations.
authors: Meijers JM; Candel MJ; Schols JM; van Bokhorst-de van der Schueren MA; Halfens RJ
citation: Meijers JM, Candel MJ, Schols JM, van Bokhorst-de van der Schueren MA, Halfens RJ. Decreasing trends in malnutrition prevalence rates explained by regular audits and feedback. J Nutr. 2009;139(7):1381-1386. doi:10.3945/jn.108.102608. PMID: 19494024.

title: Audit of post-exposure treatment to prevent lyssavirus infection in Sydney South West Area Health Service, 2005-2007.
standard: NSW Health post-exposure prophylaxis protocol for lyssavirus
finding: 76% of potential exposures occurred overseas; all people who commenced post-exposure treatment completed the prescribed course, but often not within the stipulated timeframe
setting: Sydney South West Area Health Service
cycle1_result: 76% of potential exposures occurred overseas; all people who commenced post-exposure treatment completed the prescribed course, but often not within the stipulated timeframe
other_findings: The animal's survival or health status was often not routinely recorded.
authors: Craig AT; Mannes TF; Gupta L
journal: New South Wales public health bulletin
citation: Craig AT, Mannes TF, Gupta L. Audit of post-exposure treatment to prevent lyssavirus infection in Sydney South West Area Health Service, 2005-2007. N S W Public Health Bull. 2009;20(5-6):86-89. doi:10.1071/nb07124. PMID: 19552855.

topic: Blood conservation strategy audit in cardiac surgery
title: Multi-modality blood conservation strategy in open-heart surgery: an audit.
standard: In-house blood conservation protocol for open-heart surgery

topic: Refractory status epilepticus treatment practice (global registry)
title: Preliminary results of the global audit of treatment of refractory status epilepticus.
standard: Current guidelines for status epilepticus first-line treatment
finding: First-line treatment was often delayed and not in line with current guidelines; midazolam was the most widely used first-choice anaesthetic (59%), followed by propofol and barbiturates; seizure control achieved in 74% of patients; 22% died during treatment and 4% had treatment actively withdrawn; neurological outcome good in 36%, poor in 39.3%, and 25% died in hospital.
setting: Multinational online registry, 44 countries
cycle1_result: First-line treatment was often delayed and not in line with current guidelines; midazolam was the most widely used first-choice anaesthetic (59%), followed by propofol and barbiturates; seizure control achieved in 74% of patients; 22% died during treatment and 4% had treatment actively withdrawn; neurological outcome good in 36%, poor in 39.3%, and 25% died in hospital.
other_findings: Younger age, history of epilepsy, and fewer different anaesthetics tried were associated with a better outcome.
authors: Ferlisi M; Hocker S; Grade M; Trinka E; Shorvon S; International Steering Committee of the StEp Audit
citation: Ferlisi M, Hocker S, Grade M, Trinka E, Shorvon S, International Steering Committee of the StEp Audit. Preliminary results of the global audit of treatment of refractory status epilepticus. Epilepsy Behav. 2015;49:318-324. doi:10.1016/j.yebeh.2015.04.010. PMID: 25952268.

title: A 23 years audit of packed red blood cell consumption in a university hospital in a developing country.
standard: Crossmatch:transfusion ratio as an indicator of appropriate blood ordering practice
finding: Grand total packed red blood cell consumption was 345,642 units over 23 years, peaking in 1994 then dropping 30.4% by 6 years later before rising again; the crossmatch:transfusion ratio revealed gross over-ordering and wastage of blood bank resources in most divisions, most notably Obstetrics and Gynaecology
change: Implementation of strict blood ordering guidelines, alongside heightened concern about transfusion-transmitted infection (e.g. HIV), contributed to reduced overuse of blood products
setting: 850-bed university teaching hospital
cycle1_result: Grand total packed red blood cell consumption was 345,642 units over 23 years, peaking in 1994 then dropping 30.4% by 6 years later before rising again; the crossmatch:transfusion ratio revealed gross over-ordering and wastage of blood bank resources in most divisions, most notably Obstetrics and Gynaecology
intervention: Implementation of strict blood ordering guidelines, alongside heightened concern about transfusion-transmitted infection (e.g. HIV), contributed to reduced overuse of blood products
other_findings: Consumption trends varied by department: Paediatrics showed continued decline in consumption, while the Renal Dialysis Unit had minimal use due to erythropoietin therapy.

journal: Transfusion and apheresis science : official journal of the World Apheresis Association : official journal of the European Society for Haemapheresis

topic: Resident self-reported versus independent chart audit accuracy for guideline adherence

standard: 16 US Preventive Services Task Force primary care guidelines

cycle1_result: Self-reported guideline compliance was 82%, significantly higher than the 68% found on independent external audit of 70 randomly selected charts
other_findings: Residents' self-reported chart audits significantly overestimated guideline adherence; increased supervision and independent review are recommended to accurately evaluate resident performance.

title: Audit of workplace walkability in an Irish healthcare setting.
standard: US Centre for Disease Control (CDC) Healthier Worksite Initiative Walkability Audit Tool
finding: 20 walking segments audited; campus scored medium risk to walkability overall on the CDC tool; staff survey (20% response, 151 respondents) found 66% sat at their desk for most of the day, with the majority sitting 5-7 hours a day.
setting: Hospital-based administrative campus, Ireland
cycle1_result: 20 walking segments audited; campus scored medium risk to walkability overall on the CDC tool; staff survey (20% response, 151 respondents) found 66% sat at their desk for most of the day, with the majority sitting 5-7 hours a day.

standard: Best Practice in General Surgery Management of Acute Pancreatitis Guideline
finding: 22.6% had only serum lipase tested for biochemical diagnosis; admission ultrasound performed in 70.2% (27.8% also had CT); 80.6% of non-ICU patients kept nil per os; only 34.6% of ICU patients received enteral nutrition (starting an average of 7.5 days post-admission); prophylactic antibiotics given to 25.5% of non-ICU and 48.1% of ICU patients; only 22.6% with gallstone pancreatitis had index admission cholecystectomy; ERCP with sphincterotomy was under-used (31% of biliary obstruction cases, 22% of prophylactic candidates)
setting: 8 university-affiliated hospitals
cycle1_result: 22.6% had only serum lipase tested for biochemical diagnosis; admission ultrasound performed in 70.2% (27.8% also had CT); 80.6% of non-ICU patients kept nil per os; only 34.6% of ICU patients received enteral nutrition (starting an average of 7.5 days post-admission); prophylactic antibiotics given to 25.5% of non-ICU and 48.1% of ICU patients; only 22.6% with gallstone pancreatitis had index admission cholecystectomy; ERCP with sphincterotomy was under-used (31% of biliary obstruction cases, 22% of prophylactic candidates)
