standard: Local target: 100% use of the VIP scoring tool on the oncology ward
finding: Under 30% of cannulas were properly documented and assessed using VIP scoring
change: Three PDSA cycles: junior doctor education (presentations/posters), then bedside intentional rounding charts giving ready access to the VIP tool
setting: Oncology ward, Castle Hill Hospital, Hull and East Yorkshire NHS Trust
cycle1_result: Under 30% of cannulas were properly documented and assessed using VIP scoring
intervention: Three PDSA cycles: junior doctor education (presentations/posters), then bedside intentional rounding charts giving ready access to the VIP tool

cycle2_result: Compliance rose to around 80% by end of second PDSA cycle and reached 100% by end of third cycle
other_findings: Compliance fluctuated between interventions (rose then fell) before the bedside chart intervention achieved sustained 100% compliance.

finding: Blood investigations (haemoglobin, ferritin, CRP) lagged relative to pre/post infusion timing requirements

cycle2_result: 100% adherence to investigations done prior to infusion; improved compliance and adherence, with prevention of over-treatment with iron infusion
other_findings: Nursing decision-making became more independent, freeing doctor time; one PDSA cycle identified a patient who could have received less iron.
authors: Nuti A

cycle1_result: 22/34 patients (65%) were fasted, with 43 fasting episodes and a median fasting time of 13.5 hours; fasting exceeded the 6-hour guideline on 40 of 43 occasions; 97% of patients were malnourished

topic: Paediatric grommet 'rapid turnover' list waiting times and cancellations
title: Introducing paediatric grommet "rapid turnover" lists. A Quality Improvement Project.
standard: NICE CG60 criteria for grommet insertion; NHS 18-week referral-to-treatment (RTT) target
finding: 78% of children breached the 18-week RTT target; average wait 90 days; 8% on-the-day cancellations; 38% had audiograms older than 90 days; only 5.8 grommet cases completed per list
change: Introduction of 'rapid turnover' paediatric day case theatre lists with a pre-operative consent clinic and dual anaesthetic pods
setting: Otolaryngology (ENT) department, Derriford Hospital, Plymouth
cycle1_period: preceding 2 years (Nov 2013-Nov 2015); 6 months Jan-Jul 2015 for RTT
cycle1_result: 78% of children breached the 18-week RTT target; average wait 90 days; 8% on-the-day cancellations; 38% had audiograms older than 90 days; only 5.8 grommet cases completed per list
intervention: Introduction of 'rapid turnover' paediatric day case theatre lists with a pre-operative consent clinic and dual anaesthetic pods

standard: National drug regulations for required product information leaflet content; British National Formulary and/or Australian Medicines Handbook for clinical fact compatibility
finding: 28% of product information leaflets were missing at least one essential required item (commonly pharmacokinetics, treatment duration, overdose and special dosage information); of 900 cross-matched clinical information items, 80 (8.9%) were partially compatible and 8 (0.9%) totally incompatible with reference sources; 48% of leaflets had at least one incompatibility

standard: Published NAP6/BSACI guidance on investigation of perioperative anaphylaxis, compared with a prior NAP6 baseline clinic survey

other_findings: Recommends dynamic tryptase evaluation and standardised clinic reports; communication/information provision for patients was insufficient.

topic: Institutional standardisation of distal pancreatectomy care
title: Clinical impact of developing better practices at the institutional level on surgical outcomes after distal pancreatectomy in 1515 patients: Domestic audit of the Japanese Society of Pancreatic Surgery.
standard: Institutional standardisation defined as implementing ≥6 of 11 departmental quality initiatives (Japanese Society of Pancreatic Surgery domestic audit)
finding: Standardised institutions had lower severe complications (22% vs 29%), lower clinically relevant pancreatic fistula (22% vs 31%, p<0.05); proportion of patients treated at standardised institutions rose from 16.5% (2006) to 46.4% (2014)

cycle1_result: Standardised institutions had lower severe complications (22% vs 29%), lower clinically relevant pancreatic fistula (22% vs 31%, p<0.05); proportion of patients treated at standardised institutions rose from 16.5% (2006) to 46.4% (2014)
other_findings: Multivariate analysis found pancreatic texture, drain management and surgical factors, but not standardisation itself, independently predicted complications.

title: Emergency inserted peripheral intravenous catheters: a quality improvement project.
standard: Local Queensland guideline recommending removal or replacement of ambulance/emergency inserted peripheral intravenous catheters within 24 hours
finding: Routine clinical audits demonstrated a delay in removing ambulance/emergency inserted PIVCs beyond acceptable dwell times; these catheters were not being recognised by ward staff as requiring removal
change: Key stakeholder engagement, roll-out of a sticker to identify ambulance/emergency inserted PIVCs, and education of ward staff

intervention: Key stakeholder engagement, roll-out of a sticker to identify ambulance/emergency inserted PIVCs, and education of ward staff

title: An audit of healthcare provision in internally displaced population camps in Nigeria.
standard: Sphere minimum standards in humanitarian crises
finding: 5 of 15 assessed standards met to some extent (including water and shelter availability); sanitation and vaccination unmet in five camps; severe overcrowding in five camps; inadequate waste disposal in all camps.
setting: Nine internally displaced person camps across seven states
cycle1_result: 5 of 15 assessed standards met to some extent (including water and shelter availability); sanitation and vaccination unmet in five camps; severe overcrowding in five camps; inadequate waste disposal in all camps.
other_findings: Health programme implementation was uneven and especially poor in self-settled and dispersed settlements.
authors: Ekezie W; Timmons S; Myles P; Siebert P; Bains M; Pritchard C

topic: Episiotomy rate and perineal outcome audit after educational intervention
title: Perineal outcome following educational intervention: a retrospective audit of primiparous women.
standard: Agreed standards for episiotomy use to reduce postpartum pelvic floor dysfunction
finding: Overall 30% had an intact perineum, 51% a spontaneous tear, and 19% an episiotomy; where the accoucheur was an obstetrician or obstetric registrar, the baseline episiotomy rate was 56%
change: A teaching session on pelvic floor anatomy, the impact of vaginal delivery on pelvic floor dysfunction, and relevant local/international research, delivered by the Head of Urogynaecology
setting: Tertiary hospitals
cycle1_result: Overall 30% had an intact perineum, 51% a spontaneous tear, and 19% an episiotomy; where the accoucheur was an obstetrician or obstetric registrar, the baseline episiotomy rate was 56%
intervention: A teaching session on pelvic floor anatomy, the impact of vaginal delivery on pelvic floor dysfunction, and relevant local/international research, delivered by the Head of Urogynaecology
cycle2_result: No significant overall change in episiotomy rates (p=.17); however, the episiotomy rate rose from 56% to 70% (p<.01) when the accoucheur was an obstetrician or obstetric registrar, while the midwife-led rate changed minimally (11% to 18%, p=.27)
other_findings: Feedback about a provider's own practice patterns can change behaviour to conform with agreed standards; a wide baseline variation in episiotomy use (9-100%) has been reported in the literature.
authors: Rikard-Bell J; Iyer J; Rane A
journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
citation: Rikard-Bell J, Iyer J, Rane A. Perineal outcome following educational intervention: a retrospective audit of primiparous women. J Obstet Gynaecol. 2019;39(1):36-40. doi:10.1080/01443615.2018.1462776. PMID: 30207494.

topic: Pre-operative lymphoscintigram use before sentinel node biopsy
title: Are pre-operative lymphoscintigrams needed for localization prior to sentinel node biopsy?: An audit to ensure safe practice and to provide another view.
standard: Local standard: reported node count and biopsied node count concordance to ensure safe sentinel node biopsy localisation without preoperative lymphoscintigraphy (no external guideline target stated)
finding: Reported node count vs biopsied node count showed only fair agreement (Cohen's kappa 0.34, 95% CI 0.195-0.482); reported node count was zero in two cases but sentinel node biopsy still succeeded; 90% of lymphoscintigrams performed on day of surgery.
change: Lymphoscintigraphy discontinued before sentinel node biopsy to reduce delay to theatre and demand on Nuclear Medicine
setting: Breast Care Unit, Torbay and South Devon NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: Reported node count vs biopsied node count showed only fair agreement (Cohen's kappa 0.34, 95% CI 0.195-0.482); reported node count was zero in two cases but sentinel node biopsy still succeeded; 90% of lymphoscintigrams performed on day of surgery.
intervention: Lymphoscintigraphy discontinued before sentinel node biopsy to reduce delay to theatre and demand on Nuclear Medicine
cycle2_result: Biopsied node count range 0-4 (mean 1.80); two cases of failed localisation; no significant difference in biopsied node count with vs without scans (p=0.16); sentinel node positivity 36% (with scan) vs 25.3% (without), not significant (p=0.11).
other_findings: Removing lymphoscintigram gives cost savings, saved clinical time and frees the scanner for other imaging.
authors: Ives C; Gregg L; Trust C; Green M
citation: Ives C, Gregg L, Trust C, Green M. Are pre-operative lymphoscintigrams needed for localization prior to sentinel node biopsy?: An audit to ensure safe practice and to provide another view. Lymphology. 2018;51(1):13-17. PMID: 30248727.

standard: not reported

title: The incidence of post-thyroidectomy hypocalcaemia: a retrospective single-centre audit.
standard: not reported

title: 2015 UK software audit of hepatobiliary scintigraphy.
standard: Recommended acquisition of 60 minutes after fatty stimulus (used for normal range references) and fatty stimulus content of at least 10 g, with motion correction applied
finding: Only 48.1% of centres acquired for 60 minutes after stimulus as recommended; 13.5% administered fatty stimuli below the recommended 10 g; 25% of participants did not use motion correction, which could change gallbladder ejection fraction substantially (e.g. from 44% to 9% in one dataset).
setting: 52 UK hospitals
cycle1_result: Only 48.1% of centres acquired for 60 minutes after stimulus as recommended; 13.5% administered fatty stimuli below the recommended 10 g; 25% of participants did not use motion correction, which could change gallbladder ejection fraction substantially (e.g. from 44% to 9% in one dataset).
other_findings: Widespread variation in GBEF normal ranges found; time acquired after stimulus (20-70 min) was the largest contributor to GBEF variation.
authors: O'Shaughnessy ER; Murray A; Taylor JC; Barnfield M; Cullis J; Cade S; Kenny B; Carson KJ; Towey DJ; White D; Institute of Physics and Engineering in Medicine, Nuclear Medicine Software Quality Group

topic: Hospital malnutrition and early oral nutrition supplement delivery
title: Combating hospital malnutrition: Dietitian-led quality improvement initiative.
standard: not reported
finding: Early delivery of ONS within 6h (EDONS) was 10%; delayed delivery (>24h) was 40%; ONS prescription rate 2%.
change: Sensitisation of clinical dietitians (Phase 2) followed by formation of a multidisciplinary team (MDT) coalition to improve timely ONS delivery (Phase 3)
setting: Tertiary care hospital, liver transplant service included
cycle1_period: Phase 1, part of December 2015 to February 2017
cycle1_result: Early delivery of ONS within 6h (EDONS) was 10%; delayed delivery (>24h) was 40%; ONS prescription rate 2%.
intervention: Sensitisation of clinical dietitians (Phase 2) followed by formation of a multidisciplinary team (MDT) coalition to improve timely ONS delivery (Phase 3)
cycle2_period: Phase 3, part of December 2015 to February 2017
cycle2_result: EDONS rose to 44.6%, delayed delivery (>24h) fell to 8.4%, ONS prescription rose to 16% (p=0.000); length of stay fell from 6.82 to 5.60 days (p=0.010).
other_findings: Phase 2 (n=428) showed intermediate improvement (EDONS 16.1%, ONS 13%); EDONS was the only factor independently reducing length of stay; non-ONS patients had higher readmission (72% vs 26%).
authors: Lovesley D; Parasuraman R; Ramamurthy A
citation: Lovesley D, Parasuraman R, Ramamurthy A. Combating hospital malnutrition: Dietitian-led quality improvement initiative. Clin Nutr ESPEN. 2019;30:19-25. doi:10.1016/j.clnesp.2019.02.011. PMID: 30904220.

standard: not reported (local programme encouraging immunisation against pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib infection in asplenic patients since 1992, plus issue of an 'alert' card)
finding: Vaccine uptake: pneumococcal 91%, meningococcal 80%, Hib 79%; 23% advised prophylactic antibiotics immediately post-splenectomy; 9% taking prophylaxis at time of analysis; alert cards distributed to 88% of eligible patients; 34 different antibiotic regimens recommended for adults.
setting: General practices, South Buckinghamshire, UK
cycle1_result: Vaccine uptake: pneumococcal 91%, meningococcal 80%, Hib 79%; 23% advised prophylactic antibiotics immediately post-splenectomy; 9% taking prophylaxis at time of analysis; alert cards distributed to 88% of eligible patients; 34 different antibiotic regimens recommended for adults.
other_findings: Highlighted wide variation in antibiotic prophylaxis recommendations and need for national guidelines.
authors: MacInnes J; Waghorn DJ; Haworth E
citation: MacInnes J, Waghorn DJ, Haworth E. Management of asplenic patients in South Buckinghamshire: an audit of local practice. Commun Dis Rep CDR Rev. 1995;5(12):R173-7. PMID: 8541937.

topic: Diagnostic concordance between referral and explant pathology in lung transplantation
title: Audit of referral and explant diagnoses in lung transplantation: a pathologic study of lungs removed for parenchymal disease.
standard: Quality indicator: concordance between pre-transplant clinical/referral diagnosis and final pathological diagnosis on explanted lungs
finding: 29 significant discrepancies or additional features identified; discrepancy rate 19% (12/65) in single lung recipients and 16% (17/109) in heart-lung recipients; unsuspected diagnoses included tuberculosis (8, four active), sarcoidosis (9, six unsuspected) and veno-occlusive disease (3).
setting: Transplantation Unit, Papworth Hospital
cycle1_result: 29 significant discrepancies or additional features identified; discrepancy rate 19% (12/65) in single lung recipients and 16% (17/109) in heart-lung recipients; unsuspected diagnoses included tuberculosis (8, four active), sarcoidosis (9, six unsuspected) and veno-occlusive disease (3).
other_findings: Highlights need for accurate preoperative diagnosis, especially when the diseased native lung remains in situ (single lung transplants).
authors: Stewart S; McNeil K; Nashef SA; Wells FC; Higenbottam TW; Wallwork J
journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation
citation: Stewart S, McNeil K, Nashef SA, Wells FC, Higenbottam TW, Wallwork J. Audit of referral and explant diagnoses in lung transplantation: a pathologic study of lungs removed for parenchymal disease. J Heart Lung Transplant. 1995;14(6 Pt 1):1173-1186. PMID: 8719465.

title: Preventable prehospital trauma deaths in a Hellenic urban health region: an audit of prehospital trauma care.
standard: not reported (clinical assessor judgement of preventability using autopsy, toxicology and injury scoring)
finding: 4 (4.87%) deaths judged 'definitely preventable' and 35 (42.65%) 'possibly preventable'; 24 (29.26%) had a survival probability >0.5.
setting: General Hospital of Piraeus, Greece
cycle1_result: 4 (4.87%) deaths judged 'definitely preventable' and 35 (42.65%) 'possibly preventable'; 24 (29.26%) had a survival probability >0.5.
other_findings: Concluded that upgrading of the emergency medical care service is required.

topic: Cochlear implant service quality and satisfaction
title: An audit of the cochlear implant service in Manchester.
standard: Local standard: patient satisfaction and information-provision expectations for the cochlear implant service (no external named target)
finding: 78% of patients felt the implant gave as much or more benefit than expected; areas for improvement identified: more written information, reduced waiting times for first appointment, more information on surgical risks, and more auditory training instruction for family/friends.
change: Clinical practice and service provision for cochlear implantation modified as a result of the audit findings (not further specified)
setting: Manchester Cochlear Implant Programme
cycle1_result: 78% of patients felt the implant gave as much or more benefit than expected; areas for improvement identified: more written information, reduced waiting times for first appointment, more information on surgical risks, and more auditory training instruction for family/friends.
intervention: Clinical practice and service provision for cochlear implantation modified as a result of the audit findings (not further specified)
other_findings: First 58 implant users of the programme (established 1988) were surveyed by questionnaire.

topic: Feasibility of auditing infant hearing distraction testing
title: Audit of the distraction test of hearing at about 8 months of age: results of a survey of Scottish health boards.
standard: Hall Report 'Health for all Children' recommendation of distraction testing at 8 months
finding: All boards regarded the test as worthwhile; variation found in attention to quality standards (technique, recording, equipment, training); only one board could realistically audit the test at all stages using routinely collected data.
setting: Scottish health boards
cycle1_result: All boards regarded the test as worthwhile; variation found in attention to quality standards (technique, recording, equipment, training); only one board could realistically audit the test at all stages using routinely collected data.
other_findings: Part of a Scotland-wide feasibility project; data availability was expected to improve with the national computerised Pre-school Child Health Surveillance Programme.
authors: Wallace AM; Allen AD
citation: Wallace AM, Allen AD. Audit of the distraction test of hearing at about 8 months of age: results of a survey of Scottish health boards. Br J Audiol. 1996;30(6):389-395. doi:10.3109/03005369609078426. PMID: 8985563.

topic: BCG immunisation and tuberculin testing practice
title: An audit of BCG immunisation and tuberculin skin testing in Scotland. Scottish BCG Study Group.
standard: UK national policy of BCG vaccination for tuberculin-negative schoolchildren and high-risk groups (in place since 1954)
finding: Only 6/15 (40%) Health Boards immunised all tuberculin-negative children; all boards immunised TB contacts; 11/15 offered vaccination to healthcare workers and to immigrants from high-prevalence countries; only 7/15 offered it to high-risk ethnic group offspring, 5/15 to students and 4/15 to animal workers.
setting: 15 Scottish Health Boards
cycle1_result: Only 6/15 (40%) Health Boards immunised all tuberculin-negative children; all boards immunised TB contacts; 11/15 offered vaccination to healthcare workers and to immigrants from high-prevalence countries; only 7/15 offered it to high-risk ethnic group offspring, 5/15 to students and 4/15 to animal workers.
other_findings: Marked variation in practice found; authors call for greater efforts to ensure high-risk groups receive vaccination.
authors: Pell J; Capewell S
citation: Pell J, Capewell S. An audit of BCG immunisation and tuberculin skin testing in Scotland. Scottish BCG Study Group. Health Bull (Edinb). 1996;54(6):490-494. PMID: 8990615.

topic: Flexor tendon zone II injury management outcomes
title: An audit of flexor tendon injuries in zone II and its influence on management.
standard: not reported
finding: Results of a controlled mobilization programme for zone II flexor tendon injuries were compared with results from other units (specific figures not given in the abstract).

title: Implementation of Department of Health guidelines for hepatitis B vaccination: a regional audit of NHS occupational health policies and procedures.
standard: UK Health Departments' guidelines on protecting healthcare workers and patients from hepatitis B infection
finding: Compliance with national guidelines on vaccination was variable; marked variation in interpretation of serological data; failure to establish hepatitis B status of surgeons performing exposure-prone procedures in some cases.
setting: 18 district-based occupational health departments, northern region NHS
cycle1_result: Compliance with national guidelines on vaccination was variable; marked variation in interpretation of serological data; failure to establish hepatitis B status of surgeons performing exposure-prone procedures in some cases.
other_findings: Identifies need for training of occupational health practitioners on hepatitis B and for a uniform standard of practice across the NHS.
authors: Harrison J
citation: Harrison J. Implementation of Department of Health guidelines for hepatitis B vaccination: a regional audit of NHS occupational health policies and procedures. Occup Med (Lond). 1997;47(1):5-10. doi:10.1093/occmed/47.1.5. PMID: 9136211.

title: Therapeutic drug monitoring of gentamicin: a 6-year follow-up audit.
standard: not reported (locally defined therapeutic/toxic ranges for gentamicin peak and trough concentrations)
finding: 65% of peak concentrations were within the therapeutic range at first monitoring, 79% of troughs within the non-toxic range; after dosage adjustment 81% of peaks were therapeutic and 7% of troughs became toxic.
setting: Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia, Malaysia
cycle1_result: 65% of peak concentrations were within the therapeutic range at first monitoring, 79% of troughs within the non-toxic range; after dosage adjustment 81% of peaks were therapeutic and 7% of troughs became toxic.
other_findings: Distribution of gentamicin peak and trough concentrations was reported as better than found in an earlier 1990 assessment, but comparative figures for 1990 were not given.
authors: Ismail R; Haq AH; Azman M; Rahman AF
journal: Journal of clinical pharmacy and therapeutics
citation: Ismail R, Haq AH, Azman M, Rahman AF. Therapeutic drug monitoring of gentamicin: a 6-year follow-up audit. J Clin Pharm Ther. 1997;22(1):21-25. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2710.1997.96375963.x. PMID: 9292398.

title: Audit of a pre-employment risk identification form.
standard: Local standard: accuracy of pre-employment risk identification form assessments compared with actual occupational health risks identified after starting the job
finding: Agreement between managers' assessments and actual risks identified ranged 83-100%, compared with 59-100% for an independent occupational health nurse's assessment based on job title alone; managers' assessments had higher sensitivity and positive predictive value in nearly all categories.
setting: Southmead Health Services NHS Trust
cycle1_result: Agreement between managers' assessments and actual risks identified ranged 83-100%, compared with 59-100% for an independent occupational health nurse's assessment based on job title alone; managers' assessments had higher sensitivity and positive predictive value in nearly all categories.
other_findings: Driving was the only category where the independent nurse's assessment was not less accurate than the manager's.
authors: Firman E; Park R; Madan I
citation: Firman E, Park R, Madan I. Audit of a pre-employment risk identification form. Occup Med (Lond). 1997;47(5):277-280. doi:10.1093/occmed/47.5.277. PMID: 9302810.

topic: Compliance of occupational rehabilitation with low back pain guidelines
title: An audit of occupational health care for employees with low-back pain.
standard: not reported (locally derived criteria for good practice of occupational rehabilitation for low-back pain)
finding: Six performance rates calculated: two below 25%, two around 50%, and the highest (curative policy) at 90%.
setting: Occupational health care, Netherlands
cycle1_result: Six performance rates calculated: two below 25%, two around 50%, and the highest (curative policy) at 90%.
other_findings: Authors recommended construction of guidelines and reliable registration of the rehabilitation process to support future auditing.
authors: van der Weide WE; Verbeek JH; van Dijk FJ; Doef J

topic: Compliance with guidelines for minor head injury management
title: An audit on guidelines used for the initial management of patients with minor head injuries in Denmark.
standard: Guidelines recommended by Danish neurosurgeons for management of minor head injuries
finding: More than 80% of hospitals recommended admission for unconsciousness, significant headache, dizziness, or nausea/vomiting; skull X-ray was always used in only 2 of 64 hospitals; compliance with guidance on history-taking symptoms was unsatisfactory.
setting: 68 accident and emergency departments nationwide, Denmark
cycle1_result: More than 80% of hospitals recommended admission for unconsciousness, significant headache, dizziness, or nausea/vomiting; skull X-ray was always used in only 2 of 64 hospitals; compliance with guidance on history-taking symptoms was unsatisfactory.
other_findings: Admissions per 100,000 attenders were significantly higher in small hospitals than large hospitals.
authors: Duus BR
citation: Duus BR. An audit on guidelines used for the initial management of patients with minor head injuries in Denmark. Acta Neurochir (Wien). 1997;139(8):743-748. doi:10.1007/bf01420047. PMID: 9309289.

topic: Prenatal diagnosis service utilisation for haemoglobin disorders
title: Audit of prenatal diagnosis for haemoglobin disorders in the United Kingdom: the first 20 years.
standard: Expected level of utilisation and early (first-trimester) referral for prenatal diagnosis of haemoglobin disorders, for equitable antenatal screening access
finding: National utilisation of prenatal diagnosis for haemoglobin disorders was around 20% overall - far lower than expected; steady at about 50% for thalassaemias but rose from 7% to 13% for sickle cell disorders over the past 10 years; wide regional variation (sickle cell 2-20%; thalassaemia 0% to over 60% for British Pakistanis, ~90% for Cypriots); less than 50% of first referrals were in the first trimester.
setting: Three national prenatal diagnosis centres for haemoglobin disorders
cycle1_result: National utilisation of prenatal diagnosis for haemoglobin disorders was around 20% overall - far lower than expected; steady at about 50% for thalassaemias but rose from 7% to 13% for sickle cell disorders over the past 10 years; wide regional variation (sickle cell 2-20%; thalassaemia 0% to over 60% for British Pakistanis, ~90% for Cypriots); less than 50% of first referrals were in the first trimester.
other_findings: Points to serious shortcomings in antenatal screening practice, local screening policies and inadequate counselling resources, especially for British Pakistanis.
authors: Modell B; Petrou M; Layton M; Varnavides L; Slater C; Ward RH; Rodeck C; Nicolaides K; Gibbons S; Fitches A; Old J
citation: Modell B, Petrou M, Layton M, Varnavides L, Slater C, Ward RH, et al.. Audit of prenatal diagnosis for haemoglobin disorders in the United Kingdom: the first 20 years. BMJ. 1997;315(7111):779-784. doi:10.1136/bmj.315.7111.779. PMID: 9345170.

title: Intrapartum death of nonmalformed fetuses in Denmark and Sweden in 1991. A perinatal audit.
standard: not reported (expert panel review of avoidability of intrapartum death using surveillance/intervention criteria)
finding: Insufficient care (surveillance/intervention) found in 66% of Danish cases vs 55% of Swedish cases; potentially avoidable fetal deaths 59% (Denmark) vs 52% (Sweden), difference not statistically significant.
setting: National case review, Denmark and Sweden
cycle1_n: 50 (all intrapartum deaths in Denmark and Sweden that year)
cycle1_result: Insufficient care (surveillance/intervention) found in 66% of Danish cases vs 55% of Swedish cases; potentially avoidable fetal deaths 59% (Denmark) vs 52% (Sweden), difference not statistically significant.
other_findings: Denmark's intrapartum death rate (4.2/10,000) was higher than Sweden's (1.9/10,000, OR 2.24) in 1991; comparison was between countries rather than a before/after re-audit.
authors: Westergaard HB; Langhoff-Roos J; Larsen S; Borch-Christensen H; Lindmark G
citation: Westergaard HB, Langhoff-Roos J, Larsen S, Borch-Christensen H, Lindmark G. Intrapartum death of nonmalformed fetuses in Denmark and Sweden in 1991. A perinatal audit. Acta Obstet Gynecol Scand. 1997;76(10):959-963. doi:10.3109/00016349709034909. PMID: 9435736.

title: Environmental control systems--an audit of existing provision in three inner London districts.
standard: British Society of Rehabilitation Medicine special interest group recommendations on environmental control system provision and review
finding: 6/29 users had systems so outdated or poorly planned as to be nearly useless; 7/29 users were felt not to justify an environmental control system; many systems were over-specified, leading to wastage of equipment; many other unmet medical and non-medical needs were identified.
setting: Inner London boroughs of Lambeth, Southwark and Lewisham (population 720,000)
cycle1_result: 6/29 users had systems so outdated or poorly planned as to be nearly useless; 7/29 users were felt not to justify an environmental control system; many systems were over-specified, leading to wastage of equipment; many other unmet medical and non-medical needs were identified.
other_findings: Authors felt the existing recommendations did not go far enough and proposed extending the environmental control assessor's role to case conferences and ongoing review.
authors: Novak SA
citation: Novak SA. Environmental control systems--an audit of existing provision in three inner London districts. Clin Rehabil. 1998;12(1):88-93. doi:10.1191/026921598671164157. PMID: 9549030.

topic: Investigation of folic acid deficiency aetiology
title: An audit of the investigation and treatment of folic acid deficiency.
standard: Expected standard of thorough aetiological investigation of folate deficiency (dietary, alcohol, drug history, coeliac screening) - implicit local standard, no named external guideline
finding: In 52/84 (61.9%) no diagnosis was reached; a definitive diagnosis was established in only 32/84 (38.1%): 16 dietary deficiency, 9 drug-associated, 5 coeliac disease, 1 Crohn's disease, 1 combined variable immunodeficiency; in most cases no attempt was made to establish aetiology.
setting: Teaching hospital
cycle1_result: In 52/84 (61.9%) no diagnosis was reached; a definitive diagnosis was established in only 32/84 (38.1%): 16 dietary deficiency, 9 drug-associated, 5 coeliac disease, 1 Crohn's disease, 1 combined variable immunodeficiency; in most cases no attempt was made to establish aetiology.
other_findings: Recommends younger patients without an obvious cause be investigated with dietary assessment, anti-endomysial antibody testing and duodenal biopsy if clinically indicated.
authors: Haslam N; Probert CS
journal: Journal of the Royal Society of Medicine
citation: Haslam N, Probert CS. An audit of the investigation and treatment of folic acid deficiency. J R Soc Med. 1998;91(2):72-73. doi:10.1177/014107689809100205. PMID: 9602741.

topic: Therapeutic drug monitoring service consistency across laboratories
title: An audit of therapeutic drug monitoring service provision by laboratories participating in an external quality assessment scheme.
standard: Expected consistency in therapeutic drug monitoring target ranges and reporting practice among laboratories (implicit standard, revealed as inconsistent)
finding: Target ranges for lithium, digoxin, carbamazepine and phenobarbitone were highly variable, while phenytoin, theophylline and valproic acid ranges were more consistent; units of reporting varied (45% mass, 34% molar, 22% mixed, excluding lithium); 93% provided paper reports, only 28% reported by computer; 73% offered a 24-hour emergency service.
setting: Laboratories subscribing to the UK National External Quality Assessment Scheme for Therapeutic Drug Assays
cycle1_result: Target ranges for lithium, digoxin, carbamazepine and phenobarbitone were highly variable, while phenytoin, theophylline and valproic acid ranges were more consistent; units of reporting varied (45% mass, 34% molar, 22% mixed, excluding lithium); 93% provided paper reports, only 28% reported by computer; 73% offered a 24-hour emergency service.
other_findings: Audit unexpectedly identified a wide range of target concentrations, particularly for digoxin and lithium.
authors: Thomson AH; Watson ID; Wilson JF; Sweeney G; Dawkins CE; Smith BL; Williams J; Capps NE; Toseland PA
citation: Thomson AH, Watson ID, Wilson JF, Sweeney G, Dawkins CE, Smith BL, et al.. An audit of therapeutic drug monitoring service provision by laboratories participating in an external quality assessment scheme. Ther Drug Monit. 1998;20(3):248-252. doi:10.1097/00007691-199806000-00002. PMID: 9631919.

title: An audit of anti-D sensitisation in Yorkshire.
standard: Recommendations on administration of anti-D immunoglobulin following potential RhD-sensitising events (e.g. miscarriage, termination of pregnancy)
finding: Iatrogenic failure to adhere to recommendations for anti-D immunoglobulin administration occurred in a significant proportion of women who developed immune anti-D antibodies; anti-D failed to protect against immunisation despite protocol adherence in 20/98 events (20%), 13 of which involved miscarriage or termination; 81% of all identified immunising events were miscarriages or medical terminations.
setting: 15 obstetric units, Yorkshire region
cycle1_result: Iatrogenic failure to adhere to recommendations for anti-D immunoglobulin administration occurred in a significant proportion of women who developed immune anti-D antibodies; anti-D failed to protect against immunisation despite protocol adherence in 20/98 events (20%), 13 of which involved miscarriage or termination; 81% of all identified immunising events were miscarriages or medical terminations.
other_findings: Suggests introducing antenatal anti-D administration could significantly reduce sensitisation in primigravidae; recommends reviewing the adequacy of the 250 IU dose after termination before 20 weeks' gestation.
authors: McSweeney E; Kirkham J; Vinall P; Flanagan P
journal: British journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
citation: McSweeney E, Kirkham J, Vinall P, Flanagan P. An audit of anti-D sensitisation in Yorkshire. Br J Obstet Gynaecol. 1998;105(10):1091-1094. doi:10.1111/j.1471-0528.1998.tb09941.x. PMID: 9800932.

topic: Quality scoring of occupational health units against a national audit matrix
title: Audit matrix for evaluating Finnish occupational health units.
standard: Finnish 'good practice in occupational health services' principles, scored via a 12-area, 0-72 point audit matrix
finding: No unit scored below 18/72; 9 units scored 19-36, 17 scored 37-54, 4 scored over 54; highest mean scores for maintenance of work ability (4.1), curative care (4.0) and multidisciplinarity (3.9); lowest for planning of activities (3.1), customer orientation (3.2) and quality improvement (3.2).
setting: Occupational health units, Finland
cycle1_result: No unit scored below 18/72; 9 units scored 19-36, 17 scored 37-54, 4 scored over 54; highest mean scores for maintenance of work ability (4.1), curative care (4.0) and multidisciplinarity (3.9); lowest for planning of activities (3.1), customer orientation (3.2) and quality improvement (3.2).
other_findings: Matrix was described as a practical tool, well accepted by occupational health professionals, for classifying units and promoting good practice.
authors: Martimo KP
journal: Scandinavian journal of work, environment & health
citation: Martimo KP. Audit matrix for evaluating Finnish occupational health units. Scand J Work Environ Health. 1998;24(5):439-443. doi:10.5271/sjweh.367. PMID: 9869317.

topic: Analgesia and laxative prescribing in hip fracture admission
title: 756 ORTHOPAEDIC SURGEONS CAN PRESCRIBE LAXATIVES & ANALGESICS TOO - A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT SPANNING 7 YEARS
standard: Local standard for regular laxative and analgesia prescribing at hip-fracture admission (no explicit percentage target stated)
finding: Laxative prescribing 40%, paracetamol prescribing 100%, regular strong opioid prescribing 60%
change: Repeated PDSA cycles: induction prompts and prompts in admission document (Phase 1); added flow diagram (Phase 2); induction prompts plus electronic prescribing protocol and removal of flow diagram (Phase 3); Phase 3 plus more effort explaining to locum doctors (Phase 4)
setting: District general hospital (The Royal Oldham Hospital / North Manchester General Hospital)
cycle1_result: Laxative prescribing 40%, paracetamol prescribing 100%, regular strong opioid prescribing 60%
intervention: Repeated PDSA cycles: induction prompts and prompts in admission document (Phase 1); added flow diagram (Phase 2); induction prompts plus electronic prescribing protocol and removal of flow diagram (Phase 3); Phase 3 plus more effort explaining to locum doctors (Phase 4)
cycle2_result: Laxative prescribing 74% (90% by 24h post-admission), paracetamol 82% (90% at 24h), regular strong opioid 80% (90% at 24h)
other_findings: Intermediate phases fluctuated (e.g. laxative prescribing rose to 80% in Phases 1-2 then fell to 56% in Phase 3); the electronic prescribing solution alone was insufficient as locum doctors were often unaware of it; plan to reintroduce the flow diagram.
authors: Kim K; Gibson P
citation: Kim K, Gibson P. 756 ORTHOPAEDIC SURGEONS CAN PRESCRIBE LAXATIVES & ANALGESICS TOO - A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT SPANNING 7 YEARS. Age and Ageing. 2022;51(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afac034.756.

topic: Fragility fracture risk assessment in older person's clinic
title: 1043 FRAGILITY FRACTURE RISK ASSESSMENT IN THE OLDER PERSON’S RAPID ACCESS CLINIC (OPRAC): A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT
standard: NICE recommendation for fragility fracture risk assessment in all women aged over 65 and men over 75
finding: Only 3% had a fracture risk assessment done; height and weight documented in 74%
change: Departmental teaching, posters, and inclusion of fracture risk assessment in the induction handbook
setting: Older Person's Rapid Access Clinic (OPRAC), Charing Cross Hospital, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust
cycle1_result: Only 3% had a fracture risk assessment done; height and weight documented in 74%
intervention: Departmental teaching, posters, and inclusion of fracture risk assessment in the induction handbook
cycle2_result: Risk assessment increased to 33%; height and weight documentation increased to 98%
other_findings: Across both cycles, patients who had a risk assessment were far more likely to receive correct treatment (89% and 82% in cycles 1 and 2) than those who did not (54% and 30%).
authors: Dumenci O; Alhilani M; Malani S; Suh S
citation: Dumenci O, Alhilani M, Malani S, Suh S. 1043 FRAGILITY FRACTURE RISK ASSESSMENT IN THE OLDER PERSON’S RAPID ACCESS CLINIC (OPRAC): A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT. Age and Ageing. 2022;51(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/ageing/afac126.062.

topic: Bone health plan documentation in hip fracture discharge summaries
title: 2329 A quality improvement project to improve bone health plan in trauma and orthopaedic discharge summaries
standard: National Osteoporosis Guideline Group (NOGG) recommendation of IV zoledronate as first-line treatment following hip fracture, with documentation on discharge summary
finding: 28.3% of discharge summaries had no bone health plan; Vitamin D level not mentioned in 57.1%; inpatient zoledronic acid administration mentioned in 32.1%
change: A blank bone health paragraph was copied into every discharge summary from day 1 of admission, to make completion easier for the Trauma and Orthopaedic junior doctor
setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics department, Bristol Royal Infirmary
cycle1_result: 28.3% of discharge summaries had no bone health plan; Vitamin D level not mentioned in 57.1%; inpatient zoledronic acid administration mentioned in 32.1%
intervention: A blank bone health paragraph was copied into every discharge summary from day 1 of admission, to make completion easier for the Trauma and Orthopaedic junior doctor
cycle2_result: 25% of discharge summaries had no bone health plan; Vitamin D not mentioned rose to 59.4%; mention of inpatient zoledronic acid fell to 25%
other_findings: Despite the intervention, bone health plans remained poorly communicated to GPs and the Fracture Liaison Service; next step is a teaching session with T&O juniors to design a further change.
authors: Perera H; Cannon A
citation: Perera H, Cannon A. 2329 A quality improvement project to improve bone health plan in trauma and orthopaedic discharge summaries. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae139.050.

title: 2883 Quality improvement initiatives to improve one year follow up as per FLS-DB National Recommendations in a welsh health board
standard: FLS Database (FLS-DB) recommendation to identify 80% of expected fragility fractures, treat 50%, and monitor 80% at 16 and 52 weeks; national benchmark for one-year follow-up
finding: 18.4% (92/875) followed up at one year, versus a national benchmark of 22.3%
change: Process mapping under a Plan-Do-Study-Act quality improvement methodology led to a dedicated annual review clinic code, led by a geriatrics specialty trainee
setting: Aneurin Bevan Fracture Liaison Service (AB-FLS), Welsh health board
cycle1_result: 18.4% (92/875) followed up at one year, versus a national benchmark of 22.3%
intervention: Process mapping under a Plan-Do-Study-Act quality improvement methodology led to a dedicated annual review clinic code, led by a geriatrics specialty trainee
cycle2_result: One-year follow-up performance of 21.4% (310 cases), comparable to the national benchmark of 22.2%
other_findings: In the interim year (2022) case identification rose 88% to 1649 patients but one-year follow-up fell from 18.4% to 13.8% (149 cases); challenges included inaccurate contact numbers, transfer of patients to primary care, and an osteoporosis knowledge gap in the community.
authors: Hutchins M; Maggs S; Williams A; Devyani; Vegad K; Singh I

topic: DXA scan access and turnaround for fragility fracture patients
title: 3727 Addressing inequities in dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) access: a multi-dimensional quality improvement approach
standard: Fracture Liaison Service Database (FLS-DB) Key Performance Indicator 5: percentage of patients receiving DXA within 90 days of fracture (target not stated)
finding: 29.2% (255) scanned within 90 days; average DXA waiting list 1028 patients/month
change: Multi-dimensional improvement project (Model for Improvement): process mapping, radiographer training, expanding scanning from 3 to 5 days/week, dedicated DXA reporting training and a non-reporting agreement for FLS patients
setting: Radiology department, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
cycle1_result: 29.2% (255) scanned within 90 days; average DXA waiting list 1028 patients/month
intervention: Multi-dimensional improvement project (Model for Improvement): process mapping, radiographer training, expanding scanning from 3 to 5 days/week, dedicated DXA reporting training and a non-reporting agreement for FLS patients
cycle2_result: 25.7% (673) scanned within 90 days, a 163% increase from 2021; DXA waiting list dropped to an average of 849/month
other_findings: Interim years worsened before improving: 2022, 16.8% (276/1648) scanned with waiting list rising to 1541/month; 2023, 17.4% (379/2179) scanned with waiting list at 1980/month; by 2025 the waiting list fell further to 786/month.

title: 3788 Multi-stakeholder approach: building on existing quality initiatives to improve 52-week follow-up based on FLS-DB guidance
standard: FLS Database (FLS-DB) recommendation: identify 80% of expected fragility fractures, commence treatment in 50%, and monitor 80% at 52 weeks; national benchmark for one-year follow-up 24.2%
finding: 52-week follow-up 25.9% (360 cases), just above the national benchmark of 24.2%
change: Multi-stakeholder Quality Assurance group (clinicians, pharmacist, GP, patient representatives) meeting quarterly, plus a dedicated 52-week follow-up clinic led by a specialty geriatric trainee, within ongoing PDSA cycles since 2022
setting: Aneurin Bevan Fracture Liaison Service (AB-FLS), Wales
cycle1_result: 52-week follow-up 25.9% (360 cases), just above the national benchmark of 24.2%
intervention: Multi-stakeholder Quality Assurance group (clinicians, pharmacist, GP, patient representatives) meeting quarterly, plus a dedicated 52-week follow-up clinic led by a specialty geriatric trainee, within ongoing PDSA cycles since 2022
cycle2_result: 52-week follow-up improved to 62.7% (1010 of cases), more than double the national benchmark; case identification reached 70% (2620 cases, vs 39.9% national benchmark) and treatment commencement 61.5% (1611 cases, vs 56.4% national benchmark)
other_findings: Fragility fracture case identification rose from 22.7% (2021) to 41.1% (2022) to 58.4% (2023), a 149% increase, underpinning the follow-up gains.
authors: Scanlon L; Coffey J; Thomas C; Edwards A; Rose G; Singh I;

topic: Bowel management in hip fracture patients
title: 3650 Optimising bowel management in patients with neck of femur fractures: a quality improvement project using admission pelvic X-rays
standard: Local protocol for proactive bowel management guided by pelvic X-ray (PXR) faecal loading grade
finding: Mean time to bowel opening 5 days (range 0-10); patients with higher constipation scores (2-3+) had delayed bowel opening (5.7 vs 4.4 days); only 8% received triple laxative therapy on day 0
change: Implementation of a bowel management guideline advocating early, targeted laxative use based on PXR constipation grade
setting: Orthogeriatric department, Luton and Dunstable Hospital
cycle1_result: Mean time to bowel opening 5 days (range 0-10); patients with higher constipation scores (2-3+) had delayed bowel opening (5.7 vs 4.4 days); only 8% received triple laxative therapy on day 0
intervention: Implementation of a bowel management guideline advocating early, targeted laxative use based on PXR constipation grade
cycle2_result: Mean time to bowel opening reduced to 3.8 days; patients with significant faecal loading (2-3+) opened bowels on average 2 days earlier when the protocol was followed
other_findings: Greater protocol adherence correlated with shorter time to bowel opening; continued education and adherence are seen as key to sustaining the improvement.
authors: Patel A; Mangoro M; Alam H
citation: Patel A, Mangoro M, Alam H. 3650 Optimising bowel management in patients with neck of femur fractures: a quality improvement project using admission pelvic X-rays. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.062.

topic: Postoperative pain management in hip fracture
title: 3829 Evaluating and improving post-operative pain management in hip fracture patients: a multidisciplinary quality improvement project
standard: Local standard for postoperative pain management and PRN analgesia administration to support mobilisation (no national target stated)
finding: 30% of patients reported pain of 8/10 or more on day one; poor correlation between pain scores and PRN analgesia administered
change: Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles including a trial of a one-off buprenorphine patch, staff education on prescribing behaviours, and nursing workflow optimisation
setting: Dedicated femoral fracture unit, Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
cycle1_result: 30% of patients reported pain of 8/10 or more on day one; poor correlation between pain scores and PRN analgesia administered
intervention: Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles including a trial of a one-off buprenorphine patch, staff education on prescribing behaviours, and nursing workflow optimisation
cycle2_result: Buprenorphine patch introduction gave a 20% reduction in day-one pain and 23% reduction on day two; highest reported pain fell to 7/10 (vs 10/10 pre-intervention); no significant increase in postoperative delirium; PRN administration remained inconsistent despite improved pre-op analgesia bundle prescribing
other_findings: Barriers identified included staff workload, controlled drug access delays, poor interprofessional communication, and hesitancy around stronger opioids.
authors: Joshi A; Healy S; Rahman M; Conroy S; Porter C
citation: Joshi A, Healy S, Rahman M, Conroy S, Porter C. 3829 Evaluating and improving post-operative pain management in hip fracture patients: a multidisciplinary quality improvement project. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.076.

title: 60 Post Inpatient Fall Medical Assessment (PIFMA) Performa Quality Improvement Project
standard: Local standard for assessment and documentation of inpatient falls, informed by a 2011 NPSA rapid response report
finding: Physical examination documented in 80%, neurological observations 49%, medication review 53%, lying-standing blood pressure 83% (after raising-awareness-and-teaching intervention)
change: Development of the Post Inpatient Fall Medical Assessment (PIFMA) proforma to aid assessment and documentation, following an initial raising-awareness-and-teaching (RAT) PDSA cycle

cycle1_result: Physical examination documented in 80%, neurological observations 49%, medication review 53%, lying-standing blood pressure 83% (after raising-awareness-and-teaching intervention)
intervention: Development of the Post Inpatient Fall Medical Assessment (PIFMA) proforma to aid assessment and documentation, following an initial raising-awareness-and-teaching (RAT) PDSA cycle
cycle2_result: Physical examination 97%, neurological observations 98%, medication review 83%, lying-standing blood pressure 90%
other_findings: Junior doctors' feedback rated the PIFMA proforma as useful and time-saving; it is being implemented in trust policy, with further PDSA cycles planned.

topic: Time to treatment for paediatric hand fractures

standard: Local standard for pre-operative optimisation of neck of femur fracture patients (fluids, anti-emetics, laxatives, anticoagulant reversal)

change: Development and distribution of a junior doctor checklist outlining the management plan

intervention: Development and distribution of a junior doctor checklist outlining the management plan

topic: Vitamin D assessment and supplementation in hip fracture patients
title: 366 Vitamin D3 Assessment and Supplementation in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients: A Closed Loop Quality Improvement Project
standard: Local standard for vitamin D3 assessment and supplementation in elderly hip fracture patients with orthogeriatric review within 72 hours
finding: Vitamin D3 measured during admission in 20%; vitamin D3 supplementation prescribed on discharge in 73.3%
change: Postoperative hip blood profile pathway on ICE with information posters on ordering bloods, teaching sessions for doctors and nurses, and twice-weekly orthogeriatric review emphasising bone protection
setting: Trauma unit covering the Black Country, West Midlands (University Hospitals Birmingham / Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust)
cycle1_result: Vitamin D3 measured during admission in 20%; vitamin D3 supplementation prescribed on discharge in 73.3%
intervention: Postoperative hip blood profile pathway on ICE with information posters on ordering bloods, teaching sessions for doctors and nurses, and twice-weekly orthogeriatric review emphasising bone protection
cycle2_result: Vitamin D3 measurement during admission improved to 93.3%; supplementation prescribed on discharge declined to 26.7%
other_findings: Decline in discharge supplementation may relate to planned intravenous bisphosphonate therapy and to miscommunication caused by ward doctors rotating every 4-6 months.

citation: Siddiqui R, Abou Hader K, Mathias C, Pemmaraju G. 366 Vitamin D3 Assessment and Supplementation in Elderly Hip Fracture Patients: A Closed Loop Quality Improvement Project. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.504.

title: 423 Implementation of Standardised Consent Forms for Hip Fracture Surgery: A Quality Improvement Project
standard: British Orthopaedic Association-endorsed standardised consent forms
finding: On Consent 1 forms (n=37), nearly 60% lacked documentation of benefits and 78% missed more than 5 risks; procedure name was the only documentation on Consent 4 forms; VTE was documented on all forms; 98% completed by registrars or consultants
change: Introduction of standardised consent forms endorsed by the British Orthopaedic Association (September 2023)
setting: UK District General Hospital (James Paget University Hospital)
cycle1_result: On Consent 1 forms (n=37), nearly 60% lacked documentation of benefits and 78% missed more than 5 risks; procedure name was the only documentation on Consent 4 forms; VTE was documented on all forms; 98% completed by registrars or consultants
intervention: Introduction of standardised consent forms endorsed by the British Orthopaedic Association (September 2023)
cycle2_result: New standardised forms (Consent 1 and 4) used in 86% of cases, including by foundation year 2 doctors clerking on admission
other_findings: Chronic pain, stiffness and death were missed on most of the old consent forms; future plans aim to extend standardised consent to wrist and ankle fracture fixations.
authors: Singh S; Bompalas P; Pang J; Hinton A; Genena A; Mohamed R; Modi N

topic: Best Practice Tariff variable completion in hip fracture
title: 543 Improving Outcomes in Patients with Fragility Femur Fractures: A Quality Improvement Project
standard: Best Practice Tariff (BPT) for fragility femur fractures: completion of AMTS, 4AT delirium screen, MUST and Falls Assessment
finding: AMTS completion 54.5%, 4AT 16.6%, MUST 82.7%, falls assessment consistently above 95%
change: Daily fractured femur reports identifying admitted patients and tracking BPT completion (first PDSA cycle, April 2023), followed by junior doctor induction teaching and a fragility femur fracture handbook (second PDSA cycle, August 2023)
setting: UK district general hospital (Royal Free Hospital NHS Foundation Trust)
cycle1_result: AMTS completion 54.5%, 4AT 16.6%, MUST 82.7%, falls assessment consistently above 95%
intervention: Daily fractured femur reports identifying admitted patients and tracking BPT completion (first PDSA cycle, April 2023), followed by junior doctor induction teaching and a fragility femur fracture handbook (second PDSA cycle, August 2023)
cycle2_result: AMTS completion rose to 100%, 4AT to 97.8%, MUST to 100%, falls assessment remained above 95%
other_findings: Meeting BPT criteria increased trust revenue by up to £100,000 annually.
authors: Abdolrazaghi S; Vusirikala A; Kelly C; Luker R; McConnell J

topic: Timeliness of post-operative X-rays after hip replacement
title: SRS180 - Addressing delays in post-operative X-rays in hip replacement surgery: a quality improvement project
standard: Local protocol for prompt acquisition of post-operative X-rays after hip replacement surgery
finding: 74% of X-rays requested on the day of surgery; only 50% performed within one day post-operatively
change: Structured PDSA-methodology quality improvement approach with targeted interventions, protocols and educational tools implemented across three cycles
setting: ESNEFT and NNUH, UK hospitals; trauma patients undergoing hip replacement surgery
cycle1_period: first of three cycles, April 2024-March 2025 project period
cycle1_result: 74% of X-rays requested on the day of surgery; only 50% performed within one day post-operatively
intervention: Structured PDSA-methodology quality improvement approach with targeted interventions, protocols and educational tools implemented across three cycles
cycle2_period: third of three cycles, April 2024-March 2025 project period
cycle2_result: 73% of requests submitted within one hour of surgery; average request time decreased from 12.3 to 5.8 h; time from surgery to X-ray reduced from 44 to 35.6 h; X-rays performed within one day increased from 50% to 65%
other_findings: The intermediate cycle (n=55) prospectively evaluated implementation of the targeted interventions; sustainability requires robust protocols, educational tools and addressing resource constraints such as staffing variability and patient transport equipment.
authors: Boumalha B; Louette S; Archunan M; Massa E; Paparaju S
citation: Boumalha B, Louette S, Archunan M, Massa E, Paparaju S. SRS180 - Addressing delays in post-operative X-rays in hip replacement surgery: a quality improvement project. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag018.171.

topic: CKD-MBD parameter monitoring in home haemodialysis
title: MO811: A Closed Loop Audit of CKD-MBD Parameters in Patients Receiving Home Haemodialysis in North West London Centre
standard: UK Renal Association 2015 standards for CKD-MBD (target ranges for corrected calcium, PTH and phosphate)
finding: 14 (42%) had all bone parameters within target range; 27 (82%) calcium in range, 22 (66%) PTH in range, 17 (51%) phosphate in range
change: Monthly multidisciplinary review of blood tests (nephrologists, specialist nurses, dieticians) focusing on CKD-MBD parameters to facilitate timely prescription changes, plus adherence and diet questionnaires
setting: Home haemodialysis programme under Hammersmith Hospital, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, North West London
cycle1_result: 14 (42%) had all bone parameters within target range; 27 (82%) calcium in range, 22 (66%) PTH in range, 17 (51%) phosphate in range
intervention: Monthly multidisciplinary review of blood tests (nephrologists, specialist nurses, dieticians) focusing on CKD-MBD parameters to facilitate timely prescription changes, plus adherence and diet questionnaires
cycle2_result: 10 (43%) had all bone parameters within target range; PTH in range improved from 66% to 83%; phosphate in range 54% (not significantly changed); calcium in range 78%
other_findings: Questionnaires found notable phosphate-binder non-adherence (8/15, 53%, missed doses in last month) and a lack of knowledge of hidden dietary phosphate sources in all 11 patients surveyed.
authors: Shahid K; Sahota S; Dilloway T; Dassanayake T; Coloma N; Capitan A; Boller N; Punzalan S; Duncan N
citation: Shahid K, Sahota S, Dilloway T, Dassanayake T, Coloma N, Capitan A, et al.. MO811: A Closed Loop Audit of CKD-MBD Parameters in Patients Receiving Home Haemodialysis in North West London Centre. Nephrology Dialysis Transplantation. 2022;37(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ndt/gfac082.009.

topic: Operating room efficiency for spinal fusion surgery
title: Timely completion of spinal fusion: A multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative to improve operating room efficiency
standard: Local target: timely completion of first-case spine fusion surgery within 30 minutes of scheduled time, target 80%
finding: Timely case completion 25%
change: Multidisciplinary tests of change: effective scheduling, team communication, family engagement, data collection veracity, standardised pathways, and situational awareness, over three overlapping phases across 16 months
setting: Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center
cycle1_result: Timely case completion 25%
intervention: Multidisciplinary tests of change: effective scheduling, team communication, family engagement, data collection veracity, standardised pathways, and situational awareness, over three overlapping phases across 16 months
cycle2_result: Timely case completion increased to 68% (95% CI 15.1-62.7, p=0.003), sustained in a further 14 cases; on-time surgical starts improved from 50% to 70%; timely completion improved for anaesthesia induction (60% to 85%), surgical procedure (26% to 48%) and emergence (44% to 80%), but not intraoperative patient preparation (30% to 25%)
other_findings: A prediction model for case scheduling decreased the difference between scheduled and actual end-time (33 vs 53 min baseline) and its variance; no untoward intraoperative safety events occurred; the 80% target was not fully reached (68% achieved).
authors: Du T; Chidambaran V; Kara S; Frazier M; Anadio J; Girten S; Levi S; Allen D; Kurth C; Sturm P; Varughese A
citation: Du T, Chidambaran V, Kara S, Frazier M, Anadio J, Girten S, et al.. Timely completion of spinal fusion: A multidisciplinary quality improvement initiative to improve operating room efficiency. Pediatric Anesthesia. 2022;32(8):926-936. doi:10.1111/pan.14466.

topic: Postoperative recovery after cleft palate repair
title: Quality Improvement Protocol to Reduce Excessive Postoperative Recovery Following Cleft Palate Repair.
standard: not reported
finding: Baseline PACU length of stay prior to standardisation not given numerically
change: Consistent multimodal analgesic protocol, selective use of above-elbow arm splints, intraoperative dexmedetomidine infusion, via iterative PDSA cycles
setting: Tertiary paediatric institution (The Royal Children's Hospital)
cycle1_result: Baseline PACU length of stay prior to standardisation not given numerically
intervention: Consistent multimodal analgesic protocol, selective use of above-elbow arm splints, intraoperative dexmedetomidine infusion, via iterative PDSA cycles
cycle2_result: 16% reduction in mean PACU stay with standardised anaesthetic approach, 15% with splint rationalisation, 11% with dexmedetomidine; unplanned PICU intervention reduced from 7.3% to 1.2%, with significant reductions in perioperative adverse respiratory events in the dexmedetomidine phase (23% to 12%)
other_findings: No significant reduction in pain/distress requiring opiate intervention (31% overall) across phases.
authors: Kaur B; Frawley G; Chong D; Burge J
citation: Kaur B, Frawley G, Chong D, Burge J. Quality Improvement Protocol to Reduce Excessive Postoperative Recovery Following Cleft Palate Repair. Paediatr Anaesth. 2025;35(10):838-847. doi:10.1111/pan.70019. PMID: 40704656.

topic: Obstetric outcomes audit in low-resource setting

title: Improving the management of musculoskeletal conditions: can an alternative approach to referral management underpinned by quality improvement and behavioural change theories offer a solution and a better patient experience? A mixed-methods study
standard: Locally agreed clinical pathways for musculoskeletal referral management
finding: Referral letter content on suspected diagnosis 59% (95% CI 53-65) and prior management 67% (95% CI 61-73); pathway adherence 42% (95% CI 35-48)
change: Multifaceted intervention combining locally agreed clinical pathways, feedback on referral rates, clinical audit and peer review, underpinned by quality improvement and behavioural change theories
setting: 36 general practices in East London
cycle1_result: Referral letter content on suspected diagnosis 59% (95% CI 53-65) and prior management 67% (95% CI 61-73); pathway adherence 42% (95% CI 35-48)
intervention: Multifaceted intervention combining locally agreed clinical pathways, feedback on referral rates, clinical audit and peer review, underpinned by quality improvement and behavioural change theories
cycle2_result: Referral content improved to 77% (95% CI 70-84) for diagnosis and 81% (95% CI 74-88) for prior management; pathway adherence improved to 66% (95% CI 57-76); orthopaedic referral rates fell by 32% (14-48%) at 6 months, 30% (7-53%) at 12 months and 30% (0-59%) at 18 months; patient rating of GP explanation improved 29% (14-43%) and perceived usefulness of appointment improved 24% (9-38%)
other_findings: The effect was greater across all quality outcomes for practices with baseline performance at or below the pooled baseline.
authors: Tzortziou Brown V; Underwood M; Westwood O; Morrissey D

setting: Rotunda Hospital, a tertiary maternity hospital (8500 births/year), Dublin
cycle1_result: mean annual fibrinogen concentrate use 175g (EUR93,170); 22% of PPH >=1500mL patients received fibrinogen, with only 23% meeting evidence-based transfusion criteria; 23% received empirical fibrinogen without testing
intervention: Implementation of a ROTEM-guided transfusion strategy in September 2022, supported by an electronic smartphone-based decision tool with conditional logic, departmental education (lectures, hands-on training, simulation) and regular audits

intervention: QI tests of change: 'bite-size' multidisciplinary ward teaching, a pharmacy technician gentamicin counselling service, collation of patient feedback, 'Gold Star' awards, multidisciplinary staff champions, a 'Top Tips' poster, prospective audit/feedback, and removal of outdated PAM charts
cycle2_result: Counselling/PIL provision increased to 21%; 48-hourly prescribing documentation increased to 85%; doses given on time increased to 88%; HEPMA administration documentation improved marginally to 41%; initial sample timing improved marginally to 55%; removal of outdated PAM charts was the only QI target fully met.
other_findings: The most common indications for IV gentamicin in both groups were intra-abdominal and urinary sepsis; qualitative patient feedback highlighted the value of a patient-centred approach; the authors judged further QI work necessary to meet remaining targets.

title: P31 An audit investigating community acquired pneumonia (CAP) antibiotic duration at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (MFT)
standard: National and local antimicrobial guidelines recommending 5 days of antibiotic treatment duration for community-acquired pneumonia (CAP)
finding: adherence to 5-day guidance was 58% (96/165); of the 42% (69) treated >5 days, reasons were extra doses prescribed on discharge (n=35), no reason documented (n=17), documented intent of 7-day course (n=7), symptoms not improved (n=7), infection markers not normalized (n=3); of 75 courses completed after discharge, only 53% (40/75) adhered to the 5-day guidance
change: not reported (consideration being given to an order set/digital tool to standardize antimicrobial prescribing, not yet implemented)
setting: Manchester Royal Infirmary and North Manchester General Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: adherence to 5-day guidance was 58% (96/165); of the 42% (69) treated >5 days, reasons were extra doses prescribed on discharge (n=35), no reason documented (n=17), documented intent of 7-day course (n=7), symptoms not improved (n=7), infection markers not normalized (n=3); of 75 courses completed after discharge, only 53% (40/75) adhered to the 5-day guidance
intervention: not reported (consideration being given to an order set/digital tool to standardize antimicrobial prescribing, not yet implemented)
other_findings: The leading cause of non-adherence was extra doses prescribed at discharge not being cumulatively added to inpatient duration; documentation of reasons for extended courses was often lacking.

title: In a bind: a quality improvement project for reducing fluoroquinolones drug–drug interactions with multivalent cations
standard: Local standard: avoidance of fluoroquinolone co-administration with multivalent cations within 2 hours
finding: Among patients who received a multivalent cation on the same day as a fluoroquinolone (n=101 overall), co-administration within 2 hours of the fluoroquinolone occurred in 62% pre-intervention.
change: Bundle of interventions: nursing education, updated medication administration record (MAR) comments, and new administration times
setting: OU Health hospital
cycle1_result: Among patients who received a multivalent cation on the same day as a fluoroquinolone (n=101 overall), co-administration within 2 hours of the fluoroquinolone occurred in 62% pre-intervention.
intervention: Bundle of interventions: nursing education, updated medication administration record (MAR) comments, and new administration times
cycle2_result: Co-administration within 2 hours fell to 22% post-intervention (p<0.001).
other_findings: The intervention bundle decreased but did not eliminate the interaction; the authors recommend similar interventions given fluoroquinolone-cation interaction is an independent risk factor for resistance.

title: P08 Improving antibiotic stewardship in paediatric appendicitis: a quality improvement project
standard: BSAC (British Society for Antimicrobial Chemotherapy) recommendations for antimicrobial management of paediatric appendicitis
finding: Overall guideline adherence 26%; 45% of uncomplicated cases were managed appropriately, but no complicated cases received guideline-based therapy; broad-spectrum piperacillin/tazobactam was frequently used inappropriately; only 25% of complicated cases had appropriately timed post-operative blood tests, 87.5% received prolonged antibiotic courses, and infection-related readmission occurred in 12.5% of cases.
change: Structured departmental teaching session for medical and nursing staff, supported by visual reminder posters displayed in the paediatric surgical department
setting: Paediatric surgical department
cycle1_result: Overall guideline adherence 26%; 45% of uncomplicated cases were managed appropriately, but no complicated cases received guideline-based therapy; broad-spectrum piperacillin/tazobactam was frequently used inappropriately; only 25% of complicated cases had appropriately timed post-operative blood tests, 87.5% received prolonged antibiotic courses, and infection-related readmission occurred in 12.5% of cases.
intervention: Structured departmental teaching session for medical and nursing staff, supported by visual reminder posters displayed in the paediatric surgical department
cycle2_result: Overall adherence improved substantially; appropriate management rose to 60% in uncomplicated and 40% in complicated cases; piperacillin/tazobactam use fully aligned with guideline indications; 70% of complicated cases received the correct antibiotic duration, 50% had appropriately timed post-operative blood tests, and no infection-related readmissions occurred.
other_findings: Length of stay was reduced in patients whose management adhered to guideline-directed blood monitoring and antibiotic duration.
authors: Andreyev D; Villatoro E

topic: Nurse-led antimicrobial stewardship audit and feedback

change: not reported (planned next steps: targeted ward-based interventions, strengthening the ward nurse role in IVOS, and governance reporting via performance infographics)

intervention: not reported (planned next steps: targeted ward-based interventions, strengthening the ward nurse role in IVOS, and governance reporting via performance infographics)

topic: Timing of intermittent IV vancomycin doses to protect sleep and safety
title: P29 A nudge to safe dosing and sound sleeping: using visual cues to improve safety and sleep quality of patients prescribed intermittent IV vancomycin in the acute hospital setting
standard: Local quality improvement target of reducing intermittent IV vancomycin doses prescribed between midnight and 6am to less than 10% by January 2026
finding: median 18% of intermittent IV vancomycin doses prescribed between midnight and 6am
change: Nudge-theory based visual cues (colour-coded blue prescribing boxes and moon symbols) added directly to the prescribing, administering and monitoring (PAM) chart to direct prescribing/administration away from the middle of the night
setting: Royal Alexandra Hospital, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde (medical, surgical and elderly care wards)
cycle1_result: median 18% of intermittent IV vancomycin doses prescribed between midnight and 6am
intervention: Nudge-theory based visual cues (colour-coded blue prescribing boxes and moon symbols) added directly to the prescribing, administering and monitoring (PAM) chart to direct prescribing/administration away from the middle of the night
cycle2_result: median proportion of doses prescribed between midnight and 6am fell to 7%, meeting the QI target of less than 10%
other_findings: 148 patients (55% male, mean age 67) were reviewed overall, mainly from medical, surgical and elderly care wards; the visual-cue nudge produced a sustained change in prescribing behaviour, improving sleep quality and safety for patients on IV vancomycin.
authors: Rodger R; Qadri H; Yates J

topic: Antimicrobial stewardship documentation via a structured 72-hour review
title: P64 Improving antimicrobial stewardship in critical care through a structured 72 h review: a quality improvement study
standard: NHS England 'Start Smart Then Focus' antimicrobial stewardship strategy, endorsed by the Faculty of Intensive Care Medicine, requiring early structured review of antimicrobial therapy
finding: intended duration documented in microbiology notes in 46.7% (June), 55.5% (August) and 45.4% (October) of cases; duration documented on the actual prescription in 17.6%, 18.2% and 23.5% respectively; documentation of indication was 41.2%, 9.1% and 0% respectively
change: A structured 72-hour antimicrobial review ('72h pause') embedded into electronic microbiology round documentation, with mandatory prompts to document duration and select a review outcome (continue, amend, cease), supported by departmental teaching sessions and posters
setting: Critical care unit, Glasgow Royal Infirmary, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
cycle1_period: June, August and October 2025 (baseline point prevalence surveys)
cycle1_n: not reported (58.8-75% of patients on antimicrobials across 3 surveys)
cycle1_result: intended duration documented in microbiology notes in 46.7% (June), 55.5% (August) and 45.4% (October) of cases; duration documented on the actual prescription in 17.6%, 18.2% and 23.5% respectively; documentation of indication was 41.2%, 9.1% and 0% respectively
intervention: A structured 72-hour antimicrobial review ('72h pause') embedded into electronic microbiology round documentation, with mandatory prompts to document duration and select a review outcome (continue, amend, cease), supported by departmental teaching sessions and posters
cycle2_result: duration documentation in microbiology notes improved to 84.6%; duration stated on the prescription improved to 55%; documentation of indication showed no improvement, remaining low at 10%
other_findings: The intervention significantly improved documentation of duration and facilitated earlier antimicrobial review, but did not improve documentation of indication, attributed to the lack of a dedicated field; ongoing point prevalence audits were planned to assess sustained improvement.
authors: Muir A; McCue C; Gillen S

standard: WHO AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) antibiotic classification framework
finding: Antibiotics prescribed in 44.4% (114/257); Watch group use 72.8%, Access 10.5%, Reserve 8.8%; mean duration 3.62 days (median 3, IQR 2-5); approximately 60% of prescriptions met stewardship alignment criteria; cultures obtained in 67.3%, with 28.1% positivity.
setting: Tertiary care hospital, hospitalised patients
cycle1_result: Antibiotics prescribed in 44.4% (114/257); Watch group use 72.8%, Access 10.5%, Reserve 8.8%; mean duration 3.62 days (median 3, IQR 2-5); approximately 60% of prescriptions met stewardship alignment criteria; cultures obtained in 67.3%, with 28.1% positivity.

topic: Appropriateness of systemic antifungal prescribing outside haematology/oncology
title: P85 An audit of the appropriateness of systemic antifungal prescribing for non-haematology/oncology indications
standard: Local antimicrobial guidelines with audit standards of >=90% for: indication per infection specialist advice or treatment guidelines; dose appropriate for renal/hepatic function; dose appropriate for weight; and duration appropriate per guidelines or clinical documentation
finding: choice of antifungal in line with guidelines except for dermatophyte infections (4.8%); dosing appropriate for renal function in 95.2% and for weight in 97.6% (meeting the >=90% standards); duration guideline-compliant or per specialist advice in 83.3% (below the 90% standard); therapeutic drug monitoring undertaken for all patients where indicated, but sampling timing errors were common (post-dose rather than pre-dose trough); significant azole-statin and azole-citalopram interactions were identified
setting: Non-ICU, non-haematology/oncology adult inpatient specialties, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_period: retrospective, looking backward from 1 October 2025 until 40 eligible patients found
cycle1_result: choice of antifungal in line with guidelines except for dermatophyte infections (4.8%); dosing appropriate for renal function in 95.2% and for weight in 97.6% (meeting the >=90% standards); duration guideline-compliant or per specialist advice in 83.3% (below the 90% standard); therapeutic drug monitoring undertaken for all patients where indicated, but sampling timing errors were common (post-dose rather than pre-dose trough); significant azole-statin and azole-citalopram interactions were identified
other_findings: Overall prescribing was largely appropriate and guideline-aligned; the authors recommended education on pre-dose trough sampling and EPR prompts to support correct TDM timing, plus reminders to review azole-drug interactions to reduce myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk.
authors: Fleming A; Parsons T; Tan R
