topic: Acute kidney injury detection and management quality improvement
title: SO016SPREAD OF ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY IMPROVEMENT PROGAMME ACROSS A LARGE  MULTI SITED NHS HOSPITAL
standard: UK-wide AKI audit (2009) benchmarks and local standards for timely AKI recognition and management
finding: AKI recognition within 24 hours 52% (Central Campus); poor AKI care and delays in detection identified by 2009 UK-wide and 2014 local audits
change: Multifaceted QI Programme: electronic AKI alert, education, stakeholder engagement, AKI Priority Care Checklist (PCC), AKI Clinical Nurse Specialist change agents, staggered rollout across Central, West and South Campus hospitals including paediatric adaptation
setting: Large multi-sited NHS trust (10 hospitals across 6 sites, over 2000 beds), Manchester
cycle1_period: 2014 (local audit) and since 2016 for tracked metrics
cycle1_result: AKI recognition within 24 hours 52% (Central Campus); poor AKI care and delays in detection identified by 2009 UK-wide and 2014 local audits
intervention: Multifaceted QI Programme: electronic AKI alert, education, stakeholder engagement, AKI Priority Care Checklist (PCC), AKI Clinical Nurse Specialist change agents, staggered rollout across Central, West and South Campus hospitals including paediatric adaptation
cycle2_result: Recognition within 24h improved from 52% to 100% (Central Campus); 34% reduction in AKI incidence (p<0.00001), 26% reduction in AKI length of stay, 42% reduction in AKI days, 10% less AKI-associated mortality; Children's Hospital 24% reduction in AKI incidence (p<0.0001) and 34% reduction in hospital-acquired AKI, recognition improved 42% to 100%; South Campus recognition improved 67% to 100%, 19% reduction in AKI incidence (p<0.0015); West Campus recognition 100%
other_findings: LoS and AKI days data at South Campus not yet reported pending IT harmonisation; West Campus small numbers preclude further analysis.

topic: AKI care bundle (AKI7) introduction and audit
title: P0629ESTABLISHING MORTALITY ASSOCIATED WITH AKI IN A DGH AND THEN TRYING TO DO SOMETHING ABOUT IT- INTRODUCTION AND AUDIT OF THE AKI7 CARE BUNDLE
standard: NCEPOD 2009 report benchmark that only 50% of AKI patients received good care; locally introduced AKI7 care bundle standard
finding: 79% did not progress beyond AKI stage 1, 13% stage 2, 8% stage 3; 75% investigated with urinalysis, 94% fluid balance monitoring, 5% renal tract ultrasound, 58% referred to nephrologist; 1-year mortality 29% stage 1, 51% stage 2, 65% stage 3, all-stage combined 39.1%
change: Electronic alert system and order set proforma: the AKI7 care bundle
setting: West Suffolk Hospital (district general hospital)
cycle1_result: 79% did not progress beyond AKI stage 1, 13% stage 2, 8% stage 3; 75% investigated with urinalysis, 94% fluid balance monitoring, 5% renal tract ultrasound, 58% referred to nephrologist; 1-year mortality 29% stage 1, 51% stage 2, 65% stage 3, all-stage combined 39.1%

other_findings: Plan to encourage AKI7 use during junior doctor induction plus aide-memoire cards; survival at 60 days was associated with urinalysis, fluid balance monitoring and renal tract ultrasound (all p<0.001).
authors: Paisey C; Chapman D; Achilleos K; Yiu V

topic: Maternal breast milk use in preterm infants
title: The impact of a regional care bundle on maternal breast milk use in preterm infants: outcomes of the East of England quality improvement programme
standard: Local QI programme target: increase maternal breast milk (MBM) use in preterm infants <=32+6 weeks gestation
finding: Exclusive MBM use at discharge was 26% and any MBM use was 50% before the care bundle.
change: A regional 'care bundle' to promote maternal breast milk use was introduced in the East of England Perinatal Network.
setting: 17 neonatal units in the East of England Perinatal Network (compared with 144 units in the rest of the UK Neonatal Collaborative)
cycle1_result: Exclusive MBM use at discharge was 26% and any MBM use was 50% before the care bundle.
intervention: A regional 'care bundle' to promote maternal breast milk use was introduced in the East of England Perinatal Network.
cycle2_result: Exclusive MBM use at discharge rose to 33% and any MBM use to 57%; exclusive MBM use improved significantly faster in the East of England (0.22%/month, 95% CI 0.11 to 0.34) than the rest of the UK Neonatal Collaborative (0.05%/month, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.09, p=0.007).
other_findings: There was no evidence of a step or trend change specifically coinciding with the care bundle's introduction; overall MBM use at discharge and care-days with MBM were not significantly different from the rest of the UK.

topic: Quality of local guidelines for severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia
title: PMM.41 A decade of improvement? Management of severe PET
standard: Criteria used in a 2004 national survey of severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia guidelines, updated against NICE guidance published in 2010
finding: 2004 survey found guideline standards were poor: 86.1% had clear inclusion criteria, 26.4% recommended consultant input, and 56.1% included blood pressure targets (of which all that had a target systolic threshold recommended >160 mmHg).
change: Publication of NICE guidance on severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia management in 2010.
setting: 229 UK maternity units
cycle1_result: 2004 survey found guideline standards were poor: 86.1% had clear inclusion criteria, 26.4% recommended consultant input, and 56.1% included blood pressure targets (of which all that had a target systolic threshold recommended >160 mmHg).
intervention: Publication of NICE guidance on severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia management in 2010.
cycle2_n: 137 responses (108 guidelines reviewed) of 229 units contacted
cycle2_result: 99.1% of guidelines now had clear inclusion criteria (p<0.05), 91.7% recommended consultant input (p<0.05), 99.1% recommended magnesium sulphate and fluid restriction, and 96.3% included blood pressure targets (p<0.05); only 14.8% now recommended a systolic BP target >160mmHg, though 14.8% (nearly 1 in 7) of units were still not adherent to safe BP targets.
other_findings: Authors note intracerebral haemorrhage remains the biggest killer of women with pre-eclampsia and flag the residual non-adherence to safe BP targets nationally.

journal: Archives of Disease in Childhood - Fetal and Neonatal Edition

topic: Recognition and treatment of neonatal hypoglycaemia
title: PA.08 Neonatal Hypoglycaemia-A Quality Improvement Project to Improve Service Delivery Using a RHINO
standard: Local standard for prompt sugar monitoring, referral and treatment of at-risk neonates
finding: 11% of at-risk babies missed sugar monitoring, 32% had it done incorrectly, and 4 neonates had low sugars untreated for unacceptable durations; staff familiarity with 4 key management areas was very poor.
change: The RHINO Project: a Plan-Do-Check-Act (Deming cycle) programme using point-of-care posters and nursery-nurse champions to cascade education on referral of hypoglycaemia detected in newborn observations to over 200 multidisciplinary staff.
setting: Tertiary neonatal centre, University Hospital Southampton
cycle1_result: 11% of at-risk babies missed sugar monitoring, 32% had it done incorrectly, and 4 neonates had low sugars untreated for unacceptable durations; staff familiarity with 4 key management areas was very poor.
intervention: The RHINO Project: a Plan-Do-Check-Act (Deming cycle) programme using point-of-care posters and nursery-nurse champions to cascade education on referral of hypoglycaemia detected in newborn observations to over 200 multidisciplinary staff.

other_findings: Programme targeted an area of high medico-legal risk (litigation costs of £300,000 to £7 million per claim reported nationally).

topic: Sepsis reduction care bundle in very low birthweight infants
title: The impact of a sepsis quality improvement project on neurodisability rates in very low birthweight infants
standard: not reported (locally introduced sepsis reduction care bundle target: reduce late-onset sepsis)
finding: Preintervention: coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CONS) infection rate 26.7%; death before discharge 14.1%; moderate cognitive impairment 18.8%.
change: A sepsis reduction care bundle was implemented between July 2006 and December 2007.
setting: Level 3 regional neonatal intensive care unit, South West England
cycle1_result: Preintervention: coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (CONS) infection rate 26.7%; death before discharge 14.1%; moderate cognitive impairment 18.8%.
intervention: A sepsis reduction care bundle was implemented between July 2006 and December 2007.
cycle2_period: after the bundle, up to 2011 (postintervention cohort)
cycle2_result: Postintervention: CONS infection rate fell to 14.1% (p<0.001); death before discharge fell to 10.9% (p=0.195, not significant); cognitive disability fell to 6.1% (p=0.042); adjusted OR for CONS infection was 0.46 (95% CI 0.29 to 0.72).
other_findings: Reduced cognitive disability appeared associated with the sepsis bundle, but the reduction in death did not reach statistical significance; authors call for confirmation in larger series.

topic: Alcohol-impregnated port protectors to reduce CLABSI
title: Alcohol-impregnated port protectors to reduce central line-associated bloodstream infection in the neonatal intensive care unit: a quality improvement study
standard: not reported
finding: Preimplementation CLABSI rate not separately stated in the abstract; overall preimplementation vs postimplementation CLABSI rate was 5.5 vs 6.6 per 1000 central line days (p=0.5).
change: Alcohol-impregnated port protectors (AIPPs) were applied to intravascular access ports not used for fluid infusion, from March 2018 to February 2020, with daily audits for 3 months post-implementation and quarterly audits thereafter (3-month washout period March-May 2018).
setting: Tertiary neonatal intensive care unit
cycle1_result: Preimplementation CLABSI rate not separately stated in the abstract; overall preimplementation vs postimplementation CLABSI rate was 5.5 vs 6.6 per 1000 central line days (p=0.5).

topic: Adherence to ventilator weaning quality indicator
title: Does adherence to a quality indicator regarding early weaning from invasive ventilation improve economic outcome? A single-centre retrospective study
standard: Local standard: daily weaning protocol quality indicator with a threshold of 65% or greater compliance
finding: The low adherence group (under 65% compliance) had a median negative economic result of minus €3969 versus minus €1030 in the high adherence group (p<0.001); median ventilation duration was 476 hours (low adherence) versus 389 hours (high adherence) (p<0.001); ICU length of stay was 21 days versus 16 days (p<0.001); hospital length of stay was 36 days versus 26 days (p=0.001).

cycle1_result: The low adherence group (under 65% compliance) had a median negative economic result of minus €3969 versus minus €1030 in the high adherence group (p<0.001); median ventilation duration was 476 hours (low adherence) versus 389 hours (high adherence) (p<0.001); ICU length of stay was 21 days versus 16 days (p<0.001); hospital length of stay was 36 days versus 26 days (p=0.001).

topic: Community health worker adherence to childhood illness protocol

other_findings: The authors concluded that clinical vignettes have limited utility for benchmarking symptom-checker diagnostic accuracy or triage safety and recommend real-world studies with real patients.

title: Assessing the quality of tuberculosis care using routine surveillance data: a process evaluation employing the Zero TB Indicator Framework in Mongolia
standard: Zero TB Indicator Framework, 14 indicators across 3 care cascades for TB case-finding, treatment and prevention
finding: The cumulative proportion of participants receiving guideline-adherent care ranged from 96% for community-based active case-finding to 79% for TB preventive therapy among household contacts to only 67% for passive case-finding in primary health centres and dispensaries (range 29%-80% across districts); odds of completing active TB treatment decreased with age (adjusted OR 0.76 per decade, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83, p<0.001) and among men (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.88, p=0.013); contacts of older index patients had lower odds of completing preventive therapy (aOR 0.60 per decade, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.93, p=0.022).
setting: Primary health centres and TB dispensaries, four districts
cycle1_n: 15947 community members; 8518 screened; 857 index TB patients and 2352 household contacts
cycle1_result: The cumulative proportion of participants receiving guideline-adherent care ranged from 96% for community-based active case-finding to 79% for TB preventive therapy among household contacts to only 67% for passive case-finding in primary health centres and dispensaries (range 29%-80% across districts); odds of completing active TB treatment decreased with age (adjusted OR 0.76 per decade, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83, p<0.001) and among men (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.36 to 0.88, p=0.013); contacts of older index patients had lower odds of completing preventive therapy (aOR 0.60 per decade, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.93, p=0.022).
other_findings: The Zero TB Framework was judged a feasible and adaptable approach for using routine surveillance data to evaluate TB care quality; the authors call for future deployment of quality improvement interventions.

topic: Team effects on obstetric care process quality
title: The role of teams in shaping quality of obstetrical care: a cross-sectional study in Dire Dawa, Ethiopia
standard: Recommended routine clinical actions for intrapartum and immediate postpartum care, across 5 phases of delivery
finding: For the average client, 50% of recommended routine clinical actions were completed overall, with immediate maternal postpartum care being the least well performed (17% of recommended actions); multiple providers were involved in 55% of deliveries; a one standard deviation increase in a coworker's performance was associated with a 2 percentage point increase in quality of care (p<0.01).
setting: 9 health facilities, Dire Dawa Administration
cycle1_result: For the average client, 50% of recommended routine clinical actions were completed overall, with immediate maternal postpartum care being the least well performed (17% of recommended actions); multiple providers were involved in 55% of deliveries; a one standard deviation increase in a coworker's performance was associated with a 2 percentage point increase in quality of care (p<0.01).
other_findings: The number of providers contributing to a delivery was not associated with quality of care; the association between coworker performance and quality was largest among providers in the middle quartiles of performance.

title: Impact of practicing internal benchmarking on continuous improvement of cataract surgery outcomes: a retrospective observational study at Aravind Eye Hospitals, India
standard: Local standard: internal benchmarking of cataract surgery outcome parameters against the best-performing hospital (CATQA)
finding: Intraoperative complication rate was 1.2%; surgeries with uncorrected visual acuity of 6/12 or better were 80.8%; surgeries with postoperative refractive error within plus or minus 0.5D were 76.3%.
change: Internal benchmarking of surgery outcome parameters (CATQA) practised since 2012, comparing hospitals against the best-performing hospital and driving improvements in facilities, protocols and processes
setting: 10 centres (5 tertiary, 5 secondary), Aravind Eye Care System
cycle1_result: Intraoperative complication rate was 1.2%; surgeries with uncorrected visual acuity of 6/12 or better were 80.8%; surgeries with postoperative refractive error within plus or minus 0.5D were 76.3%.
intervention: Internal benchmarking of surgery outcome parameters (CATQA) practised since 2012, comparing hospitals against the best-performing hospital and driving improvements in facilities, protocols and processes
cycle2_result: Intraoperative complication rate decreased to 0.6%; surgeries with uncorrected visual acuity of 6/12 or better rose to 89.8%; surgeries with postoperative refractive error within plus or minus 0.5D rose to 87.3%; variability in outcomes across hospitals declined.

standard: Recommended antenatal care protocols (quality-of-care scores based on actual versus expected care)
finding: Overall quality of health service provision score was 51% in comparison facilities; median antenatal care visit duration was 12 minutes (IQR 8).
change: Digital clinical decision support (CDS) tool to improve health provider adherence to recommended antenatal protocols
setting: 48 rural primary-level health facilities
cycle1_n: not reported (331 total direct observations across both arms)
cycle1_result: Overall quality of health service provision score was 51% in comparison facilities; median antenatal care visit duration was 12 minutes (IQR 8).
intervention: Digital clinical decision support (CDS) tool to improve health provider adherence to recommended antenatal protocols
cycle2_n: not reported (331 total direct observations across both arms)
cycle2_result: Overall quality score was 52% in intervention facilities, comparable to the comparison arm despite a significantly higher proportion of lower-skilled providers (42.5% vs 17.8%); median visit duration was 24 minutes (IQR 18); the intervention arm had higher scores for women's knowledge of counselling received (16.4-point difference, 95% CI 10.37 to 22.49) and satisfaction (16.18-point difference, 95% CI 9.95 to 22.40).

title: Assessing safe chemotherapy needs and practices in Ile-Ife, Nigeria: a multi-disciplinary quality improvement project
standard: American Cancer Society (ACS) ChemoSafe Facility Assessment, benchmarked against international standards for safe handling of hazardous drugs
finding: 75% of respondents reported a lack of training resources for safe chemotherapy handling; 61% reported dissatisfaction with assessment practices for preparing and administering chemotherapy.

cycle1_result: 75% of respondents reported a lack of training resources for safe chemotherapy handling; 61% reported dissatisfaction with assessment practices for preparing and administering chemotherapy.

topic: Trial of labour after caesarean (TOLAC) uptake
title: Investigating the implementation of a Trial of Labour After Caesarean (TOLAC) delivery bundle with respect to decreasing caesarean delivery rates: a multisite quality improvement initiative.
standard: Society of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists of Canada guideline on TOLAC/VBAC eligibility and safety
finding: Caesarean delivery (CD) rate in TOLAC-eligible patients 77%; TOLAC rate 31%; VBAC rate 75%; induction of labour rate 5%
change: A TOLAC delivery bundle introduced at each site in 4-month staggered stages: educational rounds for healthcare providers with individualised audit-and-feedback of CD rates, a physician-patient TOLAC discussion sheet for shared decision-making, and patient-centred educational handouts/posters/videos in 9 languages
setting: Five hospital sites (2 academic centres, 3 community hospitals), Greater Toronto Area, Canada
cycle1_period: 1-year baseline period at each site (2017-2020, staggered by site)
cycle1_result: Caesarean delivery (CD) rate in TOLAC-eligible patients 77%; TOLAC rate 31%; VBAC rate 75%; induction of labour rate 5%
intervention: A TOLAC delivery bundle introduced at each site in 4-month staggered stages: educational rounds for healthcare providers with individualised audit-and-feedback of CD rates, a physician-patient TOLAC discussion sheet for shared decision-making, and patient-centred educational handouts/posters/videos in 9 languages
cycle2_period: 1-year post-intervention period at each site (with a 4-month washout), through 2020
cycle2_result: CD rate fell to 71% (p<0.001); TOLAC rate rose to 37% (p<0.001); VBAC rate rose to 78% (p=0.277, not significant); induction of labour rate rose to 9% (p<0.001); no significant increase in uterine rupture or NICU admission rates (balance measures)
other_findings: No single bundle component was individually associated with the outcome on regression analysis; the discussion sheet was used in only 50% of audited charts; the provincial CD rate rose by 1% over the same period, supporting attribution of the decrease to the bundle.

cycle1_result: 53% of healthcare professionals showed good adherence (80-100%); 36% moderate (50-79%); 11% poor (0-49%). Increased staffing and a bachelor's degree or higher were positively associated with performing positive pressure ventilation (aOR 19.3, p=0.005; aOR 9.9, p=0.043).

topic: IMCI-based checklist assessment in primary care
title: Implementing a checklist to strengthen IMCI-based assessment of childhood illnesses in an urban primary care setting in Delhi: a quality improvement initiative.
standard: WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI) guidelines for children aged 2 months to 5 years
finding: Complete IMCI assessment was performed for 0% of children; danger sign assessment 0%; cough assessment 86.8%; diarrhoea assessment 13.2%; fever assessment 64.2%; ear problem assessment 3.8%; malnutrition assessment 23.1%; anaemia (haemoglobin) assessment 25.0%; immunisation status documentation 1.9%. Of 45 children presenting with cough/breathing difficulty, only 3 (6.7%) were assessed for pneumonia or danger signs.
change: Two 6-week PDSA cycles: age-specific IMCI-based child health assessment checklists (developed and validated with faculty input), a dedicated paediatric OPD room, improved anthropometry equipment and essential supplies; cycle 2 added formatting the checklist as the main OPD card, ensuring regular printing, 6-monthly refresher training for rotating resident doctors, and weekly case-based discussions
setting: Urban health centre, Dakshinpuri extension, South-East Delhi (population approximately 38000, average 200 under-5 OPD attendances/month)
cycle1_result: Complete IMCI assessment was performed for 0% of children; danger sign assessment 0%; cough assessment 86.8%; diarrhoea assessment 13.2%; fever assessment 64.2%; ear problem assessment 3.8%; malnutrition assessment 23.1%; anaemia (haemoglobin) assessment 25.0%; immunisation status documentation 1.9%. Of 45 children presenting with cough/breathing difficulty, only 3 (6.7%) were assessed for pneumonia or danger signs.
intervention: Two 6-week PDSA cycles: age-specific IMCI-based child health assessment checklists (developed and validated with faculty input), a dedicated paediatric OPD room, improved anthropometry equipment and essential supplies; cycle 2 added formatting the checklist as the main OPD card, ensuring regular printing, 6-monthly refresher training for rotating resident doctors, and weekly case-based discussions
cycle2_period: PDSA 1: 8 January to 20 February 2023 (endline n=60); PDSA 2: September 2024 (baseline n=33, endline n=36)
cycle2_result: Complete assessment rose to 18.3% after PDSA1 and to 50% after PDSA2 (77.8% if haemoglobin testing excluded); danger sign assessment rose to 88.3% then 97.2%; cough screening rose to 90.0% then 100%; diarrhoea assessment rose to 76.7% then 94.5%; fever assessment rose to 88.3% then 91.7%; ear problem assessment rose to 63.3% then 88.9%; malnutrition assessment rose to 41.7% then 94.4%; haemoglobin testing rose to 48.3% then 69.4%; immunisation documentation rose to 61.7% then 83.3%.
other_findings: Haemoglobin testing remained the most commonly missed component, mainly due to caregivers refusing invasive finger-prick testing. Doctors raised concerns that checklist reliance could undermine clinical acumen and increase consultation time in a high-volume setting; sustainability was limited by irregular form printing and frequent rotational turnover of resident doctors. No control group was used.

topic: Cardiac arrest prevention in paediatric intensive care
title: Quality improvement: prevention of cardiac arrest in children with heart disease on the paediatric intensive care unit.
standard: Cardiac arrest prevention (CAP) bundle modelled on the North American Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium (PC4) collaborative programme; local target of reducing cardiac arrest incidence by over 33%
finding: cardiac arrest incidence 6.2% (28/449) overall; 5.2% in surgical admissions, 9% in medical admissions
change: A comprehensive cardiac arrest prevention bundle: proactive high-risk patient identification, twice-daily safety huddles, bedside pre-prepared low-dose epinephrine, prospective adverse event data collection with risk-adjusted process monitoring (RSPRT charts), and formal multidisciplinary arrest review meetings
setting: A 31-bed tertiary mixed paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) within a 320-bed children's hospital, Birmingham
cycle1_result: cardiac arrest incidence 6.2% (28/449) overall; 5.2% in surgical admissions, 9% in medical admissions
intervention: A comprehensive cardiac arrest prevention bundle: proactive high-risk patient identification, twice-daily safety huddles, bedside pre-prepared low-dose epinephrine, prospective adverse event data collection with risk-adjusted process monitoring (RSPRT charts), and formal multidisciplinary arrest review meetings
cycle2_result: overall cardiac arrest incidence fell to 4.4% (29/664), a 30% relative reduction (target 33%, not quite met, p=0.212); in the surgical cohort, RSPRT monitoring showed a statistically significant 'halving' of risk-adjusted cardiac arrest rate (special cause variation) within fewer than 200 admissions
other_findings: No significant improvement was seen in cardiac medical admissions (arrest rate 9% vs 8%, with continued 'doubling' boundary crossings on RSPRT), with only 16.1% of medical admissions enrolled in the bundle versus 29.1% of surgical admissions; ECMO/ECPR utilisation did not significantly change; the UK PRAiS2 mortality model showed reasonable but inferior correlation with cardiac arrest risk compared with the PC4 algorithm (AUC 0.802 vs 0.846).

title: Redesigning care to meet national recommendation of four or more yearly clinic visits in patients with cystic fibrosis
standard: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation recommendation of at least 4 clinic visits per year (every 3 months); project target of 90% or greater attendance
finding: 35% of patients attended clinic 4 or more times a year in 2004, rising to 56% in 2005 (CF Foundation Registry data)
change: Redesigned scheduling system, timely rescheduling of missed appointments, and a process to monitor attendance
setting: Arkansas Children's Hospital, CF Foundation Learning and Leadership Collaborative
cycle1_result: 35% of patients attended clinic 4 or more times a year in 2004, rising to 56% in 2005 (CF Foundation Registry data)
intervention: Redesigned scheduling system, timely rescheduling of missed appointments, and a process to monitor attendance
cycle2_result: Percentage of patients attending clinic 4 or more times a year reached the goal of 90% in 2012
other_findings: Improvements were also noted in the number of patients with a BMI/weight-for-length centile of 25 or greater, potentially related to more frequent clinic attendance.
authors: Berlinski A; Chambers M; Willis L; Homa K; Com G
citation: Berlinski A, Chambers M, Willis L, Homa K, Com G. Redesigning care to meet national recommendation of four or more yearly clinic visits in patients with cystic fibrosis. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2014;23(Suppl 1):i42-i49. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2013-002345.

title: The effect of a clinical pharmacist-led training programme on intravenous medication errors: a controlled before and after study
standard: not reported
finding: Prevalence of clinically relevant erroneous doses was 64.0% on the ICU (intervention ward) and 57.9% on the PSU (control ward)
change: Clinical pharmacist-led training programme including lectures, practical ward-based teaching sessions and protocols/guidelines, delivered by a pharmacist and a nurse
setting: Intensive care unit (intervention) and post-surgical unit (control)
cycle1_result: Prevalence of clinically relevant erroneous doses was 64.0% on the ICU (intervention ward) and 57.9% on the PSU (control ward)
intervention: Clinical pharmacist-led training programme including lectures, practical ward-based teaching sessions and protocols/guidelines, delivered by a pharmacist and a nurse
cycle2_result: Erroneous dose prevalence decreased significantly on the intervention ward to 48.9% (p<0.001) but was unchanged on the control ward (64.1%, p=0.132); intervention ward doses were 2.60 times less likely to have clinically relevant errors (95% CI 1.27-5.31, p=0.013)
other_findings: The error rate remained relatively high even after the intervention; authors call for further quality improvement strategies including changes to the working environment and promoting a safety culture.
authors: Nguyen H; Pham H; Vo D; Nguyen T; van den Heuvel E; Haaijer-Ruskamp F; Taxis K
citation: Nguyen H, Pham H, Vo D, Nguyen T, van den Heuvel E, Haaijer-Ruskamp F, et al.. The effect of a clinical pharmacist-led training programme on intravenous medication errors: a controlled before and after study. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2013;23(4):319-324. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2013-002357.

topic: Cystic fibrosis clinical outcomes quality improvement
title: The impact of transforming healthcare delivery on cystic fibrosis outcomes: a decade of quality improvement at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital
standard: Cystic Fibrosis Foundation National Patient Registry benchmarks (below-average outcomes identified against registry norms)
finding: Median forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) was 81.7% predicted; median body mass index was at the 35th centile
change: Decade-long comprehensive quality improvement programme (2001-2010): sharing outcomes data, a QI steering committee with parent/hospital leadership, real-time data management, restructured chart conference and individualised inpatient schedules, an influenza vaccination campaign, redesigned infection control, best-practice airway-clearance guidelines, evidence-based clinical algorithms and added care-team members
setting: Cincinnati Children's Hospital
cycle1_result: Median forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) was 81.7% predicted; median body mass index was at the 35th centile
intervention: Decade-long comprehensive quality improvement programme (2001-2010): sharing outcomes data, a QI steering committee with parent/hospital leadership, real-time data management, restructured chart conference and individualised inpatient schedules, an influenza vaccination campaign, redesigned infection control, best-practice airway-clearance guidelines, evidence-based clinical algorithms and added care-team members
cycle2_result: Median FEV1 increased to 100.1% predicted; median body mass index increased to the 55th centile
other_findings: not reported
authors: Siracusa C; Weiland J; Acton J; Chima A; Chini B; Hoberman A; Wetzel J; Amin R; McPhail G
citation: Siracusa C, Weiland J, Acton J, Chima A, Chini B, Hoberman A, et al.. The impact of transforming healthcare delivery on cystic fibrosis outcomes: a decade of quality improvement at Cincinnati Children’s Hospital. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2014;23(Suppl 1):i56-i63. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2013-002361.

topic: Cystic fibrosis transition from paediatric to adult care
title: Improving transition from paediatric to adult cystic fibrosis care: programme implementation and evaluation
standard: not reported
finding: Discussion of transition with families occurred in 35% of encounters at the paediatric centre
change: Multi-phase transition curriculum, agreed care standards, standardised patient transfer protocols, and quarterly paediatric-adult team meetings sustained over 4 years
setting: Paediatric and adult cystic fibrosis centres
cycle1_result: Discussion of transition with families occurred in 35% of encounters at the paediatric centre
intervention: Multi-phase transition curriculum, agreed care standards, standardised patient transfer protocols, and quarterly paediatric-adult team meetings sustained over 4 years
cycle2_result: Discussion of transition with families increased to 73% (p<0.001), with a trend towards improved Transition Readiness Assessment Questionnaire self-advocacy scores and decreased in-hospital transfer
other_findings: Quarterly meetings between paediatric and adult teams continued for 4 years, sustaining the programme and harmonising care across centres.
authors: Okumura M; Ong T; Dawson D; Nielson D; Lewis N; Richards M; Brindis C; Kleinhenz M
citation: Okumura M, Ong T, Dawson D, Nielson D, Lewis N, Richards M, et al.. Improving transition from paediatric to adult cystic fibrosis care: programme implementation and evaluation. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2014;23(Suppl 1):i64-i72. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2013-002364.

title: Using quality improvement to optimise paediatric discharge efficiency
standard: Target: increase the percentage of patients discharged within 2 hours of meeting discharge criteria from 42% to 80%
finding: 42% of patients were discharged within 2 hours of meeting discharge criteria
change: Multidisciplinary development of standardised discharge criteria for 11 common diagnoses embedded in electronic medical record order sets, EMR time-stamping, pharmacy process redesign, improved subspecialty consult timeliness and feedback to frontline staff
setting: Hospital Medicine service, paediatric hospital
cycle1_result: 42% of patients were discharged within 2 hours of meeting discharge criteria
intervention: Multidisciplinary development of standardised discharge criteria for 11 common diagnoses embedded in electronic medical record order sets, EMR time-stamping, pharmacy process redesign, improved subspecialty consult timeliness and feedback to frontline staff
cycle2_result: Percentage discharged within 2 hours improved to 80%; median length of stay decreased from 1.56 to 1.44 days (p=0.01) without increased readmissions (4.60% to 4.21%, p=0.24)
other_findings: The 12-month rolling average census increased from 36.4 to 42.9 (an 18% increase in occupancy) without adverse effect on patient flow.
authors: White C; Statile A; White D; Elkeeb D; Tucker K; Herzog D; Warrick S; Warrick D; Hausfeld J; Schondelmeyer A; Schoettker P; Kiessling P; Farrell M; Kotagal U; Ryckman F
citation: White C, Statile A, White D, Elkeeb D, Tucker K, Herzog D, et al.. Using quality improvement to optimise paediatric discharge efficiency. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2014;23(5):428-436. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2013-002556.

topic: Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundle adherence and mortality
title: GUIDELINE BUNDLES ADHERENCE AND MORTALITY IN SEVERE SEPSIS AND SEPTIC SHOCK: RESULTS OF A NATIONAL PATIENT SAFETY PROGRAM IN THE NETHERLANDS
standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundles completed within 6 and 24 hours of ICU admission; target individual bundle adherence >80% and relative mortality reduction of at least 15% (absolute reduction 5.2%) by end of 2012
finding: In-hospital mortality among severe sepsis and septic shock ICU patients was 34.8%
change: National programme to screen for severe sepsis and septic shock and implement Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundles within 6 and 24 hours of ICU admission
setting: 82 ICUs (52 participating, 30 non-participating)
cycle1_n: 213677 total ICU patients (8387 severe sepsis at participating ICUs, 8031 at non-participating ICUs)
cycle1_result: In-hospital mortality among severe sepsis and septic shock ICU patients was 34.8%
intervention: National programme to screen for severe sepsis and septic shock and implement Surviving Sepsis Campaign bundles within 6 and 24 hours of ICU admission
cycle2_result: Bundle target adherence improved (adjusted OR per month 1.024, 95% CI 1.016-1.031) and in-hospital mortality decreased (adjusted OR per month 0.992, 95% CI 0.986-0.997), equivalent to 5.8% absolute and 16.7% relative mortality reduction over 3.5 years, in participating ICUs only
other_findings: Mortality did not change in non-screened patients at participating ICUs, nor in sepsis or non-sepsis patients at non-participating ICUs, supporting a direct programme effect.
authors: van Zanten A
citation: van Zanten A. GUIDELINE BUNDLES ADHERENCE AND MORTALITY IN SEVERE SEPSIS AND SEPTIC SHOCK: RESULTS OF A NATIONAL PATIENT SAFETY PROGRAM IN THE NETHERLANDS. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2014;23(4):346.1-346. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2014-002893.1.

topic: Perioperative quality indicator feedback to anaesthetists
title: ENHANCED FEEDBACK FROM PERIOPERATIVE QUALITY INDICATORS: STUDYING THE IMPACT OF A COMPLEX QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INTERVENTION
standard: not reported
finding: Preliminary audits demonstrated variations in patient temperature, pain and nausea measures; mapping showed delays in patient transfer from the Post Anaesthetic Care Unit were stretching resources
change: Continuous monitoring and feedback initiative using process mapping and statistical process control, with monthly ward reports and personalised monthly performance reports to individual consultant anaesthetists
setting: Post Anaesthetic Care Unit, large academic teaching hospital
cycle1_result: Preliminary audits demonstrated variations in patient temperature, pain and nausea measures; mapping showed delays in patient transfer from the Post Anaesthetic Care Unit were stretching resources
intervention: Continuous monitoring and feedback initiative using process mapping and statistical process control, with monthly ward reports and personalised monthly performance reports to individual consultant anaesthetists
cycle2_result: Interrupted time series analysis showed a significant increase in mean patient temperature on arrival in recovery associated with introduction of temperature feedback; large variation in transfer times between wards was attributable to bed management and staffing; pain and nausea scores remained relatively stable at the department level
other_findings: Qualitative and quantitative analysis showed high perceived value and acceptability of the feedback initiative among anaesthetists; authors note routine hospital governance data may be too high-level for quality improvement purposes.
authors: Benn J; D'Lima D; Moore J; Wei I; Arnold G
citation: Benn J, D'Lima D, Moore J, Wei I, Arnold G. ENHANCED FEEDBACK FROM PERIOPERATIVE QUALITY INDICATORS: STUDYING THE IMPACT OF A COMPLEX QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INTERVENTION. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2014;23(4):351-352. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2014-002893.10.

topic: Adverse event identification using an augmented trigger tool
title: Application of a trigger tool in near real time to inform quality improvement activities: a prospective study in a general medicine ward
standard: not reported
finding: 14 patients (10%, 95% CI 5-15%) experienced at least one preventable adverse event; 32 patients (23%, 95% CI 16-30%) experienced at least one potential adverse event; the most common contributing factors were policy/procedural problems (37%), communication/teamwork problems (34%) and medication process problems (23%)
setting: General medicine ward, tertiary academic medical centre
cycle1_result: 14 patients (10%, 95% CI 5-15%) experienced at least one preventable adverse event; 32 patients (23%, 95% CI 16-30%) experienced at least one potential adverse event; the most common contributing factors were policy/procedural problems (37%), communication/teamwork problems (34%) and medication process problems (23%)
other_findings: Contributing factor categories contained many distinct subcategories, suggesting broad categories are too heterogeneous to inform specific interventions directly.
authors: Wong B; Dyal S; Etchells E; Knowles S; Gerard L; Diamantouros A; Mehta R; Liu B; Baker G; Shojania K
citation: Wong B, Dyal S, Etchells E, Knowles S, Gerard L, Diamantouros A, et al.. Application of a trigger tool in near real time to inform quality improvement activities: a prospective study in a general medicine ward. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;24(4):272-281. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2014-003432.

topic: Early sepsis care compliance in the emergency department
title: A quality improvement project to improve early sepsis care in the emergency department
standard: Recommended sepsis management bundle: serum lactate measured in the emergency department, 2L intravenous fluid within 2 hours of triage, antibiotics within 3 hours of triage, and blood cultures drawn before antibiotic administration
finding: Overall bundle compliance was 28%; mortality rate for ED sepsis admissions was 13.3%
change: Three-tiered intervention: a nurse-driven sepsis screening and management protocol, a computer-assisted 'Sepsis Alert' pop-up in the electronic medical record, and automated suggested sepsis-specific order sets
setting: Large quaternary care referral hospital emergency department
cycle1_result: Overall bundle compliance was 28%; mortality rate for ED sepsis admissions was 13.3%
intervention: Three-tiered intervention: a nurse-driven sepsis screening and management protocol, a computer-assisted 'Sepsis Alert' pop-up in the electronic medical record, and automated suggested sepsis-specific order sets
cycle2_result: Overall bundle compliance increased 154% to 71% (p<0.001); mortality fell to 11.1% after implementation (p=0.230), and to 9.3% in the last two quarters (p=0.107)
other_findings: Bundle and intravenous fluid compliance increased significantly after the sepsis initiative launch; bundle and antibiotic compliance further increased after order set implementation; the mortality reduction was not statistically significant.
authors: Gatewood M; Wemple M; Greco S; Kritek P; Durvasula R
citation: Gatewood M, Wemple M, Greco S, Kritek P, Durvasula R. A quality improvement project to improve early sepsis care in the emergency department. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;24(12):787-795. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2014-003552.

topic: Rapid sequence intubation safety in paediatric emergency department
title: Reducing the incidence of oxyhaemoglobin desaturation during rapid sequence intubation in a paediatric emergency department
standard: not reported
finding: Frequency of oxyhaemoglobin desaturation (SpO2<90%) during rapid sequence intubation was 33%
change: Simultaneous testing of an RSI checklist, a pilot/copilot model for checklist execution, a video laryngoscope, and restricting laryngoscopy to specific providers, refined through plan-do-study-act cycles
setting: High-volume academic paediatric emergency department
cycle1_result: Frequency of oxyhaemoglobin desaturation (SpO2<90%) during rapid sequence intubation was 33%
intervention: Simultaneous testing of an RSI checklist, a pilot/copilot model for checklist execution, a video laryngoscope, and restricting laryngoscopy to specific providers, refined through plan-do-study-act cycles
cycle2_result: Frequency of desaturation fell to 16% (50% lower than historical); when all six key processes were performed, only 6% of patients experienced desaturation; special cause variation seen on G-charts for 3 of 6 key processes plus attempt failure and desaturation
other_findings: not reported
authors: Kerrey B; Mittiga M; Rinderknecht A; Varadarajan K; Dyas J; Geis G; Luria J; Frey M; Jablonski T; Iyer S
citation: Kerrey B, Mittiga M, Rinderknecht A, Varadarajan K, Dyas J, Geis G, et al.. Reducing the incidence of oxyhaemoglobin desaturation during rapid sequence intubation in a paediatric emergency department. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;24(11):709-717. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2014-003713.

topic: Pneumonia readmission quality flagging (Potentially Preventable Readmissions)
title: Do pneumonia readmissions flagged as potentially preventable by the 3M PPR software have more process of care problems? A cross-sectional observational study
standard: not reported
finding: Total quality-of-care scores were slightly higher, though non-significantly, among PPR-yes cases (71.2+/-8.7) than PPR-no cases (65.8+/-11.5), p=0.14, out of a maximum score of 100
setting: Veterans Health Administration hospitals
cycle1_result: Total quality-of-care scores were slightly higher, though non-significantly, among PPR-yes cases (71.2+/-8.7) than PPR-no cases (65.8+/-11.5), p=0.14, out of a maximum score of 100
other_findings: 11278 pneumonia readmissions were identified (readmission rate 16.5%), 77% flagged as PPR-yes; PPR categorisation did not produce the expected quality-of-care findings.
authors: Borzecki A; Chen Q; Restuccia J; Mull H; Shwartz M; Gupta K; Hanchate A; Strymish J; Rosen A
citation: Borzecki A, Chen Q, Restuccia J, Mull H, Shwartz M, Gupta K, et al.. Do pneumonia readmissions flagged as potentially preventable by the 3M PPR software have more process of care problems? A cross-sectional observational study. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;24(12):753-763. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2014-003911.

topic: Clinician experience of audit and feedback in the ICU
title: A qualitative study of the variable effects of audit and feedback in the ICU
standard: not reported
finding: not reported (qualitative grounded theory study of clinicians' experience of audit and feedback; no compliance or outcome data reported)
setting: Five academic and five community ICUs
cycle1_result: not reported (qualitative grounded theory study of clinicians' experience of audit and feedback; no compliance or outcome data reported)
other_findings: Clinicians experienced audit and feedback as fragmented, untimely, incomplete and insufficiently transparent; suggestions included peer-to-peer discussions, timely actionable feedback and greater senior management engagement.
authors: Sinuff T; Muscedere J; Rozmovits L; Dale C; Scales D

topic: Appropriate use of continuous cardiac monitoring
title: Implementing an institution-wide quality improvement policy to ensure appropriate use of continuous cardiac monitoring: a mixed-methods retrospective data analysis and direct observation study
standard: American Heart Association guidelines limiting continuous cardiac monitoring to clinically indicated patients
finding: Cardiac monitoring rate 0.535 per patient day; monitored transport rate 0.216 per patient day; emergency department boarding rate 5.5%; false alarms 18.8%
change: Institution-wide continuous cardiac monitoring policy based on AHA guidelines, developed by a cross-functional alarm management task force with leadership support
setting: Tertiary-care hospital
cycle1_period: before policy implementation, not otherwise stated
cycle1_result: Cardiac monitoring rate 0.535 per patient day; monitored transport rate 0.216 per patient day; emergency department boarding rate 5.5%; false alarms 18.8%
intervention: Institution-wide continuous cardiac monitoring policy based on AHA guidelines, developed by a cross-functional alarm management task force with leadership support
cycle2_period: after policy implementation, not otherwise stated
cycle2_result: Cardiac monitoring rate decreased 53.2% to 0.251 per patient day (p<0.001); monitored transport rate decreased 15.5% to 0.182 (p<0.001); ED boarding rate decreased 36.6% to 3.5% (p<0.001); false alarms decreased to 9.6% (p<0.001)
other_findings: Neither length of stay nor mortality changed significantly after policy implementation.
authors: Rayo M; Mansfield J; Eiferman D; Mignery T; White S; Moffatt-Bruce S
citation: Rayo M, Mansfield J, Eiferman D, Mignery T, White S, Moffatt-Bruce S. Implementing an institution-wide quality improvement policy to ensure appropriate use of continuous cardiac monitoring: a mixed-methods retrospective data analysis and direct observation study. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;25(10):796-802. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2015-004137.

topic: HIV antiretroviral therapy uptake and viral suppression quality improvement
title: Implementation of HIV treatment as prevention strategy in 17 Canadian sites: immediate and sustained outcomes from a 35-month Quality Improvement Collaborative
standard: Global targets for antiretroviral therapy (ART) coverage and viral suppression; chronic care model and HIV care and treatment guidelines
finding: 73% of HIV-diagnosed people in the intervention setting were on ART and 49% were achieving viral suppression in 2011
change: 35-month Breakthrough Series Quality Improvement Collaborative implementing the chronic care model and HIV care/treatment guidelines, with monthly implementation scoring
setting: 17 HIV care sites
cycle1_n: 2296 (median pooled HIV patient population per site)
cycle1_result: 73% of HIV-diagnosed people in the intervention setting were on ART and 49% were achieving viral suppression in 2011
intervention: 35-month Breakthrough Series Quality Improvement Collaborative implementing the chronic care model and HIV care/treatment guidelines, with monthly implementation scoring
cycle2_result: Comprehensive chronic care model implementation with evidence of improvement was achieved by 29% of sites; sustained improvement was observed in patient engagement (88.8-90.4%), ART uptake among those in need (92.9-94.8%), and ART uptake/viral suppression (57.3-78.4%), all p<0.05
other_findings: not reported
authors: Clarke C; Cheng T; Reims K; Steinbock C; Thumath M; Milligan R; Barrios R
citation: Clarke C, Cheng T, Reims K, Steinbock C, Thumath M, Milligan R, et al.. Implementation of HIV treatment as prevention strategy in 17 Canadian sites: immediate and sustained outcomes from a 35-month Quality Improvement Collaborative. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;25(5):345-354. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2015-004269.

topic: Surgical safety checklist compliance with migrated leadership
title: A ‘paperless’ wall-mounted surgical safety checklist with migrated leadership can improve compliance and team engagement
standard: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist domain and item administration compliance
finding: Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out administered in 96%, 99% and 22% of cases; relevant checklist items administered in 60%, 84% and 80% of cases respectively; two-subteam engagement at Sign In 40%; three-subteam engagement at Time Out 15% and Sign Out 9%
change: Introduction of a wall-mounted paperless checklist with migrated process leadership (Sign In led by anaesthesia, Time Out by surgery, Sign Out by nursing)
setting: Operating room suite
cycle1_result: Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out administered in 96%, 99% and 22% of cases; relevant checklist items administered in 60%, 84% and 80% of cases respectively; two-subteam engagement at Sign In 40%; three-subteam engagement at Time Out 15% and Sign Out 9%
intervention: Introduction of a wall-mounted paperless checklist with migrated process leadership (Sign In led by anaesthesia, Time Out by surgery, Sign Out by nursing)
cycle2_result: Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out administered in 98%, 99% and 84% of cases (p=0.69, 1.00, <0.001); relevant items administered in 92%, 93% and 99% (p<0.001 for all); two-subteam engagement at Sign In 94%; three-subteam engagement at Time Out 92% and Sign Out 25% (p<0.001 for all)
other_findings: The paradigm change was relatively simple and inexpensive.
authors: Ong A; Devcich D; Hannam J; Lee T; Merry A; Mitchell S
citation: Ong A, Devcich D, Hannam J, Lee T, Merry A, Mitchell S. A ‘paperless’ wall-mounted surgical safety checklist with migrated leadership can improve compliance and team engagement. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;25(12):971-976. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2015-004545.

cycle1_result: not reported
intervention: Feedback Intervention Theory (FIT)-based design of audit and feedback interventions: a personalised one-on-one intervention to reduce inappropriate CAUTI diagnosis, and a web-based report-style feedback intervention for hypertension care.

topic: Celiac disease follow-up serology testing adherence
title: STANDARDIZATION AND IMPROVEMENT IN PEDIATRIC CELIAC CARE
standard: NASPGHAN celiac disease guidelines recommending repeat serology testing 6 months after diagnosis; project target of 90% having repeat testing within 9 months by December 2015
finding: 54.8% of patients had repeat serology testing within 9 months of diagnosis; baseline follow-up clinic visit within 9 months (Q4 2012-Q4 2013) was 82.2%
change: Creation of a tracking registry, implementation of a local standard of care, practitioner educational sessions, reporting of practitioner adherence, and improved administrative staff utilisation to identify patients needing follow-up
setting: not reported
cycle1_result: 54.8% of patients had repeat serology testing within 9 months of diagnosis; baseline follow-up clinic visit within 9 months (Q4 2012-Q4 2013) was 82.2%
intervention: Creation of a tracking registry, implementation of a local standard of care, practitioner educational sessions, reporting of practitioner adherence, and improved administrative staff utilisation to identify patients needing follow-up
cycle2_result: Repeat serology testing within 9 months increased to 72.8% (p=0.000); follow-up clinic visit within 9 months increased to 96.6% (Q1 2014-Q2 2015, p=0.000)
other_findings: The project's target of 90% for repeat serology testing had not yet been reached by the reported data (72.8% achieved).
authors: Boyle B; Ediger T; Trout A; Wegener N; Ramachandran S; Cummings M; Reber S; Hill I
citation: Boyle B, Ediger T, Trout A, Wegener N, Ramachandran S, Cummings M, et al.. STANDARDIZATION AND IMPROVEMENT IN PEDIATRIC CELIAC CARE. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;24(11):719.1-719. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2015-ihiabstracts.1.

title: REDUCING THE INCIDENCE OF CLABSI IN LATIN AMERICAN ICUS: A MULTI-COUNTRY QUALITY IMPROVEMENT COLLABORATIVE. PRELIMINARY RESULTS FROM THE SECOND PHASE
standard: 'Goodbye Bacteremia' campaign target: reduce central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) rate by 50% or to less than 2 episodes per 1000 central line days within 12 months
finding: Baseline mean CLABSI rate 2.67 per 1000 central line days; insertion bundle compliance 65.55%; maintenance bundle compliance 82.56%
change: Quality improvement collaborative promoting evidence-based bundles of care for central line insertion and maintenance, with virtual bi-weekly learning sessions and continuous feedback, June 2014 to June 2015
setting: 100 ICUs across six Latin American countries
cycle1_result: Baseline mean CLABSI rate 2.67 per 1000 central line days; insertion bundle compliance 65.55%; maintenance bundle compliance 82.56%
intervention: Quality improvement collaborative promoting evidence-based bundles of care for central line insertion and maintenance, with virtual bi-weekly learning sessions and continuous feedback, June 2014 to June 2015
cycle2_result: CLABSI rate reduced 24.34% to a mean of 2.02 per 1000 central line days (median rate zero throughout); insertion bundle compliance increased 49.49% to 97.99%; maintenance bundle compliance increased 14.86% to 94.83%
other_findings: These were preliminary results from the second phase of the campaign; the target of under 2 episodes per 1000 line days was essentially met (2.02).
authors: Arrieta J; Delgado P; Orrego C; Giuffre C; Rodríguez V; Elorrio E
citation: Arrieta J, Delgado P, Orrego C, Giuffre C, Rodríguez V, Elorrio E. REDUCING THE INCIDENCE OF CLABSI IN LATIN AMERICAN ICUS: A MULTI-COUNTRY QUALITY IMPROVEMENT COLLABORATIVE. PRELIMINARY RESULTS FROM THE SECOND PHASE. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;24(11):728.2-729. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2015-ihiabstracts.14.

topic: Severe intraventricular haemorrhage reduction in preterm infants
title: REDUCING INTRAVENTRICULAR HEMORRHAGE IN A LEVEL III NEONATAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT
standard: Project target: reduce severe intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH) incidence in infants born under 30 weeks from 8% to 4% between October 2014 and December 2015
finding: Average monthly rate of severe IVH was 8.3%
change: Multidisciplinary bundle: midline head positioning during the first week of life, a minimal handling bundle with multidisciplinary admission huddle, a web-based IVH risk calculator, and standardised infusion rates for boluses/blood products
setting: Level III neonatal intensive care unit
cycle1_result: Average monthly rate of severe IVH was 8.3%
intervention: Multidisciplinary bundle: midline head positioning during the first week of life, a minimal handling bundle with multidisciplinary admission huddle, a web-based IVH risk calculator, and standardised infusion rates for boluses/blood products
cycle2_result: Average monthly rate of severe IVH decreased to 5.1%; midline head positioning and admission huddle compliance reached 100% for infants under 30 weeks
other_findings: The target of 4% had not yet been reached by the reported data (5.1% achieved); future planned interventions include delayed cord clamping and prophylactic indomethacin.
authors: Christ L; Barber J; Murray A; Dunleavy M; Stoller J; Taha D; Brown-Jackson L; McElroy M; Posencheg M
citation: Christ L, Barber J, Murray A, Dunleavy M, Stoller J, Taha D, et al.. REDUCING INTRAVENTRICULAR HEMORRHAGE IN A LEVEL III NEONATAL INTENSIVE CARE UNIT. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2015;24(11):731-732. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2015-ihiabstracts.17.

topic: Multidisciplinary rounds communication of patient daily goals
title: IMPROVING COMMUNICATION DURING CARDIAC INTENSIVE CARE UNIT MULTIDISCIPLINARY ROUNDS THROUGH VISUAL DISPLAY OF PATIENT DAILY GOALS
standard: not reported
finding: Baseline percent agreement on patient daily goals among care team members was 62%; parent selection of the best possible satisfaction score was 19% at baseline (mean satisfaction 4.6 out of 6)
change: Implementation of a daily patient goal write-down/read-back process using a whiteboard and later a laminated sheet, developed and refined through multiple plan-do-study-act cycles
