title: Adherence to guideline-recommended HbA1c testing frequency and better outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes: a 5-year retrospective cohort study in Australian general practice
standard: Australian guidelines recommending 6-monthly HbA1c testing (3-monthly if inadequate control)
finding: Overall median HbA1c testing frequency was 1.6 tests per year, with an overall adherence rate of 50%; high adherence was associated with lower risk of chronic kidney disease (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.18-0.99) than low adherence; no association found with ischaemic heart disease
setting: Approximately 250 Australian general practices
cycle1_result: Overall median HbA1c testing frequency was 1.6 tests per year, with an overall adherence rate of 50%; high adherence was associated with lower risk of chronic kidney disease (OR 0.42, 95% CI 0.18-0.99) than low adherence; no association found with ischaemic heart disease
other_findings: HbA1c levels in low-adherence patients gradually increased or remained uncontrolled, while high-adherence patients' levels remained controlled or improved over time.
authors: Imai C; Li L; Hardie R; Georgiou A
citation: Imai C, Li L, Hardie R, Georgiou A. Adherence to guideline-recommended HbA1c testing frequency and better outcomes in patients with type 2 diabetes: a 5-year retrospective cohort study in Australian general practice. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2021;30(9):706-714. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2020-012026.

topic: Reducing unnecessary urine culturing and antibiotic prescribing in long-term care
title: Virtual learning collaboratives to improve urine culturing and antibiotic prescribing in long-term care: controlled before-and-after study
standard: Quality improvement programme to reduce unnecessary urine culturing and antibiotic overprescribing for presumed UTIs
finding: Baseline rates of urine culturing and urinary antibiotic prescriptions per 1000 resident days.
change: Virtual learning collaborative sessions (May-August 2018) providing orientation and implementation guidance for a QI programme, compared with propensity-matched controls.
setting: 45 long-term care homes across five regions
cycle1_result: Baseline rates of urine culturing and urinary antibiotic prescriptions per 1000 resident days.
intervention: Virtual learning collaborative sessions (May-August 2018) providing orientation and implementation guidance for a QI programme, compared with propensity-matched controls.
cycle2_result: Differential reductions of 19% in urine culturing and 13% in urinary antibiotic prescriptions per 1000 resident days vs matched controls (p<0.0001); no significant change in ED visits, hospital admissions or mortality.
other_findings: Controlled before-and-after study with moderate adherence to the programme model.
authors: Chambers A; Chen C; Brown K; Daneman N; Langford B; Leung V; Adomako K; Schwartz K; Moore J; Quirk J; MacFarlane S; Cronsberry T; Garber G
citation: Chambers A, Chen C, Brown K, Daneman N, Langford B, Leung V, et al.. Virtual learning collaboratives to improve urine culturing and antibiotic prescribing in long-term care: controlled before-and-after study. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2021;31(2):94-104. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2020-012226.

topic: Paediatric asthma care guideline adherence sustainability
title: Sustainability of paediatric asthma care quality in community hospitals after ending a national quality improvement collaborative
standard: Paediatric asthma pathway guideline-adherence measures (early bronchodilator via MDI, secondhand-smoke screening, smoking-cessation referral)
finding: Guideline adherence improved 29% during the collaborative (vs 15% in hospitals that dropped out, p=0.02); early MDI administration 81%
change: National Pathways for Improving Paediatric Asthma Care (PIPA) QI collaborative; access to pathways, education, mobile app and mentorship continued after the collaborative ended, but active coaching stopped
setting: 23 community hospitals (of 45 in the PIPA collaborative), USA
cycle1_result: Guideline adherence improved 29% during the collaborative (vs 15% in hospitals that dropped out, p=0.02); early MDI administration 81%
intervention: National Pathways for Improving Paediatric Asthma Care (PIPA) QI collaborative; access to pathways, education, mobile app and mentorship continued after the collaborative ended, but active coaching stopped
cycle2_period: sustainability monitoring, 21-24 months from collaborative start
cycle2_result: Early MDI administration fell from 81% to 68% (adjusted OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.15 to 0.42); smoking-cessation referral rate declined (adjusted OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.75 to 0.98); no significant change in length of stay or secondhand-smoke screening
other_findings: The end of the collaborative was associated with concerning declines in two of the four guideline-adherence measures.
authors: Schechter S; Jaladanki S; Rodean J; Jennings B; Genies M; Cabana M; Kaiser S
citation: Schechter S, Jaladanki S, Rodean J, Jennings B, Genies M, Cabana M, et al.. Sustainability of paediatric asthma care quality in community hospitals after ending a national quality improvement collaborative. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2021;30(11):876-883. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2020-012292.

topic: Racial disparities in severe maternal morbidity from haemorrhage
title: Examining the effect of quality improvement initiatives on decreasing racial disparities in maternal morbidity
standard: not reported
finding: Statistically significant disparity in severe maternal morbidity from haemorrhage between Black and White women (p<0.001); rate in Black women 45.5%
change: Stratification of monitoring data by race/ethnicity presented as run charts at monthly meetings, an obstetric haemorrhage patient-safety bundle, and health-equity-focused case reviews of adverse outcomes
setting: Single hospital, Baylor College of Medicine/Texas Children's Hospital, USA
cycle1_result: Statistically significant disparity in severe maternal morbidity from haemorrhage between Black and White women (p<0.001); rate in Black women 45.5%
intervention: Stratification of monitoring data by race/ethnicity presented as run charts at monthly meetings, an obstetric haemorrhage patient-safety bundle, and health-equity-focused case reviews of adverse outcomes
cycle2_result: Disparity no longer statistically significant (p=0.138); rate in Black women fell to 31.6% (p=0.011)
other_findings: 13659 deliveries overall: 37% Hispanic, 35% White, 20% Black, 7% Asian, 1% Other.
authors: Davidson C; Denning S; Thorp K; Tyer-Viola L; Belfort M; Sangi-Haghpeykar H; Gandhi M
citation: Davidson C, Denning S, Thorp K, Tyer-Viola L, Belfort M, Sangi-Haghpeykar H, et al.. Examining the effect of quality improvement initiatives on decreasing racial disparities in maternal morbidity. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2022;31(9):670-678. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2021-014225.

title: Repurposing the Ordering of Routine Laboratory Tests in Hospitalised Medical Patients (RePORT): results of a cluster randomised stepped-wedge quality improvement study
standard: not reported
finding: Baseline routine laboratory test ordering rate used as the reference for the reported incidence rate ratio
change: Educational tools and social comparison reports with peer-facilitated discussion sessions, implemented via a stepped-wedge design across 8 units
setting: Eight medical units, University of Calgary/Alberta Health Services, Canada
cycle1_result: Baseline routine laboratory test ordering rate used as the reference for the reported incidence rate ratio
intervention: Educational tools and social comparison reports with peer-facilitated discussion sessions, implemented via a stepped-wedge design across 8 units
cycle2_result: 14% reduction in routine test ordering (incidence rate ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.79 to 0.92); 14% reduction in testing costs; $C1.15 per patient-day savings; 20% increase in routine-test-free patient-days
other_findings: No worsening of patient safety endpoints was noted with the intervention.
authors: Ambasta A; Omodon O; Herring A; Ferrie L; Pokharel S; Mehta A; Liu L; Hews-Girard J; Tam C; Taylor S; Lonergan K; Faris P; Duncan D; Woodhouse D
citation: Ambasta A, Omodon O, Herring A, Ferrie L, Pokharel S, Mehta A, et al.. Repurposing the Ordering of Routine Laboratory Tests in Hospitalised Medical Patients (RePORT): results of a cluster randomised stepped-wedge quality improvement study. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2023;32(9):517-525. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2022-015611.

topic: Variation in primary care investigations before cancer diagnosis
title: Variation in the use of primary care-led investigations prior to a cancer diagnosis: analysis of the National Cancer Diagnosis Audit
standard: not reported
finding: Odds ratio for 97.5th to 2.5th centile practice variation: 4.02 (any investigation), 4.33 (blood test), 3.12 (imaging); after accounting for patient case-mix, the spread increased to 5.61, 6.30 and 3.60 respectively
setting: 1868 general practices (National Cancer Diagnosis Audit 2018)
cycle1_result: Odds ratio for 97.5th to 2.5th centile practice variation: 4.02 (any investigation), 4.33 (blood test), 3.12 (imaging); after accounting for patient case-mix, the spread increased to 5.61, 6.30 and 3.60 respectively
other_findings: Rurality (lower use) and a higher concentration of older patients (higher use) explained some of the observed variation; possible co-existing under-testing and over-testing.
authors: Akter N; Lyratzopoulos G; Swann R; Rubin G; McPhail S; Rafiq M; Aminu A; Zakkak N; Abel G
citation: Akter N, Lyratzopoulos G, Swann R, Rubin G, McPhail S, Rafiq M, et al.. Variation in the use of primary care-led investigations prior to a cancer diagnosis: analysis of the National Cancer Diagnosis Audit. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2024;34(6):367-376. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2024-017264.

topic: Antenatal magnesium sulfate for neonatal neuroprotection uptake
title: Implementation of national guidelines on antenatal magnesium sulfate for neonatal neuroprotection: extended evaluation of the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the National PReCePT Programme in England
standard: NICE guidelines (2015): antenatal magnesium sulfate for mothers in preterm labour under 30 weeks gestation
finding: MgSO4 administration rate was 65.8% in England
change: National PReCePT quality improvement programme rolled out across England from 2018
setting: England (National Neonatal Research Database), compared with Scotland and Wales
cycle1_result: MgSO4 administration rate was 65.8% in England
intervention: National PReCePT quality improvement programme rolled out across England from 2018
cycle2_result: MgSO4 administration rate rose to 85.5%; PReCePT was associated with a 5.8 percentage point improvement (95% CI 2.69-8.86, p<0.001), and 8.67 percentage points for births under 34 weeks (95% CI 6.38-10.96, p<0.001); net monetary benefit of GBP597,000 with 89% probability of cost-effectiveness
other_findings: Most gains occurred in the first 2 years; some decline coincided with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic; England's uptake accelerated compared with Scotland and Wales, where PReCePT was not implemented.
authors: Edwards H; Sillero-Rejon C; McLeod H; Hill E; Opmeer B; Peters C; Odd D; de Vocht F; Luyt K
citation: Edwards H, Sillero-Rejon C, McLeod H, Hill E, Opmeer B, Peters C, et al.. Implementation of national guidelines on antenatal magnesium sulfate for neonatal neuroprotection: extended evaluation of the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of the National PReCePT Programme in England. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2025;35(2):95-105. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2024-017763.

topic: Socioeconomic inequalities in adherence to breast cancer guidelines
title: Socioeconomic inequalities in adherence to clinical practice guidelines and breast cancer survival: a multicentre population-based study in Spain
standard: European and Spanish clinical practice guidelines for breast cancer diagnosis and treatment (16 indicators)
finding: No differences in type of treatment received, but women in lowest SES areas were less likely to undergo sentinel lymph node biopsy, reconstruction after mastectomy, surgery within 30 days of diagnosis, and adjuvant treatment within 6 weeks after surgery; higher risk of death in lower SES areas (HR=1.57, 95% CI 1.04-2.36), attenuated after accounting for guideline adherence.
setting: Six Spanish provinces with population-based cancer registries
cycle1_result: No differences in type of treatment received, but women in lowest SES areas were less likely to undergo sentinel lymph node biopsy, reconstruction after mastectomy, surgery within 30 days of diagnosis, and adjuvant treatment within 6 weeks after surgery; higher risk of death in lower SES areas (HR=1.57, 95% CI 1.04-2.36), attenuated after accounting for guideline adherence.
other_findings: Population-based multicentre audit of guideline adherence linked to survival outcomes by socioeconomic status.
authors: Petrova D; Redondo-Sánchez D; Rodríguez-Barranco M; Marcos-Gragera R; Guevara M; Carulla M; López de Munain A; Vizcaíno A; del Barco S; González-Flores E; Pollán M; Sánchez M
citation: Petrova D, Redondo-Sánchez D, Rodríguez-Barranco M, Marcos-Gragera R, Guevara M, Carulla M, et al.. Socioeconomic inequalities in adherence to clinical practice guidelines and breast cancer survival: a multicentre population-based study in Spain. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2024;34(12):810-823. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2024-017809.

topic: Paediatric sepsis recognition and bundle compliance (equity)
title: Association between Child Opportunity Index and paediatric sepsis recognition and treatment in a large quality improvement collaborative: a retrospective cohort study
standard: IPSO recommended sepsis care bundle (standardised recognition, fluid bolus under 1 hour, antibiotic under 3 hours)
finding: Patients in the Very High Child Opportunity Index (COI) quintile were most likely to be identified via standardised recognition protocols (67.7%) and to receive the recommended care bundle (46%)
change: Improving Pediatric Sepsis Outcomes (IPSO) quality improvement collaborative, using standardisation and shared learning
setting: 24 hospitals in the IPSO collaborative, USA
cycle1_result: Patients in the Very High Child Opportunity Index (COI) quintile were most likely to be identified via standardised recognition protocols (67.7%) and to receive the recommended care bundle (46%)
intervention: Improving Pediatric Sepsis Outcomes (IPSO) quality improvement collaborative, using standardisation and shared learning
cycle2_period: over the course of the study, 2017-2021
cycle2_result: Standardised sepsis recognition improved for all COI quintiles over time; the greatest improvement was among the Very Low COI quintile
other_findings: Disparities in paediatric sepsis care delivery by neighbourhood-level Child Opportunity Index persisted overall.
authors: Rutman L; Richardson T; Auletta J; Balamuth F; Chambers A; Fitzgerald J; Gelvez J; Genzel K; Grant A; Gunnala V; Hakim H; Hueschen L; Kandil S; Larsen G; Lockwood J; Lucey K; Mack E; Madden K; Niedner M; Paul R; Reddy A; Riggs R; Rosen J; Schafer M; Scott H; Wilkes J; Eisenberg M
citation: Rutman L, Richardson T, Auletta J, Balamuth F, Chambers A, Fitzgerald J, et al.. Association between Child Opportunity Index and paediatric sepsis recognition and treatment in a large quality improvement collaborative: a retrospective cohort study. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2025;35(2):106-117. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2024-017844.

topic: Perioperative patient warming pathway (environmental and quality)
title: Implementing and evaluating a low-carbon, high-quality perioperative patient warming pathway
standard: Best-practice environmental warming guidelines, adapted locally
finding: Flannel blanket use averaged 6 per patient; active warming 55% preoperatively and 0% postoperatively; hypothermia incidence 18%
change: Optimised patient warming pathway: expanded pre-warming criteria, preserved forced-air-warming Flex Gown, staff education and training, behaviourally informed strategies, gamification and policy development, over nine PDSA cycles
setting: Tertiary care hospital, University of British Columbia, Canada
cycle1_result: Flannel blanket use averaged 6 per patient; active warming 55% preoperatively and 0% postoperatively; hypothermia incidence 18%
intervention: Optimised patient warming pathway: expanded pre-warming criteria, preserved forced-air-warming Flex Gown, staff education and training, behaviourally informed strategies, gamification and policy development, over nine PDSA cycles
cycle2_result: Flannel blanket use fell to an average of 3 per patient (p<0.01); active warming rose to 80% preoperatively (p=0.04) and 55% postoperatively (p<0.01); hypothermia 15% (p=0.77, not significant)
other_findings: Estimated annual environmental savings of 940339 kg CO2-equivalent and cost savings of $C117978.
authors: Spoyalo K; Rebello T; Schwarz C; Chhipi Shrestha G; Hewage K; Sadiq R; Mondoux S; Walker M; Mayson K; MacNeill A
citation: Spoyalo K, Rebello T, Schwarz C, Chhipi Shrestha G, Hewage K, Sadiq R, et al.. Implementing and evaluating a low-carbon, high-quality perioperative patient warming pathway. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2026;35(4):275-287. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2025-018638.

topic: De-implementation of routine gastric residual checks in NICU
title: When documentation changes but behaviour persists: de-implementation in a neonatal intensive care unit
standard: Local de-implementation protocol eliminating routine gastric residual checks in infants under 1500g birth weight
finding: Routine gastric residual checks were standard practice prior to the initiative (baseline rate not quantified)
change: Multifaceted de-implementation: education, electronic medical record workflow modification, and reinforcement of symptom-based feeding assessment
setting: Level III neonatal intensive care unit, University of Florida College of Medicine-Jacksonville/Nemours Children's Health, USA
cycle1_result: Routine gastric residual checks were standard practice prior to the initiative (baseline rate not quantified)
intervention: Multifaceted de-implementation: education, electronic medical record workflow modification, and reinforcement of symptom-based feeding assessment
cycle2_n: 56 nurses surveyed (24 responded to the relevant item)
cycle2_result: Documented gastric residual checks declined to zero, with no increase in necrotising enterocolitis or feeding intolerance and no improvement in time to full enteral feeds; 7/24 (29%) nurses reported continuing checks without documentation
other_findings: Less-experienced nurses more often feared disciplinary consequences (OR 7.33, 95% CI 1.2 to 45, p<0.05); documented practice diverged from actual bedside behaviour.
authors: Adawi M; Garber M; Nandula P; Kumar V; Alami I; Shah S
citation: Adawi M, Garber M, Nandula P, Kumar V, Alami I, Shah S. When documentation changes but behaviour persists: de-implementation in a neonatal intensive care unit. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2026;35(9):646-648. doi:10.1136/bmjqs-2026-020531.

topic: Antibiotic prescribing variation (fluoroquinolone use in UTI)
title: Inequality in quality? Regional and educational differences in treatment with fluoroquinolone in urinary tract infection of 236 376 Swedish patients
standard: not reported
finding: Fluoroquinolone prescription rate varied from 17.1% to 29.5% across 21 Swedish regions; middle-aged women with 15+ years of schooling more often prescribed fluoroquinolones (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.23 to 1.34)
setting: National outpatient prescribing data, Sweden
cycle1_result: Fluoroquinolone prescription rate varied from 17.1% to 29.5% across 21 Swedish regions; middle-aged women with 15+ years of schooling more often prescribed fluoroquinolones (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.23 to 1.34)
other_findings: Only the first antibiotic prescription in the study period was analysed.
authors: Ljung R; Reimers A; Ericsson Ö; Burström B
citation: Ljung R, Reimers A, Ericsson Ö, Burström B. Inequality in quality? Regional and educational differences in treatment with fluoroquinolone in urinary tract infection of 236 376 Swedish patients. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(1):9-14. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2008.028696.

title: Evaluation of a preoperative team briefing: a new communication routine results in improved clinical practice
standard: Accepted treatment guidelines for timing of preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis
finding: Antibiotic prophylaxis on time in 77.6% of cases
setting: Three institutions, USA
cycle1_result: Antibiotic prophylaxis on time in 77.6% of cases
cycle2_result: Antibiotic prophylaxis on time in 87.6% of cases (p<0.01)
other_findings: Data collection was complicated by great variability in documentation practices between sites and practitioners.
authors: Lingard L; Regehr G; Cartmill C; Orser B; Espin S; Bohnen J; Reznick R; Baker R; Rotstein L; Doran D
citation: Lingard L, Regehr G, Cartmill C, Orser B, Espin S, Bohnen J, et al.. Evaluation of a preoperative team briefing: a new communication routine results in improved clinical practice. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(6):475-482. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2009.032326.

topic: Central venous catheter-related bloodstream infection reduction
title: Elimination of central-venous-catheter-related bloodstream infections from the intensive care unit
standard: Evidence-based CVC insertion/maintenance care bundles; Scottish Patient Safety Programme
finding: Annual CRBSI rate 3.4 per 1000 patient days
change: Infection surveillance plus care-process bundles for CVC insertion and maintenance, supported by educational interventions and statistical process control feedback
setting: Intensive care unit, United Kingdom
cycle1_period: start of a 4-year quality improvement period
cycle1_result: Annual CRBSI rate 3.4 per 1000 patient days
intervention: Infection surveillance plus care-process bundles for CVC insertion and maintenance, supported by educational interventions and statistical process control feedback
cycle2_result: CRBSI rate fell to 0 per 1000 patient days, with zero episodes in the final 19 months
other_findings: The final 18 months of the work were carried out under the national Scottish Patient Safety Programme.
authors: Longmate A; Ellis K; Boyle L; Maher S; Cairns C; Lloyd S; Lang C
citation: Longmate A, Ellis K, Boyle L, Maher S, Cairns C, Lloyd S, et al.. Elimination of central-venous-catheter-related bloodstream infections from the intensive care unit. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(2):174-180. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2009.037200.

title: Addressing the sociotechnical drivers of quality improvement: a case study of post-operative DVT prophylaxis computerised decision support.
standard: Institutional deep venous thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis recommendations
finding: Performance compliance with DVT prophylaxis was 77% pre-implementation; initial computerised decision support menu use rate was only 20%
change: Multidisciplinary team developed and implemented electronic order menus with DVT prophylaxis recommendations, refining the intervention using the sociotechnical 'Fit between Individuals, Task and Technology' (FITT) framework to identify and address barriers (workflow styles, guideline validity concerns, cycle times, risk ambiguity)
setting: Surgical service, Portland Oregon VA Medical Center
cycle1_result: Performance compliance with DVT prophylaxis was 77% pre-implementation; initial computerised decision support menu use rate was only 20%
intervention: Multidisciplinary team developed and implemented electronic order menus with DVT prophylaxis recommendations, refining the intervention using the sociotechnical 'Fit between Individuals, Task and Technology' (FITT) framework to identify and address barriers (workflow styles, guideline validity concerns, cycle times, risk ambiguity)
other_findings: Authors conclude QI teams using health IT must understand clinical/sociotechnical context even in mature electronic health record environments.
authors: Lesselroth BJ; Yang J; McConnachie J; Brenk T; Winterbottom L
citation: Lesselroth BJ, Yang J, McConnachie J, Brenk T, Winterbottom L. Addressing the sociotechnical drivers of quality improvement: a case study of post-operative DVT prophylaxis computerised decision support. BMJ Qual Saf. 2011;20(5):381-389. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2010.042689. PMID: 21209144.

title: Quality of after-hours primary care in the Netherlands: adherence to national guidelines
standard: National guidelines for after-hours prescribing of pain medication and antibiotics, emergency case performance, and specialist referral
finding: Average guideline adherence 77%; referrals 92%, pain medication prescribing 90%, antibiotic prescribing 69%, emergency treatment 71%; antibiotics overprescribed in 42% and underprescribed in 21% of cases
setting: Five general practitioner cooperatives, Netherlands
cycle1_result: Average guideline adherence 77%; referrals 92%, pain medication prescribing 90%, antibiotic prescribing 69%, emergency treatment 71%; antibiotics overprescribed in 42% and underprescribed in 21% of cases
other_findings: Single-cycle cross-sectional audit; no re-audit was reported.
authors: Willekens M; Giesen P; Plat E; Mokkink H; Burgers J; Grol R
citation: Willekens M, Giesen P, Plat E, Mokkink H, Burgers J, Grol R. Quality of after-hours primary care in the Netherlands: adherence to national guidelines. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(3):223-227. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2010.043091.

topic: Improvement collaborative effectiveness across low- and middle-income countries
title: Effectiveness of collaborative improvement: evidence from 27 applications in 12 less-developed and middle-income countries
standard: Locally set compliance standards/indicators for maternal, newborn and child health, HIV/AIDS, family planning, malaria and tuberculosis
finding: Baseline performance was below 50% in two-thirds of charts
change: USAID-funded improvement collaborative approach (1998-2008), adapted for resource-constrained settings
setting: 1338 facility-based teams across 27 improvement collaboratives in 12 low- and middle-income countries
country: 12 low- and middle-income countries (not individually specified)
cycle1_result: Baseline performance was below 50% in two-thirds of charts
intervention: USAID-funded improvement collaborative approach (1998-2008), adapted for resource-constrained settings
cycle2_period: average of 28 months of data per chart
cycle2_result: 87% of charts reached 80% or higher performance and 76% reached at least 90%; average increase 51.9 percentage points (SE 28.0); average time to reach 80% performance was 9.2 months and to 90% was 14.4 months; performance sustained for an average of 13 months (69% of observed months)
other_findings: 27 of 54 originally funded collaboratives met the inclusion criteria (at least 12 months of data, indicators as percentages) for this analysis.
authors: Franco L; Marquez L
citation: Franco L, Marquez L. Effectiveness of collaborative improvement: evidence from 27 applications in 12 less-developed and middle-income countries. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(8):658-665. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2010.044388.

topic: Surgical safety practice adherence to WHO checklist (student observation)
title: Student-observed surgical safety practices across an urban regional health authority: Table 1
standard: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (2007)
finding: Student-observed adherence to WHO-mandated practices 75%-86%, although no formal checklist was used; 5 errors with potential for injury were observed
setting: 65 operating rooms across the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority, Canada
cycle1_result: Student-observed adherence to WHO-mandated practices 75%-86%, although no formal checklist was used; 5 errors with potential for injury were observed
other_findings: The WRHA did not employ a formal surgical checklist; most mandated practices were not monitored or enforced despite policy.
authors: Spence J; Goodwin B; Enns C; Dean H
citation: Spence J, Goodwin B, Enns C, Dean H. Student-observed surgical safety practices across an urban regional health authority: Table 1. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(7):580-586. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2010.044826.

topic: Surgical safety checklist compliance in obstetric theatres
title: The introduction of a surgical safety checklist in a tertiary referral obstetric centre
standard: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
finding: Compliance with pre- and postoperative checks 61.2% and 67.6% respectively
change: Introduction of a surgical safety checklist for elective cases in obstetric theatres
setting: A busy tertiary referral obstetric centre
cycle1_result: Compliance with pre- and postoperative checks 61.2% and 67.6% respectively
intervention: Introduction of a surgical safety checklist for elective cases in obstetric theatres
cycle2_result: Compliance improved to 79.7% (preoperative) and 84.7% (postoperative); 69.6% of staff felt interprofessional communication had improved
other_findings: Patients were mostly aware of the checks but this did not provoke anxiety.
authors: Kearns R; Uppal V; Bonner J; Robertson J; Daniel M; McGrady E
citation: Kearns R, Uppal V, Bonner J, Robertson J, Daniel M, McGrady E. The introduction of a surgical safety checklist in a tertiary referral obstetric centre. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(9):818-822. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2010.050179.

title: Rebound in ventilator-associated pneumonia rates during a prevention checklist washout period
standard: Ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle (head-of-bed elevation, oral care, suctioning device management, ventilator tubing care, standard infection-control precautions)
finding: Bundle compliance rose from under 50% to over 75%; VAP rate fell from 4.2 to 0.7 per 1000 ventilator days (p<0.059)
change: VAP prevention checklist, later incorporated into nursing and respiratory-care bedside flowsheets for sustainability
setting: Paediatric intensive care unit
cycle1_result: Bundle compliance rose from under 50% to over 75%; VAP rate fell from 4.2 to 0.7 per 1000 ventilator days (p<0.059)
intervention: VAP prevention checklist, later incorporated into nursing and respiratory-care bedside flowsheets for sustainability
cycle2_period: checklist washout phase (4 months), then flowsheet phase
cycle2_result: VAP rate rose to 4.8 per 1000 ventilator days during washout (p<0.042); rate dropped to 0.8 per 1000 ventilator days in the flowsheet phase (p<0.047)
other_findings: Staff reported documentation burden and checklist burnout; VAP rates were monitored prospectively over 42 months.
authors: Cheema A; Scott A; Shambaugh K; Shaffer-Hartman J; Dechert R; Hieber S; Gosbee J; Niedner M
citation: Cheema A, Scott A, Shambaugh K, Shaffer-Hartman J, Dechert R, Hieber S, et al.. Rebound in ventilator-associated pneumonia rates during a prevention checklist washout period. BMJ Quality & Safety. 2011;20(9):811-817. doi:10.1136/bmjqs.2011.051243.

title: Comparison of postal and non-postal post-vasectomy semen sample submission strategies on compliance and failures: an 11-year analysis of the audit database of the Association of Surgeons in Primary Care of the UK
standard: Post-vasectomy semen analysis (PVSA) required to confirm clearance before stopping other contraception; one-test/two-test clearance guidance
finding: Compliance with postal strategy 79.5% vs non-postal 59.1% (difference 20.4%, 95% CI 19.7-21.2%); early failure detection 0.73% postal vs 0.94% non-postal
setting: UK primary care vasectomy services (Association of Surgeons in Primary Care members)
cycle1_result: Compliance with postal strategy 79.5% vs non-postal 59.1% (difference 20.4%, 95% CI 19.7-21.2%); early failure detection 0.73% postal vs 0.94% non-postal
other_findings: No significant difference in late vasectomy failure rates between postal and non-postal strategies.
authors: Atkinson M; James G; Bond K; Harcombe Z; Labrecque M
citation: Atkinson M, James G, Bond K, Harcombe Z, Labrecque M. Comparison of postal and non-postal post-vasectomy semen sample submission strategies on compliance and failures: an 11-year analysis of the audit database of the Association of Surgeons in Primary Care of the UK. BMJ Sexual & Reproductive Health. 2021;48(1):54-59. doi:10.1136/bmjsrh-2021-201064.

title: Carriers of haemophilia a and B – a 5 year retrospective audit of management in pregnancy in the setting of a tertiary referral clinic
standard: Local delivery care plan guidance (regional anaesthesia, judicious fetal blood sampling/forceps use, cord bloods, oral vitamin K)
finding: 15 of 20 women had delivery care plans written at 36 weeks; postpartum haemorrhage advice included in 5 (28%) plans; of 16 delivered at the centre, 12 (75%) had normal vaginal deliveries, 1 mid-cavity forceps and 3 emergency LSCS; 3 of 15 (20%) male babies were affected, with no neonatal morbidity
setting: Joint Obstetric Haematology Clinic, Manchester, UK

other_findings: A general reluctance to undertake fetal blood sampling was noted; the role of late amniocentesis is being explored.

standard: Departmental guideline; modified Scottish Confidential Audit of Severe Maternal Morbidity (SCASMM) data collection tool; compared with the 2009 Scottish national audit
finding: Rate comparable to the Scottish national audit (4.61 vs 5.18 per 1000 for over 2500mL); consultant presence 72% for over 2000mL cases (Nov 2010-Apr 2011 subperiod)

title: Caesarean section audit spiral spanning 6 years of management in 3 major obstetric units of Glasgow
standard: NICE and local guidelines for caesarean section
finding: Decision-to-delivery time for the most urgent caesareans had a median of 33 minutes (range 20-60); syntocinon use for the third stage 91%; double-layer uterine closure 63%
change: Iterative re-auditing across the 'audit spiral' (November 2006 and January 2011), including introduction of an operative proforma to improve surgical documentation
setting: 3 major obstetric units, Glasgow, UK
cycle1_result: Decision-to-delivery time for the most urgent caesareans had a median of 33 minutes (range 20-60); syntocinon use for the third stage 91%; double-layer uterine closure 63%
intervention: Iterative re-auditing across the 'audit spiral' (November 2006 and January 2011), including introduction of an operative proforma to improve surgical documentation
cycle2_result: Decision-to-delivery time fell to a median of 26 minutes (range 20-36); syntocinon use for the third stage rose to 98%; double-layer uterine closure rose to 93%; all women received thromboprophylaxis; 95% of caesareans were under regional anaesthetic; umbilical cord pH performed in 75% of emergency caesareans

title: Quality improvement initiative to reduce adverse effects associated with parenteral nutrition overfeeding

finding: Mean maximum total daily kilocalorie dose 30.2 kcal/kg/day

setting: Two US Department of Veterans Affairs medical centres
cycle1_result: Mean maximum total daily kilocalorie dose 30.2 kcal/kg/day

cycle1_result: The rate of persistent balanitis was extremely low; in the one persistent case, treatment was changed but no biopsy was performed as the guideline recommends; no cases overall were referred for biopsy

topic: Microscopy value in male non-specific urethritis diagnosis

title: P2 Audit of clinical stage at presentation and factors contributing to antiretroviral therapy delay, in HIV patients in rural Kenya

finding: 82/100 patients were eligible for treatment at diagnosis; 74% did not commence ART within 4 weeks; mean time to ART initiation 102 days (range 4-861); reasons for delay over 28 days: patient default 23, TB diagnosis/treatment 21, counselling 18
setting: A small hospital and HIV clinic, rural Kenya
cycle1_result: 82/100 patients were eligible for treatment at diagnosis; 74% did not commence ART within 4 weeks; mean time to ART initiation 102 days (range 4-861); reasons for delay over 28 days: patient default 23, TB diagnosis/treatment 21, counselling 18

finding: Gonorrhoea cover was given in 72.9% of PID cases overall (below the 95% target); partner notification was not documented in 53.5% of STI-positive and 73.6% of non-STI cases; follow-up was attended by 81% of STI-positive and 40.3% of non-STI patients

cycle1_result: Gonorrhoea cover was given in 72.9% of PID cases overall (below the 95% target); partner notification was not documented in 53.5% of STI-positive and 73.6% of non-STI cases; follow-up was attended by 81% of STI-positive and 40.3% of non-STI patients

authors: Chan S; Hegazi A; Beardall A; Hay P

cycle1_result: Partners verified tested per case under 90 days 1.05 (range 0.17-1.3); verified or reported tested under 90 days 1.15; verified tested under 1 year 1.17; verified or reported tested under 1 year 1.27

standard: National guidelines for appropriateness of PEP provision

intervention: not reported (after this audit, the community clinic changed its pathway to follow up patients itself rather than referring to the hospital HIV clinic)

cycle1_result: 100% of requested kits distributed; 52% NAAT and 39% blood samples returned; 41% of returned blood samples insufficient; 40% of positives attended for treatment

other_findings: This scaled up a previous successful QI project on driving and ADHD in Belfast Trust; balancing measures included increased review time and more consultant reports requested from DVA; further cycles planned to obtain patient feedback.

cycle1_result: 54% Trust-wide completion rate for agreed quality standards; 53% completion for new patient checks.

topic: Melatonin prescribing and sleep hygiene intervention in CAMHS

standard: not reported
finding: Of a sample of 57 (from 115 of 346 patients on pharmacological therapies who were on melatonin), 46 were actively on melatonin; 39/46 (85%) had been on it for more than a year, including 10 for 5 years or more; 35/46 (76%) reported improved sleep or some benefit
setting: St Cadoc's Hospital, Specialist Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (S-CAMHS), Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
cycle1_result: Of a sample of 57 (from 115 of 346 patients on pharmacological therapies who were on melatonin), 46 were actively on melatonin; 39/46 (85%) had been on it for more than a year, including 10 for 5 years or more; 35/46 (76%) reported improved sleep or some benefit

topic: Antipsychotic blood and physical monitoring compliance
title: Antipsychotic Monitoring Within the Home Treatment Team in the Southern Trust, a Quality Improvement Project
standard: RCPsych PLAN Home Treatment Accreditation Scheme (HTAS) standards alongside NICE guidelines on antipsychotic monitoring; SMART aim of 100% of patients started on antipsychotics receiving appropriate blood/physical monitoring, documented within 10 days of discharge
finding: Baseline completion rates: 14-59% for various baseline bloods, 68-72% for heart rate/blood pressure/weight, 36% for ECGs; documentation of these parameters correct only 9-68% of the time

setting: Home Treatment Crisis Response (HTCR) team, Southern Trust
cycle1_result: Baseline completion rates: 14-59% for various baseline bloods, 68-72% for heart rate/blood pressure/weight, 36% for ECGs; documentation of these parameters correct only 9-68% of the time
intervention: PDSA cycle 1: multidisciplinary team education via presentation on findings and how to fix common documentation mistakes, staff input sought, and guidance posters printed

topic: Antipsychotic blood and physical monitoring compliance
title: Quality Improvement Project: Monitoring of Intellectual Disability Patients on Anti-Psychotic Medications in Outpatients Clinic, Northern Health & Social Care Trust, Northern Ireland
standard: NICE guidelines on physical health monitoring for patients on antipsychotic medication; target of monitoring 90% of patients on antipsychotics
finding: Baseline monitoring was essentially zero, as patients were often deemed too difficult in primary care for monitoring
change: Newly established Community Intellectual Disability Team implemented systematic monitoring; two PDSA cycles were run, the second involving acquisition of a new ECG machine and establishing baseline ECG testing, training and analysis
setting: Community Intellectual Disability Team outpatient clinic, Northern Health & Social Care Trust
cycle1_result: Baseline monitoring was essentially zero, as patients were often deemed too difficult in primary care for monitoring
intervention: Newly established Community Intellectual Disability Team implemented systematic monitoring; two PDSA cycles were run, the second involving acquisition of a new ECG machine and establishing baseline ECG testing, training and analysis
cycle2_result: 91% of patients met the target of having antipsychotic bloods monitored (aim 90%); 97% met the target of having physical observations monitored (aim 90%)
other_findings: ECG monitoring, started from a zero baseline in October 2021, reached 42% by January 2022, with a target of over 90% by September 2022; duplicates and nursing home patients were excluded.
authors: Flynn A; Ling P

topic: Unnecessary blood test reduction in inpatient mental health
title: Outcomes of a Quality Improvement Project to Reduce Unnecessary Blood Tests in Beechcroft Regional Child & Adolescent Mental Health Unit, Belfast Trust
standard: Local quality improvement target to reduce baseline blood testing of glucose, lipids and thyroid function tests (TFTs) by 10% by June 2021
finding: Baseline fortnightly median of 7 glucose tests and 10 lipid/TFT tests for the unit; an initial scoping exercise found one young person had 40 blood tests during a single admission
change: Six PDSA cycles: separate bloods diary per ward, diary brought into weekly care-planning meetings, education posters in clinical rooms, MDT meeting with Clinical Biochemistry, junior doctor updating the bloods diary post care-planning, and diary use plus new monitoring guidelines added to daily nursing handover
setting: Beechcroft Regional Child & Adolescent Mental Health Unit, Belfast Trust
cycle1_result: Baseline fortnightly median of 7 glucose tests and 10 lipid/TFT tests for the unit; an initial scoping exercise found one young person had 40 blood tests during a single admission
intervention: Six PDSA cycles: separate bloods diary per ward, diary brought into weekly care-planning meetings, education posters in clinical rooms, MDT meeting with Clinical Biochemistry, junior doctor updating the bloods diary post care-planning, and diary use plus new monitoring guidelines added to daily nursing handover
cycle2_result: Glucose tests reduced by 68%, to a new fortnightly median of 2.2 (from 7); lipid and TFT median of 10 remained unchanged
other_findings: COVID-19 disrupted monitoring; stopping routine blood glucose monitoring in favour of capillary blood glucose (BMs) testing drove the main improvement; continued monitoring and incorporation of patient feedback were planned.
authors: Gillanders C; Doherty F; Fitzsimmons S
citation: Gillanders C, Doherty F, Fitzsimmons S. Outcomes of a Quality Improvement Project to Reduce Unnecessary Blood Tests in Beechcroft Regional Child & Adolescent Mental Health Unit, Belfast Trust. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S94-S94.

topic: Avoidability of psychiatric admissions in older adults

standard: not reported

setting: Older adult community mental health team, NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde
cycle1_result: 14/21 admissions scored 5 (completely unavoidable), 1 scored 4, 1 scored 3, 5 scored 2 on a 1-5 avoidability scale; most common reason was behavioural/psychological symptoms of dementia (n=10)

topic: DVLA driving status documentation in self-harm/depression patients
title: Do We Know if You Drive? a Quality Improvement Project Improving Compliance With DVLA Guidelines
standard: DVLA guidance requiring advice and documentation on driving status for depression/anxiety with significant memory/concentration problems, agitation, behavioural disturbance or suicidal thoughts
finding: Baseline data collected but documentation rates not separately given for baseline weeks
change: Weekly interventions: email communication highlighting guidance (weeks 1, 3), daily handover discussion of driving status (week 2), DVLA guidance posters in office (week 4), teaching session by occupational therapist (week 12)
setting: Liaison Psychiatry, University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust / Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: Baseline data collected but documentation rates not separately given for baseline weeks
intervention: Weekly interventions: email communication highlighting guidance (weeks 1, 3), daily handover discussion of driving status (week 2), DVLA guidance posters in office (week 4), teaching session by occupational therapist (week 12)
cycle2_result: Relevant documentation only made in week 1 (10%) and week 4 (20%); no documentation in any other week
other_findings: Group discussion found clinicians did not ask as questions were not routine practice, and had concerns about implications of advice; future plans include an electronic risk assessment prompt and induction training.

topic: Inpatient violence reduction in psychiatric intensive care
title: Nile Ward PICU Violence Reduction Quality Improvement Project - One Year on
standard: not reported
finding: 35% reduction in ward violence
change: Improved risk assessment tool, staff photo board, patient feedback board, co-produced mutual expectations, gardening sessions, tailored physical fitness programmes, diversity events, consultant-led daily reviews, cooking sessions, mindfulness meditation, triangle of care
setting: Nile Ward PICU, St Charles Hospital, CNWL NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: 35% reduction in ward violence
intervention: Improved risk assessment tool, staff photo board, patient feedback board, co-produced mutual expectations, gardening sessions, tailored physical fitness programmes, diversity events, consultant-led daily reviews, cooking sessions, mindfulness meditation, triangle of care

topic: GP referral quality to community mental health team
title: Quality Improvement Project to Improve GP Referrals to a Rural Psychiatric Team
standard: not reported
finding: 17.4% of referrals accepted, 13.0% received Single Point of Access (SPOA) assessment, 17.4% rejected, 39.1% re-referred elsewhere, 21.8% no response
change: Structured referral template developed with driver diagrams, via Plan-Do-Study-Act methodology
setting: Bolsover Community Mental Health Team
cycle1_result: 17.4% of referrals accepted, 13.0% received Single Point of Access (SPOA) assessment, 17.4% rejected, 39.1% re-referred elsewhere, 21.8% no response
intervention: Structured referral template developed with driver diagrams, via Plan-Do-Study-Act methodology

topic: Efficiency of electronic prescribing and medication tasks
title: A Quality Improvement Project on Improving Electronic Prescribing System in an Adult Mental Health unit
standard: not reported
finding: 21.5 hours spent on medication tasks; 10 hours ordering medications (7 of which were ward stock); 12.6 hours re-prescribing; 42% of tasks completed on Mondays
change: Altered ward stocklists, aligned ward timings, and a collective tasks system to reduce duplication
setting: 46-bedded adult mental health unit
cycle1_result: 21.5 hours spent on medication tasks; 10 hours ordering medications (7 of which were ward stock); 12.6 hours re-prescribing; 42% of tasks completed on Mondays

topic: Sustainable antipsychotic depot and PRN prescribing
title: Sustainable Prescribing in Secure Services – a Quality Improvement Initiative
standard: Department of Health 2021 report on safer, sustainable prescribing in health and justice mental health services
finding: 17/26 (65%) depot patients prescribed at longest evidence-based interval; 9/15 (60%) PRN medications prescribed but not in use

cycle1_result: 17/26 (65%) depot patients prescribed at longest evidence-based interval; 9/15 (60%) PRN medications prescribed but not in use

topic: GP referral quality for suspected adult ADHD

standard: not reported

cycle1_result: 89% of referrals explained current difficulties; 52% described resultant impairments; 61% mentioned symptoms present in childhood; 91% contained past medical history/medication; 0% mentioned family history; 6% contained physical health data; 85% of referrals were accepted and 13% rejected, mainly for a missing ADHD self-report scale

finding: 30.2% (13/43) had high CVD risk (QRISK3 >=10%); of these, 76.7% were aged 55 or over, 69.2% were current smokers, 23% diabetic and 15.2% hypertensive; 72% of all patients were smokers; mean BMI 23.6, with 41.9% having a BMI of 25 or above
setting: Ty Cyfannol ward, YYF Hospital, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board, South Wales
cycle1_result: 30.2% (13/43) had high CVD risk (QRISK3 >=10%); of these, 76.7% were aged 55 or over, 69.2% were current smokers, 23% diabetic and 15.2% hypertensive; 72% of all patients were smokers; mean BMI 23.6, with 41.9% having a BMI of 25 or above

topic: BMI screening and intervention in psychiatric intensive care
title: Improving Screening and Standardising Interventions for Patients With Above Normal Body Mass Index (BMI) Admitted to a Male Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU): A Quality Improvement Project
standard: Local target to increase BMI documentation and standardised interventions for abnormal BMI on PICU admission
finding: 47% of PICU patients had their BMI recorded on admission; 69% of those meeting overweight criteria were offered an intervention
change: Two Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles: cycle 1 engaged nursing staff and provided training to fix an electronic form glitch preventing automatic BMI calculation; cycle 2 introduced a protocol for consistent interventions (dietician referral, PICU gym instructor referral, MDT discussion) for abnormal BMI
setting: Willow Suite Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, Littlebrook Hospital
cycle1_result: 47% of PICU patients had their BMI recorded on admission; 69% of those meeting overweight criteria were offered an intervention
intervention: Two Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles: cycle 1 engaged nursing staff and provided training to fix an electronic form glitch preventing automatic BMI calculation; cycle 2 introduced a protocol for consistent interventions (dietician referral, PICU gym instructor referral, MDT discussion) for abnormal BMI
cycle2_result: After cycle 1, 91% of patients had BMI recorded and 71% of those overweight were offered an intervention; after cycle 2, all consenting patients had BMI recorded and 100% of those meeting overweight criteria were offered all protocol interventions, though not all agreed to engage
other_findings: Next steps include implementing the screening and intervention protocol across other wards and improving patient engagement with the interventions offered.
authors: Holmes A; Rashid S; Zabrzycki D; Satisha S

topic: Baseline physical health investigations (bloods and ECG) on psychiatric admission
title: Quality Improvement Project: Increasing the Proportion of Inpatients Being Re-Offered and Receiving Baseline Physical Investigations
standard: Trust standard: comprehensive mental and physical health assessment including ECG and routine bloods within 4 hours of admission
finding: 85.14% did not receive admission bloods and 83.79% did not receive an admission ECG; before the tracking list, 55.77% had baseline bloods (admission or reoffer) and 78.85% had a baseline ECG

setting: Two wards, Greater Manchester Mental Health Trust
cycle1_result: 85.14% did not receive admission bloods and 83.79% did not receive an admission ECG; before the tracking list, 55.77% had baseline bloods (admission or reoffer) and 78.85% had a baseline ECG
intervention: A tracking list of patients not receiving admission investigations, reviewed weekly at ward rounds to prompt re-offering

authors: Thompson B
citation: Thompson B. Quality Improvement Project: Increasing the Proportion of Inpatients Being Re-Offered and Receiving Baseline Physical Investigations. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S114-S114.

topic: Clozapine prescribing/dose compliance in a general hospital
title: Improving Clozapine Prescribing at a London District General Hospital: A Quality Improvement Project
standard: not reported (safe clozapine prescribing practice)
finding: 67.4% of admissions inappropriately missed at least one clozapine dose; 40.8% of patients referred to the liaison team.
change: Hospital guideline, automatic email to liaison team on clozapine prescription, online prescribing system alert, clinician teaching (from July 2022).
setting: North Middlesex Hospital (NMH), liaison psychiatry team
cycle1_period: April 2020 to December 2023 (notes reviewed before changes from July 2022)
cycle1_result: 67.4% of admissions inappropriately missed at least one clozapine dose; 40.8% of patients referred to the liaison team.
intervention: Hospital guideline, automatic email to liaison team on clozapine prescription, online prescribing system alert, clinician teaching (from July 2022).

topic: Induction programme for Higher Specialist Trainees

topic: Use of Clinical Global Impression (CGI) scores in inpatient psychiatry
title: Quality Improvement Project on the Use of Clinical Global Impression (CGI) Scores in a Female Adult Inpatient Mental Health Ward
standard: not reported

finding: GP considered there to be an avoidable delay in 22% of records (n=3380); ranged from 7% (breast cancer) to 34% (stomach cancer); 49% of delays occurred in primary care, 38% in secondary/tertiary care
setting: 439 English general practices (National Cancer Diagnosis Audit)
cycle1_result: GP considered there to be an avoidable delay in 22% of records (n=3380); ranged from 7% (breast cancer) to 34% (stomach cancer); 49% of delays occurred in primary care, 38% in secondary/tertiary care
other_findings: 28% of delays attributed to clinician factors and 34% to health care system factors; insights to inform quality improvement initiatives in primary and secondary care.

topic: Acute kidney injury education using peer review audit
title: Effect and acceptability of AKI education using peer review audit in primary care
standard: not reported
finding: 93% of participants found the peer review audit sessions useful; significant improvement in test scores between baseline and 1-year questionnaires
change: Peer review audit sessions with consultant nephrologist presentations and case discussion
setting: Southern Derbyshire CCG primary care
cycle1_result: 93% of participants found the peer review audit sessions useful; significant improvement in test scores between baseline and 1-year questionnaires
intervention: Peer review audit sessions with consultant nephrologist presentations and case discussion
cycle2_result: Exposure to AKI teaching, self-reported awareness and confidence were higher in the second questionnaire, with significant improvement in test scores
other_findings: 45% of participants were anxious about group case discussion although 36% thought it the most useful component; peer review audit education may not be universally acceptable in primary care.

topic: Diagnostic accuracy of COPD on QOF register (spirometry)
title: Inaccurate diagnosis of COPD: the Welsh National COPD Audit
standard: Quality and Outcomes Framework (QOF) COPD register; spirometric diagnostic criteria (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio <0.70)
finding: Only 19% (n=8957) post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC Read-Coded; of these, 75% (n=6702) had compatible spirometry and 25% (n=2255) did not
setting: Welsh general practices (QOF COPD register)
cycle1_result: Only 19% (n=8957) post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC Read-Coded; of these, 75% (n=6702) had compatible spirometry and 25% (n=2255) did not
other_findings: Patients with incompatible spirometry were more likely female, never-smokers, higher BMI, and less likely to receive LAMA or LABA/ICS combinations; focus on correct diagnosis needed to improve quality of care.
authors: Fisk M; McMillan V; Brown J; Holzhauer-Barrie J; Khan M; Baxter N; Roberts C

finding: 16 (0.2%) of eligible obese patients referred to the exercise referral scheme (ERS) during cycle 1

topic: Cervical screening uptake audit and feedback
title: Evaluation of an audit and feedback intervention to improve cervical screening uptake
standard: National cervical screening programme participation targets
finding: Around a third of those eligible did not participate in cervical screening in England in 2023-24
change: Quarterly audit and feedback reports comparing practices' cervical screening coverage with similarly deprived local practices, with improvement resources
setting: 23 general practices in three Primary Care Networks, England
cycle1_result: Around a third of those eligible did not participate in cervical screening in England in 2023-24
intervention: Quarterly audit and feedback reports comparing practices' cervical screening coverage with similarly deprived local practices, with improvement resources
cycle2_n: 14 practice staff and 3 service leaders interviewed
cycle2_result: Practice teams seldom recalled seeing the feedback reports before interview invitations but viewed them positively when shown; format, length and content considered appropriate
other_findings: Audit and feedback cannot improve uptake if recipients do not receive it; more effective methods needed to engage or circumvent practice gatekeepers.

topic: Glycaemic control in critical limb-threatening ischaemia inpatients
title: An audit of glycaemic control and impact on surgical outcomes among inpatients with critical limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI)
standard: NICE guidelines for glycaemic control categorisation
finding: 45% (54/120) well controlled (Group 1), 55% (66/120) poorly controlled (Group 2); primary healing higher in Group 1 (42.5% vs 18.1%, p=0.002); major adverse events 12.9% vs 33.3% (p=0.002)
setting: Single tertiary vascular centre
cycle1_result: 45% (54/120) well controlled (Group 1), 55% (66/120) poorly controlled (Group 2); primary healing higher in Group 1 (42.5% vs 18.1%, p=0.002); major adverse events 12.9% vs 33.3% (p=0.002)
other_findings: Poor glycaemic control was significantly associated with poorer wound healing and amputations even adjusting for age, CRP and BMI; despite a multidisciplinary diabetic foot service, glycaemic management remains suboptimal.

journal: Journal of Vascular Societies Great Britain & Ireland

topic: Referral to polysomnography wait times (sleep audit)
title: P135 An audit investigating the length of time from GP referral to diagnostic polysomnography testing in an Australian tertiary center
standard: Published literature benchmarks: mean wait 88 days referral-to-first-review, 123 days first-review-to-polysomnography
finding: Mean time from referral to first clinic review 136.13 days (longer than published standard); mean time from review to polysomnography 28.95 days (category 4, within 30 days), 93.38 days (category 5, within 90 days), 180 days (category 6, non-urgent) — shorter than published standards.
setting: Sleep disorders centre, Australian tertiary hospital
cycle1_result: Mean time from referral to first clinic review 136.13 days (longer than published standard); mean time from review to polysomnography 28.95 days (category 4, within 30 days), 93.38 days (category 5, within 90 days), 180 days (category 6, non-urgent) — shorter than published standards.
other_findings: Authors recommend adjusting triaging/capacity to reduce referral-to-review time, which exceeded published standards.
authors: Sriram B; Singh V; Bandaralage S; Bashford J
journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society

topic: Volume-based feeds for burn patient nutrition

standard: Local target: increase average feeds received from 68% to over 75% of prescribed

change: Volume-based feeds calculator (later a chart) for adjusting feed volumes to make up for pauses (sedation/procedures).

cycle1_result: Baseline: patients receiving about 68% of prescribed tube feeds.
intervention: Volume-based feeds calculator (later a chart) for adjusting feed volumes to make up for pauses (sedation/procedures).

standard: 2012 Canadian Hypertension Education Program (CHEP) guidelines
finding: Adherence to CHEP guidelines assessed across blood pressure measurement, correct diagnosis/staging, risk assessment and objective measures; common naturopathic modalities were dietary, lifestyle, nutritional supplementation and botanical medicine; supplementation of omega-3, CoQ10, hibiscus, magnesium, hawthorn plus diet/exercise were most associated with SBP/DBP reduction.

cycle1_result: Adherence to CHEP guidelines assessed across blood pressure measurement, correct diagnosis/staging, risk assessment and objective measures; common naturopathic modalities were dietary, lifestyle, nutritional supplementation and botanical medicine; supplementation of omega-3, CoQ10, hibiscus, magnesium, hawthorn plus diet/exercise were most associated with SBP/DBP reduction.
other_findings: This is a naturopathic (non-conventional medical) management audit rather than a mainstream clinical audit; per the instructions veterinary/non-clinical audits are excluded but naturopathic clinical management against a recognised medical guideline (CHEP) is included as is_audit yes.

title: 222. The Impact of Education and Prospective Audit and Feedback on Reducing Ciprofloxacin Utilization at a Small Community Academic Hospital
standard: Internal Antibiotic Stewardship Program guidelines for ciprofloxacin use
finding: Ciprofloxacin utilisation averaged 73.3 DOT/1,000 patient-days (rising to 138.3 in May 2017)
change: Guidelines for ciprofloxacin use disseminated via electronic newsletter and in-person meetings (education), followed by prospective audit and feedback (PAF) for all ciprofloxacin orders
setting: Small community academic hospital (77-bed), Barnes-Jewish West County Hospital
cycle1_result: Ciprofloxacin utilisation averaged 73.3 DOT/1,000 patient-days (rising to 138.3 in May 2017)
intervention: Guidelines for ciprofloxacin use disseminated via electronic newsletter and in-person meetings (education), followed by prospective audit and feedback (PAF) for all ciprofloxacin orders

finding: 96% of patients received the standard 1g x2 (2 weeks apart) retreatment regime; 43% retreated 6-monthly, 33% 6-9 monthly, 24% more than 9 months; average age 66, 58% female, 83% seropositive
change: Departmental retreatment schedule optimised from standard 2g dose to a reduced 1g dose
setting: Rheumatology department, district general hospital
cycle1_result: 96% of patients received the standard 1g x2 (2 weeks apart) retreatment regime; 43% retreated 6-monthly, 33% 6-9 monthly, 24% more than 9 months; average age 66, 58% female, 83% seropositive
intervention: Departmental retreatment schedule optimised from standard 2g dose to a reduced 1g dose
other_findings: Projected cost savings of £236,927 over a 3-year treatment cycle for the department from switching to the reduced dose, alongside expected reduced infection risk.
citation: . P003 Quality improvement project on rituximab use in rheumatoid arthritis - how do we improve quality and cost effectiveness?. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2022;61(Suppl 1).

topic: Patient satisfaction with virtual outpatient clinics
title: TU7.4 Service Evaluation Audit of Virtual Outpatient Clinics in the Post-COVID-19 era
standard: NHS Outpatient Department Survey (2011) questions used as a comparator; no explicit compliance target stated
finding: Overall satisfaction with telephone consultations was significantly higher than pre-COVID face-to-face survey results; 51% confident and 27% confident to some extent about being listed for surgery without further examination; 8% not confident about how surgery was explained; 10% not confident about the risks of surgery; more than a third not happy to be discharged from clinic after a telephone consultation
setting: General surgery outpatient clinic
cycle1_result: Overall satisfaction with telephone consultations was significantly higher than pre-COVID face-to-face survey results; 51% confident and 27% confident to some extent about being listed for surgery without further examination; 8% not confident about how surgery was explained; 10% not confident about the risks of surgery; more than a third not happy to be discharged from clinic after a telephone consultation
other_findings: Authors call this a service evaluation/service provision audit, but it is primarily a patient satisfaction survey without a defined pass standard.
citation: . TU7.4 Service Evaluation Audit of Virtual Outpatient Clinics in the Post-COVID-19 era. Br J Surg. 2022;109(Suppl 5).

title: Benzodiazepine prescribing in tunisia: A study about psychiatrists prescribing habits
standard: Guidelines on benzodiazepine (BZD) prescribing (not individually named)
finding: Purpose of BZD treatment explained to patient in 98.2% of cases, risks explained in 87.7%; precautions taken in elderly (96.5%), respiratory failure risk (94.7%), personality disorders (80.7%), pregnancy (77.9%); 14.4% combined two BZDs for refractory symptoms; 18.4% did not systematically reassess necessity before repeating a prescription
setting: Psychiatry departments, Tunisia
cycle1_result: Purpose of BZD treatment explained to patient in 98.2% of cases, risks explained in 87.7%; precautions taken in elderly (96.5%), respiratory failure risk (94.7%), personality disorders (80.7%), pregnancy (77.9%); 14.4% combined two BZDs for refractory symptoms; 18.4% did not systematically reassess necessity before repeating a prescription
other_findings: This is a self-administered questionnaire survey of psychiatrists' reported prescribing habits (28% response rate), rather than a chart-based audit; authors conclude prescribing practices remain non-compliant with recommendations in many cases.
authors: Lagha M; Ouali U; Nacef F
journal: European psychiatry : the journal of the Association of European Psychiatrists
citation: Lagha M, Ouali U, Nacef F. Benzodiazepine prescribing in tunisia: A study about psychiatrists prescribing habits. Eur Psychiatry. 2021;64(Suppl 1):S483-S484.

topic: Umbilical cord clamping timing in preterm infants
title: Successful Implementation of a Change in Practice to Optimize Timing of Umbilical Cord Clamping in Preterm Neonates: A Quality Improvement Initiative
standard: Institutional guideline recommending natural (delayed) umbilical cord clamping (NCC) for at least 60 seconds in preterm infants; objective was to achieve over 50% compliance.
finding: not reported
change: Structured multidisciplinary educational approach: evidence presented at grand round, multidisciplinary team (neonatologists, obstetricians, neonatal nurse practitioners, respiratory therapists, nurses) developed the NCC guideline, local champions identified at each hospital, staff education before staged implementation (Oct 2013 for GA 33-35 weeks, Jan 2014 for GA >=28 weeks, Apr 2014 for GA >=26 weeks).
setting: 4 city hospitals, maternal-newborn care
cycle1_result: not reported
intervention: Structured multidisciplinary educational approach: evidence presented at grand round, multidisciplinary team (neonatologists, obstetricians, neonatal nurse practitioners, respiratory therapists, nurses) developed the NCC guideline, local champions identified at each hospital, staff education before staged implementation (Oct 2013 for GA 33-35 weeks, Jan 2014 for GA >=28 weeks, Apr 2014 for GA >=26 weeks).
cycle2_result: Compliance rates and proportion of infants receiving NCC of at least 45 seconds are reported in a table not reproduced in the abstract; 18% of infants 26-32 weeks gestational age eligible for NCC received cord clamping at less than 45 seconds to facilitate resuscitation.
other_findings: Authors conclude compliance with practice change can be achieved through a structured multidisciplinary team approach with frequent feedback.
citation: . Successful Implementation of a Change in Practice to Optimize Timing of Umbilical Cord Clamping in Preterm Neonates: A Quality Improvement Initiative. Paediatr Child Health. 2016;21(Suppl 5):e72a-e72a.

title: Implementation of a Quality Improvement Role for Unlicensed Assistive Personnel and Effects on Infection Prevention
standard: Infection prevention care bundle process measures for central-line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI), catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) and C. difficile prevention
finding: Baseline number of central-line audits and infection rates prior to the quality liaison role
change: A dedicated unlicensed assistive personnel (certified nursing assistant) quality liaison role introduced in early 2019 to perform daily rounding, direct care tasks, patient education, process measure audits, and real-time feedback to RNs
setting: 53-bed inpatient adult oncology unit, UNC Medical Center
cycle1_result: Baseline number of central-line audits and infection rates prior to the quality liaison role
intervention: A dedicated unlicensed assistive personnel (certified nursing assistant) quality liaison role introduced in early 2019 to perform daily rounding, direct care tasks, patient education, process measure audits, and real-time feedback to RNs
cycle2_result: Central-line audits increased by more than 1,400 compared with the previous year; rate reductions of 40-55% achieved for CLABSI, CAUTI and healthcare-associated C. difficile infections
other_findings: From July to October 2020, when the quality liaison was redeployed to direct patient care due to COVID-19 staffing pressures, the same infection rates increased by 30-353%; the hospital is exploring expanding the model to other units.
citation: . Implementation of a Quality Improvement Role for Unlicensed Assistive Personnel and Effects on Infection Prevention. Antimicrob Steward Healthc Epidemiol. 2021;1(Suppl 1):s73-s74.

topic: High-level disinfection compliance in ambulatory care
title: High-Level Disinfection in Ambulatory Care: Overcoming the Barriers of a Decentralized System through Auditing and Education
standard: Standard work for high-level disinfection (HLD) of semicritical instruments (manufacturer instructions and competency requirements)
finding: Audits found variability across departments with gaps in precleaning, transportation of used instruments, dilution of enzymatic cleaner, and maintenance of quality control logs; also gaps in staff understanding of standard work and inventory management
change: Centralised HLD database of supplies, methodology, standard work and competency evaluations; infection control team led direct observation audits; monthly-driven HLD calendar for annual competencies; joint education sessions between infection control and manufacturers for reprocessing staff
setting: 30-practice ambulatory care network (otolaryngology, urology, endoscopy, obstetrics/gynaecology), eastern Massachusetts
cycle1_result: Audits found variability across departments with gaps in precleaning, transportation of used instruments, dilution of enzymatic cleaner, and maintenance of quality control logs; also gaps in staff understanding of standard work and inventory management
intervention: Centralised HLD database of supplies, methodology, standard work and competency evaluations; infection control team led direct observation audits; monthly-driven HLD calendar for annual competencies; joint education sessions between infection control and manufacturers for reprocessing staff
other_findings: Authors describe an effective and sustainable strategy resulting from auditing and feedback, but no quantitative re-audit results are given.
citation: . High-Level Disinfection in Ambulatory Care: Overcoming the Barriers of a Decentralized System through Auditing and Education. Antimicrob Steward Healthc Epidemiol. 2021;1(Suppl 1):s11-s11.

title: Prospective audit and feedback of Clostridioides difficile PCR at the time of ordering increases appropriateness of testing
standard: Antibiotic stewardship program's clinical criteria for appropriate C. difficile PCR testing (no positive test in prior 7 days plus a 3-step clinical review)
finding: ASP was alerted to and collected data on C. difficile PCR orders without intervening
change: Antibiotic stewardship program implemented real-time prospective audit and feedback (PAF) at the time of C. difficile PCR test ordering, with direct provider conversation or a note on appropriate criteria, and recommendation to cancel inappropriate tests
setting: 399-bed tertiary-care Veterans Affairs Medical Center, adult inpatients and outpatients
cycle1_result: ASP was alerted to and collected data on C. difficile PCR orders without intervening
intervention: Antibiotic stewardship program implemented real-time prospective audit and feedback (PAF) at the time of C. difficile PCR test ordering, with direct provider conversation or a note on appropriate criteria, and recommendation to cancel inappropriate tests
cycle2_result: Significant reduction in monthly test rate compared with preintervention period, driven mainly by reducing tests considered clinically inappropriate
other_findings: PAF was not performed outside standard hours; authors note it requires significant ASP staff time and may not be sustainable long term.
citation: . Prospective audit and feedback of Clostridioides difficile PCR at the time of ordering increases appropriateness of testing. Antimicrob Steward Healthc Epidemiol. 2022;2(Suppl 1):s29-s29.

title: Hand hygiene adherence at entrances and exits of healthcare facilities in two rural districts of Uganda
standard: WHO recommendation for hand hygiene stations (soap and water, or alcohol-based hand rub) at entrances and exits of healthcare facilities
finding: Only 4/37 (11%) facility entrances/exits met recommended HH material guidance; 12/37 (32%) had no HH station, 13/37 (35%) had stations with no water, 8/37 (22%) had water but no soap; of 180 people observed, 52 (29%) attempted hand hygiene and only 10 (6%) used appropriate technology (4 ABHR, 6 water and soap); 42/52 (81%) used only water without soap; no hand hygiene occurred when exiting (0 of 68); only 9/180 (5%) adhered to both suggested technique and duration
setting: 37 public healthcare facilities, Moroto and Kotido districts
cycle1_result: Only 4/37 (11%) facility entrances/exits met recommended HH material guidance; 12/37 (32%) had no HH station, 13/37 (35%) had stations with no water, 8/37 (22%) had water but no soap; of 180 people observed, 52 (29%) attempted hand hygiene and only 10 (6%) used appropriate technology (4 ABHR, 6 water and soap); 42/52 (81%) used only water without soap; no hand hygiene occurred when exiting (0 of 68); only 9/180 (5%) adhered to both suggested technique and duration
other_findings: 48/52 (92%) of those who performed hand hygiene did so for the recommended >20 seconds; poor practice attributed mainly to lack of soap availability.
citation: . Hand hygiene adherence at entrances and exits of healthcare facilities in two rural districts of Uganda. Antimicrob Steward Healthc Epidemiol. 2022;2(Suppl 1):s46-s46.

title: A81 OPTIMIZING THE INDICATIONS FOR BILIARY STENT PLACEMENT IN PATIENTS WITH CBD STONES: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE TO ENHANCE PATIENT CARE AND REDUCE HEALTHCARE RESOURCE UTILIZATION
standard: Published guidelines on indications for biliary stent insertion in patients with CBD stones
finding: Inappropriate stent usage identified in 16% of CBD stone patients overall; 223/598 (37%) of first ERCPs had a stent placed, of which 63/223 (28%) were not in accordance with published guidelines
change: Pre-intervention audit findings shared with the ERCP group; education to align biliary stent insertion practice with published guidelines
setting: ERCP service, University of Alberta Hospital
cycle1_result: Inappropriate stent usage identified in 16% of CBD stone patients overall; 223/598 (37%) of first ERCPs had a stent placed, of which 63/223 (28%) were not in accordance with published guidelines
intervention: Pre-intervention audit findings shared with the ERCP group; education to align biliary stent insertion practice with published guidelines
cycle2_result: 192/661 (29%) of first ERCPs had a stent placed (vs 37% pre-intervention, not significant); only 13/192 (7%) were not in accordance with guidelines, compared with 28% pre-intervention (kappa=0.53 for independent blinded review)
other_findings: 384/661 (58%) patients were referred for CBD stones; reduction in inappropriate stent placement reduced unnecessary follow-up ERCPs and healthcare resource use.
authors: Alzahrani I; Alhaidari S; Alhanaee M; Decanini A; Mohamed M; Zepeda-Gomez S; Mathura P; Zhang J; Sandha G
journal: Journal of the Canadian Association of Gastroenterology
