A81 OPTIMIZING THE INDICATIONS FOR BILIARY STENT PLACEMENT IN PATIENTS WITH CBD STONES: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE TO ENHANCE PATIENT CARE AND REDUCE HEALTHCARE RESOURCE UTILIZATION. J Can Assoc Gastroenterol. 2023;6(Suppl 1):44-44.

topic: Prescription audit in indoor COVID-19 patients
title: Prescription audit and effects of co-morbidities on indoor covid-19 patients of a tertiary care teaching hospital
standard: WHO core prescribing indicators.
finding: Of 300 prescriptions analysed (2972 drugs prescribed), average 9.90 drugs per prescription; 88% of drugs prescribed by generic name; 99.66% of encounters had antimicrobials; 44% of encounters had injections; 83.34% of drugs were from the National Essential Drug List; 55.67% of patients had a co-morbidity; average hospital stay approximately 8 days.
setting: Tertiary care teaching hospital, indoor (inpatient) COVID-19 wards
cycle1_result: Of 300 prescriptions analysed (2972 drugs prescribed), average 9.90 drugs per prescription; 88% of drugs prescribed by generic name; 99.66% of encounters had antimicrobials; 44% of encounters had injections; 83.34% of drugs were from the National Essential Drug List; 55.67% of patients had a co-morbidity; average hospital stay approximately 8 days.
other_findings: Mortality was higher in diabetic and hypertensive patients than in patients without these co-morbidities.
authors: SM M; AR K; A S; PR C; DD R; HR P; KN H; TV H
citation: SM M, AR K, A S, PR C, DD R, HR P, et al.. Prescription audit and effects of co-morbidities on indoor covid-19 patients of a tertiary care teaching hospital. . 2023. doi:10.22541/au.168155115.53867221/v1.

title: Strengthening patient safety in a Cambodian hospital through structured weekly reporting: a low-cost quality improvement initiative.
standard: Local structured weekly reporting standard operating procedures for patient safety
finding: 0 formally adopted Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); 38% of ER staff Basic Life Support-trained; 2 expired blood product incidents per month
change: One-page Departmental Wise Checklist introduced across ER/ICU, obstetrics and gynaecology, outpatients and paediatrics; weekly reviews, feedback loops, departmental champions, PDSA cycles
setting: Tertiary hospital, Phnom Penh
cycle1_result: 0 formally adopted Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); 38% of ER staff Basic Life Support-trained; 2 expired blood product incidents per month
intervention: One-page Departmental Wise Checklist introduced across ER/ICU, obstetrics and gynaecology, outpatients and paediatrics; weekly reviews, feedback loops, departmental champions, PDSA cycles
cycle2_result: SOPs increased from 0 to 10; Basic Life Support-trained ER staff rose to 98%; expired blood product incidents fell to none; reporting compliance averaged 92%; neonatal hypothermia cases fell from 6 to 2/month; ER adverse events dropped from 4 to 1/month
other_findings: Sustainability beyond the 12-week intervention period has not yet been empirically assessed.
authors: Kanayan S
citation: Kanayan S. Strengthening patient safety in a Cambodian hospital through structured weekly reporting: a low-cost quality improvement initiative. BMJ Open Qual. 2026;15(3):e003930. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003930. PMID: 42508820.

title: A retrospective audit of accuracy of thoracolumbosacral pedicle screw fixation.
standard: Gertzbein grading of pedicle screw breach on postoperative CT, benchmarked against published accuracy rates (95.5% CT-navigation, 93.1% free-hand, 91.5% fluoroscopy-guided, 90.5% robot-assisted, from a 1990-2018 systematic review).
finding: 98.75% of screws (94.03% of patients) were accurately placed; 3 screws had asymptomatic Gertzbein grade 1 breach (<2mm); 1 patient had grade 2 breach (2-4mm) with radicular pain; accuracy by level was 99.08% lumbar, 98.39% thoracic and 97.5% sacral.
setting: Hospital spinal surgery unit
cycle1_result: 98.75% of screws (94.03% of patients) were accurately placed; 3 screws had asymptomatic Gertzbein grade 1 breach (<2mm); 1 patient had grade 2 breach (2-4mm) with radicular pain; accuracy by level was 99.08% lumbar, 98.39% thoracic and 97.5% sacral.
other_findings: Screw placement used anatomical landmarks with fluoroscopy at each stage; accuracy was better than most reported literature rates and was highest at the lumbar level.
authors: UNNITHAN AKA; SURESH C
citation: UNNITHAN AKA, SURESH C. A retrospective audit of accuracy of thoracolumbosacral pedicle screw fixation. . 2025. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-7794815/v1.

topic: Radiation dose monitoring in endovascular aneurysm repair
title: Audit of radiation doses during endovascular aneurysm repair
standard: not reported (no named diagnostic reference level or dose standard stated; project monitored trends in radiation dose over time)
finding: Median radiation dose was lower than in 2021; median screening time was 29% longer than in 2021; dose was lower with two operators than one.
setting: Leeds Teaching Hospitals Trust, endovascular aneurysm repair (fluoroscopy-guided)
cycle1_result: Median radiation dose was lower than in 2021; median screening time was 29% longer than in 2021; dose was lower with two operators than one.
cycle2_result: Median radiation dose was 46.45% higher than in 2014; median screening time was shorter than in 2014 but increased with more operators, with 4-operator procedures having the longest screening times; operator number had no significant effect on dose in 2021.
other_findings: Authors suggest the dose increase may result from ageing equipment and note possible implications for procedure protocol; this was a comparative dose audit rather than a targeted intervention re-audit.
authors: Threader M; Sketcher R; Puppala S
citation: Threader M, Sketcher R, Puppala S. Audit of radiation doses during endovascular aneurysm repair. . 2026. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-8555129/v1.

title: Operating Theatre Utilisation at Colombo South Teaching Hospital: A Single-institution Audit of Elective Surgical Efficiency
standard: not reported
finding: Mean scheduled-session utilisation 58.1% (SD 14.2%); extended capacity utilisation 38.7%; first-case delays negatively correlated with utilisation (r=-0.60)

cycle1_result: Mean scheduled-session utilisation 58.1% (SD 14.2%); extended capacity utilisation 38.7%; first-case delays negatively correlated with utilisation (r=-0.60)

title: Safely developing respiratory care during emergency neonatal transport by a long-term quality improvement program
standard: A locally defined set of quality indicators for respiratory care during transport (no external named guideline; no explicit ventilation protocol)
finding: Use of ventilation modes supporting all breaths (Volume Guarantee/HFOV) was 38%
change: Systematic computerised data collection and analysis of ventilator parameters, waveforms and loops during transport, discussed at regular case review meetings (n=21)
setting: Emergency interhospital neonatal transport service
cycle1_n: 1031 infants over the full 8.5-year study (period-specific n not reported)
cycle1_result: Use of ventilation modes supporting all breaths (Volume Guarantee/HFOV) was 38%
intervention: Systematic computerised data collection and analysis of ventilator parameters, waveforms and loops during transport, discussed at regular case review meetings (n=21)
cycle2_n: 1031 infants over the full 8.5-year study (period-specific n not reported)
cycle2_result: Use of ventilation modes supporting all breaths increased to 56%

standard: WHO recommendations for cataract surgery outcomes
finding: Majority of eyes (83.6%) had preoperative vision less than 6/18; surgical complications were not severe enough to affect final best-corrected visual acuity
setting: Sabatia Eye Hospital, rural Kenya
cycle1_result: Majority of eyes (83.6%) had preoperative vision less than 6/18; surgical complications were not severe enough to affect final best-corrected visual acuity
other_findings: Comorbidities negatively correlated with visual outcomes; local apprenticeship-based training model achieved outcomes meeting WHO recommendations.

topic: Oxytocin cessation policy in induced labour
title: Ceasing oxytocin in the active phase of the first stage of induced labours: A prospective audit at a tertiary hospital
standard: Local policy based on randomised trial evidence that ceasing oxytocin in active phase reduces uterine tachysystole/abnormal fetal heart rate
finding: Caesarean delivery 29%; oxytocin ceased for at least two hours or until birth in 13% of women
change: Introduced a policy recommending cessation of oxytocin infusion in the active phase of the first stage of induced labour
setting: Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, tertiary hospital
cycle1_result: Caesarean delivery 29%; oxytocin ceased for at least two hours or until birth in 13% of women
intervention: Introduced a policy recommending cessation of oxytocin infusion in the active phase of the first stage of induced labour
cycle2_result: Caesarean delivery 28% (p=0.77, not significant); oxytocin cessation compliance rose to 35%; instrumental birth for maternal indications increased from 6.8% to 13% (p=0.0005); median labour length increased by one hour (5.4 vs 6.4 hours, p=0.006); maternal satisfaction modestly lower (median 41 vs 38, p=0.03)
other_findings: Perinatal outcomes (cord gases, Apgar, NICU admission) were similar between groups; poor uptake and negative staff perceptions were barriers to translating trial efficacy into practice.
authors: O’Dea S; Davis G; Balendran J; Phipps H; O’Brien K; de Vries B
citation: O’Dea S, Davis G, Balendran J, Phipps H, O’Brien K, de Vries B. Ceasing oxytocin in the active phase of the first stage of induced labours: A prospective audit at a tertiary hospital. . 2026. doi:10.64898/2026.07.17.26358359.

finding: 73.5% of seriously injured patients presented outwith normal working hours; survival was 65.3% at the start of the six-year audit period among 23479 patients admitted for at least three days or who died
change: Increased presence of consultants in accident and emergency medicine, anaesthetics and surgery over the audit period
setting: 20 Scottish hospitals (25 contributing to national database), national trauma audit
cycle1_result: 73.5% of seriously injured patients presented outwith normal working hours; survival was 65.3% at the start of the six-year audit period among 23479 patients admitted for at least three days or who died
intervention: Increased presence of consultants in accident and emergency medicine, anaesthetics and surgery over the audit period
cycle2_result: Survival of seriously injured patients increased significantly to 75.6%, significantly better than the rest of the UK; no trimodal distribution of death was found
other_findings: Seniority of the accident and emergency doctor was associated with improved outcome.
authors: Beard D; Henry JM; Grant PT
citation: Beard D, Henry JM, Grant PT. National audit of the management of injured patients in 20 Scottish hospitals. Health Bull (Edinb). 2000;58(2):118-126. PMID: 12813839.

title: An audit of the positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis in cervical smears: 2001-2002.
standard: Positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis for CIN2 or worse, published annually for laboratories in the UK National Health Service Cervical Screening Programme (NHSCSP)
finding: Positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis for CIN2 or worse was as high as 91.6% for one consultant
setting: Department of Cellular Pathology (Cytology), Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne, UK
cycle1_result: Positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis for CIN2 or worse was as high as 91.6% for one consultant
cycle2_result: PPV fell for four of the five consultants reporting cervical smears, the greatest fall being from 91.6% to 77.9%; mainly attributed to the type of biopsy taken at colposcopy
other_findings: There is variation across laboratories in collection and submission of KC61 data, which needs to be considered when comparing laboratory PPV data.
authors: Wadehra V; Johnson SJ
journal: Cytopathology : official journal of the British Society for Clinical Cytology
citation: Wadehra V, Johnson SJ. An audit of the positive predictive value of high-grade dyskaryosis in cervical smears: 2001-2002. Cytopathology. 2003;14(3):107-114. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2303.2003.00047.x. PMID: 12828718.

title: An audit of a specialist registrar-run outpatient diagnostic hysteroscopy service in a district general hospital.
standard: not reported
finding: Hysteroscopy performed satisfactorily in 91.1% of cases; pathology found in 39% (endometrial polyp 34.1%, submucous fibroid 7.3%); endometrial biopsy performed in 65.8% with no malignancies found
setting: Outpatient hysteroscopy clinic, small district general hospital, Princess of Wales Hospital, Bridgend, UK
cycle1_result: Hysteroscopy performed satisfactorily in 91.1% of cases; pathology found in 39% (endometrial polyp 34.1%, submucous fibroid 7.3%); endometrial biopsy performed in 65.8% with no malignancies found
other_findings: Inpatient hysteroscopy rate was higher than expected due to the high incidence of polyps rather than failure to hysteroscope satisfactorily in clinic.
authors: Beukenholdt R; Guerrero K
journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
citation: Beukenholdt R, Guerrero K. An audit of a specialist registrar-run outpatient diagnostic hysteroscopy service in a district general hospital. J Obstet Gynaecol. 2003;23(3):294-296. doi:10.1080/01443610310000100132. PMID: 12850865.

topic: Post-splenectomy vaccination and antibiotic prophylaxis compliance
title: An audit of post-splenectomy prophylaxis--are we following the guidelines?
standard: Published guidelines for immunisation and antibiotic prophylaxis post-splenectomy
finding: 72% vaccinated (30/76 pneumococcal+HIB+meningococcal, 15/76 Pneumovax+HIB, 10/76 Pneumovax only); 63% discharged on prophylactic antibiotics; 81% of survivors had adequate GP communication
setting: District general hospital
cycle1_result: 72% vaccinated (30/76 pneumococcal+HIB+meningococcal, 15/76 Pneumovax+HIB, 10/76 Pneumovax only); 63% discharged on prophylactic antibiotics; 81% of survivors had adequate GP communication
other_findings: Non-elective splenectomy patients were less likely to be vaccinated or receive prophylactic antibiotics than elective patients; vaccination rates and patient/GP information need improvement.
authors: Ramachandra J; Bond A; Ranaboldo C; Cullis J
journal: Annals of the Royal College of Surgeons of England
citation: Ramachandra J, Bond A, Ranaboldo C, Cullis J. An audit of post-splenectomy prophylaxis--are we following the guidelines?. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2003;85(4):252-255. doi:10.1308/003588403766274962. PMID: 12855028.

title: Troponin testing: an audit in three metropolitan hospitals.
standard: Protocol for troponin I assay use disseminated at introduction
finding: Single assay used in 55% of episodes, serial in 45%; serial troponin testing followed the protocol adequately but single assays were used extensively and probably inappropriately
setting: Three metropolitan hospitals (emergency department and coronary care unit)
cycle1_result: Single assay used in 55% of episodes, serial in 45%; serial troponin testing followed the protocol adequately but single assays were used extensively and probably inappropriately
other_findings: Only 7% of single assays diagnosed a myocardial infarction.
authors: Davey RX
citation: Davey RX. Troponin testing: an audit in three metropolitan hospitals. Med J Aust. 2003;179(2):81-83. doi:10.5694/j.1326-5377.2003.tb05440.x. PMID: 12864717.

topic: Adverse reactions to intravenous immunoglobulin in primary antibody deficiency
title: Prospective audit of adverse reactions occurring in 459 primary antibody-deficient patients receiving intravenous immunoglobulin.
standard: not reported
finding: Overall reaction rate 0.8% (could have been 0.5% if predisposing factors considered); no severe reactions
setting: Multiple immunology centres
cycle1_result: Overall reaction rate 0.8% (could have been 0.5% if predisposing factors considered); no severe reactions
other_findings: Recommends ongoing training for patients and staff; suggests reviewing guidance on prescribing self-injectable adrenaline given no severe reactions occurred.
authors: Brennan VM; Salomé-Bentley NJ; Chapel HM; Immunology Nurses Study
citation: Brennan VM, Salomé-Bentley NJ, Chapel HM, Immunology Nurses Study. Prospective audit of adverse reactions occurring in 459 primary antibody-deficient patients receiving intravenous immunoglobulin. Clin Exp Immunol. 2003;133(2):247-251. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2249.2003.02199.x. PMID: 12869031.

topic: Delegated authorisation compliance for nuclear medicine referrals (IRMER)
title: Introduction, audit and review of guidelines for delegated authorization of nuclear medicine investigations in compliance with the Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations 2000.
standard: Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations 2000; local Delegated Authorization Guidelines (DAG)
finding: 437/632 (69%) referrals fitted the DAG; 12% (75) required clarification; 19% (120) were directly authorized by the practitioner
change: DAG revised following review of non-matching referrals
setting: Two sites, Sheffield Teaching Hospitals
cycle1_result: 437/632 (69%) referrals fitted the DAG; 12% (75) required clarification; 19% (120) were directly authorized by the practitioner
intervention: DAG revised following review of non-matching referrals
other_findings: Delegated authorisation procedure implemented successfully; identified need to improve the referral request card format.
authors: Harris AM; Greaves CD; Taylor CM; Taylor C; Segasby CA; Tindale WB
citation: Harris AM, Greaves CD, Taylor CM, Taylor C, Segasby CA, Tindale WB. Introduction, audit and review of guidelines for delegated authorization of nuclear medicine investigations in compliance with the Ionising Radiation (Medical Exposure) Regulations 2000. Nucl Med Commun. 2003;24(8):939-942. doi:10.1097/01.mnm.0000084590.29433.b1. PMID: 12869828.

title: Stereotactic breast biopsy: an audit of 18 months at BreastScreen Auckland.
standard: not reported
finding: 10 (2%) failed, 70.7% benign, 10.3% ADH, 18.6% malignant; failure rate and complication rate (0.5%) comparable with published series
setting: BreastScreen Auckland national breast screening programme
cycle1_result: 10 (2%) failed, 70.7% benign, 10.3% ADH, 18.6% malignant; failure rate and complication rate (0.5%) comparable with published series
other_findings: Results compared informally with other published series rather than an explicit named standard.
authors: Greenberg D; Johnston J; Hart R; Weston M; Benson-Cooper D
citation: Greenberg D, Johnston J, Hart R, Weston M, Benson-Cooper D. Stereotactic breast biopsy: an audit of 18 months at BreastScreen Auckland. Australas Radiol. 2003;47(3):261-267. doi:10.1046/j.1440-1673.2003.01197.x. PMID: 12890246.

title: Preventive medical care in remote Aboriginal communities in the Northern Territory: a follow-up study of the impact of clinical guidelines, computerised recall and reminder systems, and audit and feedback.
standard: Best practice guidelines for preventive medical services (developed and disseminated as part of the intervention)
finding: Baseline levels of preventive service delivery prior to the multifaceted intervention
change: Development and dissemination of best practice guidelines, an electronic client register with recall and reminder systems, associated staff training, and regular audit and feedback of clinical records against the guidelines
setting: Seven remote Aboriginal community health centres, Northern Territory
cycle1_result: Baseline levels of preventive service delivery prior to the multifaceted intervention
intervention: Development and dissemination of best practice guidelines, an electronic client register with recall and reminder systems, associated staff training, and regular audit and feedback of clinical records against the guidelines
cycle2_result: Initial improvement in service delivery levels following the intervention for most services, but improvements were in general not fully sustained over the 3-year period; baseline and follow-up levels were in many cases higher than comparable North American/UK studies
other_findings: Levels of service delivery varied between services and between communities; authors suggest sustainability may need institutionalisation of work practices and enhanced health centre capacity.
authors: Bailie RS; Togni SJ; Si D; Robinson G; d'Abbs PH
citation: Bailie RS, Togni SJ, Si D, Robinson G, d'Abbs PH. Preventive medical care in remote Aboriginal communities in the Northern Territory: a follow-up study of the impact of clinical guidelines, computerised recall and reminder systems, and audit and feedback. BMC Health Serv Res. 2003;3(1):15. doi:10.1186/1472-6963-3-15. PMID: 12890291.

title: Early warning system scores and response times: an audit.
standard: Established response timescale for calls triggered by the modified early warning system (DMEWS) (specific target not stated)
finding: Response by members of the surgical teams to calls triggered by DMEWS was below the agreed standard response timescale
setting: Intensive Care Unit, Derbyshire Royal Infirmary, Southern Derbyshire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust, Derby, UK
cycle1_result: Response by members of the surgical teams to calls triggered by DMEWS was below the agreed standard response timescale
other_findings: DMEWS successfully triggered nurses to initiate action for immediate treatment; further studies were planned to determine whether longer response times affect patient outcome.
authors: Day BA
citation: Day BA. Early warning system scores and response times: an audit. Nurs Crit Care. 2003;8(4):156-164. doi:10.1046/j.1478-5153.2003.00026.x. PMID: 12940691.

topic: Hand-arm vibration syndrome cold provocation test evaluation
title: Cold provocation testing and hand-arm vibration syndrome--an audit of the results of the Department of Trade and Industry scheme for the evaluation of miners.
standard: not reported
finding: The cold provocation test with measurement of digital rewarming times was found to be of no value in assessing vibration-induced vascular damage to the hands
setting: 18 HAVS test centres in the UK, Department of Trade and Industry scheme for evaluation of miners
cycle1_result: The cold provocation test with measurement of digital rewarming times was found to be of no value in assessing vibration-induced vascular damage to the hands
other_findings: This report was the second analysis of continuous audit findings monitored by the Medical Reference Panel advising the Department of Trade and Industry.
authors: Proud G; Burke F; Lawson IJ; McGeoch KL; Miles JN
citation: Proud G, Burke F, Lawson IJ, McGeoch KL, Miles JN. Cold provocation testing and hand-arm vibration syndrome--an audit of the results of the Department of Trade and Industry scheme for the evaluation of miners. Br J Surg. 2003;90(9):1076-1079. doi:10.1002/bjs.4200. PMID: 12945074.

title: An audit of medicolegal conferencing.
standard: not reported
finding: Prospective study of 50 consecutive medicolegal conferences found conferencing time-consuming and expensive, of limited value where little disagreement existed, and more effective when held in person than by telephone
setting: Medicolegal practice, Shrewsbury, UK, within the English civil justice system
cycle1_result: Prospective study of 50 consecutive medicolegal conferences found conferencing time-consuming and expensive, of limited value where little disagreement existed, and more effective when held in person than by telephone
other_findings: An agenda and advance provision of relevant documents to participants were recommended; a formal combined audit of conferencing by medical and legal professions was recommended.
authors: Pringle RG
journal: Journal of the Royal Society of Medicine
citation: Pringle RG. An audit of medicolegal conferencing. J R Soc Med. 2003;96(9):454-457. doi:10.1177/014107680309600910. PMID: 12949203.

title: Pathways for continence care: an audit to assess how they are used.
standard: Guidelines for Continence Care (Department of Health, 2000) promoting use of care pathways
finding: Nearly half of respondents were currently using the continence care pathways and found them effective
setting: Healthcare professionals in continence care nationally
cycle1_result: Nearly half of respondents were currently using the continence care pathways and found them effective
other_findings: Variance tracking, intended as the driver for pathway change, had not significantly influenced local pathways.
authors: Bayliss V; Salter L; Locke R
journal: British journal of nursing (Mark Allen Publishing)
citation: Bayliss V, Salter L, Locke R. Pathways for continence care: an audit to assess how they are used. Br J Nurs. 2003;12(14):857-863. doi:10.12968/bjon.2003.12.14.11410. PMID: 12951537.

title: Audit of the care of women requesting induced abortion.
standard: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists Evidence-Based Guideline No. 7 (2000)
finding: Prospective audit of all induced abortions identified areas of practice not meeting RCOG guideline standards (details not reported)
change: Department guidelines produced to address identified areas for improvement
setting: Buckinghamshire district general hospital, UK
cycle1_result: Prospective audit of all induced abortions identified areas of practice not meeting RCOG guideline standards (details not reported)
intervention: Department guidelines produced to address identified areas for improvement
other_findings: The audit demonstrates how change can be implemented when local practice is audited against national guidelines.
authors: Morrison J
journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology
citation: Morrison J. Audit of the care of women requesting induced abortion. J Obstet Gynaecol. 2003;23(5):521-524. doi:10.1080/0144361031000153774. PMID: 12963512.

title: Auditing and improving notification and chemoprophylaxis in bacterial meningitis.
standard: not reported
finding: 28/79 (35%) cases notified; chemoprophylaxis given to 20/26 (77%) meningococcal cases, inappropriate drugs used in 4 cases, distributed too widely in 10 cases
change: Clinician education in the hospital with poorest notification performance, and districtwide education on chemoprophylaxis
setting: Mid Glamorgan Health Authority, four acute hospitals
cycle1_result: 28/79 (35%) cases notified; chemoprophylaxis given to 20/26 (77%) meningococcal cases, inappropriate drugs used in 4 cases, distributed too widely in 10 cases
intervention: Clinician education in the hospital with poorest notification performance, and districtwide education on chemoprophylaxis
cycle2_result: Significant improvement in notification in the targeted hospital, no change in control hospital; chemoprophylaxis improved districtwide, though rifampicin still distributed too widely
other_findings: Provides an example of a completed audit cycle in public health medicine.
authors: Harvey I; Kaul S; Peters TJ
journal: Journal of epidemiology and community health
citation: Harvey I, Kaul S, Peters TJ. Auditing and improving notification and chemoprophylaxis in bacterial meningitis. J Epidemiol Community Health. 1992;46(4):329-331. doi:10.1136/jech.46.4.329. PMID: 1431700.

title: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance: audit and the impact of potential litigation. Retrospective review of 682 cases.
standard: not reported
finding: 28.6% of original Class III diagnoses were cytological overdiagnoses on retrospective review; 197 cases reclassified to Class II
setting: National Cervical Cancer Screening Programme
cycle1_result: 28.6% of original Class III diagnoses were cytological overdiagnoses on retrospective review; 197 cases reclassified to Class II
other_findings: Investigation triggered by a threefold increase in Class III diagnoses; conducted for quality assurance rather than against a stated external guideline.
authors: Scheiden R; Wagener C; Knolle U; Dippel W; Capesius C
journal: Cytopathology : official journal of the British Society for Clinical Cytology
citation: Scheiden R, Wagener C, Knolle U, Dippel W, Capesius C. Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance: audit and the impact of potential litigation. Retrospective review of 682 cases. Cytopathology. 2003;14(5):257-262. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2303.2003.00070.x. PMID: 14510889.

topic: Hepatitis B vaccination uptake in GUM clinics
title: Offering the vaccine and accepting it: an audit of hepatitis B vaccination in West Midlands region.
standard: 1999 Medical Society for the Study of Venereal Disease National Guidelines
finding: not reported
setting: Genitourinary medicine clinics, West Midlands
cycle1_result: not reported
other_findings: not reported
authors: Jaleel H; Allan PS; Huengsberg M; Natin D; West Midlands Regional Audit Committee
citation: Jaleel H, Allan PS, Huengsberg M, Natin D, West Midlands Regional Audit Committee. Offering the vaccine and accepting it: an audit of hepatitis B vaccination in West Midlands region. Int J STD AIDS. 2003;14(9):632-635. doi:10.1258/095646203322301112. PMID: 14511502.

topic: Soft tissue sarcoma referral and management pathway
title: An audit of the management of soft tissue sarcoma within a health region in the UK.
standard: not reported
finding: 49.5% first referred to general surgeons, 16% to orthopaedic surgeons; only 15% of patients fit for surgery were referred to a specialist sarcoma surgeon before definitive exploration; 64% of deep tumours had a preoperative biopsy and only 68% had a scan before biopsy or definitive surgery
setting: Trent Cancer Registry region, UK
cycle1_result: 49.5% first referred to general surgeons, 16% to orthopaedic surgeons; only 15% of patients fit for surgery were referred to a specialist sarcoma surgeon before definitive exploration; 64% of deep tumours had a preoperative biopsy and only 68% had a scan before biopsy or definitive surgery
cycle2_result: Only a marginal improvement in management compared with the first audit
other_findings: Tumour grade, completeness of excision and site of the sarcoma influenced survival.
authors: Glencross J; Balasubramanian SP; Bacon J; Robinson MH; Reed MW
journal: European journal of surgical oncology : the journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
citation: Glencross J, Balasubramanian SP, Bacon J, Robinson MH, Reed MW. An audit of the management of soft tissue sarcoma within a health region in the UK. Eur J Surg Oncol. 2003;29(8):670-675. doi:10.1016/s0748-7983(03)00134-3. PMID: 14511616.

topic: Peer chart audit and preventive care
title: Do peer chart audits improve residents' performance in providing preventive care?
standard: not reported
finding: Mean total chart audit scores across five time blocks over 45 months; performance improved significantly then declined in last 10 months but remained higher than baseline.
change: Peer chart audit programme in which residents scored each other on 12 clinical preventive services
setting: Academic medical centre residency programme
cycle1_result: Mean total chart audit scores across five time blocks over 45 months; performance improved significantly then declined in last 10 months but remained higher than baseline.
intervention: Peer chart audit programme in which residents scored each other on 12 clinical preventive services
other_findings: Diffusion of innovations theory may explain the prolonged implementation phase and difficulty maintaining the chart audit programme.
authors: Paukert JL; Chumley-Jones HS; Littlefield JH
journal: Academic medicine : journal of the Association of American Medical Colleges
citation: Paukert JL, Chumley-Jones HS, Littlefield JH. Do peer chart audits improve residents' performance in providing preventive care?. Acad Med. 2003;78(10 Suppl):S39-41. doi:10.1097/00001888-200310001-00013. PMID: 14557091.

topic: Down syndrome prenatal screening programme audit
title: The use of record linkage for auditing the uptake and outcome of prenatal serum screening and prenatal diagnostic tests for Down syndrome.
standard: not reported
finding: Overall uptake of serum screening 58%, uptake of prenatal diagnosis 4% (54% after a positive screen); detection rate 49%, false-positive rate 4%, odds of being affected after a positive result 1:59
setting: 4 London maternity units offering Bart's maternal serum screening, 1990-1999
cycle1_result: Overall uptake of serum screening 58%, uptake of prenatal diagnosis 4% (54% after a positive screen); detection rate 49%, false-positive rate 4%, odds of being affected after a positive result 1:59
cycle2_result: Detection rate rose to 78%, false-positive rate 7%, odds of being affected after a positive result 1:58; using maternal age alone (cut-off >=37) would have given 40% detection and 7-9% false-positive rates across both periods
other_findings: Significant independent influences on uptake of screening included maternal age, ethnicity, year and referring hospital.
authors: Alberman E; Huttly W; Hennessy E; McIntosh A
citation: Alberman E, Huttly W, Hennessy E, McIntosh A. The use of record linkage for auditing the uptake and outcome of prenatal serum screening and prenatal diagnostic tests for Down syndrome. Prenat Diagn. 2003;23(10):801-806. doi:10.1002/pd.683. PMID: 14558023.

title: Two-stage hypospadias repair: audit in a district general hospital.
standard: not reported
finding: Audit of van der Meulen single-stage hypospadias repairs found an unsatisfactory revision rate of 11% and sub-optimal cosmetic result
change: Senior surgeon retrained and changed to the two-stage Bracka technique from 1995
setting: Department of Plastic Surgery, South Manchester University Teaching Hospital, Manchester, UK (district general hospital)
cycle1_result: Audit of van der Meulen single-stage hypospadias repairs found an unsatisfactory revision rate of 11% and sub-optimal cosmetic result
intervention: Senior surgeon retrained and changed to the two-stage Bracka technique from 1995
cycle2_result: Primary repairs (n=81): stage I graft loss 2.5%, stage II complication rate 9.8% (fistula 7.4%, stenosis 1.2%, baggy urethra 1.2%); revision group with prior unsatisfactory single-stage repairs (n=31): graft loss 10%, fistula 12.9%, stenosis 6.5%
other_findings: Results compare favourably with published series from surgeons super-specialised in hypospadias repair.
authors: Price RD; Lambe GF; Jones RP
citation: Price RD, Lambe GF, Jones RP. Two-stage hypospadias repair: audit in a district general hospital. Br J Plast Surg. 2003;56(8):752-758. doi:10.1016/j.bjps.2003.08.015. PMID: 14615249.

topic: Routine preoperative CXR and ECG audit
title: The usefulness of routine preoperative chest X-rays and ECGs: a prospective audit.
standard: not reported
finding: Only 11/324 CXRs and 13/375 ECGs affected anaesthetic technique or choice of therapeutic procedure.
setting: KK Women's and Children's Hospital
cycle1_result: Only 11/324 CXRs and 13/375 ECGs affected anaesthetic technique or choice of therapeutic procedure.
other_findings: Prospective audit of the clinical usefulness of routine preoperative investigations; concluded targeted rather than age-based testing should be used.
authors: Lim EH; Liu EH
citation: Lim EH, Liu EH. The usefulness of routine preoperative chest X-rays and ECGs: a prospective audit. Singapore Med J. 2003;44(7):340-343. PMID: 14620724.

title: Subclinical hypothyroidism: an audit of management.
standard: Thyroxine recommended if serum TSH is 10 mU/L or more, or 5-9.9 mU/L (mild subclinical hypothyroidism) with risk factors such as thyroid peroxidase antibody (TPOAb) positivity
finding: TPOAb and goitre status were both determined in only 39% of subjects with mild subclinical hypothyroidism overall; determined more often by endocrinologists than general physicians (TPOAb 63% vs 22%; goitre 47% vs 17%, P = 0.001); endocrinologists treated 96% of eligible subjects with mild SH versus 67% treated by non-endocrine colleagues (P = 0.024)
setting: Department of Medicine, Caerphilly Miner's Hospital, Caerphilly, UK
cycle1_result: TPOAb and goitre status were both determined in only 39% of subjects with mild subclinical hypothyroidism overall; determined more often by endocrinologists than general physicians (TPOAb 63% vs 22%; goitre 47% vs 17%, P = 0.001); endocrinologists treated 96% of eligible subjects with mild SH versus 67% treated by non-endocrine colleagues (P = 0.024)
other_findings: Both groups sometimes treated subjects with unknown TPOAb status (endocrinologists 21% vs general physicians 40%, P = 0.21); overall evaluation of mild subclinical hypothyroidism was incomplete.
authors: Prakash PK; Bolusani H; Hameed A; Premawardhana LD
citation: Prakash PK, Bolusani H, Hameed A, Premawardhana LD. Subclinical hypothyroidism: an audit of management. Ann Clin Biochem. 2003;40(Pt 6):694-696. doi:10.1258/000456303770367324. PMID: 14629811.

title: An audit of the management of induced abortion in England and Wales.
standard: Agreed audit criteria assessed via single-round questionnaire, prior to publication of the RCOG evidence-based guideline
finding: Standards of care were generally appropriate but areas for improvement were identified: choice of method, infection screening and delays in referral; unnecessary investigations such as cross-matching remained evident; only half of units audited their own procedures and complications
setting: 324 units providing abortion care across England and Wales (NHS hospitals, NHS-funded clinics, agency agreements and private units)
cycle1_n: 240 units (74% response, covering 80% of 176,000 termination procedures)
cycle1_result: Standards of care were generally appropriate but areas for improvement were identified: choice of method, infection screening and delays in referral; unnecessary investigations such as cross-matching remained evident; only half of units audited their own procedures and complications
other_findings: A further round of audit to assess the impact of the subsequent RCOG guideline was recommended.
authors: Thomas J; Paranjothy S; Templeton A
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
citation: Thomas J, Paranjothy S, Templeton A. An audit of the management of induced abortion in England and Wales. Int J Gynaecol Obstet. 2003;83(3):327-334. doi:10.1016/s0020-7292(03)00305-9. PMID: 14643053.

topic: Surgeon awareness of postoperative VTE readmissions
title: Audit of surgeon awareness of readmissions with venous thrombo-embolism.
standard: not reported
finding: Of 34 unplanned readmissions with DVT/PE after surgery, 70.6% were readmitted under a different specialty, 8.8% under the same specialty but different surgeon, and 20.6% under the same surgeon; of 27 patients admitted under a different consultant, only 44.4% had documented evidence the original surgeon was aware of the readmission
setting: John Hunter Hospital, a major tertiary referral teaching hospital, Newcastle, New South Wales, Australia
cycle1_result: Of 34 unplanned readmissions with DVT/PE after surgery, 70.6% were readmitted under a different specialty, 8.8% under the same specialty but different surgeon, and 20.6% under the same surgeon; of 27 patients admitted under a different consultant, only 44.4% had documented evidence the original surgeon was aware of the readmission
other_findings: DVT/PE complication rates after surgery are likely underestimated; improved communication between teams was recommended to improve care.
authors: Swan J; Spigelman AD
citation: Swan J, Spigelman AD. Audit of surgeon awareness of readmissions with venous thrombo-embolism. Intern Med J. 2003;33(12):578-580. doi:10.1111/j.1445-5994.2003.00425.x. PMID: 14656231.

title: National biometry audit.
standard: Royal College of Ophthalmologists (RCOphth) biometry guidelines, including use of the Hoffer Q formula in eyes with axial lengths outside 22.0-26.0 mm
finding: Only 4% of departments adhered to RCOphth guidelines on formula selection by axial length; 17% still used the obsolete SRK II formula for all eyes; 36% used two or more formulae; only 37% of biometrists had attended external training courses; 71% of units claimed to audit refractive results but only 16% (17 departments) knew their percentage of eyes with a given prediction error
setting: 178 eye departments across the United Kingdom (107 surveyed)
cycle1_result: Only 4% of departments adhered to RCOphth guidelines on formula selection by axial length; 17% still used the obsolete SRK II formula for all eyes; 36% used two or more formulae; only 37% of biometrists had attended external training courses; 71% of units claimed to audit refractive results but only 16% (17 departments) knew their percentage of eyes with a given prediction error
other_findings: The study demonstrates poor awareness/implementation of RCOphth biometry guidelines and suggests local audits are not highlighting poor results or driving practice change; the guidelines should be updated to emphasise customising A constants and set benchmark prediction-error standards.
authors: Gale RP; Saha N; Johnston RL
citation: Gale RP, Saha N, Johnston RL. National biometry audit. Eye (Lond). 2004;18(1):63-66. doi:10.1038/sj.eye.6700550. PMID: 14707969.

title: National audit of women with abnormal cervical smears in New Zealand.
standard: National Cervical Screening Programme recommended assessment/treatment/follow-up times
finding: Initial assessment, treatment or follow-up fell outside recommended times in 17-35% of women; 72% of high-grade smears underwent treatment (91% excision biopsy).
setting: National Cervical Screening Programme
cycle1_n: 57% response rate of women with first abnormal smear in 1999
cycle1_result: Initial assessment, treatment or follow-up fell outside recommended times in 17-35% of women; 72% of high-grade smears underwent treatment (91% excision biopsy).
other_findings: Areas for improvement identified, particularly longer than recommended waiting times for assessment and treatment.

cycle1_result: Incidence 0.64/100,000/yr; all 18 units combined bone marrow examination with cytogenetics/FISH but only 13 performed RT-PCR; of 4 units calculating the Hasford Score, only 2 used it to inform decisions; 52% of patients entered clinical trials (57% involving imatinib mesylate); of 23 tissue-typed patients, suitable donors were found for 18 (11 sibling, 7 unrelated), 28% of the total patient population; only 13/64 (20%) lacked a transplant donor or trial entry; 56% received hydroxyurea +/- interferon as first-line therapy
other_findings: 38% of units would consider reduced-intensity allografting in patients over 60 but none routinely tissue-typed such patients; most units felt imatinib should be reserved for clinical trials (83%) and would consider oral ara-C (83%) or pegylated interferon (89%).

title: What's the evidence that NICE guidance has been implemented? Results from a national evaluation using time series analysis, audit of patients' notes, and interviews.
standard: National Institute for Clinical Excellence (NICE) guidance across multiple topics
finding: Implementation of NICE guidance varied by trust and by topic; guidance was more likely to be adopted where there was strong professional support, a stable and convincing evidence base, no increased or unfunded costs, established systems for tracking implementation, and professionals were not isolated
setting: Acute and primary care trusts in England and Wales (random sample of 20 acute trusts, 17 mental health trusts and 21 primary care trusts, plus all primary care prescribing and hospital pharmacies)
cycle1_result: Implementation of NICE guidance varied by trust and by topic; guidance was more likely to be adopted where there was strong professional support, a stable and convincing evidence base, no increased or unfunded costs, established systems for tracking implementation, and professionals were not isolated
other_findings: The design combined interrupted time series analysis, review of case notes, survey and interviews; guidance needs to be clear and reflect the clinical context to improve adoption.
authors: Sheldon TA; Cullum N; Dawson D; Lankshear A; Lowson K; Watt I; West P; Wright D; Wright J

title: Influence of guidelines on CPR decisions: an audit of clerking proforma.
standard: Local guidelines for documenting CPR/DNAR decisions
finding: Consultant documentation of CPR decisions was present in 27/75 (36%) departmental discharges before the proforma was introduced
change: Introduction of new guidelines and a clerking proforma for CPR/DNAR decisions
setting: Department of Elderly Care Medicine, Mayday University Hospital, Croydon, UK
cycle1_result: Consultant documentation of CPR decisions was present in 27/75 (36%) departmental discharges before the proforma was introduced
intervention: Introduction of new guidelines and a clerking proforma for CPR/DNAR decisions
cycle2_result: Documentation improved to 102/109 (94%), 135/148 (91%), 133/140 (95%), 96/119 (81%), 148/157 (94%) and 167/169 (98%) across audits 2-7; the proportion of decisions that were DNAR was 64%, 72%, 45%, 68% and 62% across audits 3-7, with a statistically significant fall in both documentation and DNAR proportion in audit 5, when guidelines required discussion with the patient before a DNAR order
other_findings: No significant difference in age, diagnosis, cognitive function or disability between patients across audits 3-7 when these were recorded.

title: IgA antibodies to human tissue transglutaminase: audit of routine practice confirms high diagnostic accuracy.
standard: not reported
finding: Prevalence of new coeliac disease diagnoses in the population tested was 2.8%; positive predictive value at a 3 units/mL cut-off was 0.77 for primary care samples and 0.92 for hospital samples, with a sensitivity of 92% (75 consecutive new diagnoses assessed); EMA was rarely negative at TGA levels of 4.9 units/mL or above
setting: Department of Chemical Pathology, Southern Derbyshire Acute Hospitals NHS Trust, Derby, UK
cycle1_period: following introduction of the TGA test into routine practice in 2002
cycle1_result: Prevalence of new coeliac disease diagnoses in the population tested was 2.8%; positive predictive value at a 3 units/mL cut-off was 0.77 for primary care samples and 0.92 for hospital samples, with a sensitivity of 92% (75 consecutive new diagnoses assessed); EMA was rarely negative at TGA levels of 4.9 units/mL or above
other_findings: TGA is recommended as the first-line serological test for coeliac disease; IgA deficiency should be excluded with low TGA absorbance readings, and interference considered with slightly raised TGA and negative EMA.

topic: Down syndrome prenatal screening programme audit

standard: Age-standardised target detection and false-positive rates for Down syndrome screening (e.g. 59-64% detection and 4.2-5.4% false-positive at a 1-in-250 term cut-off; 65-68% detection and 6.1-7.3% false-positive at a 1-in-270 mid-trimester cut-off)

cycle1_result: Audited detection rates among the five centres ranged from 7% below target to 10% above target; audited false-positive rates were better than target by 0.3 to 1.5 percentage points

topic: Costed profile audit of stress incontinence surgery
title: A costed profile audit of the surgical management of female stress incontinence.

finding: Tension-free vaginal tape was the cheapest treatment by both expected profile and observed real-patient cost; colposuspension was the most expensive, with real costs significantly greater than the expected profile; length of stay was the main determinant of overall cost
setting: Department of Gynaecology, Southern General Hospital, Glasgow, UK
cycle1_result: Tension-free vaginal tape was the cheapest treatment by both expected profile and observed real-patient cost; colposuspension was the most expensive, with real costs significantly greater than the expected profile; length of stay was the main determinant of overall cost
other_findings: Exception reporting (comparing expected vs real costs) revealed clinical issues such as length of stay, duration of surgery, patient selection and complication rates; the technique is limited by the need for accurate, detailed activity data.
authors: Tierney JP; Robins JB; Anthony GS; Bjornsson S; Orr G

title: Electrophysiologic and objective monitoring of the cochlear implant during surgery: implementation, audit and outcomes.

title: Quality improvement process in the adherence to gastric decontamination guidelines for poison exposures as recommended by a poison control center.
standard: A revised (February 2002) guideline narrowing the use of ipecac syrup, gastric lavage, cathartics and activated charcoal for poison exposures.

finding: GP adherence to guideline referral criteria was 55%; hospital doctor adherence was 70%; hospital doctor referrals averaged 26.6 per week
change: Referrals were assessed against NICE dyspepsia guidelines by two part-time GPs, with feedback sent to clinicians whose requests did not adhere to the referral criteria
setting: Three endoscopy units in two hospital trusts
cycle1_result: GP adherence to guideline referral criteria was 55%; hospital doctor adherence was 70%; hospital doctor referrals averaged 26.6 per week

standard: Audit standard derived from published guidelines: patients prescribed antipsychotics should have blood pressure, BMI (or other obesity measure), blood glucose (or HbA1c) and plasma lipids measured at least once a year
finding: A recorded measurement within the previous year was found for blood pressure in 26%, obesity in 17%, blood glucose/HbA1c in 28% and plasma lipids in 22%, with all four measures documented in only 11%; 6% had a documented diagnosis of diabetes, 6% hypertension and 6% dyslipidaemia
setting: 48 multidisciplinary assertive outreach teams, 21 mental health services
cycle1_result: A recorded measurement within the previous year was found for blood pressure in 26%, obesity in 17%, blood glucose/HbA1c in 28% and plasma lipids in 22%, with all four measures documented in only 11%; 6% had a documented diagnosis of diabetes, 6% hypertension and 6% dyslipidaemia
other_findings: Extrapolation suggested for every known case of diabetes another was undiagnosed, for every known hypertension case 4 were missed, and for every known dyslipidaemia case 7 were missed; clinical teams cited uncertainty over responsibility, low confidence interpreting abnormal results and limited access to equipment as barriers to screening.
authors: Barnes TR; Paton C; Cavanagh MR; Hancock E; Taylor DM; UK Prescribing Observatory for Mental Health

topic: Care of the dying against the Liverpool Care Pathway
title: Audit of the care of the dying in a network of hospitals and institutions in Queensland.
standard: 18 goals of the Liverpool Care Pathway for the dying
finding: Several goals were poorly documented, especially communication, resuscitation orders and care after death; written information for families was rarely documented; hospice units achieved most goals more often than other settings.
setting: Network of 8 institutions (4 hospitals, 3 hospices, 1 nursing home), Queensland
cycle1_result: Several goals were poorly documented, especially communication, resuscitation orders and care after death; written information for families was rarely documented; hospice units achieved most goals more often than other settings.
other_findings: Marked differences in practice were noted between institutions; end-stage care pathways may provide a model for improving care of the dying more widely.
authors: Hardy JR; Haberecht J; Maresco-Pennisi D; Yates P; Australian Best Care of the Dying  Network, Queensland

intervention: A new system was introduced including a patient education leaflet and removal date scheduling prior to hospital discharge, replacing the stent logbook

cycle1_result: Poor quality of care was noted in 59% of maternal deaths; direct obstetric causes accounted for 74%, mainly haemorrhage (32.2%) and infection (31.6%); maternal mortality ratio did not improve over 10 years.
other_findings: Deficiencies in the health system, medical errors, patients' financial constraints and inadequate management of septic abortion were the main contributing factors.

title: Perioperative fluid management: prospective audit.
standard: not reported
finding: No correlation between routinely available fluid balance parameters and quantities of fluid/electrolytes prescribed; 57 of 106 patients (54%) developed at least one fluid-related complication; these patients received significantly more fluid and sodium, had higher non-fluid complication and death rates and longer hospital stay; mean daily fluid load predicted fluid-related complications on multivariate analysis
setting: General surgical unit
cycle1_result: No correlation between routinely available fluid balance parameters and quantities of fluid/electrolytes prescribed; 57 of 106 patients (54%) developed at least one fluid-related complication; these patients received significantly more fluid and sodium, had higher non-fluid complication and death rates and longer hospital stay; mean daily fluid load predicted fluid-related complications on multivariate analysis
other_findings: Fluid prescribing practice in general surgical units was sub-optimal, causing avoidable iatrogenic complications; involvement of senior staff, education and possibly prescribing protocols may improve the situation.

title: Peer chart audits: a tool to meet Accreditation Council on Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) competency in practice-based learning and improvement.
standard: ACGME practice-based learning and improvement competency requirement for documentation of diabetic foot examination (neurological, vascular, skin)
finding: 13% of patients had documented neurological foot exams; 45% had documented vascular exams
change: Repeated peer chart audits by resident physicians on their peers' patient records, with no formal feedback or education provided

cycle1_result: 13% of patients had documented neurological foot exams; 45% had documented vascular exams
intervention: Repeated peer chart audits by resident physicians on their peers' patient records, with no formal feedback or education provided
cycle2_result: Documentation increased to 33% for neurological exams (+20 points, p=0.001) and to 71% for vascular exams (+26 points); skin exam documentation also improved (exact figure truncated in the abstract)

topic: Community-acquired pneumonia severity assessment guideline adherence
title: Community-acquired pneumonia: doctors do not follow national guidelines.
standard: British Thoracic Society (BTS) guidelines for assessment and management of community-acquired pneumonia, including severity scoring
finding: 65 of 165 patients were wrongly coded as CAP and excluded, leaving 100 in the study; 48% did not receive a severity score
change: An educational programme on CAP management was introduced
setting: Medical assessment unit
cycle1_result: 65 of 165 patients were wrongly coded as CAP and excluded, leaving 100 in the study; 48% did not receive a severity score
intervention: An educational programme on CAP management was introduced
cycle2_period: 2005/6, 3 months of winter, 3 years after the educational programme
cycle2_result: 43 of 130 were excluded, leaving 87 enrolled; 87% did not receive a severity score, a significant increase (worsening) from 48% in 2001/2
other_findings: Coding of CAP remained poor; adherence to BTS management guidelines was poor and significantly worsened after the educational programme; the authors conclude education alone does not improve adherence and suggest restricting antibiotic prescribing should be considered.
authors: Collini P; Beadsworth M; Anson J; Neal T; Burnham P; Deegan P; Beeching N; Miller A

title: An audit of treatment outcome in acromegalic patients attending our center at Bergamo, Italy.
standard: not reported (hormonal targets for GH/IGF-I)
finding: At last evaluation 22% were cured, 37.1% controlled by ongoing drugs, 22.6% had discordant GH/IGF-I, and 18.2% still had active disease; safe GH and normal IGF-I achieved in 78% and 63.5% overall.

topic: Practice policy on pharmaceutical sales representative access
title: General practitioners and pharmaceutical sales representatives: quality improvement research.
standard: Locally developed practice policy on GP-pharmaceutical sales representative interaction
finding: Before intervention GPs spent an average of 40 min/doctor/month with pharmaceutical sales representatives; 239 items of promotional material and 4,660 sample tablets were present.
change: Staff survey and feedback, followed by a staff-voted practice policy restricting reception booking of PSR visits, sample cupboard access and consulting-hours visits.
setting: Australian general practice
cycle1_result: Before intervention GPs spent an average of 40 min/doctor/month with pharmaceutical sales representatives; 239 items of promotional material and 4,660 sample tablets were present.
intervention: Staff survey and feedback, followed by a staff-voted practice policy restricting reception booking of PSR visits, sample cupboard access and consulting-hours visits.
cycle2_result: Promotional material reduced by 32% and sample tablets by 59% at 3 months, sustained at 9 months; generic prescribing increased significantly at 3 months (OR 2.28) and 9 months (OR 2.07).

topic: TVT sling insertion NICE guideline compliance
title: Audit of compliance with NICE guidelines on the use of tension-free vaginal tape slings for stress incontinence.
standard: NICE guidelines on the use of tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) slings for stress urinary incontinence, including trialling conservative measures first and documenting risk factors and consent
finding: 95 TVT sling insertions (79 by gynaecologists, 16 by urologists); conservative measures had been tried by 43 patients (45.3%); documentation of risk factors ranged from 70% (failure, intermittent catheterisation) to 1% (laparotomy, dyspareunia); compliance and consent documentation were significantly better when insertions were carried out by gynaecologists than by urologists; all insertions were performed by, or under direct supervision of, consultants
setting: Gynaecology and urology departments, district general hospital
cycle1_result: 95 TVT sling insertions (79 by gynaecologists, 16 by urologists); conservative measures had been tried by 43 patients (45.3%); documentation of risk factors ranged from 70% (failure, intermittent catheterisation) to 1% (laparotomy, dyspareunia); compliance and consent documentation were significantly better when insertions were carried out by gynaecologists than by urologists; all insertions were performed by, or under direct supervision of, consultants
other_findings: The audit highlighted the need to try conservative measures before TVT insertion and to document patient counselling on the consent form; developing patient information leaflets and specific consent forms and improving gynaecology-urology cooperation is likely to improve compliance.

journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology : the journal of the Institute of Obstetrics and Gynaecology

topic: Blood pressure control in clinical practice

topic: A&E to medical ward transfer time
title: Transfer delay audit.
standard: not reported
finding: Average transfer time for all patients was 91.5 minutes; the longest average (105 minutes) occurred in the 17:00-24:00 interval; 26.5% of patients arrived later than 2 hours after referral

cycle1_result: Average transfer time for all patients was 91.5 minutes; the longest average (105 minutes) occurred in the 17:00-24:00 interval; 26.5% of patients arrived later than 2 hours after referral
other_findings: The findings confirm unacceptably long transfer times for a significant number of patients; causes for the delay should be investigated to find and implement solutions.

title: National audit of cerebrospinal fluid testing.
standard: National guidelines for spectrophotometric scanning of CSF for haem pigments and bilirubin; national reference ranges for CSF glucose, protein and lactate are not yet standardised
finding: Most laboratories analysed CSF satisfactorily; there was variation in reference ranges used for glucose, protein and lactate; concerns were raised about sample rejection policies and the wavelengths used to measure bilirubin; some hospitals lacked spectrophotometric scanning for haem pigments and bilirubin, though those that performed it did so in line with national guidelines
setting: UK clinical biochemistry laboratories (NEQAS survey)
cycle1_result: Most laboratories analysed CSF satisfactorily; there was variation in reference ranges used for glucose, protein and lactate; concerns were raised about sample rejection policies and the wavelengths used to measure bilirubin; some hospitals lacked spectrophotometric scanning for haem pigments and bilirubin, though those that performed it did so in line with national guidelines
other_findings: National agreement on reference ranges for glucose, protein and lactate should be achievable; some hospitals may not have responded because they do not offer spectrophotometric scanning.

topic: Health promotion screening and delivery documentation vs patient perception
title: A comparison of patients' perceptions and an audit of health promotion practice within a UK hospital.
standard: Requirement for UK hospitals to monitor health promotion services (screening for smoking, alcohol, obesity, diet, physical activity)
finding: Agreement between audit and questionnaire for screening was at best fair; agreement for health promotion delivery was moderate for alcohol, poor for exercise, and no different from chance for smoking and diet; agreement on risk factor identification was very good for obesity, good for smoking, moderate for alcohol

cycle1_result: Agreement between audit and questionnaire for screening was at best fair; agreement for health promotion delivery was moderate for alcohol, poor for exercise, and no different from chance for smoking and diet; agreement on risk factor identification was very good for obesity, good for smoking, moderate for alcohol
other_findings: Authors recommend patient questionnaire as preferred method for monitoring health promotion delivery, and audit as preferred method for screening evaluation, ideally validated screening tools.

change: New guidelines for nosebleed management, nasal packing protocol, discharge policy, staff training, and patient information leaflets

cycle1_result: Previously all patients requiring nasal packing were admitted; mean 28 patients admitted per month, mean inpatient stay 2.67 days

topic: Thromboprophylaxis use in elderly medical inpatients

setting: 30 wards, 10 hospitals, Yorkshire region
cycle1_result: 601 patients studied (mean age 84.6 years); 117 (19.5%) had indications for thromboprophylaxis with no contraindications, of whom only 34 (29%) were receiving prophylaxis as per guidelines; more than one indication was present in 17% of those left untreated; medical ward patients were more likely to receive appropriate treatment than geriatric ward patients (43% vs 23%, p=0.03)

cycle1_result: 85 of 285 hospitals (29.8%) contributed 3262 cases; overall technical success rate 98% and complication rate 6.3%; significant risk factors for complications included rigors, anaemia and impaired renal function; low frequency operators had lower success and higher complication rates than high frequency operators, though all groups exceeded target thresholds; sepsis was a risk factor in most serious complications and all deaths

topic: Medical evacuation (MEDEVAC) command and control timeliness
title: Audit of the effectiveness of command and control arrangements for medical evacuation of seriously ill or injured casualties in southern Afghanistan 2007.
standard: 90-minute standard from notification to helicopter landing for Category A/B casualties (in hospital within 2 hours of wounding)
finding: Prior rotations showed comparatively longer response times (specific figures not given).
change: Medical operations staff were relocated into the Combined Joint Operations Centre (CJOC), collocating medical and operations staff.
setting: NATO Regional Command (South), southern Afghanistan field hospitals
cycle1_period: Two previous RC-S rotations (prior to 1 May 2007)
cycle1_result: Prior rotations showed comparatively longer response times (specific figures not given).
intervention: Medical operations staff were relocated into the Combined Joint Operations Centre (CJOC), collocating medical and operations staff.
cycle2_result: Three-quarters of Category A and B missions met the 90-minute target; mean response time improved compared with the two previous rotations, though median response changed little; no casualties died who were recoverable.
other_findings: Reasons for missing the target included distance, delay securing a hostile landing site, delayed information, incorrect casualty categorisation, and asset overmatch.

cycle1_result: 64% of junior doctors reported no sick note certification training; only 40% felt confident writing sick note certificates; 54% could not identify commonly completed hospital certificates.

cycle1_result: Hip arthroplasty procedures followed guidelines in 95.4% (retrospective) and 96.9% (prospective) of cases; cardiac stimulator audit showed 100% agreement with guidelines; traceability audit found 97% of files complete.

title: "The 3/3 strategy": a successful multifaceted hospital wide hand hygiene intervention based on WHO and continuous quality improvement methodology.

finding: Baseline hand hygiene performance prior to intervention (exact percentage not stated; a 25% mean increase was achieved during the intervention relative to baseline).
change: Multifaceted intervention: increased alcohol hand rub placement, increased audit frequency ('3/3 strategy'), a standardised corrective-action register, and Statistical Process Control (Continuous Quality Improvement, phase 2, 2011).

cycle1_result: Baseline hand hygiene performance prior to intervention (exact percentage not stated; a 25% mean increase was achieved during the intervention relative to baseline).

topic: Clinical relevance of elevated National Early Warning Score (NEWS) triggers

standard: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) trigger threshold of ≥7 warranting escalation of care
finding: A NEWS score ≥7 did not result in a change in clinical management in 64.6% of cases; 94.1% of those with no management change were subsequently discharged home; oxygen supplementation and oxygen saturation were the primary determinants of elevated NEWS (89.9% and 31.6% of cases); 19.7% were on home oxygen therapy; retrospective application of the CREWS score would have reduced reviews by 70.3%.
setting: Model 2 hospital, medical patients, Ireland
cycle1_result: A NEWS score ≥7 did not result in a change in clinical management in 64.6% of cases; 94.1% of those with no management change were subsequently discharged home; oxygen supplementation and oxygen saturation were the primary determinants of elevated NEWS (89.9% and 31.6% of cases); 19.7% were on home oxygen therapy; retrospective application of the CREWS score would have reduced reviews by 70.3%.
other_findings: NEWS respiratory variables are poor discriminators of clinical deterioration in patients with chronic respiratory illness; a modified score (CREWS) may better distinguish acutely from chronically ill patients.

standard: Local guideline/algorithm for management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleed (UGIB)
finding: verbalisation of concern for hypotension 60%, two points of IV access requested in 53% of cases
change: Simulation-based teaching with immediate debriefing and an algorithm summarising guidelines, introduced as an aide-memoire
setting: Royal United Hospital, Bath
cycle1_result: verbalisation of concern for hypotension 60%, two points of IV access requested in 53% of cases
intervention: Simulation-based teaching with immediate debriefing and an algorithm summarising guidelines, introduced as an aide-memoire
cycle2_result: verbalisation of concern for hypotension increased to 100%, two points of IV access in 100% of cases, 76 second reduction in time to call for senior support
other_findings: All FY1s expressed improved confidence in managing UGIB after the intervention.
authors: Saunsbury E; Allison E; Colleypriest B
citation: Saunsbury E, Allison E, Colleypriest B. Promoting the management of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeds among junior doctors: a quality improvement project. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u206305.w3502. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u206305.w3502. PMID: 26732056.

topic: Vaccination schedule completion in diabetes patients
title: Improving physician's adherence to completing vaccination schedules for patients with type 2 diabetes attending non-communicable diseases clinics in West Bay Health Center, Qatar.
standard: American Diabetes Association (ADA) vaccination recommendations (target: 25% improvement by January 2015)
finding: 20% of type 2 diabetes patients had complete vaccination
change: Vaccination form attached to NCD progress note, physician reminders about ADA guidelines, vaccination schedule summary, reminder posters, education/orientation sessions
setting: West Bay Health Center, non-communicable diseases clinic
cycle1_result: 20% of type 2 diabetes patients had complete vaccination
intervention: Vaccination form attached to NCD progress note, physician reminders about ADA guidelines, vaccination schedule summary, reminder posters, education/orientation sessions
other_findings: not reported
authors: Tawfik H; Bashwar Z; Al-Ali A; Salem M; Abdelbagi I
citation: Tawfik H, Bashwar Z, Al-Ali A, Salem M, Abdelbagi I. Improving physician's adherence to completing vaccination schedules for patients with type 2 diabetes attending non-communicable diseases clinics in West Bay Health Center, Qatar.
