topic: Care bundle for chronic kidney disease management in primary care
title: A quality improvement project to improve the effectiveness and patient-centredness of management of people with mild-to-moderate kidney disease in primary care.
standard: NICE (2008) guidance-based Care Bundle for CKD (blood pressure targets and other high-impact interventions)
finding: NICE (2008) blood pressure target achievement at baseline: 74.8% in CKD stage 3-5 without diabetes, 48% in CKD stage 3-5 with diabetes
change: Care Bundle for CKD: three evidence-based interventions from NICE (2008) guidance plus a novel patient-led self-management element, with practice training and ongoing QI support
setting: 29 GP practices, England and Wales
cycle1_result: NICE (2008) blood pressure target achievement at baseline: 74.8% in CKD stage 3-5 without diabetes, 48% in CKD stage 3-5 with diabetes
intervention: Care Bundle for CKD: three evidence-based interventions from NICE (2008) guidance plus a novel patient-led self-management element, with practice training and ongoing QI support
cycle2_period: project end (monthly outcome data over the study)
cycle2_n: 998 patients (13 practices); 315 additional patients in 6 non-reporting practices
cycle2_result: Blood pressure target achievement at project end: 76.7% (no diabetes) and 49.2% (diabetes); Care Bundle reliability 100% in those who received it; 671/998 (75%) agreed to self-management component
other_findings: 10 of 29 practices dropped out after training; 6 continued applying the bundle but submitted incomplete data; maintaining primary care engagement was a significant challenge.
authors: Thomas N; Gallagher H; Jain N
citation: Thomas N, Gallagher H, Jain N. A quality improvement project to improve the effectiveness and patient-centredness of management of people with mild-to-moderate kidney disease in primary care. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u201337.w825. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u201337.w825. PMID: 26734284.

title: Intravenous fluid prescribing: Improving prescribing practices and documentation in line with NICE CG174 guidance.
standard: NICE CG174 (December 2013): Intravenous fluid therapy in adults in hospital
finding: Necessary documentation components infrequently documented: prescriptions often had no indication for IV fluid, no 24-hour plan/review, no patient weight, no fluid balance charts
change: Lanyard cards emphasising necessary IV fluid prescription components plus a copy of the NICE fluid prescribing algorithm, distributed to junior doctors on acute admissions units
setting: Acute admissions units, medical and surgical, Lincoln County Hospital
cycle1_result: Necessary documentation components infrequently documented: prescriptions often had no indication for IV fluid, no 24-hour plan/review, no patient weight, no fluid balance charts
intervention: Lanyard cards emphasising necessary IV fluid prescription components plus a copy of the NICE fluid prescribing algorithm, distributed to junior doctors on acute admissions units
cycle2_result: Significant increase in documentation of defined prescription components, including indication for IV fluid and patient weight, on both medical and surgical units; increased percentage of maintenance IV fluid prescriptions conforming to NICE guidelines
other_findings: Lanyard cards subsequently issued to all new Foundation Year 1 doctors at Trust induction to sustain improvement.
authors: Sansom LT; Duggleby L
citation: Sansom LT, Duggleby L. Intravenous fluid prescribing: Improving prescribing practices and documentation in line with NICE CG174 guidance. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;3(1):u205899.w2409. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u205899.w2409. PMID: 26734287.

title: The endoscopy safety checklist: A longitudinal study of factors affecting compliance in a tertiary referral centre within the United Kingdom.
standard: Local endoscopy safety checklist (devised by expert panel)
finding: Baseline highly variable safety check procedure; completed checklist rate 53%, blank checklists 10%
change: Devised a safety checklist via expert panel, then used electronic and physical reminders and incentives to increase compliance
setting: Wolfson Unit for Endoscopy, St Mark's Hospital, London (tertiary referral centre)
cycle1_result: Baseline highly variable safety check procedure; completed checklist rate 53%, blank checklists 10%
intervention: Devised a safety checklist via expert panel, then used electronic and physical reminders and incentives to increase compliance
cycle2_result: Completed checklist rate increased from 53% to 66% (p=0.021); blank checklists decreased from 10% to 2% (p=0.03)
other_findings: Authors highlight post-implementation validation of safety checklists as important to ensure proper use.
authors: Matharoo M; Sevdalis N; Thillai M; Bouri S; Marjot T; Haycock A; Thomas-Gibson S
citation: Matharoo M, Sevdalis N, Thillai M, Bouri S, Marjot T, Haycock A, et al.. The endoscopy safety checklist: A longitudinal study of factors affecting compliance in a tertiary referral centre within the United Kingdom. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u206344.w2567. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u206344.w2567. PMID: 26734331.

topic: Recognition and escalation of the deteriorating patient (NEWS)
title: Recognition of the deteriorating patient.
standard: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) guidelines, escalation for NEWS ≥5
finding: High NEWS escalated for review in 57% of cases; only half reviewed by a doctor; only a third reviewed within an hour; all NEWS guideline criteria met in only 20% of cases
change: Education first, then monthly cycles over 6 months with increased medical staff availability, grand round presentations, and increased outreach provision
setting: Acute wards, Buckinghamshire NHS Trust
cycle1_result: High NEWS escalated for review in 57% of cases; only half reviewed by a doctor; only a third reviewed within an hour; all NEWS guideline criteria met in only 20% of cases
intervention: Education first, then monthly cycles over 6 months with increased medical staff availability, grand round presentations, and increased outreach provision
cycle2_result: Increase to 87% of cases reviewed by a doctor of appropriate seniority
other_findings: Arose from Keogh review findings of higher-than-average mortality at the Trust; project recruited a new cohort of juniors to continue the QI cycle.
authors: Spiers L; Singh Mohal J; Pearson-Stuttard J; Greenlee H; Carmichael J; Busher R
citation: Spiers L, Singh Mohal J, Pearson-Stuttard J, Greenlee H, Carmichael J, Busher R. Recognition of the deteriorating patient. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u206777.w2734. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u206777.w2734. PMID: 26734344.

title: Quality improvement in resident education: a pilot project to mitigate metabolic side effects from atypical antipsychotic medications in youth.
standard: Atypical antipsychotic metabolic monitoring guidelines
finding: baseline metabolic monitoring rate 9% (<1 year on medication), 58.9% (≥1 year); standardized data collection instrument use 0%
change: Resident education on monitoring guidelines and side effects, provision of calibrated scales, introduction of monitoring templates
setting: two psychiatry resident outpatient clinics, UCLA
cycle1_result: baseline metabolic monitoring rate 9% (<1 year on medication), 58.9% (≥1 year); standardized data collection instrument use 0%
intervention: Resident education on monitoring guidelines and side effects, provision of calibrated scales, introduction of monitoring templates
cycle2_result: monitoring rate 29% for newly initiated patients post-intervention; standardized data collection instrument use increased to 70%
other_findings: Residents reported increased knowledge of guidelines and increased monitoring for side effects after the PDSA-based project.
authors: Jeffrey J
citation: Jeffrey J. Quality improvement in resident education: a pilot project to mitigate metabolic side effects from atypical antipsychotic medications in youth. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u208804.w3544. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u208804.w3544. PMID: 26734359.

topic: Nasogastric tube insertion documentation and guideline adherence
title: Improving the documentation of nasogastric tube insertion and adherence to local enteral nutrition guidelines.
standard: National Patient Safety Agency 2005 guidelines (and 2011 update) for NG tube insertion and placement confirmation
finding: 3-point guideline quality score: 8/13 (62%) followed guidelines appropriately; 7-point documentation score: no case notes had full documentation
change: Teaching intervention for junior doctors and nurses, followed by an NG tube bundle (pro forma, information poster, nurse sticker) trialled on the stroke unit
setting: 10 hospital wards, Noble's Hospital, Isle of Man
cycle1_result: 3-point guideline quality score: 8/13 (62%) followed guidelines appropriately; 7-point documentation score: no case notes had full documentation
intervention: Teaching intervention for junior doctors and nurses, followed by an NG tube bundle (pro forma, information poster, nurse sticker) trialled on the stroke unit
cycle2_period: 90 days after teaching intervention; 6-week bundle trial
cycle2_result: No significant improvement after teaching alone (49 insertions); after bundle, 10/12 (83%) followed guidelines appropriately, but only 2/12 (16%) had full documentation
other_findings: Full documentation occurred only on the two occasions the pro forma was correctly completed and filed.
authors: Cole E
citation: Cole E. Improving the documentation of nasogastric tube insertion and adherence to local enteral nutrition guidelines. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u203207.w1513. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u203207.w1513. PMID: 26734394.

title: Improving venous thromboembolism risk assessment compliance using the electronic tool in admitted medical patients.
standard: Local VTE risk assessment key performance indicator using electronic VTE risk assessment tool
finding: VTE risk assessment compliance in general medicine 4%; overall SKMC compliance 21%
change: Introduction of electronic VTE risk assessment form (computerized decision support tool) via multidisciplinary task force
setting: General Medicine department, Sheikh Khalifa Medical City, Abu Dhabi
cycle1_result: VTE risk assessment compliance in general medicine 4%; overall SKMC compliance 21%
intervention: Introduction of electronic VTE risk assessment form (computerized decision support tool) via multidisciplinary task force
cycle2_result: compliance in general medicine improved to 98%; overall SKMC compliance improved to above 90%
other_findings: not reported
authors: Taha H; Raji SJ; Ellahham S; Bashir N; Al Hanaee M; Boharoon H; AlFalahi M

topic: VTE risk assessment and prophylaxis in surgical inpatients
title: Risk assessment and prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism in surgical inpatients: improving adherence to national guidelines.
standard: National guidelines for VTE risk assessment (target 95% of surgical inpatients assessed at admission) and prescribing/wearing anti-embolism stockings with 24-hour reassessment
finding: Performance below the national target of 95% VTE risk assessment; gaps in prescribing anti-embolism stockings, ensuring correct wear, and 24-hour reassessment
change: Multidisciplinary team approach with email reminders, posters, and senior input during ward rounds
setting: Surgical wards, St George's University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, London
cycle1_result: Performance below the national target of 95% VTE risk assessment; gaps in prescribing anti-embolism stockings, ensuring correct wear, and 24-hour reassessment
intervention: Multidisciplinary team approach with email reminders, posters, and senior input during ward rounds
cycle2_result: Sustained improvement achieved, meeting the national guideline of 95% VTE risk assessment; improved performance across all parameters
other_findings: Authors highlight that simple interventions involving all team members improved patient safety and care.
authors: Johnson O; Kumar S
citation: Johnson O, Kumar S. Risk assessment and prophylaxis of venous thromboembolism in surgical inpatients: improving adherence to national guidelines. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u206691.w2692. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u206691.w2692. PMID: 26734420.

title: Audit and review for evidence-based red cell wastage reduction measures.
standard: not reported
finding: Red blood cell (RBC) wastage was 6.4% overall (5.3% non-AB/B RhD-positive); Group O RhD-negative wastage was 10.4%.
change: Service improvement measures to reduce unnecessary RBC wastage based on a laboratory dashboard query, while maintaining adequate supply.
setting: Hospital transfusion laboratory
cycle1_result: Red blood cell (RBC) wastage was 6.4% overall (5.3% non-AB/B RhD-positive); Group O RhD-negative wastage was 10.4%.
intervention: Service improvement measures to reduce unnecessary RBC wastage based on a laboratory dashboard query, while maintaining adequate supply.
cycle2_result: RBC wastage reduced to 4.4% overall (2.5% non-AB/B RhD-positive), a 32.8% reduction (P<0.0001); Group O RhD-negative wastage reduced to 4.4%; saved approximately 225 RBC units per annum.
other_findings: Increased staff time and associated Group and Screen testing (3.4 to 3.8 per unit issued) were required but did not negate the cost savings.
authors: Smith GA; Gopal-Patel J; Joseph JV; Hobson A; Clarke K
citation: Smith GA, Gopal-Patel J, Joseph JV, Hobson A, Clarke K. Audit and review for evidence-based red cell wastage reduction measures. Br J Biomed Sci. 2015;72(4):185-190. doi:10.1080/09674845.2015.11665751. PMID: 26738401.

topic: Medicines reconciliation compliance with NICE guidance in mental health organisations
title: Medicines reconciliation in comparison with NICE guidelines across secondary care mental health organisations.
standard: NICE guidance on medicines reconciliation
finding: 88.1% had a formal medicines reconciliation policy; ~80% of reconciliation carried out within 24h of admission; 71.4% conducted daily reconciliation on acute admission wards; only 38% reconciled medication for patients admitted from primary care to other teams
setting: Secondary care mental health organisations, England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales
cycle1_result: 88.1% had a formal medicines reconciliation policy; ~80% of reconciliation carried out within 24h of admission; 71.4% conducted daily reconciliation on acute admission wards; only 38% reconciled medication for patients admitted from primary care to other teams
other_findings: Full reconciliation rarely completed on transfer between mental health wards; authors recommend formal training and competency assessments.
authors: Kothari M; Maidment I; Lyon R; Haygarth L
citation: Kothari M, Maidment I, Lyon R, Haygarth L. Medicines reconciliation in comparison with NICE guidelines across secondary care mental health organisations. Int J Clin Pharm. 2016;38(2):289-295. doi:10.1007/s11096-015-0236-7. PMID: 26739128.

topic: International variation in adherence to cancer referral guidelines

finding: Guideline adherence to clinical vignettes ranged from 20-82%; UK adherence for lung vignette was lower than other jurisdictions (47% vs 58%)

topic: CKD diagnosis and blood pressure control in primary care

standard: Local blood pressure targets and modelled CKD prevalence estimates (NIHR CLAHRC Greater Manchester programme)
finding: BP target achievement at baseline: 34% (P1), 60% (P2), 68% (P3), 63% (P4)
change: Multifaceted quality improvement programme tailored to each practice's support needs following contextual analysis, over four phased 12-month QI projects.
setting: 49 primary care practices, Greater Manchester
cycle1_result: BP target achievement at baseline: 34% (P1), 60% (P2), 68% (P3), 63% (P4)
intervention: Multifaceted quality improvement programme tailored to each practice's support needs following contextual analysis, over four phased 12-month QI projects.
cycle2_result: BP target achievement at close: 74% (P1), 83% (P2), 71% (P3), 76% (P4); total CKD cases increased by 2,347 (27%) to 10,968 in an adult population of 231,568; 88-91% of nonproteinuric CKD patients achieved target BP
other_findings: Halving undiagnosed CKD was exceeded in 3 of 4 projects; achievement of tighter BP targets in proteinuric patients was notably less than in nonproteinuric patients.
authors: Humphreys J; Harvey G; Hegarty J
citation: Humphreys J, Harvey G, Hegarty J. Improving CKD Diagnosis and Blood Pressure Control in Primary Care: A Tailored Multifaceted Quality Improvement Programme. Nephron Extra. 2017;7(1):18-32. doi:10.1159/000458712. PMID: 28553315.

topic: Guideline compliance for perihilar cholangiocarcinoma management
title: Compliance with evidence-based multidisciplinary guidelines on perihilar cholangiocarcinoma.
standard: Evidence-based multidisciplinary guideline on perihilar cholangiocarcinoma management (implemented 2013)
finding: Biliary drainage attempted at regional centres in 83/158 (52.5%), with technical/therapeutic success of 79.5%/50% and a 45.8% complication rate; CT protocol not guideline-compliant in 52.8% of referrals; 54.2% of drained patients needed additional drainage after referral.
setting: Regional referring centres to an academic centre, Amsterdam
cycle1_result: Biliary drainage attempted at regional centres in 83/158 (52.5%), with technical/therapeutic success of 79.5%/50% and a 45.8% complication rate; CT protocol not guideline-compliant in 52.8% of referrals; 54.2% of drained patients needed additional drainage after referral.
other_findings: Inadequate initial drainage was associated with more procedures and longer waiting time to surgery.
authors: Coelen RJ; Huiskens J; Olthof PB; Roos E; Wiggers JK; Schoorlemmer A; van Delden OM; Klümpen HJ; Rauws EA; van Gulik TM
citation: Coelen RJ, Huiskens J, Olthof PB, Roos E, Wiggers JK, Schoorlemmer A, et al.. Compliance with evidence-based multidisciplinary guidelines on perihilar cholangiocarcinoma. United European Gastroenterol J. 2017;5(4):519-526. doi:10.1177/2050640616673517. PMID: 28588883.

title: Choosing Wisely: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Unnecessary Preoperative Testing.
standard: Choosing Wisely recommendations against routine low-value preoperative testing
finding: unnecessary testing rate approximately 36%
change: Associate Provider (NP/PA)-run preoperative clinic with standardized protocols, scheduling changes, and EHR tools using PDSA cycles
setting: General Internal Medicine (GIM) division preoperative clinic, Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center
cycle1_result: unnecessary testing rate approximately 36%
intervention: Associate Provider (NP/PA)-run preoperative clinic with standardized protocols, scheduling changes, and EHR tools using PDSA cycles
cycle2_result: unnecessary testing rate 4% in Associate Provider clinic vs 23% in usual care cohort (p<.001)
other_findings: No significant change in testing rates when analyzed across the entire division.
authors: Matulis J; Liu S; Mecchella J; North F; Holmes A
citation: Matulis J, Liu S, Mecchella J, North F, Holmes A. Choosing Wisely: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Decrease Unnecessary Preoperative Testing. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2017;6(1):bmjqir.u216281.w6691. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u216281.w6691. PMID: 28607678.

topic: Acute kidney injury care bundle compliance
title: A Multifaceted Quality Improvement Programme to Improve Acute Kidney Injury Care and Outcomes in a Large Teaching Hospital.
standard: Local Priority Care Checklist for nine key aspects of AKI care (detection within 24 hours, fluid assessment, drug review etc.)
finding: Detection of AKI within 24 hours 53%, fluid assessment 42%, drug review 48%, adherence to nine key aspects of care 40%
change: Electronic AKI alert system, a nurse-supported Priority Care Checklist, and targeted education activities implemented through sequential PDSA cycles.
setting: Large teaching hospital
cycle1_result: Detection of AKI within 24 hours 53%, fluid assessment 42%, drug review 48%, adherence to nine key aspects of care 40%
intervention: Electronic AKI alert system, a nurse-supported Priority Care Checklist, and targeted education activities implemented through sequential PDSA cycles.
cycle2_result: Detection of AKI within 24 hours 100%, fluid assessment 90%, drug review 95%, adherence to nine key aspects of care 90%; e-alert sensitivity 99%; AKI incidence reduced from 9% to 6.5% of hospitalisations (28% reduction); AKI-related length of stay 22.1 to 17 days; time to recovery 15.5 to 9.8 days; hospital-acquired AKI cases reduced 28% (120 to 86 per month); AKI-related deaths reduced from average 38 to 34 (10.5%)
other_findings: Significant reduction in variability of delivered AKI care was also observed.
authors: Ebah L; Hanumapura P; Waring D; Challiner R; Hayden K; Alexander J; Henney R; Royston R; Butterworth C; Vincent M; Heatley S; Terriere G; Pearson R; Hutchison A
citation: Ebah L, Hanumapura P, Waring D, Challiner R, Hayden K, Alexander J, et al.. A Multifaceted Quality Improvement Programme to Improve Acute Kidney Injury Care and Outcomes in a Large Teaching Hospital. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2017;6(1):u219176.w7476. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u219176.w7476. PMID: 28607684.

topic: Technical quality of root canal fillings by undergraduate dental students
title: An audit on technical quality of root fillings performed by undergraduate students.
standard: Radiographic assessment criteria for taper, length and lateral adaptation of root fillings
finding: 66% (253) of root fillings were acceptable across all assessment parameters; 97% of canals had good taper, 72% appropriate length, 91% good lateral condensation; 23% underfilled and 5% overfilled
setting: Dental School, Queen's University Belfast
cycle1_result: 66% (253) of root fillings were acceptable across all assessment parameters; 97% of canals had good taper, 72% appropriate length, 91% good lateral condensation; 23% underfilled and 5% overfilled
other_findings: No significant association found between tooth type (anterior/posterior) and quality of root filling provided
authors: Fong W; Heidarifar O; Killough S; Lappin MJ; El Karim IA
citation: Fong W, Heidarifar O, Killough S, Lappin MJ, El Karim IA. An audit on technical quality of root fillings performed by undergraduate students. Int Endod J. 2018;51 Suppl 3:e197-e203. doi:10.1111/iej.12803. PMID: 28644527.

topic: Guideline adherence for psychopharmacological prescribing in eating disorders
title: Adherence of psychopharmacological prescriptions to clinical practice guidelines in patients with eating behavior disorders.
standard: American Psychiatric Association (APA) and NICE/Spanish Ministry of Health and Consumption (SMHC) clinical practice guidelines
finding: Adherence to APA guidelines 30.1%; adherence to NICE/SMHC guidelines 45.1%.
setting: Eating disorders unit, Ciudad Real Hospital
cycle1_result: Adherence to APA guidelines 30.1%; adherence to NICE/SMHC guidelines 45.1%.
other_findings: Weekly weight gain was higher in the APA-adherent group (807.6 g vs 544.4 g, p=0.037); adherence was associated with higher 5-year full recovery.
authors: Alañón Pardo MDM; Ferrit Martín M; Calleja Hernández MÁ; Morillas Márquez F
citation: Alañón Pardo MDM, Ferrit Martín M, Calleja Hernández MÁ, Morillas Márquez F. Adherence of psychopharmacological prescriptions to clinical practice guidelines in patients with eating behavior disorders. Eur J Clin Pharmacol. 2017;73(10):1305-1313. doi:10.1007/s00228-017-2287-2. PMID: 28653297.

title: An Audit of Comparison of Perioperative Outcomes with the Introduction of Standardized Preoperative Evaluation form at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Rural India.
standard: 11 locally devised quality indicators for pre-, peri- and post-operative documentation
finding: last-minute postponement/change of surgery plan in 134 (8.9%) cases; 784 (52.26%) patients not formally handed over to recovery staff
change: Introduction of a standardized Preoperative Evaluation Form (PEF)
setting: tertiary care hospital, Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences, Karad, rural India
cycle1_result: last-minute postponement/change of surgery plan in 134 (8.9%) cases; 784 (52.26%) patients not formally handed over to recovery staff
intervention: Introduction of a standardized Preoperative Evaluation Form (PEF)
cycle2_result: postponement/change reduced to 23 (1.53%) cases; non-handover reduced to 147 (9.8%) cases
other_findings: not reported
authors: Naik SV; Mohammad B; Dhulkhed VK
citation: Naik SV, Mohammad B, Dhulkhed VK. An Audit of Comparison of Perioperative Outcomes with the Introduction of Standardized Preoperative Evaluation form at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Rural India. Anesth Essays Res. 2017;11(2):426-430. doi:10.4103/0259-1162.194584. PMID: 28663635.

title: A specialty-specific, multimodality educational quality improvement initiative to deimplement rarely appropriate myocardial perfusion imaging.
standard: American College of Cardiology Foundation Appropriate Use Criteria (AUC) for myocardial perfusion imaging
finding: Rarely appropriate myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) rate was 4.9%; appropriate testing rate was 80.5%
change: Specialty-specific, multimodality educational initiative (tailored lectures for cardiology, primary care and hospital medicine, plus printed posters) to raise awareness of Appropriate Use Criteria
setting: Single VA medical facility, Florida
cycle1_result: Rarely appropriate myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) rate was 4.9%; appropriate testing rate was 80.5%
intervention: Specialty-specific, multimodality educational initiative (tailored lectures for cardiology, primary care and hospital medicine, plus printed posters) to raise awareness of Appropriate Use Criteria
cycle2_period: immediately after, and 4 months after, the intervention
cycle2_result: Rarely appropriate MPI fell to 1.3% immediately post-intervention and remained at 1.4% 4 months later (p<0.0001); appropriate testing rose to 95.2% post-intervention and 92.7% at 4 months (n=289 in the late-post cohort)
other_findings: Lack of symptoms (OR 31.3) and preoperative testing in patients with good exercise capacity were the predominant rarely appropriate indications; none of the rarely appropriate tests showed ischaemia.
authors: Winchester DE; Schmalfuss C; Helfrich CD; Beyth RJ
citation: Winchester DE, Schmalfuss C, Helfrich CD, Beyth RJ. A specialty-specific, multimodality educational quality improvement initiative to deimplement rarely appropriate myocardial perfusion imaging. Open Heart. 2017;4(1):e000589. doi:10.1136/openhrt-2017-000589. PMID: 28674630.

title: Outcome after Discontinuation of Proton Pump Inhibitors at a Residential Care Site: Quality Improvement Project.
standard: not reported
finding: Discontinuation recommendation was accepted for 27 of 28 residents.
change: Pharmacist review of long-term PPI use against discontinuation criteria, with a faxed recommendation to physicians and 8 weeks of pharmacist follow-up.
setting: Single residential care site
cycle1_n: 28 residents identified as meeting discontinuation criteria
cycle1_result: Discontinuation recommendation was accepted for 27 of 28 residents.
intervention: Pharmacist review of long-term PPI use against discontinuation criteria, with a faxed recommendation to physicians and 8 weeks of pharmacist follow-up.
cycle2_result: 19 of 27 residents (70%) remained asymptomatic without needing to restart medication.
other_findings: This is a single-cohort deprescribing project rather than a classic two-cycle audit against a named standard.
authors: Lee C; Lo A; Ubhi K; Milewski M
journal: The Canadian journal of hospital pharmacy
citation: Lee C, Lo A, Ubhi K, Milewski M. Outcome after Discontinuation of Proton Pump Inhibitors at a Residential Care Site: Quality Improvement Project. Can J Hosp Pharm. 2017;70(3):215-223. doi:10.4212/cjhp.v70i3.1661. PMID: 28680175.

topic: Unplanned extubation reduction in intensive care
title: Multidisciplinary interventions and continuous quality improvement to reduce unplanned extubation in adult intensive care units: A 15-year experience.
standard: Local target to reduce unplanned extubation (UE) rate via continuous quality improvement
finding: UE rate 6.82/100 ventilated patients (9.0/1000 ventilator-days) in 2001
change: Multidisciplinary QI interventions over 15 years: standardizing procedures, communication, sedation/weaning protocols, restraint strategies, high-risk patient task force, breakthrough series/TRM models, accountability without blame, new tube-securing method
setting: adult ICUs, Chi Mei Medical Center
cycle1_result: UE rate 6.82/100 ventilated patients (9.0/1000 ventilator-days) in 2001
intervention: Multidisciplinary QI interventions over 15 years: standardizing procedures, communication, sedation/weaning protocols, restraint strategies, high-risk patient task force, breakthrough series/TRM models, accountability without blame, new tube-securing method
cycle2_result: UE rate fell to 0.95/100 ventilated patients (1.36/1000 ventilator-days) in 2015 (overall trend p<.0001)
other_findings: Overall 15-year total was 1404 UE episodes across 44,015 mechanical ventilation episodes.
authors: Chao CM; Lai CC; Chan KS; Cheng KC; Ho CH; Chen CM; Chou W
citation: Chao CM, Lai CC, Chan KS, Cheng KC, Ho CH, Chen CM, et al.. Multidisciplinary interventions and continuous quality improvement to reduce unplanned extubation in adult intensive care units: A 15-year experience. Medicine (Baltimore). 2017;96(27):e6877. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000006877. PMID: 28682859.

title: Finding the time: an audit of the acute ward mealtime processes.
standard: Basic standards for nutritional and hydrational care/mealtime support
finding: not reported
change: Quality improvement initiatives altering ward mealtime processes following initial audit findings
setting: Acute hospital ward, Tallaght Hospital
cycle1_result: not reported
intervention: Quality improvement initiatives altering ward mealtime processes following initial audit findings
other_findings: Quality improvement initiatives had a positive impact, enabling ward staff to improve adequacy of mealtime support and patient quality of care
authors: Digan E; O'Reilly H; Halley MJ; Hickey M; Feehan S; Collins R; Bent E
citation: Digan E, O'Reilly H, Halley MJ, Hickey M, Feehan S, Collins R, et al.. Finding the time: an audit of the acute ward mealtime processes. Br J Community Nurs. 2017;22(Sup7):S30-S32. doi:10.12968/bjcn.2017.22.sup7.s30. PMID: 28686054.

topic: VMAT planning and pretreatment verification quality
title: Multi-centre audit of VMAT planning and pre-treatment verification.
standard: Gamma index dosimetric tolerance criteria (e.g. 3%/3 mm) for pretreatment verification
finding: All centres met dosimetric goals; pretreatment verification results were within tolerance for gamma 3%-3mm evaluation in all cases, but differences of up to 20% arose between in-house and external audit results for stricter 2%-2mm criteria.
setting: 9 radiotherapy centres, Spain
cycle1_n: 9 centres, 2 mock cases (prostate, head and neck)
cycle1_result: All centres met dosimetric goals; pretreatment verification results were within tolerance for gamma 3%-3mm evaluation in all cases, but differences of up to 20% arose between in-house and external audit results for stricter 2%-2mm criteria.
other_findings: Plan quality and delivery complexity varied by machine manufacturer and planner methodology and were not correlated; in-house measurement could not fully replace external audit.
authors: Jurado-Bruggeman D; Hernández V; Sáez J; Navarro D; Pino F; Martínez T; Alayrach ME; Ailleres N; Melero A; Jornet N
journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
citation: Jurado-Bruggeman D, Hernández V, Sáez J, Navarro D, Pino F, Martínez T, et al.. Multi-centre audit of VMAT planning and pre-treatment verification. Radiother Oncol. 2017;124(2):302-310. doi:10.1016/j.radonc.2017.05.019. PMID: 28687395.

title: A Simulation-based Quality Improvement Approach to Improve Pediatric Resident Competency with Required Procedures.
standard: ACGME Graduating Resident Survey (GRS) procedural competency requirements
finding: bag/mask ventilation competency 77%, neonatal intubation 39%, peripheral IV placement 10%, umbilical catheter placement 35% (baseline years)
change: Simulation-based quality improvement with three PDSA cycles: increased awareness of procedural experiences, procedural educational conferences, and a senior resident procedure boot camp
setting: pediatric residency program, Seattle Children's Hospital
cycle1_result: bag/mask ventilation competency 77%, neonatal intubation 39%, peripheral IV placement 10%, umbilical catheter placement 35% (baseline years)
intervention: Simulation-based quality improvement with three PDSA cycles: increased awareness of procedural experiences, procedural educational conferences, and a senior resident procedure boot camp
cycle2_n: 32 of 34 residents (30 of 34 completed boot camp)
cycle2_result: competency increased to bag/mask ventilation 94%, neonatal intubation 69%, peripheral IV placement 50%, umbilical catheter placement 53%
other_findings: Response rates to ACGME GRS were consistent across years (92-94%).
authors: Starr M; Sawyer T; Jones M; Batra M; McPhillips H
citation: Starr M, Sawyer T, Jones M, Batra M, McPhillips H. A Simulation-based Quality Improvement Approach to Improve Pediatric Resident Competency with Required Procedures. Cureus. 2017;9(6):e1307. doi:10.7759/cureus.1307. PMID: 28690941.

title: A prospective audit on the effect of training and educational workshops on the incidence of urethral catheterization injuries.
standard: not reported
finding: Incidence of iatrogenic urethral catheterisation injuries was 4.3 per 1000 catheters inserted
change: Educational training workshops and training modules for junior doctors
setting: Department of Urology, Tallaght Hospital, Dublin
cycle1_result: Incidence of iatrogenic urethral catheterisation injuries was 4.3 per 1000 catheters inserted
intervention: Educational training workshops and training modules for junior doctors
cycle2_result: Incidence reduced to 3.8 per 1000 catheters (p=0.59, not significant); morbidity increased (additional inpatient stay 22 to 79 days; urosepsis n=2 to n=4); cost of managing injuries almost doubled (€50,449 to €90,100)
other_findings: Authors conclude current training interventions did not significantly change morbidity or cost despite a reduction in incidence; call for improved and intensive training protocols
authors: Bhatt NR; Davis NF; Quinlan MR; Flynn RJ; McDermott TED; Manecksha RP; Thornhill JA
journal: Canadian Urological Association journal = Journal de l'Association des urologues du Canada
citation: Bhatt NR, Davis NF, Quinlan MR, Flynn RJ, McDermott TED, Manecksha RP, et al.. A prospective audit on the effect of training and educational workshops on the incidence of urethral catheterization injuries. Can Urol Assoc J. 2017;11(7):E302-E306. doi:10.5489/cuaj.4271. PMID: 28761592.

topic: Glucose testing frequency during hyperbaric oxygen therapy
title: Applying quality improvement methods in a hyperbaric oxygen program: reducing unnecessary glucose testing.
standard: not reported (local nurse-led glucose-testing protocol)
finding: 2.84 glucose checks per session pre-protocol; compliance with the existing protocol 84.2%.
change: Nurse-led protocol for glucose checks in diabetic patients undergoing hyperbaric oxygen therapy, developed and refined over several PDSA cycles.
setting: Hyperbaric oxygen programme, Mayo Clinic
cycle1_result: 2.84 glucose checks per session pre-protocol; compliance with the existing protocol 84.2%.
intervention: Nurse-led protocol for glucose checks in diabetic patients undergoing hyperbaric oxygen therapy, developed and refined over several PDSA cycles.
cycle2_result: Glucose checks per session fell 37.7% to 1.77 (P<0.001); compliance with the new protocol rose to 97.3% (P<0.001); no symptomatic hypoglycaemic events occurred after implementation.
other_findings: Quality improvement project run by a multidisciplinary team using Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles.
authors: Stevens SL; Sorita A; Narr AJ; Claus PL; Tescher A; Millman MP; Shields RC; Buchta WG; Haddon R; Murad MH
journal: Undersea & hyperbaric medicine : journal of the Undersea and Hyperbaric Medical Society, Inc
citation: Stevens SL, Sorita A, Narr AJ, Claus PL, Tescher A, Millman MP, et al.. Applying quality improvement methods in a hyperbaric oxygen program: reducing unnecessary glucose testing. Undersea Hyperb Med. 2016;43(4):427-435. PMID: 28763172.

title: On-site audits to investigate the quality of radiation physics of radiation therapy institutions in the Republic of Korea.
standard: National/international radiotherapy physics tolerance standards (e.g. isocentre deviation <1 mm, wedge transmission factor deviation <2%, beam output deviation <3%)
finding: Average mechanical and radiation isocentre deviations were less than 1 mm; average difference between light and radiation fields 0.9+/-0.6 mm; every institution met wedge transmission factor deviation <2% except one; output deviations were within +/-3% for every institution.
setting: 13 radiation therapy institutions, Republic of Korea
cycle1_result: Average mechanical and radiation isocentre deviations were less than 1 mm; average difference between light and radiation fields 0.9+/-0.6 mm; every institution met wedge transmission factor deviation <2% except one; output deviations were within +/-3% for every institution.
other_findings: On-site auditing effectively detected inappropriately operating linear accelerators and allowed recommendations to be given.
authors: Park JM; Park SY; Chun M; Kim ST
journal: Physica medica : PM : an international journal devoted to the applications of physics to medicine and biology : official journal of the Italian Association of Biomedical Physics (AIFB)
citation: Park JM, Park SY, Chun M, Kim ST. On-site audits to investigate the quality of radiation physics of radiation therapy institutions in the Republic of Korea. Phys Med. 2017;40:110-114. doi:10.1016/j.ejmp.2017.07.021. PMID: 28784573.

topic: Gynaecologic history documentation in surgical patients
title: Results of a national multicenter audit assessment of gynecologic history in surgical patients.
standard: not reported
finding: Date of last menstrual period documented for 38.3%, contraception use for 28.1%, sexual activity for 15.7%, pregnancy status for 51.7%, possibility of pregnancy for 44.7%
setting: 18 general surgery departments across Scotland (national multicentre audit)
cycle1_n: 530 females of reproductive age (169 elective, 361 emergency)
cycle1_result: Date of last menstrual period documented for 38.3%, contraception use for 28.1%, sexual activity for 15.7%, pregnancy status for 51.7%, possibility of pregnancy for 44.7%
other_findings: Higher documentation of last menstrual period and pregnancy status among certain admission types (p=0.002); authors recommend education of surgical teams and medical undergraduates
authors: Wilson MSJ; Powell-Bowns M; Robertson AG; Luhmann A; Richards CH; Scottish Surgical Research Group

title: Knowledge and Compliance in Practices in Diagnosis and Treatment of Syphilis in Maternity Hospitals in Teresina - PI, Brazil.
standard: Brazilian Ministry of Health protocols for syphilis diagnosis and treatment
finding: obstetricians agreed with only 2 of 5 serological-test knowledge criteria; nurses had no matches between practice and guidelines
setting: public maternity hospitals, Teresina, Piauí
cycle1_result: obstetricians agreed with only 2 of 5 serological-test knowledge criteria; nurses had no matches between practice and guidelines
other_findings: Cross-sectional knowledge/compliance survey; low compliance identified but no intervention or re-audit reported.
authors: Santos RRD; Niquini RP; Domingues RMSM; Bastos FI
journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia
citation: Santos RRD, Niquini RP, Domingues RMSM, Bastos FI. Knowledge and Compliance in Practices in Diagnosis and Treatment of Syphilis in Maternity Hospitals in Teresina - PI, Brazil. Rev Bras Ginecol Obstet. 2017;39(9):453-463. doi:10.1055/s-0037-1606245. PMID: 28834998.

title: Maternal mortality audit in Suriname between 2010 and 2014, a reproductive age mortality survey.
standard: Millennium Development Goal 5 (75% MMR reduction target 1990-2015)
finding: MMR 226 per 100,000 live births (1991-1993)
change: Maternal mortality committee audit of identified deaths, examining underlying causes and substandard care factors
setting: national reproductive age mortality survey
cycle1_result: MMR 226 per 100,000 live births (1991-1993)
intervention: Maternal mortality committee audit of identified deaths, examining underlying causes and substandard care factors
cycle2_result: MMR 130 per 100,000 live births (42% reduction from 1991-1993); vital registration MMR 96 (26% underreporting); substandard care factors present in 95% of cases

citation: Kodan LR, Verschueren KJC, van Roosmalen J, Kanhai HHH, Bloemenkamp KWM. Maternal mortality audit in Suriname between 2010 and 2014, a reproductive age mortality survey. BMC Pregnancy Childbirth. 2017;17(1):275. doi:10.1186/s12884-017-1466-6. PMID: 28851302.

title: Captivating a captive audience: a quality improvement project increasing participation in intradialytic exercise across five renal dialysis units.
standard: not reported
finding: 23.3% pre-intervention uptake of exercise on dialysis (EOD)
change: Patient and nursing staff education, equipment modification, and introduction of patient motivation schemes, led by a senior physiotherapist after root-cause analysis of barriers.
setting: Five satellite haemodialysis units, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, London
cycle1_result: 23.3% pre-intervention uptake of exercise on dialysis (EOD)
intervention: Patient and nursing staff education, equipment modification, and introduction of patient motivation schemes, led by a senior physiotherapist after root-cause analysis of barriers.
cycle2_result: 74.3% post-intervention uptake of EOD (chi-squared(1, N=174)=44.18, p<0.001)
other_findings: Barriers identified via semi-structured interviews and questionnaires included staff knowledge, patient motivation and equipment problems.
authors: Abdulnassir L; Egas-Kitchener S; Whibley D; Fynmore T; Jones GD
citation: Abdulnassir L, Egas-Kitchener S, Whibley D, Fynmore T, Jones GD. Captivating a captive audience: a quality improvement project increasing participation in intradialytic exercise across five renal dialysis units. Clin Kidney J. 2017;10(4):516-523. doi:10.1093/ckj/sfw142. PMID: 28852491.

title: A systematic checklist approach to immunosuppression risk management: An audit of practice at two clinical neuroimmunology centers.
standard: Systematic immunosuppression risk evaluation checklist
finding: Average 1.9 comorbidities with potential to adversely affect immunosuppression identified per patient; inadequate documentation of risk mitigation tasks in 40.1% of total tasks across both cohorts
setting: Two clinical neuroimmunology centres (Concord Repatriation General Hospital, Addenbrooke's Hospital)
cycle1_result: Average 1.9 comorbidities with potential to adversely affect immunosuppression identified per patient; inadequate documentation of risk mitigation tasks in 40.1% of total tasks across both cohorts
other_findings: Diabetes and smoking were the most common relevant comorbidities identified; recommends routine systematic checklist approach for quality improvement
authors: Mori AM; Agarwal S; Lee MWM; Rafferty M; Hardy TA; Coles A; Reddel SW; Riminton DS
citation: Mori AM, Agarwal S, Lee MWM, Rafferty M, Hardy TA, Coles A, et al.. A systematic checklist approach to immunosuppression risk management: An audit of practice at two clinical neuroimmunology centers. J Neuroimmunol. 2017;312:4-7. doi:10.1016/j.jneuroim.2017.08.009. PMID: 28886954.

title: A prospective observational assessment of Surgical Safety Checklist use in Brasov Children's Hospital, barriers to implementation and methods to improve compliance.
standard: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
finding: None of the checklists in patient files were fully completed; average of 55% of checklist components performed, not significantly different by staff numbers, speciality or elective/emergency status

cycle1_result: None of the checklists in patient files were fully completed; average of 55% of checklist components performed, not significantly different by staff numbers, speciality or elective/emergency status
other_findings: Staff questionnaires (n=15) explored barriers to implementation; authors conclude training and communication are essential for improving compliance
authors: McGinlay D; Moore D; Mironescu A
journal: Romanian journal of anaesthesia and intensive care
citation: McGinlay D, Moore D, Mironescu A. A prospective observational assessment of Surgical Safety Checklist use in Brasov Children's Hospital, barriers to implementation and methods to improve compliance. Rom J Anaesth Intensive Care. 2015;22(2):111-121. PMID: 28913466.

title: Improving inpatient medication adherence using attendant education in a tertiary care hospital in Uganda.
standard: Local target for inpatient medication adherence rate (no external guideline named)
finding: pre-intervention median inpatient medication adherence rate 46.5%
change: PDSA cycle interventions focused on attendant (lay caretaker) involvement and education, physician prescribing practices, and pharmacy-clinician communication
setting: internal medicine wards, Mulago National Referral Hospital, Kampala
cycle1_result: pre-intervention median inpatient medication adherence rate 46.5%
intervention: PDSA cycle interventions focused on attendant (lay caretaker) involvement and education, physician prescribing practices, and pharmacy-clinician communication

title: Optimizing an Enhanced Recovery Pathway Program: Development of a Postimplementation Audit Strategy.
standard: not reported (institutional 18-measure Enhanced Recovery Pathway protocol)

topic: Radiation safety in neonatal bedside imaging
title: Reducing radiation hazard opportunities in neonatal unit: quality improvement in radiation safety practices.
standard: ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) radiation safety principle; local target to reduce radiation hazard opportunities by at least 75% from the Q2 2015 baseline within 6 months
finding: Median radiation hazard opportunities were 12.5 per week; an annual audit found 42% of chest X-rays and 63% of abdominal X-rays were done as combined X-rays; the discordance rate between request forms and images taken was 18%
change: Mandatory lead protective gear for staff, gonadal shielding for neonates, a standardised collimation and positioning protocol, and regular staff awareness/education sessions
setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Singapore General Hospital
cycle1_result: Median radiation hazard opportunities were 12.5 per week; an annual audit found 42% of chest X-rays and 63% of abdominal X-rays were done as combined X-rays; the discordance rate between request forms and images taken was 18%
intervention: Mandatory lead protective gear for staff, gonadal shielding for neonates, a standardised collimation and positioning protocol, and regular staff awareness/education sessions
cycle2_result: Radiation hazard opportunities fell by 100% for staff and 75% for neonates (overall reduction 83%-84%); discordance rate fell by 77% (from 18% to 4%); improvements were sustained at 18-month follow-up, with baby hazard opportunities falling further (median 2 to 1)
other_findings: Follow-up staff survey showed improved confidence (100%) and reduced worry about radiation exposure; the revised policy was uploaded to the hospital intranet and mandatory orientation given to new staff to sustain the change.

title: Oxygen prescription: improving compliance using methods from BMJ Open Quality journal.
standard: British Thoracic Society Guidelines: oxygen must be prescribed for all patients with target saturations stated on the prescription
finding: Poster reminders and multidisciplinary team education failed to significantly improve oxygen prescription rate
change: Sequential quality improvement interventions: poster reminders, MDT education, then targeted stickers placed above oxygen taps, based on a previously published BMJ Open Quality method.
setting: Respiratory ward, district general hospital
cycle1_result: Poster reminders and multidisciplinary team education failed to significantly improve oxygen prescription rate
intervention: Sequential quality improvement interventions: poster reminders, MDT education, then targeted stickers placed above oxygen taps, based on a previously published BMJ Open Quality method.
cycle2_result: Targeted stickers significantly improved oxygen prescription rate from 20% (non-targeted group) to 60% (targeted group)

topic: Preoperative anaemia optimisation before elective surgery
title: Improving preoperative haemoglobin using a quality improvement approach to treat iron deficiency anaemia.

title: A Pilot Quality Improvement Project to Reduce Preoperative Fasting Duration in Pediatric Inpatients.
standard: ASA preoperative fasting guidelines (clear liquids up to 2 hours before anaesthesia); project aim to reduce fasting duration by 25% within 1 year
finding: Average fasting duration 12.5 hours with NPO-at-midnight order
change: Creation of a standardised preanaesthesia clear liquid diet order integrated into the EMR to replace the NPO-at-midnight order, plus provider and nursing education

topic: CT scan utilisation for minor head injury
title: Checklist for Head Injury Management Evaluation Study (CHIMES): a quality improvement initiative to reduce imaging utilisation for head injuries in the emergency department.
standard: Choosing Wisely Canada campaign and the Canadian CT Head Rule (CCTHR); aim to reduce CT scan rate by 10% over 6 months
finding: 49.2% of patients underwent a CT scan of the head; audit of 200 charts found 79% of CT scans were not indicated by the CCTHR; mean weekly baseline CT rate 48.1%
change: Four PDSA cycles: education on CWC/CCTHR recommendations, introduction of the CHIMES flow-chart checklist at triage/registration, a CWC-themed patient handout, and bi-monthly feedback of CT rates to providers
setting: Two emergency department sites, adult academic tertiary care centre, University Health Network, Toronto
cycle1_result: 49.2% of patients underwent a CT scan of the head; audit of 200 charts found 79% of CT scans were not indicated by the CCTHR; mean weekly baseline CT rate 48.1%
intervention: Four PDSA cycles: education on CWC/CCTHR recommendations, introduction of the CHIMES flow-chart checklist at triage/registration, a CWC-themed patient handout, and bi-monthly feedback of CT rates to providers
cycle2_period: up to 16 months after project start
cycle2_result: 13.9% relative reduction in CT rate at 3 months and a sustained 8.0% reduction at 16 months (48.1% vs 44.3%, p<0.05); ED length of stay fell by 1.5 minutes (p=0.74); 72-hour return visits unchanged (4.4% vs 4.6%, p=0.68); 33.3% of audited charts had the checklist added, of which 84.0% were completed

title: Quality improvement model (IHI) as a strategy to implement a sepsis protocol in a public hospital in Brazil.
standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 3-hour care bundle (blood cultures, lactate, antibiotics, fluids); local target case fatality rate ≤25%
finding: Case fatality rate highly variable, 15%-35%; general 3-hour bundle compliance about 30%-40%; time to antibiotics and fluids 60-120 minutes
change: IHI Model for Improvement using PDSA cycles across ICU, wards, obstetric and emergency units: a 'suspected sepsis stamp', priority lab stamp, nurse sepsis training, a sepsis standard order set, revised colour-coded vital sign forms, sepsis champions, a patient education video and a communication plan
setting: Public quaternary hospital (Hospital Municipal da Vila Santa Catarina), São Paulo, Brazil - ICU, wards, emergency and obstetric units
cycle1_period: 1 January to 30 June 2016 (first 6 months of an 18-month project)
cycle1_result: Case fatality rate highly variable, 15%-35%; general 3-hour bundle compliance about 30%-40%; time to antibiotics and fluids 60-120 minutes
intervention: IHI Model for Improvement using PDSA cycles across ICU, wards, obstetric and emergency units: a 'suspected sepsis stamp', priority lab stamp, nurse sepsis training, a sepsis standard order set, revised colour-coded vital sign forms, sepsis champions, a patient education video and a communication plan
cycle2_period: 15-month prospective audit, 1 January 2016 to 31 March 2017 (project continued to 30 November 2017)
cycle2_result: Case fatality rate stabilised at about 15.9%, below the 25% target; overall 3-hour bundle compliance about 38.94%; average time to antibiotics 39 min 19s, to fluid administration 1h20min, to blood cultures 46 min

standard: CAP care bundle: chest X-ray, CURB-65 severity score, lower respiratory tract sample and antibiotics all completed within 8 hours of admission
finding: Full care bundle completed within 8 hours in 7.1%-11% of cases at baseline; CURB-65 documented in 31.2% (26.9% within 8h); lower respiratory tract samples collected in 60.6% (39.6% within 8h); chest X-ray within 8h 88.7%; antibiotics within 8h 75.1%
change: Tailored technical (hands-on tracheal suction/sputum induction training) and non-technical interventions (repeated education, personal feedback, standard educational material, authorising nurses to order X-rays/samples, combined microbiology sampling, CURB-65 EHR tool, CAP order sets) at three intervention sites via PDSA cycles, March-October 2018
setting: Four Danish regional hospitals (emergency departments, respiratory medicine and infectious diseases departments); three intervention sites and one control site
cycle1_n: 2015 total audited across the study (baseline periods of 12-48 patients per 10-day period per site)
cycle1_result: Full care bundle completed within 8 hours in 7.1%-11% of cases at baseline; CURB-65 documented in 31.2% (26.9% within 8h); lower respiratory tract samples collected in 60.6% (39.6% within 8h); chest X-ray within 8h 88.7%; antibiotics within 8h 75.1%
intervention: Tailored technical (hands-on tracheal suction/sputum induction training) and non-technical interventions (repeated education, personal feedback, standard educational material, authorising nurses to order X-rays/samples, combined microbiology sampling, CURB-65 EHR tool, CAP order sets) at three intervention sites via PDSA cycles, March-October 2018
cycle2_n: 2015 total (Site1 n=694, Site2 n=532, Site3 n=242, control Site4 n=547)
cycle2_result: Care bundle completion rose from 11% at baseline to 41% at follow-up at intervention sites (control site remained below 3%); CURB-65 documentation rose from 34% to 68%; lower respiratory tract sample collection rose from 43% to 63%

finding: ABC compliance 4.4% (95% CI 2.0-8.2%); safe sleep position/location 78.4%; safe sleep environment only 5.9%

setting: Five general pediatric inpatient units across three Georgia children's hospital campuses (two tertiary, one community)
cycle1_result: ABC compliance 4.4% (95% CI 2.0-8.2%); safe sleep position/location 78.4%; safe sleep environment only 5.9%
intervention: Multi-pronged QI initiative: nursing education, nurse safe-sleep champions, crib cards with an ABC checklist, regular crib audits, and weekly tracking boards reporting unit compliance
cycle2_period: 2-4 months post-intervention (audits taken 24 hours to 7 days after crib cards/tracking boards introduced)

other_findings: No significant difference in improvement between the three hospitals; crib card compliance itself was not recorded, so the specific driver of change and a possible Hawthorne effect could not be excluded.

setting: Teaching hospital Spaarne Gasthuis, Haarlem/Hoofddorp, Netherlands (inpatients)

finding: 74/96 labs communicated optimal sampling time; 81/96 used immunoassays; wide variability in reference range limits (50% from manufacturers, 18.8% historical); 64/96 used action limits but 63/96 did not report a borderline range as guidance suggests; interpretative comments provided by 67/96 labs but none referenced management guidelines; UK NEQAS data showed considerable variation in assay performance
setting: UK and Republic of Ireland clinical biochemistry laboratories
cycle1_result: 74/96 labs communicated optimal sampling time; 81/96 used immunoassays; wide variability in reference range limits (50% from manufacturers, 18.8% historical); 64/96 used action limits but 63/96 did not report a borderline range as guidance suggests; interpretative comments provided by 67/96 labs but none referenced management guidelines; UK NEQAS data showed considerable variation in assay performance
other_findings: Authors call for standardisation of testosterone assays and harmonisation of laboratory practice.
authors: Livingston M; Downie P; Hackett G; Marrington R; Heald A; Ramachandran S
citation: Livingston M, Downie P, Hackett G, Marrington R, Heald A, Ramachandran S. An audit of the measurement and reporting of male testosterone levels in UK clinical biochemistry laboratories. Int J Clin Pract. 2020;74(11):e13607. doi:10.1111/ijcp.13607. PMID: 32649008.

topic: Urinary tract stone surgery mortality clinical management issues
title: Urinary tract stone deaths: data from the Australian and New Zealand Audits of Surgical Mortality.
standard: Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality (ANZASM) peer review process
finding: 100 (9.7%) of 1034 urological deaths related to stones; 39% (37/95) of stone deaths associated with clinical management issues (CMIs), vs 26% for general urology/all surgery
setting: National (Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality, ANZASM)
cycle1_period: 1 January 2009 to 31 December 2018 (deaths 2009-2017 analysed for CMIs)
cycle1_result: 100 (9.7%) of 1034 urological deaths related to stones; 39% (37/95) of stone deaths associated with clinical management issues (CMIs), vs 26% for general urology/all surgery
other_findings: Ureterorenoscopy had the highest CMI rate at 54% (12/22); urinary sepsis caused 49.5% of deaths and cardiac events 20%.
authors: Galiabovitch E; Hansen D; Retegan C; McCahy P

title: Implementation of a Clinical Decision Laboratory Ordering Algorithm for Preeclampsia: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
standard: Institutional protocol for preeclampsia laboratory investigations (updated to evidence-based algorithm)
finding: 2923 tests ordered monthly at a cost of CAD$18,306; most providers ordered broad panels and were unaware of associated costs
change: Multidisciplinary-developed laboratory ordering algorithm for preeclampsia investigations, posted on wards, with pocket aides and educational seminars, implemented via PDSA cycles
setting: Obstetrics wards, tertiary care centre
cycle1_result: 2923 tests ordered monthly at a cost of CAD$18,306; most providers ordered broad panels and were unaware of associated costs
intervention: Multidisciplinary-developed laboratory ordering algorithm for preeclampsia investigations, posted on wards, with pocket aides and educational seminars, implemented via PDSA cycles
cycle2_result: 39.9% reduction in costs related to blood tests (savings of CAD$7304/month); performance of essential investigations (e.g. creatinine) unchanged as control measure
other_findings: Annualised savings of CAD$87,643 with reduced iatrogenic blood loss and no evidence of harm; effects sustained over time.
authors: Thompson X; Sullivan MB; Mathura P; Wong A; Crawford J; Sia W
journal: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC

topic: Microbiological pus swab practice for perianal abscess
title: Auditing the Routine Microbiological Examination of Pus Swabs From Uncomplicated Perianal Abscesses: Clinical Necessity or Old Habit?
standard: not reported
finding: Pus swabs sent in 66.7% of cases; only a third of microbiology reports were reviewed by the surgical team; all patients were discharged before results were released with no subsequent change in management; no consistent association found between microbiology results and re-admission with perianal abscess or fistula-in-ano
setting: George Eliot Hospital NHS Trust
cycle1_result: Pus swabs sent in 66.7% of cases; only a third of microbiology reports were reviewed by the surgical team; all patients were discharged before results were released with no subsequent change in management; no consistent association found between microbiology results and re-admission with perianal abscess or fistula-in-ano
other_findings: Authors do not recommend routine microbiological swabs unless specific clinical concerns (recurrent sepsis, immunocompromise, extensive necrosis, systemic sepsis) are present.

topic: Medication adherence screening in paediatric liver transplant recipients

finding: not reported
change: Multiple PDSA cycles developing a system to screen for adherence risk, identify barriers, and partner with patients/families to address them

cycle1_result: not reported
intervention: Multiple PDSA cycles developing a system to screen for adherence risk, identify barriers, and partner with patients/families to address them

title: Designing a Process for Cardiology Patient Transfers: A Quality Improvement, Descriptive Study on Interprovider Communication and Resident Education.
standard: Internal QI target: increase resident-reported comfort at handoff (no fixed percentage target stated)
finding: 15% of residents reported feeling 'always'/'very often' prepared; 23% had concerns about floor appropriateness
change: Failure Mode Effect Analysis and key driver diagram leading to a transfer checklist and algorithm, inter-team huddle, and education on the transfer process
setting: Cardiac ICU to cardiology acute care unit, 323-bed pediatric hospital
cycle1_result: 15% of residents reported feeling 'always'/'very often' prepared; 23% had concerns about floor appropriateness
intervention: Failure Mode Effect Analysis and key driver diagram leading to a transfer checklist and algorithm, inter-team huddle, and education on the transfer process
cycle2_result: Residents reporting preparedness increased to 83%; concerns about floor appropriateness decreased to 4%
other_findings: Authors note small post-intervention sample size limits definitive conclusions about improved comfort.
authors: Kulesa JT; Balsara SL; Ghebremariam ET; Colyer J

title: Improving Concussion Management by Including Driving Recommendations for Adolescents with Concussions: A Quality Improvement Project.
standard: Internal QI target: 75% of adolescents with concussion receive driving recommendations
finding: not reported
change: EHR 'smart phrase' reminding providers to give driving recommendations during concussion visits (August 2017-August 2018)

cycle1_result: not reported
intervention: EHR 'smart phrase' reminding providers to give driving recommendations during concussion visits (August 2017-August 2018)

title: Auditing RadExam: Employing Psychometrics to Improve Exam Quality.
standard: Psychometric validity standards for exam questions (question p value, Discrimination Index)
finding: Audit 1 identified 617 questions with poor Discrimination Index performance
change: RadExam subspecialty editors evaluated and modified/removed/replaced poorly performing questions identified by audit
setting: National resident assessment programme (100 residency programs)
cycle1_result: Audit 1 identified 617 questions with poor Discrimination Index performance
intervention: RadExam subspecialty editors evaluated and modified/removed/replaced poorly performing questions identified by audit
cycle2_period: nearly 1 year after full RadExam implementation (Audit 2)
cycle2_result: Significant decrease in number of flagged questions and improved overall exam performance in Audit 2
other_findings: Audit process used statistical data including question/exam administration numbers, p value, Discrimination Index, Bloom's taxonomy level, and image-based question counts.
authors: Smith EB; Lewis P; Benefield T; Catanzano TM; Khan MJ; Nyberg E; Jordan S

topic: Adherence to neonatal early-onset sepsis antibiotic guidelines
title: Multicentre study found that adherence to national antibiotic recommendations for neonatal early-onset sepsis was low.
standard: Dutch neonatal early-onset sepsis (EOS) guidelines (adapted from UK guidance)
finding: Antibiotics recommended for 438/1024 (42.8%) at-risk neonates, but only 186/438 (42.5%) received them; withholding recommended for 586/1024 (57.2%), adhered to in 570/586 (97.3%); antibiotics continued >3 days in 56/178 (31.5%) despite negative blood culture
setting: Seven hospitals, multicentre
cycle1_result: Antibiotics recommended for 438/1024 (42.8%) at-risk neonates, but only 186/438 (42.5%) received them; withholding recommended for 586/1024 (57.2%), adhered to in 570/586 (97.3%); antibiotics continued >3 days in 56/178 (31.5%) despite negative blood culture
other_findings: Single-cycle prospective observational audit finding low adherence to guideline-recommended antibiotic initiation; authors recommend guideline revision.
authors: van der Weijden BM; Achten NB; Bekhof J; Evers EE; Berk M; Kamps AWA; Rijpert M; Ten Tusscher GW; van Houten MA; Plötz FB

topic: National policy for trichiasis surgical follow-up and surgeon audit
title: National approaches to trichiasis surgical follow-up, outcome assessment and surgeon audit in trachoma-endemic countries in Africa.
standard: WHO recommendation for regular follow-up, outcome assessment and audit of trichiasis surgeons
finding: Only 4/27 countries had a national policy for surgical follow-up/outcome assessment; only 2/27 had a national policy for surgeon audit; only 9/27 had a cut-off for poorly performing surgeons
setting: National trachoma elimination programmes, 27 African countries
cycle1_result: Only 4/27 countries had a national policy for surgical follow-up/outcome assessment; only 2/27 had a national policy for surgeon audit; only 9/27 had a cut-off for poorly performing surgeons
other_findings: A survey of national policy/systems presence (a policy-level audit of country programmes) rather than a single-service clinical audit measuring patient outcomes against a numeric target.
authors: Mwangi G; Courtright P; Solomon AW
citation: Mwangi G, Courtright P, Solomon AW. National approaches to trichiasis surgical follow-up, outcome assessment and surgeon audit in trachoma-endemic countries in Africa. Br J Ophthalmol. 2021;105(7):904-908. doi:10.1136/bjophthalmol-2019-315777. PMID: 32713838.

topic: VTE prophylaxis compliance in medical inpatients
title: Multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to improving compliance with venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis in a district general hospital.
standard: NICE guidance on prevention of VTE in hospitalised patients; local target of over 85% compliance with VTE prophylaxis prescription within 3 months
finding: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission 51% compliance; dose adjustment for patient weight 69% compliance; dose adjustment for renal function 80% compliance
change: Multidisciplinary quality improvement team introduced a 'VTE sticker' to prompt risk assessment, educational material for medical staff and allied health professionals, and patient information leaflets, over three quality improvement cycles.
setting: District general hospital, Royal Glamorgan Hospital
cycle1_result: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours of admission 51% compliance; dose adjustment for patient weight 69% compliance; dose adjustment for renal function 80% compliance
intervention: Multidisciplinary quality improvement team introduced a 'VTE sticker' to prompt risk assessment, educational material for medical staff and allied health professionals, and patient information leaflets, over three quality improvement cycles.
cycle2_result: VTE risk assessment within 24 hours improved to 94% compliance; dose adjustment for weight improved to 100%; dose adjustment for renal function improved to 100%; results were replicated in a different clinical environment
other_findings: Improvements were sustainable and replicable across different clinical environments.
authors: Nana M; Shute C; Williams R; Kokwaro F; Riddick K; Lane H
citation: Nana M, Shute C, Williams R, Kokwaro F, Riddick K, Lane H. Multidisciplinary, patient-centred approach to improving compliance with venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis in a district general hospital. BMJ Open Qual. 2020;9(3):e000680. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2019-000680. PMID: 32718914.

title: A quality improvement programme to reduce hospital-acquired pressure injuries.
standard: Internal QI target: reduce HAPIs by 60% within 2 years, using IHI evidence-based practices (SSKIN bundle)
finding: HAPI incidence 6.1/1000 patient-days; prevalence 9.7/100 patients surveyed
change: SSKIN bundle (Surface, Skin inspection, Keep moving, Incontinence, Nutrition), turning clocks, PI 'calendars', attention to endotracheal tube ties, tested via PDSA with IHI collaboration
setting: Heart Hospital, all inpatient units
cycle1_result: HAPI incidence 6.1/1000 patient-days; prevalence 9.7/100 patients surveyed
intervention: SSKIN bundle (Surface, Skin inspection, Keep moving, Incontinence, Nutrition), turning clocks, PI 'calendars', attention to endotracheal tube ties, tested via PDSA with IHI collaboration
cycle2_result: HAPI incidence dropped to 1.1/1000 patient-days (83.5% reduction); prevalence fell to 2.0/100 patients surveyed (73.4% decline)
other_findings: Reduction sustained over a 4-year period; independent t-test used to confirm statistical significance.
authors: Gupta P; Shiju S; Chacko G; Thomas M; Abas A; Savarimuthu I; Omari E; Al-Balushi S; Jessymol P; Mathew S; Quinto M; McDonald I; Andrews W

topic: Adherence to Surviving Sepsis Campaign hour-1 bundle
title: A Descriptive Study on Sepsis: Causes, Outcomes, and Adherence to Guidelines on Patients with Sepsis at a Tertiary Care Hospital in Sri Lanka.
standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) hour-1 bundle, International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2018
finding: Bundle compliance: IV fluids 10.9%, blood cultures before antibiotics 58.1%, first-dose antibiotic within 1 hour 3.9%, arterial blood gas 15.5%; mortality rate 9.6%
setting: University Medical Unit, tertiary care hospital
cycle1_result: Bundle compliance: IV fluids 10.9%, blood cultures before antibiotics 58.1%, first-dose antibiotic within 1 hour 3.9%, arterial blood gas 15.5%; mortality rate 9.6%
other_findings: Single-cycle descriptive audit finding poor sepsis bundle adherence in a resource-poor setting; staffing capacity did not affect adherence; recommends education/training to improve.
authors: Matthias AT; Indrakumar J; Ranasinghe T; Wijekoon S; Yashodara C

topic: Clinician attention to patient contextual factors (audio audit and feedback)
title: Evaluation of a Patient-Collected Audio Audit and Feedback Quality Improvement Program on Clinician Attention to Patient Life Context and Health Care Costs in the Veterans Affairs Health Care System.
standard: Content Coding for Contextualization of Care (4C) method standard for addressing patient contextual 'red flags'
finding: At baseline, clinicians addressed 413/618 contextual factors in care plans (67%)
change: Audio audit and feedback QI programme: clinicians received feedback (standard or enhanced intensity) on attention to patient contextual factors, stepped wedge design
setting: 6 Veterans Affairs outpatient primary care facilities
cycle1_n: 4496 encounters, 666 clinicians (618 contextual factors at baseline)
cycle1_result: At baseline, clinicians addressed 413/618 contextual factors in care plans (67%)
intervention: Audio audit and feedback QI programme: clinicians received feedback (standard or enhanced intensity) on attention to patient contextual factors, stepped wedge design
cycle2_result: Contextual factors addressed increased to 1707/2367 (72%), OR 1.3 (95% CI 1.1-1.6, p=0.01); associated with greater likelihood of improved outcomes (adjusted OR 2.5, 95% CI 1.5-4.1) and cost savings
other_findings: Stepped-wedge QI trial design; audio-recorded encounters analysed and fed back to clinicians, improving contextualised care and reducing hospitalisation costs.
authors: Weiner S; Schwartz A; Altman L; Ball S; Bartle B; Binns-Calvey A; Chan C; Falck-Ytter C; Frenchman M; Gee B; Jackson JL; Jordan N; Kass B; Kelly B; Safdar N; Scholcoff C; Sharma G; Weaver F; Wopat M
citation: Weiner S, Schwartz A, Altman L, Ball S, Bartle B, Binns-Calvey A, et al.. Evaluation of a Patient-Collected Audio Audit and Feedback Quality Improvement Program on Clinician Attention to Patient Life Context and Health Care Costs in the Veterans Affairs Health Care System. topic: Overweight and obesity screening in college students
title: Increasing Assessment, Diagnosis, and Intervention of Overweight and Obesity Among College Students: A Quality Improvement Project.
standard: Evidence-based practice recommendations for screening/diagnosis/intervention of overweight and obesity
finding: Baseline manual EHR audit of 241 records; assessment, diagnosis and intervention rates before education not numerically stated
change: Two educational seminars to increase provider awareness of evidence-based practice recommendations and available resources

cycle1_result: Baseline manual EHR audit of 241 records; assessment, diagnosis and intervention rates before education not numerically stated
intervention: Two educational seminars to increase provider awareness of evidence-based practice recommendations and available resources

other_findings: not reported
authors: Thomas PM
