title: Reducing opioid utilization after appendectomy: A lesson in implementation of a multidisciplinary quality improvement project.
standard: Internal QI targets: three measures (ice packs, pain scores, standardised order set) to minimise opioid use post-appendectomy
finding: not reported (baseline opioid utilisation, no specific percentage given)
change: Three measures: ice packs to incision in PACU, standard pain scores within 30 minutes of ward admission, standardised postoperative order set minimising opioids with limited discharge prescriptions
setting: Children's Hospital of Wisconsin, paediatric surgery
cycle1_result: not reported (baseline opioid utilisation, no specific percentage given)
intervention: Three measures: ice packs to incision in PACU, standard pain scores within 30 minutes of ward admission, standardised postoperative order set minimising opioids with limited discharge prescriptions
cycle2_result: Compliance: ice packs 66.9%, pain scores 88%, postoperative order set 94.7%; statistically significant decreases in IV/enteral opioids administered, discharge opioid doses, and patients discharged with an opioid prescription
other_findings: Multidisciplinary assessment addressing parental, patient and nursing expectations enabled reduced opioid consumption.
authors: Somers KK; Amin R; Leack KM; Lingongo M; Arca MJ; Gourlay DM
citation: Somers KK, Amin R, Leack KM, Lingongo M, Arca MJ, Gourlay DM. Reducing opioid utilization after appendectomy: A lesson in implementation of a multidisciplinary quality improvement project. Surg Open Sci. 2020;2(1):27-33. doi:10.1016/j.sopen.2019.08.001. PMID: 32754705.

topic: Standardising surfactant delivery timing in noninvasive ventilation
title: A Quality Improvement Project to Standardize Surfactant Delivery in the Era of Noninvasive Ventilation.
standard: Internal standard criteria for timely intubation and surfactant administration (within 1 hour of intubation) for premature infants
finding: Mean time to intubation for infants 28-32 weeks gestation was 321 minutes; surfactant given within 1 hour of intubation in 78% of cases
change: Literature review and education for physicians, free-text orders for notification, trainee program, coordination with radiology
setting: Neonatal intensive care unit
cycle1_result: Mean time to intubation for infants 28-32 weeks gestation was 321 minutes; surfactant given within 1 hour of intubation in 78% of cases
intervention: Literature review and education for physicians, free-text orders for notification, trainee program, coordination with radiology
cycle2_result: Mean time to intubation for 28-32 week infants decreased to 81 minutes (no change for infants <28 weeks); surfactant given within 1 hour of intubation improved to 100%
other_findings: No adverse occurrences noted; educational and process interventions successfully implemented standard criteria for intubation/surfactant timing.
authors: Kim JE; Brewer M; Spinazzola R; Wallace E; Casatelli J; Beachy J; Weinberger B; Perveen S
citation: Kim JE, Brewer M, Spinazzola R, Wallace E, Casatelli J, Beachy J, et al.. A Quality Improvement Project to Standardize Surfactant Delivery in the Era of Noninvasive Ventilation. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2020;5(4):e311. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000311. PMID: 32766486.

topic: Influenza vaccination in the emergency department
title: Vaccinating in the Emergency Department, a Novel Approach to Improve Influenza Vaccination Rates via a Quality Improvement Initiative.
standard: AAP/CDC recommendation for universal annual influenza vaccination from 6 months of age; local project goal to increase ED-administered vaccines from 75 to 1000 in one season
finding: Only 75 influenza vaccinations given in the ED; 0% of patients screened for vaccine status
change: Mandatory EHR vaccine screening, a nurse-driven vaccine administration protocol with clinical decision support/best practice advisories, provider/nurse/family education, a revised pharmacy workflow to reduce wastage, and weekly staff feedback, tested via PDSA cycles
setting: 296-bed tertiary paediatric academic emergency department, Milwaukee, Wisconsin
cycle1_result: Only 75 influenza vaccinations given in the ED; 0% of patients screened for vaccine status
intervention: Mandatory EHR vaccine screening, a nurse-driven vaccine administration protocol with clinical decision support/best practice advisories, provider/nurse/family education, a revised pharmacy workflow to reduce wastage, and weekly staff feedback, tested via PDSA cycles
cycle2_result: Screening improved from 0% to 90%; 1,323 vaccines administered (1,167 via the protocol, 8.5% of eligible patients), exceeding the goal of 1,000; no significant increase in ED length of stay (139 min); about $22,500 net revenue to the hospital
other_findings: Main barriers were high vaccine refusal (87%) and patients leaving before administration (33%); acceptance was higher in Hispanic/Latino patients, ages 5-17 and Medicaid-insured patients, reducing vaccination disparities.
authors: Baumer-Mouradian SH; Kleinschmidt A; Servi A; Jaworski B; Lazarevic K; Kopetsky M; Nimmer M; Hanson T; Gray MP; Drendel AL
citation: Baumer-Mouradian SH, Kleinschmidt A, Servi A, Jaworski B, Lazarevic K, Kopetsky M, et al.. Vaccinating in the Emergency Department, a Novel Approach to Improve Influenza Vaccination Rates via a Quality Improvement Initiative. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2020;5(4):e322. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000322. PMID: 32766495.

topic: Perioperative blood transfusion in craniosynostosis repair
title: The Road to Transfusion-free Craniosynostosis Repair in Children Less Than 24 Months Old: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
standard: Local goal of transfusion-free craniosynostosis repair, informed by multimodal blood management literature (Pediatric Craniofacial Collaborative Group benchmark of 95% transfusion rate)
finding: Total allogeneic transfusion rate 100% in 2013
change: Sequential PDCA cycles 2014-2016: a perioperative temperature-management protocol, a postoperative transfusion protocol (transfuse only if haemoglobin <7 g/dL), intraoperative tranexamic acid (12.5 mg/kg bolus), preincisional 0.25% lidocaine with epinephrine injection, a dedicated core anaesthesia team, and intraoperative cell salvage
setting: Tertiary children's hospital, Omaha, Nebraska (craniofacial reconstruction in children ≤24 months)
cycle1_result: Total allogeneic transfusion rate 100% in 2013
intervention: Sequential PDCA cycles 2014-2016: a perioperative temperature-management protocol, a postoperative transfusion protocol (transfuse only if haemoglobin <7 g/dL), intraoperative tranexamic acid (12.5 mg/kg bolus), preincisional 0.25% lidocaine with epinephrine injection, a dedicated core anaesthesia team, and intraoperative cell salvage
cycle2_result: Total allogeneic transfusion rate fell to 22.7% by 2018, a statistically significant 77.3 percentage point reduction from the 2013 baseline (p<0.05)
other_findings: Uptake of tranexamic acid was gradual, not universal until 2017; cell salvage volumes declined as bleeding decreased; preoperative iron supplementation was used inconsistently and was not included as a formal PDCA intervention.
authors: Beethe AB; Spitznagel RA; Kugler JA; Goeller JK; Franzen MH; Hamlin RJ; Lockhart TJ; Lyden ER; Glogowski KR; LeRiger MM
citation: Beethe AB, Spitznagel RA, Kugler JA, Goeller JK, Franzen MH, Hamlin RJ, et al.. The Road to Transfusion-free Craniosynostosis Repair in Children Less Than 24 Months Old: A Quality Improvement Initiative. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2020;5(4):e331. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000331. PMID: 32766502.

title: Appropriateness of trimethoprim as empiric treatment for cystitis in 15-55 year-old women: an audit.
standard: not reported

setting: General practice, multiple regions
cycle1_result: Of 340 eligible samples, 181 (53.2%) had a urinary pathogen identified; trimethoprim susceptibility 73.6% (E. coli), nitrofurantoin 100%, cefalexin 96.6%; overall trimethoprim resistance 13.5%

authors: Ussher JE; McAuliffe GN; Elvy JA; Upton A

topic: Inpatient glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes

cycle1_result: Adequate glycaemic control (7.8-10 mmol/L) achieved in 45% of patients; lack of uniformity in insulin regimen initiation
intervention: Standardised inpatient hyperglycaemia management protocol, teaching sessions for trainees and nurses, consultant supervision, regular reminders/feedback, and patient education
cycle2_result: Target glycaemic control of 70% achieved in 4 of 10 PDSA cycles, without increase in hypoglycaemic episodes
other_findings: Used Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) model across 10 cycles.
authors: Khan AA; Shahzad A; Rose S; Al Mohanadi DHSH; Zahid M
citation: Khan AA, Shahzad A, Rose S, Al Mohanadi DHSH, Zahid M. Quality improvement project for improving inpatient glycaemic control in non-critically ill patients admitted on medical floor with type 2 diabetes mellitus. topic: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia reduction in preterm infants
title: A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in a Level 4 NICU-Golden Hour Management of Respiratory Distress Syndrome in Preterm Newborns.
standard: Vermont Oxford Network (VON) average chronic lung disease rate of 24% (need for mechanical ventilation or supplemental oxygen at 36 weeks corrected gestational age)
finding: Baseline chronic lung disease (CLD) rate 33.5%-34.0%; delivery-room prophylactic surfactant use averaged 80.8% in infants ≤28 weeks gestation
change: Multidisciplinary QI initiative using PDSA cycles: a gestational-age based 'Golden Hour' delivery-room protocol standardising early surfactant administration and timely extubation, an admission huddle, standardised non-invasive (Bubble CPAP) ventilation guidelines, later less invasive surfactant administration (LISA), stopping prophylactic indomethacin, and frequent chart audits with staff re-education
setting: 68-bed level 4 regional perinatal NICU, Golisano Children's Hospital, Rochester, New York
cycle1_n: not reported (711 total admissions across both study periods)
cycle1_result: Baseline chronic lung disease (CLD) rate 33.5%-34.0%; delivery-room prophylactic surfactant use averaged 80.8% in infants ≤28 weeks gestation
intervention: Multidisciplinary QI initiative using PDSA cycles: a gestational-age based 'Golden Hour' delivery-room protocol standardising early surfactant administration and timely extubation, an admission huddle, standardised non-invasive (Bubble CPAP) ventilation guidelines, later less invasive surfactant administration (LISA), stopping prophylactic indomethacin, and frequent chart audits with staff re-education
cycle2_period: April 2018 to December 2020 (Golden Hour protocol launched July 2018)
cycle2_n: not reported (711 total admissions across both study periods)
cycle2_result: Overall CLD rate fell from 33.5% to 16.5%, a 51% reduction sustained for over 18 months; delivery-room surfactant compliance rose from 80.8% to 98.1%; intubation rates fell across all gestational age groups, most among infants 26-27 weeks (~50% reduction); discharge diuretic use fell from 44% to 22%
other_findings: Postnatal steroid use remained stable below 10%; maternal chorioamnionitis diagnoses decreased significantly between periods (31.4% to 24.7%), a potential confounder; repeat surfactant dosing increased transiently after a product change.
authors: Dylag AM; Tulloch J; Paul KE; Meyers JM
citation: Dylag AM, Tulloch J, Paul KE, Meyers JM. A Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia in a Level 4 NICU-Golden Hour Management of Respiratory Distress Syndrome in Preterm Newborns. Children (Basel). 2021;8(4):301. doi:10.3390/children8040301. PMID: 33920871.

title: Reduction in massive postpartum haemorrhage and red blood cell transfusion during a national quality improvement project, Obstetric Bleeding Strategy for Wales, OBS Cymru: an observational study.
standard: OBS Cymru PPH care bundle (universal risk assessment, quantitative blood loss measurement, structured escalation, viscoelastometry-guided fibrinogen replacement), informed by international PPH management guidelines
finding: massive PPH (>2500mL) rate 6.4/1000 maternities; 350/15204 (2.3%) women transfused red cells; quantitative blood loss measurement in 83% of PPH >=1000mL episodes
change: National PPH care bundle rollout: universal risk assessment, quantitative (volumetric/gravimetric) blood loss measurement, structured escalation to senior clinicians at set blood loss thresholds, point-of-care viscoelastometry (ROTEM)-guided fibrinogen replacement, standardised paperwork proforma, and multi-professional training
setting: All 12 obstetric units in Wales (500-6000 births/year each)
cycle1_result: massive PPH (>2500mL) rate 6.4/1000 maternities; 350/15204 (2.3%) women transfused red cells; quantitative blood loss measurement in 83% of PPH >=1000mL episodes
intervention: National PPH care bundle rollout: universal risk assessment, quantitative (volumetric/gravimetric) blood loss measurement, structured escalation to senior clinicians at set blood loss thresholds, point-of-care viscoelastometry (ROTEM)-guided fibrinogen replacement, standardised paperwork proforma, and multi-professional training
cycle2_result: massive PPH rate fell to 4.9/1000 maternities (regression: decrease of 1.10/1000 maternities/year, 95% CI 0.28-1.92, p=0.011); red cell transfusion fell to 268/15150 (1.8%, p=0.001); quantitative blood loss measurement rose to 98.1%
other_findings: Fewer women progressed from moderate to massive PPH in the last 6 months (5.0%) than the first (7.0%, p=0.021); units of red cells transfused fell by 7.4/1000 maternities/year (p=0.015); no increase in haemostatic impairment or low haemoglobin despite reduced transfusion; five repeated audits of up to 30 consecutive women per unit tracked uptake of individual bundle components.
authors: Bell SF; Collis RE; Pallmann P; Bailey C; James K; John M; Kelly K; Kitchen T; Scarr C; Watkins A; Edey T; Macgillivray E; Greaves K; Volikas I; Tozer J; Sengupta N; Roberts I; Francis C; Collins PW

cycle1_result: 100% protocol compliance; FTCA success achieved in 4/16 (25%) patients; median postoperative ventilation duration 2.1 hours; median ICU stay 22 hours

topic: Dispatcher recognition of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
title: Assessment of a quality improvement programme to improve telephone dispatchers' accuracy in identifying out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
standard: Resuscitation Academy/American Heart Association performance goals: OHCA recognition sensitivity >95%, median time to recognition <120s, median time to first compression <180s
finding: Sensitivity for OHCA recognition 82.3% (95% CI 76.4-87.2%); median time to recognise OHCA 68s (IQR 43-114.5); median time to first compression 148s
change: Quality improvement programme: mandatory NO-NO-GO algorithm pop-up tool on the dispatcher's screen, quarterly telephone-CPR education and CPR training, quarterly voice-log audits with individual feedback, and focus-group review of recorded OHCA calls
setting: Emergency Medical Dispatch Centre, Region of Southern Denmark (serving 1.2 million inhabitants)
cycle1_result: Sensitivity for OHCA recognition 82.3% (95% CI 76.4-87.2%); median time to recognise OHCA 68s (IQR 43-114.5); median time to first compression 148s

cycle2_result: Sensitivity for OHCA recognition improved to 92.7% (95% CI 88.2-95.8%, p=0.0014), still below the 95% target; median time to recognition 56s (not statistically significant, p=0.097); median time to first compression 148s (unchanged, p=0.918)
other_findings: Time taken to ask about consciousness and breathing did not change significantly between periods; the Resuscitation Academy's 95% recognition target was not met despite the improvement.

cycle1_result: in-hospital mortality 20.0%, 30-day mortality 22.4% (crude); guideline adherence not separately quantified at baseline

finding: UE rate 2.02 per 100 ventilated/day; mean 59 days between UE events
change: Six-driver bundle tested via PDSA cycles: a new endotracheal tube fixation technique, standardised endotracheal tube positioning assessment, new physical restraint devices, sedation monitoring with the COMFORT-B scale, family education, and a UE-prevention checklist
setting: 20-bed paediatric intensive care unit, private quaternary hospital, São Paulo, Brazil
cycle1_result: UE rate 2.02 per 100 ventilated/day; mean 59 days between UE events
intervention: Six-driver bundle tested via PDSA cycles: a new endotracheal tube fixation technique, standardised endotracheal tube positioning assessment, new physical restraint devices, sedation monitoring with the COMFORT-B scale, family education, and a UE-prevention checklist

topic: Severe hypertension in pregnancy treatment time

standard: Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health (AIM) Severe Hypertension in Pregnancy bundle: appropriate acute antihypertensive therapy within 60 minutes of onset

change: Multimodal statewide QI support adapting the AIM severe hypertension bundle across level 1-4 maternity hospitals, with statistical process control monitoring
setting: 29 hospitals, statewide maternal safety QI project, Ohio, USA
cycle1_result: Baseline proportion receiving timely, appropriate treatment 56.5%.

cycle1_result: Adequate CPG adherence was highest among recently diagnosed T2DM patients (91.6%) and lowest among frail T2DM patients (74.7%); inadequate adherence was mainly among obese/frail patients treated by physicians with low CPG knowledge (3.4%/3.5%).
other_findings: 57% of primary care physicians had moderate CPG knowledge; patients with inadequate adherence were generally older, with higher BMI, poorer HbA1c control and fewer visits.

title: Recognizing Nonaccidental Trauma in a Pediatric Tertiary Hospital: A Quality Improvement Imperative.
standard: American Academy of Pediatrics-recommended nonaccidental trauma (NAT) workup bundle for infants under 7 months with concerning injuries
finding: Appropriate NAT bundle completion 31%
change: Hospital-wide NAT clinical guideline and EHR order bundle (age-based), a visual injury-indication chart, multidisciplinary education sessions, a 'Be a S.T.A.R.' communication campaign, caregiver communication scripts/handouts, and a 'One and Down in a Gown' infant examination protocol
setting: Pediatric emergency department and inpatient units, large freestanding urban tertiary children's hospital, United States
cycle1_n: 952 total study population over the project period
cycle1_result: Appropriate NAT bundle completion 31%
intervention: Hospital-wide NAT clinical guideline and EHR order bundle (age-based), a visual injury-indication chart, multidisciplinary education sessions, a 'Be a S.T.A.R.' communication campaign, caregiver communication scripts/handouts, and a 'One and Down in a Gown' infant examination protocol
cycle2_result: Appropriate bundle completion rose to 100% and was sustained (no suspicious/incomplete cases from March 2020 to June 2021, up from a baseline of 11 patients between such cases); infant gowning compliance rose from 38% to 95%
other_findings: Chart review reclassified many 'incomplete' cases as appropriate (e.g., accidental injuries not needing a full bundle, or patients who died or left before evaluation); 313 child protective services reports were made for infants under 7 months over the study period.
authors: Greene HM; Letson MM; Spencer SP; Dolan K; Foster J; Crichton KG

title: Hospital-acquired E. coli bacteraemia at a large UK NHS Trust. A return towards baseline following implementation of a 5-year quality improvement programme.

finding: 134 episodes of hospital-acquired E. coli bacteraemia in the baseline year
change: PDSA cycles modifying antibiotic prophylaxis for high-risk procedures and introducing 'good practice' interventions around medical devices
setting: Barts Health NHS Trust
cycle1_result: 134 episodes of hospital-acquired E. coli bacteraemia in the baseline year
intervention: PDSA cycles modifying antibiotic prophylaxis for high-risk procedures and introducing 'good practice' interventions around medical devices

topic: Early mobility and functional independence after cardiac surgery
title: Enhancing early functional independence following cardiac surgery: a quality improvement programme.
standard: Local QI target: Functional Independence Measure (FIM) score of 80% or more by postoperative day 3 in over 80% of uncomplicated cardiac surgery patients, and a 6-minute walk distance over 250m by postoperative day 4
finding: Only 5.3% achieved FIM 80% or more by postoperative day 3 (mean FIM 73.71±4.81%); mean 6-minute walk distance on day 4 was 188.23±48.65m (only 54% completed the test); only 21.4% reported confidence in independent activities of daily living by day 5
change: Multidisciplinary QI programme ('4Is': Inform, Involve, Integrate, Inspect) via PDSA cycles: a standardised evidence-based mobility/activity protocol by postoperative day, staff education, standardised documentation, patient/family preoperative education, visual cues (floor markings, colour-coded flags, whiteboards), mandatory pain assessment before mobilisation, and a colour-coded risk categorisation system
setting: 20-bed high-dependency surgical unit for post-cardiac surgery patients, Heart Hospital, Hamad Medical Corporation, Doha, Qatar
cycle1_result: Only 5.3% achieved FIM 80% or more by postoperative day 3 (mean FIM 73.71±4.81%); mean 6-minute walk distance on day 4 was 188.23±48.65m (only 54% completed the test); only 21.4% reported confidence in independent activities of daily living by day 5
intervention: Multidisciplinary QI programme ('4Is': Inform, Involve, Integrate, Inspect) via PDSA cycles: a standardised evidence-based mobility/activity protocol by postoperative day, staff education, standardised documentation, patient/family preoperative education, visual cues (floor markings, colour-coded flags, whiteboards), mandatory pain assessment before mobilisation, and a colour-coded risk categorisation system

topic: Community health worker home visiting for pediatric asthma

finding: At baseline: average 4.1 days of daytime symptoms, 3.0 nights of symptoms, 4.1 days of rescue medication use in the past 2 weeks; 34.5% uncontrolled and 42.4% partly controlled asthma; average 0.92 ED visits per year pre-enrollment
change: A community health worker (CHW) home/phone visiting programme integrated into standard care: asthma management education, home environmental trigger assessment and remediation, and care coordination and communication with providers
setting: 4 hospitals/health centers (South Side Pediatric Asthma Center collaborative), Chicago, Illinois, serving predominantly Black, low-income children
cycle1_result: At baseline: average 4.1 days of daytime symptoms, 3.0 nights of symptoms, 4.1 days of rescue medication use in the past 2 weeks; 34.5% uncontrolled and 42.4% partly controlled asthma; average 0.92 ED visits per year pre-enrollment
intervention: A community health worker (CHW) home/phone visiting programme integrated into standard care: asthma management education, home environmental trigger assessment and remediation, and care coordination and communication with providers

title: Increasing venous thromboembolism risk assessment through a whole hospital-based intervention: a pre-post service evaluation to demonstrate quality improvement.
standard: American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) 9th edition VTE prevention guidelines using the Modified Caprini risk assessment tool; local SMART aim of >80% of inpatients assessed for VTE risk on admission by December 2019
finding: VTE risk assessment documented on admission for 42% (3790/8971); within 24 hours for 55% (4989/8971); within hospital stay (no time limit) for 71% (6395/8971); VTE incidence rate 0.5% (44/8971)
change: FOCUS-PDCA quality improvement methodology: educational sessions, sharing VTE documentation compliance results, reminders during ward rounds, a VTE liaison physician per specialty, and updated/communicated hospital VTE guidelines (5 parallel PDCA cycles over 3 months, April-June 2019)
setting: 600+ bed acute hospital providing medical and surgical services for adults, Dubai
cycle1_result: VTE risk assessment documented on admission for 42% (3790/8971); within 24 hours for 55% (4989/8971); within hospital stay (no time limit) for 71% (6395/8971); VTE incidence rate 0.5% (44/8971)
intervention: FOCUS-PDCA quality improvement methodology: educational sessions, sharing VTE documentation compliance results, reminders during ward rounds, a VTE liaison physician per specialty, and updated/communicated hospital VTE guidelines (5 parallel PDCA cycles over 3 months, April-June 2019)

finding: 85% had a colonoscopy ordered; only 21% completed colonoscopy within 6 months of the abnormal FIT
change: Multicomponent, multi-level patient navigation intervention with a structured checklist covering results review, colonoscopy ordering, results communication, insurance approval, pre-colonoscopy visit scheduling/completion, and colonoscopy scheduling/completion, refined over 2 PDSA cycles
setting: Federally Qualified Health Center system (Family Health Centers of San Diego), 2 clinic sites serving predominantly Hispanic/Latinx patients, California
cycle1_result: 85% had a colonoscopy ordered; only 21% completed colonoscopy within 6 months of the abnormal FIT
intervention: Multicomponent, multi-level patient navigation intervention with a structured checklist covering results review, colonoscopy ordering, results communication, insurance approval, pre-colonoscopy visit scheduling/completion, and colonoscopy scheduling/completion, refined over 2 PDSA cycles

topic: Hand hygiene adherence among research personnel
title: Improving research personnel's hand hygiene adherence in the pediatric acute care setting during the COVID-19 pandemic: a quality improvement initiative.
standard: Provincial hand hygiene target of 80% adherence (British Columbia), based on the WHO Multimodal Hand Hygiene Improvement Strategy
finding: Hand hygiene adherence 12.5% (95% CI 0-31.3)
change: Sequential PDSA cycles: a mandatory hand hygiene education module, performance feedback, COVID-19 pandemic protocol changes, visual reminder posters plus written feedback, a self-reflection survey, and positive reinforcement plus improved hand sanitiser accessibility
setting: Pediatric emergency department, BC Children's Hospital, Vancouver, Canada
cycle1_result: Hand hygiene adherence 12.5% (95% CI 0-31.3)

finding: Institutional CAUTI incidence rate was six times higher than the US-NHSN benchmark; incidence rate 7.07 per 1000 catheter days
change: Kotter and Rathgeber's changing-behaviour model combined with formal CAUTI prevention education (National Strategy Model) and bundle implementation

finding: Only 19% (8/43) of staff were aware of their individual CPR role on the day of a resuscitation; only 13% followed preassigned team roles
change: Four PDSA cycles: staff sensitisation on team dynamics; a simplified standardised format for assigning team roles on the whiteboard; assigning responsibility for role allocation to the shift nursing team leader; and sharing progress charts to sustain motivation
setting: 22-bed emergency department, Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital, Thimphu, Bhutan
cycle1_result: Only 19% (8/43) of staff were aware of their individual CPR role on the day of a resuscitation; only 13% followed preassigned team roles
intervention: Four PDSA cycles: staff sensitisation on team dynamics; a simplified standardised format for assigning team roles on the whiteboard; assigning responsibility for role allocation to the shift nursing team leader; and sharing progress charts to sustain motivation
cycle2_period: over an 8-week period following the 4 PDSA cycles
cycle2_result: Process indicator (percentage of shifts with roles preassigned) rose to 70% after cycle 1, 81% after cycle 2, 91% after cycle 3 and 95% by week 8; outcome indicator (CPRs where preassigned roles were followed) reached 100% by the end of cycle 3

setting: Five surgical wards including the Emergency Surgical Unit, Royal Blackburn Hospital, a district general hospital, Blackburn, UK
cycle1_period: retrospective baseline, one-month sample before intervention
cycle1_result: 70% (42/60) of TTOs were missing at least one essential element, most often follow-up details; 55% missed two or more, 35% missed three or more; format varied widely by individual writing style
intervention: A standardised TTO framework agreed with surgical consultants, introduced via teaching sessions and ward posters (PDSA cycle 1), then integrated as an auto-text e-template into the electronic patient record (CERNER) system (PDSA cycle 2)

finding: compliance with the 72-hour standard was 18%; average pathway time was 172 hours

topic: Obesity screening and documentation in primary care
title: Aligning with Obesity Guidelines: A Quality Improvement Initiative in Pediatric Primary Care.
standard: American Academy of Pediatrics Expert Committee Recommendations (2007, updated 2023) for BMI-based obesity diagnosis and comorbidity screening from age 2; USPSTF 2017 screening recommendations; local target of a 20% increase in appropriate coding and universal laboratory screening
finding: Appropriate combined E+Z obesity diagnosis coding averaged 15% (clinic 1) and 40% (clinic 2); nutrition/physical activity counseling codes used in near 0% (clinic 1) and about 10% (clinic 2) of charts; baseline lipid panel, A1c and ALT screening in ages 9-18 were 56%, 67% and 31% respectively
change: 6 PDSA cycles: initial staff training and clinical toolkit introduction, monthly education sessions, an SBAR memo on E/Z coding, large-group staff training with a coding expert, individual provider coaching/feedback, and EMR changes (diagnosis label update, pop-up prompts, and later nutrition/activity counseling templates)
setting: 2 Children's National Hospital community health centres (of 6 total), Anacostia region, Washington, DC
cycle1_result: Appropriate combined E+Z obesity diagnosis coding averaged 15% (clinic 1) and 40% (clinic 2); nutrition/physical activity counseling codes used in near 0% (clinic 1) and about 10% (clinic 2) of charts; baseline lipid panel, A1c and ALT screening in ages 9-18 were 56%, 67% and 31% respectively
intervention: 6 PDSA cycles: initial staff training and clinical toolkit introduction, monthly education sessions, an SBAR memo on E/Z coding, large-group staff training with a coding expert, individual provider coaching/feedback, and EMR changes (diagnosis label update, pop-up prompts, and later nutrition/activity counseling templates)
cycle2_period: intervention period March 2021 to March 2022, with 6-month sustainment through September 2022
cycle2_result: E/Z obesity coding rose above 80% and was sustained; nutrition/activity counseling coding rose to up to 96% after EMR templates were added; ALT screening met the 20% increase target, but lipid panel and A1c screening did not; extraneous laboratory test collection decreased significantly, though inconsistencies persisted, especially in the 2-8 year age group

title: Reducing prematurity-related neonatal mortality: a quality improvement project in Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
standard: Local QI target to reduce prematurity-related neonatal mortality from a median of 20.7% to 14.5%, informed by evidence-based CPAP therapy and infection prevention practice
finding: Median prematurity-related neonatal mortality 20.7 per 100 live births; Pareto analysis showed 57.7% of neonatal deaths were prematurity-related
change: Three change ideas via PDSA cycles: transporting premature neonates from the labour ward to NICU using CPAP, increasing use of a CPAP device with integrated oxygen concentrator/blender/compressor in the NICU (blenders increased from 1 to 4), and implementing a 4-component infection prevention checklist
setting: 44-bed NICU and 12-room labour and delivery ward, Gandhi Memorial Hospital, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (approximately 14,889 deliveries/year, 3828 preterm)
cycle1_result: Median prematurity-related neonatal mortality 20.7 per 100 live births; Pareto analysis showed 57.7% of neonatal deaths were prematurity-related
intervention: Three change ideas via PDSA cycles: transporting premature neonates from the labour ward to NICU using CPAP, increasing use of a CPAP device with integrated oxygen concentrator/blender/compressor in the NICU (blenders increased from 1 to 4), and implementing a 4-component infection prevention checklist
cycle2_result: Prematurity-related neonatal mortality fell from a median of 20.7% to 15.4% (a 25.6% relative reduction), shown by 7 consecutive data points below the baseline median; CPAP transport use rose from 40% to 100%; checklist adherence rose from 0% to 100%; staff satisfaction rose from 81% to 83%
other_findings: Limitations included inadequate neonatal resuscitation training and transport equipment shortages; very low birth weight infants remained high risk; pneumothorax/chest tube rates were not tracked as balancing measures.

finding: Robson-1 CS rate 65.7%; Robson-3 CS rate 25.4%; overall CS rate (internal HCPs) 82.7%
change: A 5-component intrapartum QI bundle for internal on-duty healthcare providers: a collaborative midwifery-obstetrician model of care for Robson-1 and 3 women, a new labour ward medical coordinator, daily supportive supervision, updated evidence-based intrapartum guidelines, and refresher simulation training
setting: Hospital e Maternidade Santa Joana, a large private tertiary maternity hospital (10,000 births/year), Sao Paulo, Brazil
cycle1_n: 8985 (internal HCP group across both periods; 3344 in first period)
cycle1_result: Robson-1 CS rate 65.7%; Robson-3 CS rate 25.4%; overall CS rate (internal HCPs) 82.7%

finding: Mean 60 hours to pathogen identification using older API biochemical technology; 0% availability of ID within 24 hours

topic: Surgical consent form risk documentation completeness

finding: Mean 64.00% of standardised risks documented for laparoscopic appendicectomy and 55.79% for laparoscopic cholecystectomy on handwritten consent forms; infertility and urinary retention frequently omitted
change: Development and introduction of pre-filled, procedure-specific consent forms incorporating the standardised risk set, layman's-term explanations, risks grouped by prevalence, and space for patient-specific additional risks

cycle1_result: Mean 64.00% of standardised risks documented for laparoscopic appendicectomy and 55.79% for laparoscopic cholecystectomy on handwritten consent forms; infertility and urinary retention frequently omitted

topic: Call diversion uptake for home hospice care
title: Quality Improvement Initiative to Improve Uptake of an Alternative Call Management Strategy for Home-Based Hospice Care.
standard: Local QI target of a 50% call diversion rate to the MediHELP telemedicine call-centre service (no external clinical standard; an internal operational benchmark)
finding: Call diversion rate 11% (approximately 15 of an expected 135 calls/day diverted); MediHELP answered a mean of 258 calls/month
change: Two PDSA cycles following root cause analysis: cycle 1 developed a standardised communication/documentation protocol with nurse input and chat-group updates; cycle 2 extended MediHELP operational hours to match office hours (enabling default call forwarding), added staff, and introduced patient/caregiver education on call diversion at admission
setting: HCA Hospice, a nonprofit home-based palliative care service with 30 frontline nurses across 5 satellite offices, Singapore
cycle1_period: baseline period (approximately September to December 2023, 3 months after MediHELP launch)
cycle1_result: Call diversion rate 11% (approximately 15 of an expected 135 calls/day diverted); MediHELP answered a mean of 258 calls/month
intervention: Two PDSA cycles following root cause analysis: cycle 1 developed a standardised communication/documentation protocol with nurse input and chat-group updates; cycle 2 extended MediHELP operational hours to match office hours (enabling default call forwarding), added staff, and introduced patient/caregiver education on call diversion at admission
cycle2_result: Call diversion rate rose to 65% (600 calls/month by July 2024, a 3.25-fold increase); nurse-reported daily incoming calls fell from 4.8 to 1.9 (p<0.001); nurses rating MediHELP as not concerning about diverting calls rose from 80.0% to 96.3%, and rating it effective rose from 48.0% to 81.5% (both p<0.05, Fisher's exact test)
other_findings: The first PDSA cycle alone did not significantly increase diversion rates, illustrating that trust-building needed to be paired with removing the operational hassle of manual call forwarding; qualitative feedback described reduced nurse stress and fewer disrupted home visits.

standard: WHO Quality Assessment/Quality Improvement Tool for Maternal and Newborn Care (WHO QA/QI MN); local SMART aims: kangaroo mother care (KMC) 70% to 85%, exclusive mother's own milk (MoM) by day 7 59% to 70%, antibiotic point prevalence 25% to 15%
finding: At least 1 hour/day KMC provided in 70.25%; exclusive MoM by day 7 in 59.24%; antibiotic point prevalence 25.5%; composite outcome (mortality plus major morbidities) 14.19 per 1000 patient days

setting: 90-bed Department of Neonatology (32 intensive care beds), a tertiary medical college, Lady Hardinge Medical College, New Delhi, India
cycle1_result: At least 1 hour/day KMC provided in 70.25%; exclusive MoM by day 7 in 59.24%; antibiotic point prevalence 25.5%; composite outcome (mortality plus major morbidities) 14.19 per 1000 patient days
intervention: Point of Care Quality Improvement (POCQI) methodology with multiple PDSA cycles per focus area, guided by fishbone/key driver diagram root-cause analysis of gaps identified using the adapted WHO QA/QI MN tool, targeting KMC, MoM use and antibiotic stewardship

cycle1_result: Mean score for assessment of suspected pneumonia 2.1 (Kyrgyzstan) and 1.6 (Tajikistan) out of 3; unnecessary painful/invasive procedures in 66% (Kyrgyzstan) and 70% (Tajikistan) of reviewed cases; incorrect ARI treatment in 63% and 70% of cases respectively

title: From lines to lifelines: a quality improvement study to reduce CLABSI at a level III NICU in LMIC.
standard: Local standard: central line insertion and maintenance care bundle compliance; unit aim to reduce CLABSI rate from 66 to below 30 per 1000 catheter days within 3 months
finding: CLABSI rate averaged 58.67 per 1000 catheter days across six data points, 66 per 1000 catheter days at the start; hand hygiene rate 58%; line utilisation ratio 0.4.
change: Point-of-care quality improvement (POCQI) using 12 PDSA cycles: WhatsApp group for communication, increased sterile tray availability, buffer stock of central lines, insertion checklist with simulation-based training, a 3-member insertion team for real-time checklist completion, maintenance bundle checklist incorporated into nursing handover, training mothers to detect soakage/leakage/swelling, restricted hub handling, standardised closed drip system use with syringe/line changes every 96 hours, and daily review of line necessity for early removal
setting: Level III NICU, Government Medical College Hospital, tertiary care centre (~18000 deliveries and 3500 NICU admissions annually)
cycle1_period: phase I baseline, first 3 months (May 2023 start)
cycle1_n: 30 babies with central lines, 125 catheter days
cycle1_result: CLABSI rate averaged 58.67 per 1000 catheter days across six data points, 66 per 1000 catheter days at the start; hand hygiene rate 58%; line utilisation ratio 0.4.
intervention: Point-of-care quality improvement (POCQI) using 12 PDSA cycles: WhatsApp group for communication, increased sterile tray availability, buffer stock of central lines, insertion checklist with simulation-based training, a 3-member insertion team for real-time checklist completion, maintenance bundle checklist incorporated into nursing handover, training mothers to detect soakage/leakage/swelling, restricted hub handling, standardised closed drip system use with syringe/line changes every 96 hours, and daily review of line necessity for early removal
cycle2_period: phase III sustainability, sustained over 12 months
cycle2_n: 335 babies with central lines, 1608 catheter days
cycle2_result: Mean CLABSI rate fell to 18 per 1000 catheter days, a 66% reduction (95% CI 0.14 to 0.78, p=0.012) versus baseline; insertion bundle compliance 88-89%; maintenance bundle compliance 56% (lowest for 'scrub the hub' at 48%, highest for hand hygiene at 68.9%); line utilisation ratio fell to 0.18; hand hygiene rate exceeded 70%.
other_findings: An intervention-phase (phase II) mean CLABSI rate of 37 per 1000 catheter days was also reported (47% reduction from baseline), with insertion compliance 86% and maintenance compliance 46%. A December 2024 resurgence in CLABSI, linked to a Klebsiella outbreak and a substandard liquid soap supply causing a dip in hand hygiene, resolved after the soap was changed. A scatter plot showed a negative correlation between CLABSI rate and volume of central lines inserted (Pearson r approximately -0.73, p<0.05), indicating the CLABSI reduction was not due to fewer insertions.

finding: median times exceeded targets for most KPIs: 2.6h to stop sedation (target 1h), 8.0h to extubation (target 4h), 10.9h to oral intake (target 6h), 18.6h to mobilisation (target 12h); drain removal and ICU discharge readiness were within target
change: Phased educational intervention over four PDSA cycles: introductory teaching, an electronic patient record (EPR) tool for real-time KPI tracking, an e-learning module, and targeted educational interventions addressing persistent delays
setting: Cardiothoracic intensive care unit, a major UK tertiary cardiac and lung referral centre
cycle1_result: median times exceeded targets for most KPIs: 2.6h to stop sedation (target 1h), 8.0h to extubation (target 4h), 10.9h to oral intake (target 6h), 18.6h to mobilisation (target 12h); drain removal and ICU discharge readiness were within target

topic: Early postnatal hypothermia in transported neonates
title: A regional quality-improvement collaborative to reduce early neonatal hypothermia in critically ill newborns.
standard: Local SMART target: reduce admission hypothermia (axillary temperature under 36.5C) from a baseline of 82.1% to below 60% within 12 months across the referral network, aligned with WHO thermal care criteria
finding: Early postnatal hypothermia (EPH) incidence was 82.1%; severe (grade 3 or higher) intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH) occurred in 2.6%; mortality within 7 days 0.6%; hypoglycaemia 4.8%; shock 4.3%.
change: Regional quality improvement collaborative: a standardised evidence-based thermal management protocol ('double RHBT' bundle covering room/radiant warmer, pre-warming/head, body/body weight, temperature/cluster care), staff training (action phase May 2023-April 2024) and monthly monitoring with feedback (sustain phase May-December 2024), developed via Delphi consultation and a key driver diagram
setting: Regional neonatal transport network, 6 referral hospitals, led by Shanghai Children's Medical Center NICU
cycle1_result: Early postnatal hypothermia (EPH) incidence was 82.1%; severe (grade 3 or higher) intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH) occurred in 2.6%; mortality within 7 days 0.6%; hypoglycaemia 4.8%; shock 4.3%.
intervention: Regional quality improvement collaborative: a standardised evidence-based thermal management protocol ('double RHBT' bundle covering room/radiant warmer, pre-warming/head, body/body weight, temperature/cluster care), staff training (action phase May 2023-April 2024) and monthly monitoring with feedback (sustain phase May-December 2024), developed via Delphi consultation and a key driver diagram
cycle2_result: EPH incidence fell to 59.0% (adjusted p<0.001); severe IVH fell to 0.2% (adjusted p=0.002); no significant differences in mortality (0.7%), pulmonary haemorrhage, shock (3.7%), hypoglycaemia (4.1%), DIC, or invasive mechanical ventilation use.
other_findings: EPH fell to 57.1% during the action phase but rebounded slightly to 60.9% during the sustain phase, attributed to new staff turnover and reduced monitoring intensity; no cases of hyperthermia were observed post-QI; reduction in EPH did not significantly reduce hypothermia in infants born under 28 weeks, though it did in other gestational age groups.
authors: Shen Y; Chen X; Zhang Y; Liu L; Liu JQ; Zhang L; Sheng W; Dong C; Chen X; Bei F

standard: American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and Joint Committee on Infant Hearing (JCIH) recommendation that all children with hearing loss be referred for genetic evaluation
finding: Any documented genetics referral occurred in 35.2% of patients; referral order placed in 18.2%; documentation in clinical note in 34.1%; note routed to genetics team in 5.7%; genetics appointment completed in 11.4%; genetic mutation identified in 4.6%. In Phase 1 all referral orders and documentation were made exclusively by ENT providers.
change: Standardised referral protocol: three predefined referral pathways (documentation in clinical note, routing note to genetics team, electronic referral order) applied at diagnosis, supported by provider email communication, discussion at a monthly department meeting, laminated ID badge cards and posted clinic workstation instructions, and an EMR smart phrase for documentation
setting: Children's Hearing Program, otology and audiology clinic, University of Miami
cycle1_result: Any documented genetics referral occurred in 35.2% of patients; referral order placed in 18.2%; documentation in clinical note in 34.1%; note routed to genetics team in 5.7%; genetics appointment completed in 11.4%; genetic mutation identified in 4.6%. intervention: Standardised referral protocol: three predefined referral pathways (documentation in clinical note, routing note to genetics team, electronic referral order) applied at diagnosis, supported by provider email communication, discussion at a monthly department meeting, laminated ID badge cards and posted clinic workstation instructions, and an EMR smart phrase for documentation

standard: International Paediatric Fever and Neutropenia Guideline Panel: first dose of antibiotic within 60 minutes of arrival (door-to-needle time, DTNT) for children with febrile neutropenia
finding: Median DTNT was 80 minutes (IQR 65-105); only 22% of children received antibiotics within 60 minutes; chemoport was accessed to administer antibiotics in only 19% of children; 10% required PICU admission.
change: PDSA-based quality improvement: development and implementation of a validated clinical care pathway (triage, assessment, investigations, antibiotic dosing, disposition), a dedicated isolation cubicle for febrile neutropenia patients, mannequin-assisted and bedside training for doctors/nurses in chemoport access and maintenance, redefined nursing handover responsibilities, a dedicated chemoport access equipment trolley, stocking restricted antibiotics in the PER pharmacy, and repeated training to address staff attrition
setting: 13-bed Paediatric Emergency Unit, tertiary teaching hospital (St. John's Medical College Hospital)
cycle1_n: 129 episodes of febrile neutropenia in 92 children
cycle1_result: Median DTNT was 80 minutes (IQR 65-105); only 22% of children received antibiotics within 60 minutes; chemoport was accessed to administer antibiotics in only 19% of children; 10% required PICU admission.
intervention: PDSA-based quality improvement: development and implementation of a validated clinical care pathway (triage, assessment, investigations, antibiotic dosing, disposition), a dedicated isolation cubicle for febrile neutropenia patients, mannequin-assisted and bedside training for doctors/nurses in chemoport access and maintenance, redefined nursing handover responsibilities, a dedicated chemoport access equipment trolley, stocking restricted antibiotics in the PER pharmacy, and repeated training to address staff attrition
cycle2_period: PDSA 1 July-September 2023, PDSA 2 October-December 2023, sustenance phase January-June 2024
cycle2_n: 80 episodes during intervention (44 and 36 in each PDSA cycle) and 47 during the sustenance phase
cycle2_result: Median DTNT fell to 40 minutes (IQR 30-50), a 50% reduction (p<0.001); the proportion of children receiving antibiotics within 60 minutes rose to 86% after PDSA 1 and 100% after PDSA 2; chemoport was accessed to administer antibiotics in all children post-intervention; no PICU admissions occurred post-intervention (versus 10% at baseline, p=0.002); no CLABSIs were reported from chemoport handling in the PER.

finding: CLABSI rate was 14.1 per 1000 central line days (14 per 1000 in the latter half of 2023); CLIP tool completion, full-body drape use and aseptic insertion practice were infrequently documented at baseline (quantitative baseline data unavailable due to poor documentation); crude mortality among CLABSI patients was 31.3% (5 of 16).
change: 9 PDSA cycles: staff education/training on infection prevention and central line care, increased frequency of ICU rounds by infection control nurses and the QI team, mandatory use of the electronic Central Line Insertion Practice (CLIP) tool with monthly audits, maximal barrier precaution monitoring via checklist, mandatory chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, hand hygiene refresher training with WHO 'Five Moments' monitoring and public recognition of top compliers, a central line maintenance bundle with daily necessity review and early removal, a maintenance bundle checklist, and 'scrub the hub' training and monitoring
setting: 12-bed polytrauma ICU, Level 1 trauma centre, All India Institute of Medical Sciences (2800-bed tertiary referral hospital)
cycle1_n: 16 CLABSI events over 1134 central line days
cycle1_result: CLABSI rate was 14.1 per 1000 central line days (14 per 1000 in the latter half of 2023); CLIP tool completion, full-body drape use and aseptic insertion practice were infrequently documented at baseline (quantitative baseline data unavailable due to poor documentation); crude mortality among CLABSI patients was 31.3% (5 of 16).
intervention: 9 PDSA cycles: staff education/training on infection prevention and central line care, increased frequency of ICU rounds by infection control nurses and the QI team, mandatory use of the electronic Central Line Insertion Practice (CLIP) tool with monthly audits, maximal barrier precaution monitoring via checklist, mandatory chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, hand hygiene refresher training with WHO 'Five Moments' monitoring and public recognition of top compliers, a central line maintenance bundle with daily necessity review and early removal, a maintenance bundle checklist, and 'scrub the hub' training and monitoring
cycle2_period: post-intervention 6-month period, with a CLABSI-free streak in March 2024
cycle2_n: 11 CLABSI events over 1368 central line days
cycle2_result: CLABSI rate fell to 8.04 per 1000 central line days, a 43% reduction (p=0.04), with 49 consecutive CLABSI-free days; CLIP tool completion rose to 88.3%; full-body drape use documented in 78.4% of cases; aseptic conditions maintained in 75%; central line maintenance bundle compliance rose to 75%; 'scrub the hub' compliance rose to 65%; chlorhexidine skin antisepsis compliance reached 100%; crude mortality among CLABSI patients fell to 27.3% (3 of 11).
other_findings: Device utilisation ratio did not change significantly (p=0.0772). standard: Local standard: institutional clinical practice guideline (CPG) for neonatal sepsis, as part of the Andean Health Organization (ORAS) regional antibiotic stewardship initiative, with a target of reducing antibiotic use rate (AUR) by 20% for early-onset (EOS) and late-onset sepsis (LOS)
finding: AUR for EOS was approximately 104 days per 1000 patient-days and for LOS approximately 158 days per 1000 patient-days at project start; institutional infection-related mortality was 4.4 deaths per 1000 live births (not broken down by sepsis type); CPG adherence in a 2021 evaluation was 84.4% for EOS and 66.8% for LOS.
change: 5 PDSA cycles: (1) identifying antibiotic overuse and adding an infectious disease specialist; (2) faster blood culture reporting, evolving from photographed results to an automated electronic platform updating every 8 hours; (3) improving blood culture collection technique (chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, minimum 1 mL blood volume, staff training); (4) updating the neonatal sepsis clinical practice guideline (minimum blood volumes, 48-hour antibiotic discontinuation for negative cultures without compatible symptoms, extension to 5 days if symptoms persist, delayed collection of acute-phase reactants); (5) regular dissemination of AUR control charts to staff
setting: Tertiary NICU, National Maternal and Perinatal Institute (INMP), largest delivery centre in Peru (approximately 13000 deliveries annually)
cycle1_n: 117 hospitalised patients sampled for baseline review; 37% of newborns hospitalised January-March 2023 received at least one course of antibiotics
cycle1_result: AUR for EOS was approximately 104 days per 1000 patient-days and for LOS approximately 158 days per 1000 patient-days at project start; institutional infection-related mortality was 4.4 deaths per 1000 live births (not broken down by sepsis type); CPG adherence in a 2021 evaluation was 84.4% for EOS and 66.8% for LOS.
intervention: 5 PDSA cycles: (1) identifying antibiotic overuse and adding an infectious disease specialist; (2) faster blood culture reporting, evolving from photographed results to an automated electronic platform updating every 8 hours; (3) improving blood culture collection technique (chlorhexidine skin antisepsis, minimum 1 mL blood volume, staff training); (4) updating the neonatal sepsis clinical practice guideline (minimum blood volumes, 48-hour antibiotic discontinuation for negative cultures without compatible symptoms, extension to 5 days if symptoms persist, delayed collection of acute-phase reactants); (5) regular dissemination of AUR control charts to staff
cycle2_result: AUR fell by 17.3% for EOS (from 104 to 86 days per 1000 patient-days, with the steepest decline from January to April 2024) and by 25.9% for LOS (central line falling from 158 to 117 days per 1000 patient-days, steepest decline September-October 2023, reaching a minimum AUR of 36 for EOS by May 2024); rule-out sepsis predominated in EOS (67.2%) while confirmed sepsis predominated in LOS (40.6%); no treatment failures or early recurrent sepsis were observed after antibiotic discontinuation, and no readmissions occurred within 30 days.
other_findings: EOS mortality was 15.8% and LOS mortality 20.2%; overall infection-related mortality declined from 3.5 to 3.0 per 1000 live births between semesters. The project met its 20% reduction target for LOS but not for EOS (17.3% reduction). Most frequently isolated pathogens were unspecified Gram-positive bacteria and Listeria monocytogenes in EOS, and coagulase-negative Staphylococcus in LOS.

topic: Perioperative hypothermia prevention in neonatal surgery

standard: Local standard, developed via the STEPP IN collaborative framework: normothermia defined as core temperature 36.5-37.5C on return to the NICU after surgery

setting: NICU of a tertiary paediatric hospital, part of the Wake Up Safe (WUS) collaborative
cycle1_result: Only 4 of 8 neonates (approximately 50%) returned to the NICU within the normothermic range after surgery, prompted by a serious safety event involving a neonate with an undetectable temperature on return.
intervention: 3 sequential PDSA phases: (1) a multidisciplinary hypothermia prevention checklist with standardised OR temperature (80F), pre-arrival supply preparation, warming lights and prewarmed transport beds; (2) an intraoperative 'temperature guardian' (OR circulating nurse) continuously monitoring temperature trends and alerting the team near threshold; (3) dual-source intraoperative temperature monitoring to validate readings, following a false-low reading during bowel irrigation
cycle2_period: September 2024 onward, phase 1 (14 cases), phase 2 (5 cases), phase 3 (12 cases)
cycle2_result: Hypothermia fell from 14% (2/14, including 1 bedside case) in phase 1 to 0% in phases 2 and 3 (5 and 12 cases respectively); mild hyperthermia occurred in 21% (phase 1), 20% (phase 2) and 8% (phase 3, due to a false-low core reading); checklist completion improved from approximately 75% to 92% after reassigning responsibility to the NICU charge nurse; intraoperative temperature monitoring compliance reached 100% in phases 2 and 3.
other_findings: Two special-cause outlier events were identified: a hypothermic neonate during an emergent bedside procedure (hypothermic before surgery) and a hyperthermic neonate following bowel irrigation with a falsely low core reading. No meaningful correlation was found between neonatal weight and postoperative temperature. This was a single-centre experience within the multicentre WUS Neonatal Hypothermia Prevention Task Force.

standard: PICU Up! early mobility protocol, which assigns patients a mobility level (1-3) based on physiologic criteria and recommends corresponding activities
finding: Agreement between protocol-expected and nurse-reported mobility level was moderate (53.5%, kappa=0.32); agreement for highest level of mobility (HLM) achieved was poor (40.6%, kappa=0.20); the PICU Up! level was undocumented in the EHR for 13.9% of patients and reported as unknown by nurses for 27.7%; median mobilisations per shift were 1 by EHR documentation versus 6 by nurse report versus 6 expected; discordance between nurse-reported and expected mobility level occurred in 46.5% of patients and discordance in HLM in 59.4%; severe baseline disability (Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category) was associated with higher odds of discordant mobility level (OR 8.33, 95% CI 2.50 to 27.76, p=0.001) and discordant HLM (OR 3.71, 95% CI 1.15 to 12.01, p=0.029), while mechanical ventilation, vascular access lines, and sedation over 30 minutes were associated with lower odds of HLM discordance.
setting: 28-bed academic PICU, Johns Hopkins Hospital (PICU Up! early mobility programme, running since 2014)
cycle1_result: Agreement between protocol-expected and nurse-reported mobility level was moderate (53.5%, kappa=0.32); agreement for highest level of mobility (HLM) achieved was poor (40.6%, kappa=0.20); the PICU Up! level was undocumented in the EHR for 13.9% of patients and reported as unknown by nurses for 27.7%; median mobilisations per shift were 1 by EHR documentation versus 6 by nurse report versus 6 expected; discordance between nurse-reported and expected mobility level occurred in 46.5% of patients and discordance in HLM in 59.4%; severe baseline disability (Pediatric Cerebral Performance Category) was associated with higher odds of discordant mobility level (OR 8.33, 95% CI 2.50 to 27.76, p=0.001) and discordant HLM (OR 3.71, 95% CI 1.15 to 12.01, p=0.029), while mechanical ventilation, vascular access lines, and sedation over 30 minutes were associated with lower odds of HLM discordance.
other_findings: Potential safety events with mobilisation were rare (0.02 per mobilisation), with no equipment dislodgements or cardiac arrests. The authors note that simulation-based nurse education has separately been shown to improve protocol adherence at this centre and call for real-time audit-and-feedback with mandatory EHR documentation of mobility.

title: Quality improvement project for minimising red blood cell unit wastage at a secondary referral hospital in Malawi.
standard: Local target: reduce blood unit wastage to zero; First Expire First Out (FEFO) adherence
finding: Mean expiry rate 4.16% (37/890), highest in March at 5.4%.
change: Adjusted blood ordering mechanism, strict FEFO adherence, improved coordination and staff coverage (5 PDSA cycles).
setting: Secondary referral hospital, Rumphi District Hospital, Malawi
cycle1_result: Mean expiry rate 4.16% (37/890), highest in March at 5.4%.
intervention: Adjusted blood ordering mechanism, strict FEFO adherence, improved coordination and staff coverage (5 PDSA cycles).
cycle2_result: Wastage declined to 1% (6/520, p=0.007); zero expiries from September 2024 to March 2025; ward-returned units declined from 1.1% (8/713) to 0.7% (4/570), p=0.45.
other_findings: Baseline over-ordering was driven by long distance and transport logistics.
